title: Leash the arena skeleton to its post and walk it home after a chase
description:
## Why
Leaving the fight room mid-combat must create a new situation, not a reset (CONSTITUTION §2, "failure creates stories"). e01-slice-skeleton-encounter requires a 25 m leash, but no AI item owns a leash: combat behaviour (e11-combat-behaviour) pursues indefinitely and return-to-routine (e11-return-to-routine) is m2.

## What
As a knight, I want the arena skeleton to chase me only so far from its post and then walk back, keeping its wounds, so that I can retreat, recover and come back to a fight I have already started.

A creature placement may carry `leash: { radius, post }` (post defaults to the spawn point). In Combat, when the creature's own distance from its post exceeds the radius it drops the target and enters Searching at the leash edge; when Searching ends it paths back to its post (e11-patrol-routines resume) and settles to Unaware in its post idle. It keeps its health and poise damage. A target that steps back inside the radius during Searching can be re-acquired by normal perception.

## Scope
- In: Leash data on creature spawns, leash check in the combat loop, walk-home to the post, slice skeleton leash of 25 m
- Out: Post-alert changes such as relighting torches (e11-return-to-routine, mw-e11.15)
- Out: Search patterns (e11-search-behaviour, mw-e11.11)

## Notes
Spec: docs/design/vertical-slice.md §6 (failure F5). With the skeleton's post at (2.5, 32.5) the leash edge crosses the corridor near z = 7.5, so the spawn room is out of reach.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature in Combat with leash radius 25 m, when its distance from its post exceeds 25 m, then within one tick it drops the target and enters Searching.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the creature's Searching timer expires, when simulated, then it paths to its post, arrives and is Unaware in its post idle within 10 s on an open path.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the creature took 40 damage before leaving the leash, when it returns to its post, then its health is still 40 below max (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature with no leash, when chasing beyond 25 m, then behaviour is unchanged (backwards compatible).
- AC-5 [integration] Given the slice arena and a player who flees down the corridor into the spawn room, when 15 s pass, then the skeleton never enters the spawn room and is back at its post.

title: Lock classes that are not playable yet on the class select screen
description:
## Why
The owner decided (2026-10-02) that the m1 slice supports the Knight only. Class choice is the game's core promise (CONSTITUTION §1–2), so the screen should still show all four classes while making it impossible to start a run the slice cannot support.

## What
As a player, I want to see all four classes on the class select screen, with the ones not yet playable shown as locked and a reason, so that I know what is coming and cannot start a run the build does not support.

A data field `game.playableClasses` (next to `game.startScene`, e01-title-new-game-flow) lists the selectable class ids; m1 ships `["knight"]`. Cards for other classes stay visible with their name, pitch and signature verbs, greyed, with a lock badge and the reason "Not playable in this build yet". They stay focusable (so screen readers announce the reason) but Confirm is disabled while one is focused. The Knight card is focused by default. Debug and test builds can override the list (e.g. the dev content layer) so e19-class-selection's per-class tests still run.

## Scope
- In: `game.playableClasses` field and validator, locked-card state on the e19-class-selection screen, default focus, debug override
- Out: The selection screen and apply-class (e19-class-selection, mw-e19.5)
- Out: Class data (e19-class-definitions, mw-e19.4)

## Notes
Spec: docs/design/vertical-slice.md §3 (beat B1). m2 unlocks classes by editing the list, with no code change.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given game.playableClasses = ["knight"], when the class select screen opens, then four cards show, the Knight card is focused and the other three show a lock badge and the reason "Not playable in this build yet".
- AC-2 [integration] Given focus on a locked card, when Confirm is pressed (keyboard, mouse or gamepad), then nothing starts and Confirm reports disabled with the same reason (edge).
- AC-3 [content] Given game.playableClasses lists a class id with no class data file, when content is validated, then validation fails naming the id.
- AC-4 [unit] Given game.playableClasses is empty, when validated, then validation fails (a build must offer at least one class) (edge).
- AC-5 [e2e] Given a production build, when the player picks New Game, then only the Knight can be confirmed and the slice spawns with player.class = knight.

title: Dev server reloads on agent worktree and coverage output
description: pnpm dev at the repo root watches .claude/worktrees/** and coverage/**, so every parallel agent's coverage run triggers thousands of full page reloads (125k logged overnight), making the game unplayable in the browser. Ignore .claude/, coverage/, playwright output in server.watch.

title: Step up onto steps whose edges are rounded, as on the Rapier CollisionWorld
description:
## Why

On the in-memory fake, box edges are square (the capsule's Minkowski sum is sharp), so the controller's step-up landing probe hits a step's top face and sees a walkable normal. On the real Rapier CollisionWorld (mw-e02.21) edges are rounded, as the CollisionWorld contract allows ('only face contacts are pinned'). The landing probe, advanced only one tick's travel (~0.08 m at run speed) past the wall, meets the step's top edge with a normal of about 50° (y ≈ 0.64 < cos 45°), so the step is refused and the player stops dead at a 0.30 m step. Found by the greybox traversal course on Rapier (tests/integration/character-course-rapier.test.ts, currently marked it.fails).

## What

Make stepUp robust to rounded edges, e.g. probe the landing at least one capsule radius past the wall (then place the feet at the real advance), or accept an edge contact whose witness lies on a walkable top face. Keep the fake and Rapier runs of the course behaving the same.

## Scope

- In: controller step-up (src/sim/character/controller.ts), its tests, flipping the Rapier course test from it.fails to it, re-recording the course replays if hashes change
- Out: CollisionWorld contract changes (edges stay unpinned)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 0.30 m step and a CollisionWorld with rounded edges (Rapier), when the player runs at it, then it steps up losing no more than 10% speed (mw-e02.2 AC-4 on Rapier).
- AC-2 [integration] Given the greybox traversal course on the Rapier adapter, when the recorded log runs, then every course feature passes as on the fake.

title: Put a controllable player capsule into the greybox testbed
description:
## Why
The controller (mw-e02.2), input (mw-e02.1), loop (mw-e00.20) and testbed (mw-e00.21) all exist, but nothing connects them, so there's still nothing to walk around.
## What
In ?scene=testbed, spawn a player character, feed sampled ActionFrames and camera yaw into createFrameLoop and characterControllerSystem, resolve collisions against the scene's greybox colliders, and render an interpolated placeholder capsule. Use the Rapier CollisionWorld (mw-e02.21) if it has merged; otherwise, a fake CollisionWorld built from the scene's GreyboxShapes behind the same interface, swapped out later.
## Scope
- In: spawn point from scene data, input to loop to controller wiring, placeholder capsule mesh, simple fixed follow camera until mw-e02.4
- Out: orbit camera (mw-e02.4), animation (mw-e02.6)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given ?scene=testbed, when the Playwright bot holds W for 1 s, then the player capsule moves at least 4 m forward and there are no console errors.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the testbed wall, when the bot walks into it, then the capsule stops in front of it and does not pass through.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given Space pressed, when grounded, then the capsule leaves the ground and lands again within 1 s.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the same recorded input log, when replayed through the testbed wiring twice, then the final sim hashes match.

title: Host a sim-owned deterministic Rapier world with static colliders
description:
## Why
mw-e03.10 (size:l) bundles the physics foundation with dynamic-object behaviour. Walking the greybox testbed only needs the foundation, and mw-e02.21 (the CollisionWorld adapter) needs it too. Split out per contract §4.
## What
A sim-owned physics port (ADR-0001): the @dimforge/rapier3d-deterministic world created and stepped inside the sim fixed tick, owned by World and not by the renderer. It implements StaticColliderSink (src/sim/physics/static-colliders.ts) with fixed colliders from GreyboxShape and replaces InMemoryColliderSink in src/main.ts. Physics state is included in the sim state hash and snapshot/restore. Vitest can load the WASM (the non-compat package has no main/exports; see the mw-e03.10 notes).
## Scope
- In: port interface plus Rapier implementation, lazy WASM init via the physics loader, fixed-step stepping, static colliders, hash and snapshot integration, test WASM loading
- Out: dynamic bodies, properties→mass, impacts, sleeping budget (mw-e03.10); CollisionWorld adapter (mw-e02.21)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a greybox scene loaded into the Rapier sink, when unloaded, then the physics world has zero colliders.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the same scene, when the sim runs 600 ticks twice, then state hashes including physics are identical.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a physics snapshot taken at tick 300, when restored into a new World and run to tick 600, then the hash equals the uninterrupted run.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given ?scene=testbed, when the app loads, then static colliders are registered in the Rapier world (debug attribute count > 0) with zero console errors.
- AC-5 [unit] Given physics WASM fails to load, when the sim starts, then a clear error state is reported rather than an uncaught exception (edge).

title: Implement CollisionWorld on Rapier for the character controller
description:
## Why
mw-e02.2 moves the player through a Rapier-free CollisionWorld interface (src/sim/character/collision-world.ts) tested against a fake. The real game needs it backed by the sim-owned Rapier physics port from mw-e03.10.
## What
An adapter implementing CollisionWorld (capsule shape-cast, raycast, overlap) on the deterministic Rapier world, plus contract tests shared with the fake.
## Scope
- In: adapter, shared contract test suite run against fake and Rapier
- Out: controller logic (mw-e02.2), physics port and stepping (mw-e03.10)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the shared CollisionWorld contract suite, when run against the Rapier adapter and the fake, then both pass.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the greybox traversal course and a recorded input log, when replayed twice on the Rapier adapter, then final sim state hashes are identical.

title: Add the Forgotten skeleton with the e04 three-move set
description:
## Why
The skeleton is the game's first creature and the m1 fight; it must be fun to fight with no reward.

## What
As a player, I want a skeleton that fights with readable, parryable attacks so that my first fight feels intrinsically good.
Creature data forgotten-miner on e12-creature-schema: walker, sight + hearing, no smell; resistances blunt 1.5, pierce 0.5, poison 0 (per e04 example); adopts the e04-creature-attack-hooks greybox skeleton set exactly: overhead chop (parryable), 2-hit slash (parryable), lunging thrust (unparryable, blockable). Placeholder capsule-plus-bones mesh.

## Scope
- In: Creature data, move references, resistance table, content test
- Out: Crumble/reassemble (e13-forgotten-reassembly)
- Out: Monk variant and habits (e13-forgotten-habits)
- Out: Model/animation (E37)

## Notes
Adopts the e04-creature-attack-hooks greybox skeleton set verbatim. Related: e04-skeleton-fun-validation uses this creature.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given forgotten-miner.json, when validated, then it passes CreatureDef and all three moves pass the readability rule (windup >= 18 ticks; the thrust flagged unparryable).
- AC-2 [integration] Given the knight parries the overhead chop in window, when resolved, then the skeleton enters Parried and a riposte is available.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a 30-blunt hit, when resolved against the skeleton, then 45 damage is applied; given 30 poison, then 0 and immune feedback (edge).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the creature arena, when spawned, then it ticks 600 frames, perceives a player at 10 m in lit space and enters Combat.

title: Prove the slice plays start-to-finish in a CI e2e test
description:
## Why
Releases must be trusted without reading the code; the m1 loop is the most important thing to never break.

## What
A Playwright e2e test that boots the build, starts a new game as Knight, drives the slice via a recorded input log (e00-replay-harness) through fight → loot → save → deliberate death → reload → exit, and asserts slice.complete. Also asserts perf and load budgets on the reference CI runner profile.

## Scope
- In: Recorded input log, Playwright spec, CI job wiring, perf/load assertions
- Out: Per-class gauntlet e2e (e01-class-gauntlet-e2e)

## Notes
Replays must be regenerated when controller tuning changes; provide a pnpm script to re-record.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the CI build, when the slice e2e runs, then it reaches slice.complete = true with zero console errors or unhandled rejections.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the scripted death step, when the reload completes, then the replay continues and the final sim state hash equals the committed golden hash.
- AC-3 [perf] Given the slice run, when measured, then initial load to playable <= 10 s at 50 Mbps throttling, warm reload <= 3 s and JS heap <= 1.5 GB.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the build is served with IndexedDB unavailable, when the slice runs, then saving shows the documented fallback message and the run still reaches the exit (edge).

title: Run the player death and respawn loop
description:
## Why
E01 owns dying: death must be a quick, clear beat that invites another attempt ("failure creates stories").

## What
As a player, I want dying to play a short death beat and then offer respawn or reload so that I am back in play within seconds.
On the player's Died event (e04-damage-model): freeze input, 1.5 s death beat (camera pull-back, fade), then hand off to the e30-death-reload screen. Adds a data-driven respawn-rule resolver (content/world/respawn-rules.json): rules of {region, conditions, destination, mode: reload|wake-in-place, factsToSet}. m1 ships a single rule: slice → reload last save. Emits player.died and player.respawned telemetry-ready events.

## Scope
- In: Died handling for the player entity, death beat, respawn-rule schema + resolver, m1 rule, events
- Out: Death screen and reload mechanics (e30-death-reload)
- Out: Contextual wake-up rules such as the Fold (e01-contextual-respawn)

## Notes
Coordinate with foundation: e30-death-reload owns the screen and reload; this item owns everything between Died and that screen plus the rule table. Related: e39-failure-narratives (texts), e34-gameplay-events (death telemetry).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player entity emits Died, when the next tick runs, then player input is ignored and exactly one player.died event is emitted with position and killer id.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the player dies in the slice arena, when "Load last save" is chosen, then the game is playable within 3 s warm and the skeleton's state matches the save.
- AC-3 [unit] Given two respawn rules whose conditions both match, when resolved, then the rule with the higher priority wins and ties break by rule id deterministically.
- AC-4 [unit] Given no respawn rule matches the current region, when the player dies, then the resolver falls back to reload-last-save and logs a content warning (edge).
- AC-5 [content] Given respawn-rules.json, when validated, then every destination references an existing scene spawn point.

title: Save and reload the slice with world state intact
description:
## Why
Save/reload is part of the m1 loop; reloading must restore the world, not just the player.

## What
As a player, I want to save anywhere safe and reload into exactly the same situation so that I trust the game with my time.
Wire the slice to autosave on the arena checkpoint and after slice completion; manual save from the pause menu (e01-pause-menu). Persisted: player vitals/inventory, skeleton alive/dead, chest looted, door state.

## Scope
- In: Checkpoint autosave trigger, fact registrations for slice state, pause-menu save
- Out: Save format, storage and UI (E30)
- Out: World-state store (e27-world-state-store)

## Notes
Autosave must defer while the skeleton is in Combat (e30-autosave safe predicate).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the skeleton is dead and the chest looted, when the game is saved and reloaded, then the skeleton does not respawn, the chest is empty and the sim state hash matches.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player enters the checkpoint trigger while the skeleton is in Combat, when the trigger fires, then the autosave is deferred until combat ends (edge).
- AC-3 [e2e] Given a manual save in the corridor, when the page is reloaded and Continue chosen, then play resumes in the corridor within 3 s warm.

title: Add slice loot: skeleton key drop and an alcove chest
description:
## Why
The loop is explore → fight → loot; the reward should matter (it opens the exit) and be interesting (item text with voice).

## What
As a player, I want to loot the skeleton and a chest so that I get the exit key and a small surprise.
The skeleton carries "Rusted gallery key"; the alcove chest uses a slice loot table (a healing draught, a few coins, one oddity with bible-voice text). The exit door accepts the key via the keyring.

## Scope
- In: Item data for the key and oddity, slice loot table, chest placement, door lock id
- Out: Container/loot runtime (E18)
- Out: Keyring (e17-keys-keyring)

## Notes
Item text follows bible §7.4 voice (1–3 sentences with a turn of feeling). Placeholder text is fine until e39-item-creature-text.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the slice loot table, when validated, then it passes e18-loot-validator and every entry references an existing item.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player holds the gallery key, when interacting with the exit door, then it unlocks and opens without opening the inventory.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the chest has been looted and the game is saved and reloaded, when the chest is opened again, then it is empty (edge).

title: Place the Forgotten skeleton fight in the slice arena
description:
## Why
"Fighting a skeleton should be enjoyable even when the player doesn't need XP or loot." The slice's fight is that promise in miniature.

## What
As a player, I want a skeleton that wakes when I enter the arena and fights with readable attacks so that the slice has a real fight.
Spawns e13-forgotten-skeleton (miner variant) seated against the far pillar in a Unaware "resting" idle; enters Combat on sight or on noise in the arena. On death it drops its carried key.

## Scope
- In: Encounter data (spawn, idle, wake trigger), key carried by the skeleton
- Out: Skeleton data and moves (e13-forgotten-skeleton)
- Out: AI (E11)

## Notes
Leaving the arena mid-fight: the skeleton pursues to the corridor then returns to its post (leash 25 m) — failure creates a new situation, not a reset.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player enters the arena in view of the skeleton, when 2 s elapse, then the skeleton is in Combat state and has targeted the player.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the skeleton is killed, when its Died event fires, then the exit key is dropped as a world item within 1 m of its body.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player flees beyond the 25 m leash, when 10 s pass, then the skeleton returns to its post in Searching then Unaware state and retains its damage (edge).
- AC-4 [manual] Given 3 internal testers, when they play the slice, then each can name at least one skeleton attack by its telegraph.

title: Build the slice grey-box level: room, corridor, arena, loot, exit
description:
## Why
The loop needs a place: a small, readable space that exercises movement, a door, a fight and a reward.

## What
As a player, I want a short grey-box level so that I can explore, fight and loot in one continuous space.
Scene data (content/scenes/slice.json): spawn room with an interactable door, a 20 m corridor with one side alcove, a 12×12 m fight arena with two pillars for spacing, a loot alcove, and an exit door locked by a key. Checkpoint trigger at the arena entrance. Uses only e00 greybox kit pieces.

## Scope
- In: Scene data, navmesh bake, door/lock wiring, checkpoint trigger, slice-complete trigger
- Out: Skeleton spawn (e01-slice-skeleton-encounter)
- Out: Loot (e01-slice-loot)

## Notes
Pillars exist so a knight can break line of attack and so the skeleton's lunge can whiff — combat must be fun without rewards (e04-skeleton-fun-validation).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given slice.json, when validated, then it passes the scene schema and references only greybox kit pieces.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the scene loaded headless, when the navmesh is queried, then a path exists from spawn to exit and the arena is fully connected.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player walks into the exit trigger without the key, when it fires, then the door stays locked and a "locked" prompt appears (no slice complete).
- AC-4 [perf] Given the slice scene, when idling at spawn, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).
notes: 2026-10-02 from mw-e01.1: docs/design/vertical-slice.md is the layout of record — coordinates, two checkpoints (CP-1 at the spawn-room door, CP-2 before the arena), braziers, the 1.4 m loot-alcove sill and the exit vestibule trigger that writes slice.complete.

title: Pause the game with resume, settings, save and quit to title
description:
## Why
The m1 loop must be playable without dev tools: players need to stop, change settings, save and leave.

## What
As a player, I want Esc (or Start) to pause the game and offer Resume, Settings, Save, Load and Quit to Title so that I control my session.
Pausing halts the sim step (and therefore the world clock). Save is disabled with a reason when the autosave "unsafe" predicate vetoes (combat, mid-air, dialogue). Quit to Title asks for confirmation when there is unsaved progress since the last save. Keyboard and gamepad navigable.

## Scope
- In: Pause overlay on e00-ui-framework, sim pause/resume, wiring to settings, save and load screens, quit-to-title teardown
- Out: Settings screens (e31-settings-framework)
- Out: Save/load screens (e30-save-load-ui)

## Notes
Pause must be deterministic-safe: no sim ticks while paused, so replays are unaffected by pause duration.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the slice running, when Esc is pressed, then the sim stops stepping within one frame and the state hash is unchanged after 10 real seconds paused.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the skeleton is in Combat, when the pause menu opens, then Save is disabled with the reason "Can't save during combat" and Resume still works (edge).
- AC-3 [e2e] Given progress since the last save, when Quit to Title is chosen, then a confirmation appears; on confirm the title screen shows with zero console errors and Continue loads the last save.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the menu opened with a gamepad, when navigating with the d-pad, then every option is reachable with visible focus.
notes: 2026-09-29 from mw-e02.9: a gamepad disconnect already emits the pause action (pressed+released on one ActionFrame, GamepadSettings.pauseOnDisconnect) and the testbed shows 'Controller disconnected'. The pause screen should open on frame.pause.pressed, which also covers the pad's Menu button. See docs/design/controls.md.

title: Title screen flows into class select, spawn and continue
description:
## Why
The player must be able to "enter the game" (E01 outcome) without developer tools.

## What
As a player, I want a title screen with New Game, Continue and Load so that I can start or resume the slice in two clicks.
New Game → e19 class selection → loads the slice scene at its spawn point with the class kit. Continue loads the most recent save. Load opens e30-save-load-ui. Grey-box styling; build SHA shown (per e35-playtest-builds).

## Scope
- In: Title screen, New Game/Continue/Load wiring, scene hand-off to the slice spawn point
- Out: Class selection screen (e19-class-selection)
- Out: Save/load menus (e30-save-load-ui)
- Out: Final title art/music (E37/E38)

## Notes
The first scene id comes from a data field (game.startScene) so E24 can switch the start to the mountain road at m3 without code.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a clean profile, when the player clicks New Game, selects Knight and confirms, then the slice spawn room is playable within 10 s of page load on a 50 Mbps connection.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given no saves exist, when the title screen shows, then Continue is disabled and has an accessible "no saves yet" tooltip.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a save exists, when Continue is chosen, then the most recent save loads and the sim state hash equals the saved hash.
- AC-4 [unit] Given game.startScene references a scene id that does not exist, when the content check runs, then it fails naming the missing id.
notes: 2026-10-02 from mw-e01.1: the owner decided the m1 slice is Knight only; class select shows four cards with three locked (mw-e01.15). AC-1 already selects Knight. Continue with no saves is disabled with a reason, not hidden (see the note on mw-e30.11).

title: Write the m1 vertical slice spec and grey-box level plan
description:
## Why
M1 is the first proof the game loop works end to end; everyone building toward it needs one shared definition of "done".

## What
docs/design/vertical-slice.md: the exact flow (title → class select → spawn room → corridor → skeleton fight room → loot alcove → locked exit → slice complete), a top-down grey-box sketch with dimensions, which systems each beat exercises, the pass criteria for the e2e test, and what is explicitly faked (placeholder art, one class required, no dialogue).

## Scope
- In: Slice flow, level sketch, beat → system mapping, pass criteria, placeholder list
- Out: Building the level (e01-slice-greybox-level)
- Out: m2 class gauntlet (e01-class-gauntlet-level)

## Notes
Keep the slice under 5 minutes for a first-time player. Related: e35-fun-hypotheses (the slice should be the stimulus for e35-greybox-combat-test).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spec, when reviewed, then every beat names the owning bead key (e.g. e04-melee-core, e18-containers) of the system it exercises.
- AC-2 [content] Given the spec, when reviewed, then it defines a single machine-checkable "slice complete" condition (world fact slice.complete = true).
- AC-3 [content] Given the spec, when reviewed, then it lists the failure paths in scope (player death, reload with no save, leaving the fight room mid-combat) and their expected outcomes.

title: Add class selection at new game that applies kit and capabilities
description:
## Why
Choosing a class is the game's core promise; the choice must be clear and apply fully at start.
## What
As a player, I want to choose Knight, Archer, Sorcerer or Thief at the start and see what each can do so that I pick the fantasy I want.

New-game flow: class cards with short pitch, 3 signature verbs listed, starting kit preview. Confirm applies class: grants starting capabilities (source `class`), adds kit to inventory, equips kit, sets stats. Class stored in save and exposed to conditions (`player.class`).
## Scope
- In: Selection screen (grey-box styling), apply-class sim function, save field, keyboard/gamepad navigation
- Out: Character customization/appearance (not MVP)
- Out: Final class card art (asset group)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: 4 class card illustrations/portraits, 4 class emblem icons.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the thief class applied to a fresh player, when complete, then the registry, inventory and equipment exactly match the thief data file.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the selection screen, when the player tries to confirm without a class highlighted, then confirm is disabled.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given a new game, when the player selects Sorcerer and enters the greybox testbed, then the HUD shows the sorcerer starting kit and `player.class` is `sorcerer`.
- AC-4 [unit] Given apply-class is called on a player who already has a class, when executed, then it throws `class-already-set` (no stacking of classes).

title: Define the four classes as data: kit, capabilities, proficiencies
description:
## Why
Classes change possibilities; defining them as data keeps class checks out of code and makes dialogue/quest gating uniform.
## What
Class schema + four class files (knight, archer, sorcerer, thief): `startingCapabilities`, `startingKit` (items, gold), `proficiencies` (weight classes, weapon tags), `supportingStats` start values, `dialogueTag` (for [Thief]-style options), `unlockChannels` (which progression channels apply), `iconId`, `portraitId`. Grey-box starting kits only; final kits tuned later.
## Scope
- In: Class schema, 4 class data files with placeholder kits, validator
- Out: Selection UI (e19-class-selection)
- Out: Final starting kits (tuned during m2/m3)

**Integration note:** Archer class data should grant `sense.tracking` (used by the Sleepers' Path in E25 to reveal sleepwalker trails in daylight); if not granted, the path falls back to night-only visibility.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 4 class files, when validated, then each has ≥ 2 starting capabilities, a starting kit whose items all resolve, and a unique dialogueTag.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a class whose startingCapabilities include an id not in the registry, when validated, then validation fails naming the class and id.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a class file with no unlock channel, when validated, then validation fails (every class must be able to progress).

title: Implement capability-unlock progression with prerequisite chains
description:
## Why
Progression should unlock new verbs (constitution §3). This is the rule engine every class channel plugs into.
## What
As a player, I want each thing I learn to give me a new way to act, building on what I already know, so that my character grows in possibilities rather than numbers.

Unlock definitions: `{capability, prerequisites: [capIds], requirements: conditions, source channel}`. `learn(capId, channel)` checks prerequisites and requirements and grants with source `learned`. Supports verb chains (Firebolt → Flame Jet → Fire Wall) and upgrades that *replace or extend* a verb (Telekinesis → throw creatures). Learned set persists via save.
## Scope
- In: Unlock definitions schema, learn API, prerequisite resolution, "why can't I learn this" explanations, save section
- Out: Class-specific channels (e19-*-channel items)
- Out: UI (e19-capabilities-screen)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given `spell.flame-jet` requiring `spell.ember`, when a player without Ember tries to learn Flame Jet, then learning fails with reason `missing-prerequisite: spell.ember`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given all prerequisites met, when learned, then the capability is granted with source `learned` and `progression.learned` is emitted with the channel.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a capability already learned, when learned again, then the call is a no-op returning `already-known` (no duplicate events).
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unlock that `replaces` a previous capability, when learned, then the old capability's `learned` source is revoked and the new one granted atomically.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a learned set, when saved and loaded, then the registry state is identical.
- AC-6 [content] Given all unlock definitions, when validated, then there are no prerequisite cycles and no unlock is a pure numeric upgrade unless flagged `supporting`.

title: Create capability registry with source-tracked grants
description:
## Why
Dialogue, quests, puzzles, interaction prompts and equipment all ask "can the player do X?"; one registry avoids class checks scattered through code.
## What
Capability definitions as data (`id` like `verb.climb.ledge`, `spell.ember`, `arrow.rope`, `tool.lockpick`, `sense.detect-magic`; `nameKey`, `descKey`, `icon`, `class` affinity, `supporting` flag). Runtime registry per actor: `grant(capId, source)`, `revoke(capId, source)`, `has(capId)`, `sources(capId)`, reference-counted by source (`class`, `learned`, `equipment:<id>`, `temporary:<effectId>`). Emits `capability.gained` / `capability.lost` only on 0↔1 transitions.
## Scope
- In: Capability schema + validator, registry runtime, events, query API
- Out: Unlock rules and prerequisites (e19-progression-core)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a capability granted by two sources, when one source revokes it, then `has` is still true and no `capability.lost` event is emitted.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a capability with zero sources, when granted, then exactly one `capability.gained` event is emitted.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a grant of an undefined capability id, when called, then it throws in dev/test builds and is a logged no-op in production builds.
- AC-4 [content] Given the capability data files, when validated, then ids are unique and match the pattern `^(verb|spell|arrow|tool|trick|technique|sense)\.[a-z0-9.-]+$`.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: mw-e15.1 added a minimal capability id registry as content: src/content/types/capability.ts (group files src/content/data/capability/<group>.json with {id, name, description}, the AC-4 id pattern, cross-file uniqueness via checkCapabilities). Seeded only with spell.mage-hand. This bead should extend that schema (nameKey/descKey, icon, class affinity, supporting flag) and add the runtime registry rather than create a second one.

title: Spike: capability-unlock progression model, stats and respec policy
description:
## Why
The anti-grind rule demands progression that unlocks verbs, not numbers. We must decide the model before class, loot and shop data are authored against it.
## What
Time-box: 1.5 days. Questions: (1) Is there XP/levels at all, or do unlocks come only from in-world sources (books, trainers, schematics, tools, deeds)? (2) Which minimal supporting stats exist (health, stamina, focus/mana) and how do they grow (found items, shrines, deeds)? (3) How does each class earn verbs: sorcerer books, knight trainer techniques, archer arrows + trick-shot techniques, thief tools + tricks? (4) Can classes cross-learn (a knight reading a simple spellbook)? (5) Respec policy: none (additive capabilities), loadout swapping, or paid retraining?
## Scope
- In: ADR with recommendation, per-class unlock channel table, stat list with ranges, respec decision, anti-grind validation rules for content
- Out: Implementation (e19-capability-registry onward)
## Notes
Leaning: no XP; unlocks are in-world acquisitions; supporting stats grow via rare found items/deeds; capabilities are additive so respec is limited to loadout choices (e.g. prepared spell slots) — revisit if playtests disagree.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the spike, when complete, then docs/adr/ contains an Accepted progression ADR answering all five questions.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it contains a table listing each class's unlock channels with at least 3 example verb chains per class following the Firebolt → Flame Jet → Fire Wall pattern.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it lists the supporting stats (≤ 5) with numeric start values and caps.
- AC-4 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it defines content validation rules that reject pure numeric-upgrade unlocks unless flagged `supporting`.
notes: ADR: docs/adr/0004-progression-model.md (Accepted 2026-10-02). Follow-ups: mw-e19.15, mw-e19.16, mw-e19.17. mw-e19.13 (respec/loadout) is superseded: no respec, no loadout slots.

title: Build container window and loot pickup notifications
description:
## Why
Discoveries need a moment of presentation; looting should be one or two inputs.
## What
As a player, I want a compact container window with Take / Take All and a short pickup toast so that looting is fast and discoveries feel noticed.

Container window lists contents with icons; Take All bound to a single key/button. Pickup toasts stack in a corner (max 4, merged by def). Unique artifacts get a distinct "discovery" toast with the item's flavour line.
## Scope
- In: Container window, take/take-all, pickup toasts, artifact discovery toast, gamepad support
- Out: Item inspection details (e17-inventory-ui)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: container window frame, pickup toast frame, artifact discovery banner.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given an open container with 3 items, when Take All is pressed, then all 3 are in inventory and the window closes within the same frame.
- AC-2 [integration] Given 6 items picked up within 1 second, when toasts display, then at most 4 toasts are visible and duplicates by def are merged with a count.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a unique artifact picked up, when displayed, then the discovery toast shows its flavour line and remains for ≥ 4 s.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an empty container, when opened, then the window shows "Empty" and Take All is disabled.

title: Add lootable containers that persist their contents
description:
## Why
The m1 loop requires loot; the constitution says bookshelves, chests and wells should contain things, and looted state must persist.
## What
As a player, I want to open chests, barrels, bookshelves and corpses and take what's inside so that exploring pays off.

Container component: `contents` either fixed list or `lootTable` rolled once on first open (seed derived from container id + world seed so it is stable across reloads). Take one / take all, put items back. Hooks: `lockId` (e03), `trapId` (mw-e10), `ownerId` (e18-ownership-stolen). Contents persisted via world-state store after first open.
## Scope
- In: Container component, open/take/put, roll-once semantics, persistence, lock hook, empty-state
- Out: Container UI (e18-container-ui)
- Out: Trap mechanics (mw-e10)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an unopened container with a loot table, when opened twice across a save/reload, then the contents are identical both times (rolled once).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a container, when the player takes all, then contents move to inventory, container becomes empty and `container.looted` fact is set.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a locked container without a key, when opened, then it refuses with reason `locked` and does not roll its table.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player puts an item into a container, when saved and reloaded, then the item is still inside.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox testbed chest, when the player loots it, saves, reloads and opens it again, then it is empty.

title: Validate loot tables: references, uniques, cycles, weights
description:
## Why
Broken loot data silently produces empty chests or duplicate artifacts; CI must catch it.
## What
Content validator run in CI over all loot tables and placements: all item/table references exist, weights > 0, count ranges valid, no cycles in nested tables, each unique item appears in at most one guaranteed placement across the world, every table is referenced by something (warning).
## Scope
- In: Validator module + CLI entry + CI hook via content pipeline
- Out: Balance analysis (e18-treasure-audit-tool)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a table referencing a missing item id, when validated, then validation fails naming the table, entry index and missing id.
- AC-2 [unit] Given tables A→B→A, when validated, then validation fails reporting the cycle path "A > B > A".
- AC-3 [unit] Given a unique artifact guaranteed in two placements, when validated, then validation fails listing both placements.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unreferenced table, when validated, then a warning (not an error) is reported.
- AC-5 [content] Given the repository's loot content, when CI runs the validator, then it exits 0.

title: Implement loot table schema and deterministic seeded roller
description:
## Why
Loot is data (contract §1) and must be deterministic for replay tests; tables let designers favour handcrafted guarantees over random stat-sticks.
## What
As a designer, I want to author loot tables with guaranteed and weighted entries so that containers and creatures yield intentional discoveries.

Schema: `id`, `guaranteed: [{item, count}]`, `rolls: {min,max}`, `entries: [{item | table, weight, count:{min,max}, conditions?}]`, `noDuplicates`. Roller takes the seeded RNG stream + context (player class, world facts) and returns item stacks. Nested tables supported with depth limit 4. Unique items can only drop if not already in world state as obtained.
## Scope
- In: Schema + zod types, roller, uniqueness check against world state, conditional entries using simple predicates (class, fact) until the DSL lands
- Out: Containers (e18-containers)
- Out: Creature drops (e18-creature-drops)
- Out: Validator (e18-loot-validator)
## Notes
Conditions migrate to the shared DSL (e22-condition-effect-dsl) when available; keep the predicate interface identical.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a table with 2 guaranteed items and 0 rolls, when rolled with any seed, then exactly those 2 items are returned.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same table, seed and context, when rolled 10,000 times in two runs, then both result sequences are identical.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a weighted table (weights 3:1) rolled 40,000 times with seeded RNG, then observed ratios are within ±2% of 75%/25%.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a unique item already marked obtained in world state, when a table containing it is rolled, then the entry is skipped and its weight redistributed.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an entry conditioned on class `thief`, when rolled for a knight, then that entry never appears.
- AC-6 [unit] Given nested tables exceeding depth 4 at runtime, when rolled, then rolling stops at depth 4 and an error event is emitted (no infinite loop).

title: Build inventory screen with category tabs, inspect and actions
description:
## Why
The m1 loop includes loot; players need to see, inspect and use what they found with minimal friction.
## What
As a player, I want an inventory screen organized by category where I can inspect, equip, use, drop and assign items to quick slots so that managing gear takes seconds.

Tabs: All, Weapons & Armor, Tools, Consumables, Books, Keys, Quest & Artifacts. Item card shows icon, name, flavour description (room for QfG-style humour), granted verbs listed as verbs (not numbers first), stolen marker, value. Keyboard+mouse, gamepad navigation; respects text-size setting. Quick-slot HUD strip on the game screen.
## Scope
- In: Inventory screen, item inspect panel, context actions, quick-slot assignment, quick-slot HUD, placeholder icons by category
- Out: Paper-doll equipment view (e17-equipment-ui)
- Out: Final icon art (asset prompt beads)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: item category placeholder icons, stolen marker icon, gold icon, quick-slot frame, inventory panel frame. Final icons via asset group.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given an inventory with items in 4 categories, when the Books tab is selected, then only book items are listed, sorted by acquisition time descending.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a stolen item, when its card is displayed, then the stolen marker is visible and the tooltip names the owner if known.
- AC-3 [integration] Given gamepad input only, when navigating the grid and pressing confirm on a consumable, then a context menu with Use/Assign/Drop opens and each action works.
- AC-4 [unit] Given text size set to 150%, when the inventory renders, then item names wrap without overlapping and no text is clipped (DOM overflow check).
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the player opens inventory, assigns a potion to quick slot 2 and closes inventory, then pressing the quick-slot-2 action consumes the potion.
- AC-6 [unit] Given an empty inventory, when opened, then an empty-state message is shown instead of an empty grid.

title: Serialize inventory, equipment and quick slots into saves
description:
## Why
The m1 loop ends with save/reload; losing or duplicating items breaks trust immediately.
## What
Register inventory, equipment and quick-slot state with the versioned save format. Includes migration stub, round-trip tests and property-based randomized inventories.
## Scope
- In: Save section schema, serialize/deserialize, migration v1 stub, round-trip + fuzz tests
- Out: World item entities in the level (owned by e27 world-state persistence)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 100 randomized inventories (seeded) with stolen flags, stacks and equipped items, when saved and loaded, then state is deep-equal to the original.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a save referencing an item def that no longer exists, when loaded, then the instance is dropped, a warning is logged, and the rest of the inventory loads.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a v1 inventory save, when the migration runner processes it at current version, then it loads without error.

title: Pick up, drop and throw items as physical world objects
description:
## Why
Items should exist in the world with properties (a dropped key can fall through a grate; a thrown bottle distracts a guard), reinforcing systemic play.
## What
As a player, I want to pick up items I see, and drop or throw items from my inventory so that I can use them as bait, distractions or puzzle pieces.

World item entity: mesh placeholder by category, interact prompt "Take <name>", pickup adds to inventory and removes entity; drop/throw spawns an entity with physics and world properties. Pickup respects ownership (owned items marked stolen via e18-ownership-stolen when it lands).
## Scope
- In: World item entity, pickup/drop/throw bindings, placeholder meshes per category, noise event on impact via e09 hook
- Out: Containers (e18-containers)
- Out: Ownership logic (e18-ownership-stolen)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given an item entity within interact range, when the player interacts, then the item is added to inventory and the entity is despawned in the same sim tick.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an item in inventory, when dropped, then an item entity with identical instance flags (e.g. stolen) spawns in front of the player.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a thrown item that hits a surface, when impact resolves, then a noise event is emitted with loudness from the item weight class.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a quest item, when drop is requested, then it is rejected with reason `no-drop`.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the player picks up, drops and re-picks the same item, then inventory count returns to the original and no duplicate entity remains.
notes: **Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — required by the E01 grey-box vertical slice: the arena skeleton drops the exit key as a world item that the knight picks up (docs/design/vertical-slice.md beat B5, mw-e01.5 AC-2).

title: Use consumables from inventory and assignable quick slots
description:
## Why
Potions, food, oil flasks and scrolls are tactical tools; using them mid-fight must be fast and systemic.
## What
As a player, I want to drink, eat, apply or throw consumables from four quick slots so that I can react in combat without pausing.

Use pipeline: validate → apply `use` effects (heal, restore stamina/mana, apply status, coat weapon with oil, spawn thrown object) → consume one unit → emit `item.used`. Throwable consumables spawn a physics object carrying their world properties (a thrown oil flask shatters and leaves a flammable puddle via e03). Quick slots persist and auto-refill from same-def stacks; empty slots display as depleted.
## Scope
- In: Use pipeline, 4 quick slots, auto-refill, cooldown/animation-lock hook, throwables via world properties
- Out: Quick-slot HUD visuals (e17-inventory-ui)
- Out: Spell scrolls casting (e06-spell-pipeline consumes the effect)
## Notes
Effects expressed via property/effect vocabulary, never item-specific scripts (contract §5: properties, not pairings).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a healing draught in quick slot 1 and 3 in stock, when used, then health increases per data, stock becomes 2 and `item.used` is emitted.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the last unit in a quick slot is used and another stack of the same def exists, when used, then the slot refills from that stack.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a throwable consumable with `worldProperties: [flammable, liquid]`, when thrown, then a spawn request is emitted carrying exactly those properties.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a consumable used while a use-lock is active, when the second use is requested, then it is rejected with reason `busy` and no unit is consumed.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox testbed, when the player throws an oil flask then ignites it, then the resulting area is on fire via e03 propagation (no flask-specific code).

title: Auto-use keys from the keyring on matching locks
description:
## Why
Keys are core to exploration loops and shortcuts; fumbling through menus to use them is busywork.
## What
As a player, I want locked doors and chests to open automatically when I hold the right key so that finding the key is the reward.

Locks (e03-doors-locks-switches) expose `lockId`; keys declare `opens: [lockId]` or `opensTag`. Interacting with a lock checks the keyring; single-use keys are consumed; master keys open by tag. Missing key produces a contextual prompt hint ("Locked. Perhaps someone in town has the key.") driven by lock data.
## Scope
- In: Key matching, consumption rules, prompt text hooks, events for quests (`lock.opened` with keyId)
- Out: Lockpicking (mw-e10)
- Out: Forcing/smashing locks (mw-e03 / mw-e04)

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — required by the E01 grey-box vertical slice.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a door with lockId `tower-door` and a key whose `opens` includes it, when the player interacts, then the door unlocks and a `lock.opened` event records the key id.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a single-use key, when it opens its lock, then it is removed from the inventory; a reusable key remains.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a lock with no matching key, when interacted with, then the lock stays locked and the prompt shows the lock's `lockedHintKey` text.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the greybox testbed door with a key placed nearby, when the player picks up the key and interacts with the door, then the door opens without opening any menu.

title: Add equipment slots with class proficiencies and equip events
description:
## Why
Weapons, shields, armor and tools must be equipped to matter; equip state drives combat, stealth noise and granted verbs.
## What
As a player, I want to equip weapons, armor and tools so that my character looks and plays differently.

Slots: mainHand, offHand, head, body, hands, feet, trinket×2, ammo (quiver), toolBelt×2. Two-handed items occupy both hands. Class proficiency is soft: non-proficient equips are allowed but apply a data-defined penalty (e.g. slower draw, louder) rather than an outright block, so improvisation is possible. Emits `equip.changed` events; exposes a derived `EquipmentState` (weight class, noise modifier, light emitted, granted capabilities list).
## Scope
- In: Slot model, equip/unequip/swap, two-handed rules, proficiency penalties from data, derived state, events
- Out: What granted capabilities do (e17-equipment-verbs)
- Out: Paper-doll UI (e17-equipment-ui)
- Out: Combat stats consumption (mw-e04/mw-e05)
## Notes
Derived noise/weight feed e09-visibility-model and e09-sound-propagation via the derived state; those epics consume it.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a sword in mainHand and a shield in offHand, when a two-handed greatsword is equipped, then both previous items return to inventory and both hand slots reference the greatsword.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a sorcerer equipping heavy plate, when equipped, then the equip succeeds and the derived state includes the data-defined non-proficiency penalty.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an item without an `equip` block, when equip is requested, then it fails with reason `not-equippable`.
- AC-4 [unit] Given any equip change, when it completes, then exactly one `equip.changed` event is emitted with before/after slot maps.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the inventory ADR weight classes, when heavy body armor is equipped, then derived `weightClass` is `heavy` and `noiseModifier` matches the data value.

title: Implement inventory model with stacks, keys, books and quest items
description:
## Why
Players need to carry the things they discover without busywork; every loot, shop, quest and puzzle interaction reads or writes the inventory.
## What
As a player, I want picked-up items to land in a tidy inventory grouped by category so that I spend time adventuring, not sorting.

Pure sim module: `Inventory` holding item instances `{instanceId, defId, count, flags: {stolen?, ownerId?, bound?}}`. Operations: add (auto-stack; stolen and non-stolen never merge), remove, move-to-keyring/bookshelf views, query by category/tag/capability, gold as currency counter. Emits events (`item.added`, `item.removed`, `item.flagChanged`) on the sim event bus. Enforces capacity only as the encumbrance ADR dictates.
## Scope
- In: Inventory data structure, operations, events, category views (keys, books, quest objects, artifacts, consumables)
- In: Quest items cannot be removed except by effects with `force: true`
- In: Gold counter with overflow protection
- Out: Equip slots (e17-equipment-slots)
- Out: World pickup/drop (e17-world-pickup-drop)
- Out: Serialization (e17-inventory-persistence)
- Out: UI (e17-inventory-ui)
## Notes
Instances rather than bare counts so that stolen/owner flags and unique artifacts are tracked individually. Deterministic instance ids from the sim id generator (no Math.random).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an empty inventory, when 3 then 4 of a stackable item with maxStack 5 are added, then the inventory holds stacks of 5 and 2 and emits two `item.added` events.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an inventory holding 2 non-stolen apples, when 1 stolen apple is added, then there are two separate stacks and the stolen stack carries its ownerId.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a quest item in inventory, when a non-forced remove is requested, then removal is rejected with reason `quest-item` and the inventory is unchanged.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an inventory, when querying category `key`, then only key-category instances are returned in stable acquisition order.
- AC-5 [unit] Given gold at 2^31-10, when 100 gold is added, then gold clamps at the configured maximum and a `gold.capped` event is emitted.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a remove of more units than held, when executed, then it fails atomically and no partial removal occurs.

title: Define item definition schema and content validator
description:
## Why
Items are data, not code (contract §1). Every other systems epic (loot, shops, quests, progression) references item IDs, so a single validated schema is the foundation.
## What
A zod schema in src/content/items for item definitions: `id`, `category` (weapon, armor, shield, ammo, book, key, consumable, tool, quest, artifact, currency, misc), `nameKey`/`descKey` text ids, `icon` asset id, `value`, `stackable` + `maxStack`, `weightClass` (per encumbrance ADR), `worldProperties` (e03 tags so a dropped oil flask is flammable), `grants` (capability ids, see e19-capability-registry), `equip` (slot + class proficiency tags), `use` (effect list), `flags` (unique, questItem, noSell, noDrop).
## Scope
- In: Schema, TS types inferred from zod, loader integration, validator tests
- In: Cross-ref checks: icon asset ids exist in the asset manifest (placeholder allowed), capability ids exist, unique ids unique
- In: Five fixture items (one per major category) for tests
- Out: Inventory runtime (e17-inventory-core)
- Out: Actual game item content (world-content group)
## Notes
Keep `use` effects referencing the shared effect vocabulary from e22-condition-effect-dsl once it lands; until then a minimal effect union is acceptable and migrated later.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given a valid item fixture for each category, when validated, then validation passes and the inferred type exposes category-specific fields.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an item with `stackable: false` and `maxStack: 5`, when validated, then validation fails with a message naming the item id and field.
- AC-3 [unit] Given two items with the same id, when the item catalogue is loaded, then loading fails listing both source files.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an item whose `grants` references an unknown capability id, when validated against the capability registry, then validation fails naming the capability.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an item flagged `questItem: true` without `noSell` and `noDrop`, when validated, then those flags are defaulted to true.

title: Spike: decide encumbrance model (weightless vs light encumbrance)
description:
## Why
The epic outcome forbids inventory busywork, but some weight is useful when it creates decisions (heavy armor = loud and slow for stealth). We need a decision before the inventory model hardens.
## What
Time-box: 1 day. Question: which inventory capacity model best serves "no busywork" while keeping equipment choices meaningful? Evaluate (a) fully weightless with category tabs, (b) weightless inventory + equipped-armor weight that affects noise/stamina/movement verbs, (c) light encumbrance with generous soft cap, (d) grid/slot inventory. Also decide whether large world objects (crates, bodies, statues) are carried physically instead of stored.
## Scope
- In: Comparison matrix against constitution pillars, reference games (QfG5, DOS2, Skyrim, Zelda BotW)
- In: ADR in docs/adr/ with recommendation and consequences for mw-e17/mw-e10/mw-e09
- Out: Implementation (e17-inventory-core)
## Notes
Leaning: option (b) — inventory is weightless; only *equipped* armor/weapon weight class feeds e09 noise and stamina. Physically carried world objects handled by e03-physics-objects.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the spike is complete, when the ADR is reviewed, then docs/adr/ contains an encumbrance ADR with status "Accepted", the options matrix, and the chosen model.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it states explicitly how (if at all) equipment weight affects stealth noise, stamina and movement speed, with numeric ranges.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it lists the edge cases the model must handle: picking up an item while "full" (if caps exist), quest items, stacks, and physically carried world objects.
notes: ADR: docs/adr/0003-encumbrance-model.md (Accepted 2026-10-02). Follow-ups: mw-e17.13, mw-e17.14.

title: Propagate noise events through rooms, doors and walls with occlusion
description:
## Why
Sound propagation, surfaces and doors are constitution-mandated stealth inputs. Guards should hear a dropped bottle through an open door but not through thick stone.

## What
As a thief, I want noise to travel like it does in a building so that closing a door or taking the long way round actually keeps me quiet. Noise events {source, loudness dB at 1 m, kind, tags} propagate over a room/portal graph built from level data: distance attenuation (inverse-square approximation in dB), portal attenuation by door state (open 0 dB, ajar −6 dB, closed −20 dB, configurable per door material), wall transmission for adjacent rooms (−30 dB default, per wall material), floor/ceiling transmission for verticality. Listeners receive perceived level and the perceived position (the last portal the sound came through when routed indirectly).

## Scope
- In: Room/portal graph build from level data
- In: Propagation (Dijkstra over portals, bounded)
- In: Perceived position routing
- In: Event bus API for emitters (footsteps, impacts, shouts, spells)
- In: Hook for e28-audio-engine to reuse the occlusion result
- Out: Footstep emission rules (e09-footstep-noise)
- Out: Actual audio playback (e28-audio-engine)

## Notes
Perceived position is what makes the no-omniscience rule hold for sound. Bounded search: stop when level < global floor (10 dB).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 60 dB noise and a listener 10 m away in the same room, when propagated, then perceived level is 40 dB ± 0.5 (−20 dB for 10 m).
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same geometry with a closed door on the only path, when propagated, then perceived level is 20 dB lower than with the door open.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a noise in room A heard in room B via a doorway, when propagated, then the perceived position is the doorway, not the source.
- AC-4 [unit] Given two paths (open corridor 25 m, closed door 8 m), when propagated, then the louder of the two routes is used.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a noise on the floor above through a wooden floor (−15 dB), when propagated to a listener below, then perceived level reflects the floor transmission loss.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a door that changes from open to closed between two noise events, when the second event propagates, then it uses the new door state (graph edges update on door events).
- AC-7 [unit] Given a noise emitted outside any room (open terrain), when propagated, then pure distance attenuation applies without error.
- AC-8 [perf] Given 20 noise events per tick in a 60-room level, when propagated, then cost p95 ≤ 0.5 ms per tick.

title: Compute player visibility from light, stance, motion and distance
description:
## Why
Stealth cannot be crouching plus an eye icon. Visibility must emerge from light and darkness, stance, movement and distance so players can reason about it.

## What
As a thief, I want how visible I am to depend on the light on my body, my stance, how fast I move and what I wear so that shadows and patience are my tools. `visibility(target, observer)` = lightTerm (light-field sample at target sample points, adjusted by observer dark-vision) × stanceTerm (prone/crouch/stand) × motionTerm (speed band) × profileTerm (equipment brightness, disguise/cloak modifiers) × LOS fraction × distance falloff. A per-target self-visibility (observer-independent) is also exposed for the HUD.

## Scope
- In: Pure function + components, all weights from tuning data
- In: Self-visibility for UI
- In: Contrast rule: a silhouette against a bright background raises visibility
- Out: Sight cone / accumulation (E11)
- Out: Light-field implementation (e03-light-field)

## Notes
Terms multiply so any zero term hides the target. Keep the function pure: inputs are sampled values, not entity lookups, for trivial unit testing.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given light level 0.05 at all sample points, crouched and still at 10 m, when computed with default tuning, then visibility ≤ 0.1.
- AC-2 [unit] Given light level 0.9, standing and sprinting at 10 m, when computed, then visibility ≥ 0.8.
- AC-3 [unit] Given identical inputs except distance 5 m vs 20 m, when computed, then the 20 m result is strictly lower per the falloff curve.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an observer with dark-vision 1.0, when the target stands in 0.0 light, then the light term is 1.0 (darkness gives no benefit).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a dark target silhouetted against a background light ≥ 0.7 along the observer ray, when computed, then the contrast bonus applies and visibility rises by the configured amount.
- AC-6 [unit] Given LOS fraction 0, when computed, then visibility is exactly 0 regardless of other terms.
- AC-7 [content] Given the stealth tuning file, when a weight is outside 0–2, then validation fails.

title: Multi-point line-of-sight queries with partial cover and see-through
description:
## Why
Hiding behind a crate with your head poking out should be different from full cover; windows and grates should let guards see but not pass.

## What
A sim LOS service: raycast from the observer’s eye to N sample points on the target (head, chest, hips, feet — configurable) returning fraction visible 0–1. Colliders carry an `occlusion` property: `opaque`, `transparent` (glass, grates), `partial:<factor>` (foliage, curtains, smoke volumes). Queries go through a physics adapter with a pure-TS fake for unit tests.

## Scope
- In: LOS service, sample points, occlusion properties, adapter + fake
- In: Dynamic occluders (smoke volumes, closing doors)
- Out: Visibility score composition (e09-visibility-model)
- Out: Sight cone logic (e11-perception)

## Notes
Smoke and foliage are volumes; their factor multiplies along the ray. Batch API for many observers per tick.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a target fully behind an `opaque` wall, when queried, then visible fraction is 0.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a target crouched behind a crate that hides hips and feet only, when queried with 4 sample points, then visible fraction is 0.5.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a target behind a `transparent` window, when queried, then visible fraction equals the unobstructed value.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a ray through two `partial:0.5` foliage volumes, when queried, then the per-ray visibility is 0.25.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a zero-length ray (observer eye inside target), when queried, then visible fraction is 1 and no error is thrown.
- AC-6 [perf] Given 24 observers × 4 samples, when batched, then the query cost p95 ≤ 0.3 ms per tick on the reference machine.

title: AI debug overlay: sight cones, hearing, states, LKP and paths
description:
## Why
AI is untuneable if you cannot see what it thinks. Developers need to see every agent’s senses, state and memory live.

## What
As a developer, I want a toggleable AI overlay so that I can understand and tune behaviour in seconds. Per agent: sight cone (primary/peripheral, tinted by alert state), hearing radius, awareness bars per source, state label + time in state, active behaviour node / top utility scores, LKP marker with confidence, current path, claimed search points. Global: noise event rings with loudness and propagation route, light level probe under cursor. Console: `ai.debug on|off|select <id>`, `ai.freeze`, `ai.step`.

## Scope
- In: Overlay rendering from sim introspection data
- In: Console commands incl. freeze/step
- In: Selection by clicking an agent
- Out: Player-facing stealth UI (E09 UI items)
- Out: Visual behaviour editor (post-MVP)

## Notes
Render layer reads introspection snapshots; sim must not depend on overlay. Overlay code excluded from unit coverage per coverage-exclusions.md; introspection data builders are 100% covered in sim.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an agent, when the introspection snapshot is built, then it contains state, timeInState, awareness per source, LKP, path and cone parameters.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the grey-box testbed with 3 guards, when `ai.debug on` is entered, then overlay elements for 3 agents render with no console errors.
- AC-3 [integration] Given `ai.freeze`, when 60 frames render, then the sim tick counter does not advance; `ai.step` advances exactly 1 tick.
- AC-4 [perf] Given the overlay on with 24 agents, when measured, then added frame time p95 ≤ 2 ms on the reference machine (High).
- AC-5 [unit] Given the overlay is off, when the sim runs, then no introspection snapshots are built (zero overhead check via counter).

title: Combat behaviour: engage, space, select attacks and share targets
description:
## Why
Combat is intrinsically fun only if enemies fight readably: spacing, telegraphing, taking turns and punishing mistakes.

## What
As a knight, I want enemies to circle, pressure and take turns so that fights reward reading behaviour. In Combat: maintain preferred range per creature, strafe/circle, pick attacks from `attacks` by preconditions + weights + personality aggression, respect an attack token budget per target (max N simultaneous attackers, default 2), react to player block/parry (stagger response), reposition when target is out of reach (path/wait/ranged fallback).

## Scope
- In: Engage/space/attack-select loop
- In: Attack token manager
- In: Out-of-reach handling (e.g. player on ledge)
- Out: Retreat/flee (e11-retreat-flee)
- Out: Boss-specific patterns (E13/E26)

## Notes
All selection deterministic with seeded RNG. Losing the target transitions via alert states to Searching.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 4 hostile guards in Combat vs one player with token budget 2, when simulated for 10 s, then at no tick are more than 2 guards in an attack windup/active phase.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an attack whose precondition (distance ≤ 2 m) is false, when selecting, then it is never chosen.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player stands on a ledge unreachable by nav, when a melee-only guard is in Combat, then it moves to the closest point, waits and after 8 s transitions to a taunt/wait behaviour rather than jittering (≤ 1 path request per second).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the grey-box fight room, when the player fights 2 fixture guards, then both guards attack at least once within 10 s and the fight resolves without AI errors.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a guard is staggered, when the stagger ends, then it re-evaluates attack selection rather than resuming the cancelled attack.

title: Patrol routes, guard posts and idle routines authored as data
description:
## Why
Believable routines are what a thief observes, times and exploits; they are also where guards return after an alert.

## What
As a designer, I want to author patrol routes and posts in level data so that guards have readable, exploitable routines. Route types: loop, ping-pong, random-weighted graph; waypoints with dwell time, look-direction, and optional idle action (lean, warm hands at fire, check door). Posts: stationary with scan arcs. Routines can be scheduled by time windows. Agents remember their routine and resume the nearest sensible waypoint after an alert.

## Scope
- In: Route/post schema in level data, runtime behaviour
- In: Idle action hooks as cue ids
- In: Resume-nearest-waypoint logic
- Out: Day/night schedules beyond simple windows (Related: world clock)
- Out: Animation assets (placeholder cues only)

## Notes
Random-weighted routes use seeded RNG per agent.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a loop route A→B→C with 2 s dwell at each, when simulated, then the guard visits A, B, C, A in order with dwell ±1 tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a ping-pong route, when the guard reaches the last waypoint, then it reverses direction.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a guard returning from Searching, when it resumes, then it paths to the nearest waypoint on its route by nav distance, not the next index.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a route waypoint that becomes unreachable (door locked), when the guard attempts it, then it skips to the next reachable waypoint and emits a `RouteBlocked` event (door-check anomaly hook).
- AC-5 [content] Given a route referencing a nonexistent waypoint id, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Target memory and last-known position without omniscience
description:
## Why
Enemies must not magically know the player’s position after losing sight. Last-known position is what lets players slip away, double back and set up ambushes.

## What
As a thief, I want guards to hunt where they last saw me, not where I actually am, so that breaking line of sight is meaningful. Agent memory stores per target: LKP, last observed velocity, time last seen, confidence decaying over time, and a bounded prediction (LKP + velocity × min(t, 1.5 s)). Memory updates only from perception stimuli or ally communication. Memories of anomalies (bodies, open doors) persist with timestamps.

## Scope
- In: Memory records, confidence decay, bounded prediction
- In: Update sources: own stimuli, ally reports (tagged second-hand, lower confidence)
- In: Forgetting after configured duration
- Out: Search behaviour choosing where to look (e11-search-behaviour)
- Out: Player-facing LKP ghost (e09-lkp-ghost)

## Notes
Architecture test: memory module has no access to ground-truth transforms. Prediction cap prevents agents tracking the player through walls.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player is last seen at P moving 3 m/s east, when 10 s pass without stimuli, then the predicted position is P + 4.5 m east (capped at 1.5 s) and never updates further.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player, unseen, moves 30 m away, when the guard queries memory, then the returned LKP is unchanged (no leak of true position).
- AC-3 [unit] Given an ally shouts a report of the player at Q, when the listener updates memory, then LKP becomes Q with confidence × 0.7 and source `second-hand`.
- AC-4 [unit] Given confidence decay 0.02/s from 1.0, when 50 s pass, then the memory is forgotten and queries return none.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a scenario where the player breaks LOS around a corner then climbs to a ledge, when the guard arrives at the LKP, then it has no knowledge of the ledge position unless it perceives the player there.

title: Six-state alert machine: Unaware to Combat with timed decay
description:
## Why
The constitution mandates Unaware → Suspicious → Investigating → Searching → Alerted → Combat. Readable states let players understand and manipulate guards.

## What
As a thief, I want guards to escalate and de-escalate through recognisable states so that I can recover from mistakes. A hierarchical state machine per agent: Unaware, Suspicious (stops, looks toward stimulus), Investigating (moves to stimulus position), Searching (lost the target, searches around last-known position), Alerted (knows an intruder exists, active hunt, may raise alarm), Combat (has a confirmed target in perception). Transitions driven by awareness thresholds, timers and events (ally alarm, damage taken). Each state has a data-defined timeout and fallback. De-escalation goes to a `postAlert` flag (heightened baseline) rather than straight to fully relaxed.

## Scope
- In: States, transition table as data, timers, events emitted on every transition
- In: Damage-from-unseen-source → Alerted (not Combat) since the attacker is unknown
- In: Heightened baseline after de-escalation (faster accumulation)
- Out: Behaviours inside states (investigate/search/combat items)
- Out: Group communication (e11-communication)

## Notes
Transition table example lives in tuning data. Combat → Searching when target lost for > N s; Searching → Unaware(postAlert) after search timeout. Never Combat → Unaware directly.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an Unaware guard, when awareness crosses 0.3, then it enters Suspicious and emits `AlertStateChanged{from: Unaware, to: Suspicious, cause}`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a Suspicious guard, when no stimulus is received for 6 s, then it returns to Unaware with `postAlert=false` and resumes its routine.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a guard in Combat, when the target leaves perception for 5 s, then it enters Searching (never Unaware directly) with the target’s last observed position as LKP.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a Searching guard, when the search timeout (60 s default) elapses without re-acquisition, then it enters Unaware with `postAlert=true` and awareness accumulation rate ×1.5 for 300 s.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an Unaware guard hit by a projectile from an unperceived source, when damage is applied, then it enters Alerted (not Combat) and the LKP is estimated from the projectile direction, not the shooter position.
- AC-6 [unit] Given the transition table, when fuzzed with 10,000 random event sequences, then no transition ever occurs that is absent from the table and state is always one of the six.
- AC-7 [content] Given a tuning file with a timeout ≤ 0, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Accumulate and decay awareness from stimuli per perceived target
description:
## Why
Detection should build gradually so players have time to react; a glimpse at the edge of vision is not the same as walking into a torch-lit room.

## What
Per agent, per perceived source: awareness 0–1 accumulated each think as `strength × senseRate × traitModifiers × dt`, with decay when unstimulated after a grace period. Thresholds from tuning data (e.g. 0.3 Suspicious, 0.6 Investigating, 1.0 Detected) drive alert transitions. Tracks the stimulus that contributed most, used by UI to explain why the player was noticed.

## Scope
- In: Accumulation/decay curves
- In: Per-source records with dominant-cause tracking
- In: Instant-detection rule for very close contact (touch/bump)
- Out: State machine (e11-alert-states)
- Out: UI (e09-awareness-indicators)

## Notes
Curves and thresholds come from e11-ai-tuning-data; this item ships defaults.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a constant sight stimulus of strength 1.0 and rate 1.0/s, when 0.6 s passes, then awareness is 0.6 ± 0.01.
- AC-2 [unit] Given awareness 0.5 and no stimuli, when grace 2 s then decay 0.1/s applies, then awareness is 0.5 at t=2 s and 0.3 at t=4 s.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player bumps into an Unaware guard, when contact is registered, then awareness jumps to 1.0 immediately regardless of light.
- AC-4 [unit] Given sight and hearing stimuli in the same think, when accumulated, then the dominant cause recorded is the one with the larger contribution.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a source that despawns, when the next think runs, then its awareness record is removed without error.

title: Creature perception: sight cones, hearing and special senses
description:
## Why
Enemies must perceive the world honestly — through senses that the player can understand, predict and exploit — rather than knowing everything.

## What
As a thief, I want enemies to only know what their senses tell them so that darkness, silence and cover genuinely protect me. Each agent evaluates senses from its resolved sense profile: sight (cone test with primary/peripheral zones, vertical limit, range falloff, LOS via e09-line-of-sight, target visibility score via e09-visibility-model, dark-vision factor), hearing (receives noise events from e09-sound-propagation above its threshold), smell/special senses via registered channel handlers. Output is a list of typed stimuli {source, kind, position, strength 0–1, certainty} per think, fed to awareness.

## Scope
- In: Sight, hearing, special-sense channel registry
- In: Stimulus types: seen-target, heard-noise, seen-anomaly, sensed-life
- In: Time-slicing so expensive LOS checks respect a budget
- Out: Awareness accumulation (e11-awareness-accumulation)
- Out: Alert state logic (e11-alert-states)
- Out: Anomaly definitions (e09-anomaly-detection)

## Notes
Perception never reads the player position directly outside senses — enforced by an API boundary (agents receive only stimuli). This is the no-omniscience guarantee.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a guard with primary half-angle 35° and range 20 m, when a fully visible target stands at 10 m and 20° off-axis, then a seen-target stimulus is produced with strength > 0.5.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same target at 10 m and 120° off-axis (outside peripheral), when evaluated, then no sight stimulus is produced.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a target in the cone but with LOS fully blocked, when evaluated, then no sight stimulus is produced.
