- AC-4 [unit] Given a target in the cone with visibility score 0.1 (deep shadow, crouched), when evaluated at 15 m, then stimulus strength is below the Suspicious contribution threshold per tuning data.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a noise event of 45 dB at the listener and threshold 30 dB, when evaluated, then a heard-noise stimulus carries the noise’s propagated position, not the true source if the noise was occluded and routed through a doorway.
- AC-6 [unit] Given the perception API, when an agent attempts to access the player entity transform outside a stimulus, then the type system disallows it (compile-time) and an architecture test asserts no such import exists.
- AC-7 [perf] Given 24 agents and 1 target, when perception runs at 10 Hz, then sim perception cost p95 ≤ 0.8 ms per tick on the reference machine.
notes: 2026-10-02: PR #140 (mw-e11.3) ships stand-in senses in src/sim/testing/senses.ts behind the swappable deps.senses port (sight cone/range/light/crouch/LOS, hearing threshold/falloff). Real perception must plug into that port and the scenario harness tests should then run against it; delete the stand-in once replaced.

title: Navmesh generation and deterministic pathfinding for creatures
description:
## Why
Patrol, investigate, search, flee and flank all need reliable paths, including doors, ladders and climb links that make verticality matter.

## What
Navmesh baked from grey-box and level geometry at content build time (Recast-style tool or chosen library, decided within this item), stored as data. Sim-side A* over the navmesh with per-creature capability masks (from e12-locomotion-types), dynamic obstacles (closed/locked doors toggling links), off-mesh links (ladders, jumps, climb). Path smoothing and a request queue with a per-tick budget.

## Scope
- In: Bake step + data format
- In: Pathfinding in sim, deterministic
- In: Door state integration, off-mesh links
- In: Local steering/avoidance between agents (simple)
- Out: Flying 3D navigation beyond height-offset flight (post-MVP)
- Out: Crowd simulation

## Notes
If a WASM library is used, the query layer must still be deterministic and wrapped behind a sim interface with a pure-TS fake for unit tests. Related: level geometry format from E00 greybox kit.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a baked grey-box navmesh, when a path is requested between two connected points, then the returned path is valid (every segment on-mesh) and identical across runs.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a closed locked door between two rooms, when a walker requests a path through it, then no path through that door is returned; after `unlock + open`, the path is found.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a climb link, when a walk-only creature and a climber request the same path, then only the climber’s path uses the link.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unreachable target, when requested, then the result is `Unreachable` with the closest reachable point, not an exception.
- AC-5 [perf] Given 30 path requests in one tick, when the budget is 0.5 ms, then excess requests are deferred to later ticks and all complete within 10 ticks.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the grey-box testbed, when the bake runs, then a navmesh file is produced in ≤ 10 s and content validation passes.
notes: Decision: docs/adr/0006-navmesh-and-pathfinding.md (pure-TS bake + query in src/sim/nav; recast-navigation-js rejected for now). Follow-ups: mw-e11.20 (navmesh per agent size class), mw-e11.21 (run creature AI on the scene navmesh in the game loop).
close_reason: Completed in PR #162 (ADR-0006 proposed; awaiting owner acceptance)

title: Scenario harness for scripted AI tests with asserted states over time
description:
## Why
Stealth and AI rules must be trustworthy without reading code; readable, deterministic scenario tests are how we prove guard behaviour.

## What
A test DSL in `src/sim/testing/scenario.ts`: load a grey-box layout (JSON), spawn fixtures with routes, script a player path (waypoints, stance, speed, actions like `throw`, `extinguish`), and assert over time (`at(12.0).expect(guard1).state("Investigating")`, `during(0, 5).expect(guard1).notState("Combat")`). Runs headless on the replay harness; failures print a timeline of state changes and stimuli.

## Scope
- In: DSL, headless runner, failure timeline output
- In: Snapshot hash recording for regression
- In: Example scenario using fixture-guard
- Out: The scenario suite itself (e09-infiltration-scenarios)
- Out: Browser e2e (Playwright)

## Notes
Built on e00-replay-harness; scripted player drives the same input actions as a real player where possible.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a scenario asserting `state("Suspicious")` at t=3.0 s, when the guard is actually Unaware at 3.0 s, then the test fails and output lists every state transition with timestamps.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a scenario, when run twice, then the recorded state hash sequence is identical.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the example scenario (player walks through guard view in light), when run, then the guard transitions Unaware→Suspicious within 1.5 s and the test passes.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a layout JSON referencing an unknown fixture id, when the scenario loads, then it fails before ticking with a clear error.
- AC-5 [perf] Given a 120 s scenario with 6 agents, when run headless in CI, then it completes in ≤ 3 s wall time.

title: Implement the deterministic behaviour runtime chosen by the ADR
description:
## Why
A single, deterministic behaviour runtime lets all creatures share patrol/investigate/search/combat behaviours authored as data.

## What
Production implementation of the ADR architecture in `src/sim/ai/`: behaviour definitions loaded as content (`behaviour:*`), per-agent blackboard (typed keys), action primitives (move-to, look-at, wait, play-cue, emit-noise, attack), condition primitives (state, stimulus, timer, trait), time-slicing so each agent thinks at a configurable rate (default 10 Hz) with deterministic ordering by entity id.

## Scope
- In: Runtime, primitives, blackboard, behaviour schema + loader
- In: Deterministic scheduler with think budgets
- In: Introspection API for debug visualisation
- Out: Individual behaviours (later E11 items)
- Out: Visual editor (post-MVP, E33)

## Notes
Actions return Running/Success/Failure (or utility equivalents); all timing uses sim ticks. Introspection returns current node/score table per agent.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given two agents with think rate 10 Hz on a 60 Hz sim, when 60 ticks run, then each agent thinks exactly 10 times and their think ticks are staggered deterministically by entity id.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a behaviour definition referencing an unknown primitive, when loaded, then loading fails with the behaviour id and primitive name.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an action that fails (move-to unreachable), when the runtime ticks, then the failure propagates per the ADR semantics and a fallback branch runs.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an agent is despawned mid-action, when the runtime ticks, then no further callbacks run for it and no exception is thrown.
- AC-5 [perf] Given 50 agents running a patrol behaviour, when the sim runs headless, then AI think cost p95 ≤ 1.0 ms per tick on the reference machine.
- AC-6 [unit] Given an agent, when introspected, then it returns the active node path (or top-3 utility scores) as serialisable data.

title: Spike: choose AI architecture (utility AI, behaviour trees, HFSM)
description:
## Why
Every enemy behaviour sits on this choice. It must be deterministic, data-driven, debuggable and cheap enough for 24+ agents in a browser.

## What
Time-box 2 days. Question: which decision architecture (utility AI, behaviour trees, hierarchical FSM, or hybrid — e.g. HFSM for the 6 alert states with utility selection inside states) best fits deterministic sim, data authoring, debug visualisation and the alert state machine? Build the same scenario (patrol → hear noise → investigate → return) in two candidates inside `spikes/ai-architecture/`, measure tick cost and authoring effort, write an ADR.

## Scope
- In: Two prototype implementations in `spikes/`
- In: Micro-benchmark: 50 agents, cost per tick
- In: ADR `docs/adr/NNNN-ai-architecture.md` with recommendation and data format sketch
- Out: Production runtime (e11-behaviour-runtime)
- Out: Navigation (e11-navigation)

## Notes
Evaluation criteria: determinism (no hidden time/random), data-authorability (JSON), debuggability (current node/scores visualisable), perf, testability at 100% coverage, fit with personality traits and needs as utility inputs.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the spike is complete, when the ADR is reviewed, then it records the decision, at least 2 rejected alternatives with reasons and the measured numbers.
- AC-2 [perf] Given each prototype, when 50 agents run the scenario headless for 60 s, then per-tick cost is recorded (mean and p95) in the ADR.
- AC-3 [unit] Given each prototype, when the scenario replays twice with the same seed, then the agent state hash sequences are identical.
- AC-4 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it includes a JSON sketch of a behaviour definition for `fixture-guard` in the chosen format.
notes: ADR: docs/adr/0005-ai-architecture.md (HFSM alert states + utility inside states). Prototypes: spikes/ai-architecture/.

title: Persist creature runtime state across save and load
description:
## Why
Failure creates stories only if consequences persist: a guard who is searching, a befriended hound or a knocked-out patrol must survive a reload.

## What
A creature state serializer covering position/facing, health, alert state + timers, memory (last-known positions), morale, needs, disposition, current behaviour node/intent, carried inventory changes (pickpocketed items), and status (`alive`, `unconscious`, `dead`, `befriended`). Integrates with the versioned save format and world state store.

## Scope
- In: Serializer + migration test scaffold
- In: Deterministic resume: a loaded sim continues identically to an unsaved one
- Out: Save UI (E30)
- Out: Global world facts (e27-world-state-store owns them; this item writes creature facts into it)

## Notes
Resume determinism is the key property: save at tick N, load, run to N+M, hash must equal an uninterrupted run.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature in Searching with 12.5 s remaining and an LKP, when saved and loaded, then state, remaining timer and LKP are identical.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a replay of 600 ticks with a save/load at tick 300, when compared with an uninterrupted replay, then sim state hashes at tick 600 are equal.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a save from creature-state schema v1 missing `morale`, when migrated to v2, then morale defaults to 100 and the migration test passes.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unconscious creature, when saved and loaded, then it remains unconscious with its wake timer preserved.
notes: **Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — required by the E01 grey-box vertical slice: a save after the skeleton has leashed home wounded, and the e2e golden hash after death and reload, need creature runtime state in saves (docs/design/vertical-slice.md §6, mw-e01.7 AC-1, mw-e01.9 AC-2).

title: Support walker, climber, flier, swimmer and burrower locomotion data
description:
## Why
Verticality and alternate routes only matter if creatures move differently: a spider on the ceiling, a harpy over a chasm, a hound that cannot climb.

## What
A `LocomotionMode` schema (`walk`, `climb`, `fly`, `swim`, `burrow`, `wallcrawl`) with speeds per gait (sneak/walk/run), step height, jump height, max slope, and nav-area permissions. Creatures list one or more modes; the navigation layer receives a per-creature nav capability mask derived from them.

## Scope
- In: Schema + capability mask derivation
- In: Gait speeds used by patrol/investigate/combat
- In: Area-cost multipliers (e.g. swimmer prefers water)
- Out: Navmesh generation itself (e11-navigation)
- Out: Flight physics beyond kinematic movement (post-MVP)

## Notes
Mask is a bitfield so nav queries stay cheap. Mode transitions (walk→climb) are nav link types.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature with only `walk`, when its capability mask is derived, then `climb`, `fly` and `swim` bits are 0.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature with `walk` and `climb`, when the mask is derived, then climb-only nav links are traversable for it and not for a walk-only creature.
- AC-3 [content] Given a locomotion entry with `run` speed lower than `walk` speed, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature with no locomotion modes, when validated, then validation fails (every creature must move or declare `stationary`).

title: Data-driven creature attack definitions bound to the damage model
description:
## Why
Combat is intrinsically fun only when attacks are readable and varied; creatures need telegraphed, data-defined attacks that behave consistently with player combat.

## What
An `AttackDef` schema: id, kind (`melee` | `projectile` | `area` | `grab` | `special`), range min/max m, windup/active/recovery frames, telegraph cue id, hitbox shape ref, damage packets (type + amount + poise), cooldown s, selection weight, preconditions (distance, target stance, own health band). A sim executor runs an attack’s phases and emits hitbox activations to the damage model.

## Scope
- In: Schema + executor for melee and projectile kinds
- In: Telegraph events for render/audio to consume
- In: Preconditions evaluated deterministically
- Out: Choosing which attack to use (e11-combat-behaviour)
- Out: Grab/special runtime beyond a stub event (post-MVP or bestiary items)

## Notes
Frame counts are in fixed sim ticks. Telegraph cues are string ids so placeholder sfx/vfx can be swapped later.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a melee attack with windup 12, active 4, recovery 10 ticks, when executed, then the hitbox is active exactly on ticks 13–16 and the attack completes on tick 26.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an attack executing, when the attacker is staggered during windup, then the attack is cancelled and no hitbox activates.
- AC-3 [content] Given an attack with `range.min` > `range.max`, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a telegraph cue id, when windup starts, then exactly one `AttackTelegraph` event is emitted on the event bus with the attacker id and cue id.
- AC-5 [integration] Given `fixture-guard` attacking a player hurtbox in range, when the active window overlaps, then the damage model receives one damage packet per packet definition.

title: Spawn data-defined creatures into the sim and grey-box scenes
description:
## Why
Designers and tests must be able to put any creature into the world from data alone, fast.

## What
As a designer, I want to spawn any creature by id at a position (from level data, debug console or tests) so that I can iterate on encounters without code. The spawner builds the entity/component set from a resolved `CreatureDef` (transform, health, senses, locomotion, behaviour, faction, needs), binds a placeholder capsule render proxy in `src/game`, and supports despawn and respawn. Debug console: `spawn <creatureId> [count] [at-cursor]`, `despawn all`.

## Scope
- In: Sim-side factory (pure) + game-side render binding
- In: Level-data spawn points with optional patrol route and faction override
- In: Console commands
- Out: Spawn waves / encounter director (E26 content)
- Out: Final meshes (asset integration beads)

## Notes
Factory must be deterministic: entity ids allocated from the sim entity store, any per-spawn variance from seeded RNG.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given `fixture-guard` and a seed, when spawned twice in fresh sims with the same seed, then both entity component snapshots hash identically.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an unknown creature id, when spawn is requested, then no entity is created and a typed `SpawnError` is returned (sim does not throw).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the grey-box testbed, when `spawn fixture-hound 3` is run in the debug console, then 3 hound entities exist with render proxies within 1 frame.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a spawn point with a faction override, when spawned, then the entity faction equals the override, not the def default.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the grey-box testbed, when a level with 4 spawn points loads, then 4 creatures are visible and the console shows no errors.

title: Author three grey-box creature fixtures for AI and stealth tests
description:
## Why
AI and stealth tests need stable, deliberately boring creatures that are not bestiary content so tuning the real bestiary never breaks rule tests.

## What
Three test-fixture creature defs in `src/content/fixtures/creatures/`: `fixture-guard` (humanoid, sight-dominant, patrols, can communicate), `fixture-hound` (beast, hearing + smell dominant, fast), `fixture-sentinel` (undead, life-sense, never sleeps, ignores darkness). Each uses placeholder capsule meshes and the baseline sense profiles.

## Scope
- In: Fixture data + README explaining that fixtures are frozen for tests
- In: Excluded from shipping content bundles
- Out: Real bestiary creatures (E13)
- Out: Art (capsules only)

## Notes
Changing fixture values requires updating dependent scenario tests; add a header comment saying so.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the three fixture files, when validated against `CreatureDef`, then all pass.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a production content build, when bundled, then no fixture creature id appears in the output manifest.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `fixture-sentinel`, when its resolved senses are inspected, then dark-vision factor is 1.0 and it declares the `life-sense` channel.
- AC-4 [content] Given each fixture, when its content smoke test runs, then it spawns, ticks 600 sim frames without error and despawns.
notes: From mw-e12.2 (PR #48): creature senses can be a profile id, {base, ...overrides} or inline; overrides are only validated when resolved, so fixture tests here should call resolveSenses(creature.senses, content) (src/content/types/sense.ts). The undead profile has a 3 m life-sense for the fixture-sentinel.

title: Add sense profile data: sight cones, hearing, smell, special senses
description:
## Why
Creatures should perceive differently — a spider feels vibration, a wraith senses life, a goblin sees in the dark. Unique senses make stealth a puzzle rather than one global rule.

## What
A `SenseProfile` sub-schema and data files: `sight` (near/far range m, primary and peripheral half-angles, vertical half-angle, dark-vision factor 0–1, detection speed multiplier), `hearing` (sensitivity dB threshold, range cap), `smell` (range m, wind-sensitivity flag, tracks scent trails flag), and extensible `special` senses (`tremor`, `life-sense`, `magic-sense`) each with range and gating properties. Profiles are reusable (`senses: "sense:humanoid-guard"`) and overridable per creature.

## Scope
- In: Sub-schema + validation
- In: Three baseline profiles used by test fixtures: humanoid, beast, undead
- In: Merge semantics for per-creature overrides
- Out: Runtime evaluation of senses (e11-perception)
- Out: Smell trail simulation beyond hooks (post-MVP)

## Notes
Units are metres, degrees and seconds everywhere. Special senses are declared as data with a `channel` name so e11-perception can register handlers without schema changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given a sense profile with `sight.primaryHalfAngle` greater than `sight.peripheralHalfAngle`, when validated, then validation fails with a message naming both fields.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature referencing `sense:humanoid` and overriding `sight.farRange: 30`, when resolved, then far range is 30 and every other sight field equals the base profile.
- AC-3 [content] Given the baseline humanoid profile, when validated, then it defines sight far range between 15 and 30 m and hearing threshold between 20 and 40 dB (documented tuning band).
- AC-4 [content] Given a profile declaring an unknown special sense channel, when validated, then validation fails listing the registered channels.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a profile with negative range values, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Define zod creature schema with senses, locomotion, attacks and needs
description:
## Why
The constitution says enemies are creatures, not target dummies, and creatures must be data-driven. Every AI, stealth and bestiary feature needs one shared, validated creature definition.

## What
A `CreatureDef` zod schema in `src/content/schemas/creature.ts` with typed sections: `id`, `family`, `tags`, `stats` (health, poise, mass, size class), `senses` (ref to sense profile or inline), `locomotion` (list of locomotion modes), `attacks` (list of attack refs), `properties` (world-property tags such as `flammable`, `undead`, `conductive`), `vulnerabilities`/`resistances`, `faction`, `disposition` defaults, `fears`, `personality`, `needs`, `behaviour` (behaviour profile id + tuning overrides), `interactions` (non-hostile affordances), `loot` ref, `presentation` (placeholder mesh id, sfx set id). Every section except `id`, `family`, `stats`, `senses`, `locomotion` is optional with documented defaults. A loader registers creatures into the content registry and resolves refs.

## Scope
- In: Schema, TypeScript types inferred from zod, ref resolution, default filling
- In: Clear validation errors naming the file and JSON path
- In: Schema version field for future migrations
- Out: Specific creatures (E13 Bestiary / world-content group)
- Out: Runtime behaviour for each section — later E12/E11 items consume the fields
- Out: Dialogue content (E22/E14)

## Notes
Section sub-schemas are owned by later items (e12-sense-profiles, e12-locomotion-types, e12-attack-definitions, …); this item creates the envelope with stub sub-schemas they extend. Keep refs string-typed (`attack:goblin-slash`) and resolved at load. Related: E13 Bestiary and E14 Social Creatures consume this schema.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given a creature file containing only `id`, `family`, `stats`, `senses` and `locomotion`, when validated, then it passes and all optional sections are filled with the documented defaults.
- AC-2 [content] Given a creature file missing `stats.health`, when validated, then validation fails with an error message containing the file path and `stats.health`.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature referencing `attack:does-not-exist`, when the content registry resolves refs, then loading fails listing every unresolved ref (not just the first).
- AC-4 [unit] Given two creature files with the same `id`, when loaded, then loading fails with a duplicate-id error naming both files.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a valid creature def, when round-tripped through serialize → parse, then the result deep-equals the input.
- AC-6 [content] Given the schema, when `pnpm content:docs` runs, then a field reference table is generated at `docs/content/creature-schema.md` with every field, type and default.

title: Inject a DifficultyConfig of tunable multipliers into the sim
description:
## Why
Combat and stealth rules (P0/m1) must read difficulty/assist multipliers from day one, but the assists UI (e31-difficulty-assists) lands at m3. A tiny config seam avoids a milestone inversion and keeps assists data-driven.

## What
As a developer, I want a typed, immutable DifficultyConfig injected into the sim at world creation so that any rule can read multipliers (damageTaken, damageDealt, detectionSpeed, parryWindow, dodgeWindow, fallDamage, puzzleHints) without knowing about settings or UI.

## Scope
- In: schema with defaults (all 1.0), validation (ranges), injection into sim context, inclusion in state hash + save, change-at-runtime event.
- Out: the assists UI and presets (e31-difficulty-assists), per-system consumption ACs (owned by each consumer).

## Notes
Consumers: e04-damage-model, e04-parry-riposte, e04-dodge-iframes, e04-environmental-damage, e11-awareness-accumulation, e15 hints.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given no overrides, when a world is created, then every multiplier equals 1.0 and the config is frozen.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a multiplier outside its allowed range (e.g. detectionSpeed 0 or 10), when the config is validated, then validation fails with the field name and range.
- AC-3 [unit] Given two worlds differing only in damageTaken, when their state is hashed, then the hashes differ; given identical configs, they match.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a save made with detectionSpeed 0.5, when it is loaded, then the restored sim reads 0.5.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a runtime change event, when applied between ticks, then the new value takes effect on the next tick and is recorded in the replay log so replays stay identical.

title: Consolidate world-property vocabulary assumed by other epics
description:
## Why
Interactions come from properties, never pairings — which only works if every group uses the same property names. Magic, combat, stealth and systems each assumed properties that e03-world-properties does not define, some with conflicting spellings (`soft_anchor` vs camelCase keys).

## What
As a designer, I want every property other systems rely on defined once, with type, range, default and meaning, so that spells, arrows, tools and AI all read the same vocabulary.

Add to the closed, versioned property set (camelCase, matching e03-world-properties):
- `flammable` (explicit boolean alongside ignitionPoint), `flammableGas` (gas type ignites/explodes), `extinguishable` (fire/light source that water, force or interaction can put out)
- `reflective` (confirm semantics for beams), `waterSurface` (liquid top surface; freezable into walkable ice)
- `unstable` (collapses/topples when force or charge exceeds threshold), `suspended` (hangs from a support entity; falls when it breaks/burns/is cut)
- `breakable` + `toughness` per damage type (blunt/slash/pierce/force, joules) alongside `fragile`; `bashable` (shield bash/kick shove/break), `cuttable` (slash/pierce severs), `shootable` (projectile hit emits a signal)
- `softAnchor` (rope arrows embed), `surfaceHardness` (soft/medium/hard: footstep loudness and arrow sticking)
- `chargeActivated` / `lightActivated` (mechanism inputs with thresholds)
- `hidden` (not perceivable/targetable until revealed), `trapped` (links a trap definition; triggers on interaction unless disarmed), `container` (marker linking to the e18 container component), `remains` (skeletal/corpse remains usable by summoning)
- Actor-derived `noiseMultiplier` (product of equipped items' noise multipliers, read by stealth)

Plus query helpers (`breaksUnder(type, energy)`, `isRevealed`, `supportOf`) and a generated docs table.

## Scope
- In: Schema additions, defaults, invariants, query helpers, material preset updates, alias rejection, docs table, save-schema bump with migration fixture
- Out: Behaviour using the properties — owned by consumers (e03-breakables, e03-ropes-supports, e05-arrow-schema, e10-trap-disarm, e08 spells…)
- Out: Container inventory logic — see e18-containers

## Notes
Sources: magic (reflective, unstable, remains, container, water-surface, flammable-gas, charge-activated, light-activated, hidden, trapped), combat (breakable+toughness, shootable, cuttable, bashable, soft_anchor, surface hardness, armor noiseMultiplier), core/stealth (extinguishable, suspended, fragile). e18-containers (P0/m1) must not wait on this item: it keeps its own container component and this item only adds the marker/alias.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the property schema, when validated, then every property listed in this bead exists with type, range, default and doc string, and the generated docs table lists each one.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an entity with breakable toughness {blunt: 200 J, slash: 800 J}, when breaksUnder is queried for a 300 J blunt hit and a 300 J slash hit, then only the blunt hit returns true.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an entity with hidden=true, when perception and interaction-targeting queries run, then it is excluded until a reveal clears the flag, and the reveal emits exactly one propertyChanged event.
- AC-4 [content] Given content using a non-canonical alias such as `soft_anchor` or `water-surface`, when validated, then validation fails with a message naming the canonical key (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given invalid combinations (suspended without a support reference, trapped without a trap definition, waterSurface on a non-liquid material), when invariants run, then each is reported with the entity id.
- AC-6 [content] Given the material presets, when resolved, then every preset declares surfaceHardness and softAnchor (wood and earth true; stone, iron and glass false).
- AC-7 [unit] Given armour items with noiseMultiplier 1.4 and 1.2 equipped, when actor properties are derived, then the actor noiseMultiplier is 1.68, clamped to 0.2–3.0.
notes: From mw-e03.1 (PR #41): the property set is closed and versioned (WORLD_PROPERTY_KEYS, WORLD_PROPERTIES_VERSION = 1 in src/sim/properties/spec.ts); extending it means bumping the version and updating the cross-layer contract test tests/contracts/world-properties.test.ts.

title: Build HUD/menu UI layer, component kit, focus nav and UI test harness
description:
## Why
Every group has HUD and menu work (vitals, inventory, containers, death screen, class select, dialogue, spell hotbar, stealth HUD) and nobody owned the layer underneath. Without one kit, each screen reinvents focus handling, input capture and text scaling, and accessibility becomes a retrofit.

## What
As a developer, I want one UI layer with a screen stack, reusable components, keyboard/gamepad focus navigation and test helpers so that every HUD element and menu is consistent, accessible and cheap to build.

- **Layer & screen stack:** `src/ui` renders DOM UI over the canvas (unless the engine ADR mandates engine UI). A HUD layer (non-focusable, pointer-through) plus a menu stack: push/pop screens and modals; each screen declares `pausesSim` and `capturesInput`. While a capturing screen is open, gameplay action frames are suppressed and (if `pausesSim`) the loop bridge pauses the sim.
- **Component kit:** button, list/grid (virtualised), tabs, toggle, slider, select, meter/bar (with delayed-damage segment), icon slot with count/cooldown, tooltip, toast, modal confirm, key-glyph prompt. Themed only through CSS custom-property tokens that follow the style bible's UI section.
- **Focus & navigation:** focus manager with spatial navigation, focus trap inside modals, focus restore on pop, visible focus ring. UI navigation reads keyboard and the Gamepad API through a small UI input adapter (`ui.up/down/left/right/confirm/back/tabPrev/tabNext`), so it does not depend on gameplay remapping; key glyphs are resolved later from e02-input-actions bindings.
- **Scaling & comfort hooks:** `--ui-text-scale` (0.8–2.0) and `prefers-reduced-motion`/setting hooks consumed by e31-text-scaling and e31-motion-comfort.
- **HUD binding:** HUD widgets read an immutable view model derived from sim snapshots after each tick; they never mutate sim state (commands go through action frames). Dirty-checking avoids DOM writes when nothing changed.
- **Test harness:** component tests (Vitest + DOM environment) and Playwright helpers: `openScreen`, `navigate(path)`, text-overflow check, axe-core scan; a component gallery screen used by e2e tests.

## Scope
- In: Screen stack, input capture, component kit, focus manager, UI input adapter, tokens, view-model binding pattern, test helpers, component gallery
- Out: Settings store and options screens — see e31-settings-framework (builds on this)
- Out: Per-screen features (inventory, dialogue, shop…) — owned by their epics
- Out: Full accessibility audit and per-menu ARIA coverage — see e31-menu-navigation, e31-accessibility-audit
- Out: Final UI art — see mw-e37 UI assets

## Notes
Overlap resolved: e31-menu-navigation specified a "shared focus manager (spatial navigation)" at m3; the focus manager now lives here at m1, and e31-menu-navigation becomes the audit/ARIA/axe pass over every screen. Must not depend on e02-input-actions or e31-settings-framework (both build on top of it; avoiding a cycle).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the HUD plus an open inventory modal that captures input, when `ui.back` (Esc / gamepad B) is pressed, then the modal pops, focus returns to the element focused before it opened, and gameplay input capture is released on the same frame.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a screen with `pausesSim: true` open, when gameplay keys are pressed for 60 ticks, then no gameplay action frames are recorded and the sim tick counter does not advance.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the component gallery, when traversed with arrow keys and with an emulated gamepad D-pad, then every interactive component is reachable, the focus ring is visible with contrast ≥ 3:1, and focus never escapes an open modal.
- AC-4 [integration] Given `--ui-text-scale` set to 2.0, when the component gallery renders at 1280×720, then the overflow helper finds no clipped text node.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a HUD bar bound to a view model, when the sim snapshot is unchanged between frames, then zero DOM writes occur; when health changes, the bar updates within one rendered frame.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a gamepad disconnects while a menu item is focused, when input continues from the keyboard, then focus is preserved and no error is thrown (edge).
- AC-7 [e2e] Given the component gallery, when axe-core runs, then there are zero serious or critical violations.
- AC-8 [perf] Given a HUD with health, stamina and 4 quick slots updating every tick, when profiled for 30 s, then UI update cost ≤ 0.5 ms per frame p95 on the reference machine (High).

title: Build layered animation state machine synced to sim timelines
description:
## Why
Combat is intrinsically fun only if what the player sees lines up with what the sim decides: a parry flash on the frame the sword connects, a skeleton's windup that honestly telegraphs its attack. Every character — player, NPC, creature — needs one shared animation runtime that never becomes a second source of truth.

## What
As a developer, I want one data-driven animation runtime for every rig so that the player, NPCs and creatures animate from sim state and events without animation ever deciding gameplay.

- **State machine + blending:** per-rig state graphs in content data (zod-validated): states, blend trees (1D/2D by sim-published parameters such as speed and turn rate), transitions with crossfade durations and conditions on sim state. Layers: base locomotion, upper-body/action (masked), additive hit-react. Humanoid and non-humanoid rigs use the same runtime with different graphs.
- **Root motion policy:** the sim is authoritative for position. Clips are played in place and the renderer never moves an entity's transform from animation. Root translation found in source clips is extracted as a velocity curve for tuning reference only (matches e37-animation-pipeline AC-5).
- **Animation events:** gameplay-relevant timing (footsteps from stride distance, hit/active frames from e04 move data, release/cast frames) is emitted by the **sim**. Clip markers (`footstep`, `hit`, `release`, `cast`) are for alignment only: the runtime time-warps action clips so the `hit` marker lands on the sim's first active tick, and the content validator reports drift between markers and move data. Render-side hooks (VFX/SFX flourishes) may subscribe to marker callbacks, but sim hooks subscribe only to sim events.
- **Time:** animation follows each entity's sim local time-scale (hit-stop, slow-motion, pause). Distant characters update at a lower rate (LOD).

## Scope
- In: Runtime (src/render/animation), state-graph schema (src/content), sim-parameter binding, crossfades, layers/masks, marker-to-sim alignment and drift validator, animation LOD, dev state probe for tests
- In: One humanoid and one non-humanoid grey-box placeholder rig with idle/move/attack/hit-react clips
- Out: Player locomotion parameter mapping — see e02-animation-hooks (consumes this runtime)
- Out: Clip sourcing, retargeting and manifests — see e37-animation-pipeline
- Out: Move frame data — see e04-move-data-schema
- Out: IK (foot placement, look-at) — post-MVP polish

## Notes
Resolves an inconsistency across groups: e28-footsteps mentions "foot plant events from animation" while e02-animation-hooks produces footsteps from sim stride distance. Per this item the sim event is authoritative; audio may use the clip marker only to fine-align the one-shot within the same rendered frame. Engine-agnostic API; the implementation targets whatever e00-engine-decision picks. Related: creature users e04-creature-attack-hooks, e04-melee-core, e10-takedowns (paired placeholder snaps).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given a state graph with a transition to an unknown state or a clip id missing from the clip manifest, when validated, then validation fails naming the graph file and path (edge).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a 0.2 s crossfade from idle to run, when the blend is sampled at 0.1 s, then weights are 0.5/0.5 ± 0.01 and weights across all layers sum to 1.0 on every sample.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a move whose first active tick is 12 and a clip whose `hit` marker is at 0.40 s, when played at the 60 Hz sim rate, then the clip is time-warped so the marker coincides with tick 12 ± 1 tick; a marker drifting > 1 tick from move data is reported by the content validator.
- AC-4 [integration] Given an entity whose sim local time-scale is 0 for 4 ticks (hit-stop), when rendered, then its pose holds for those ticks and resumes with no pop (max bone rotation delta on resume ≤ 5°).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a clip containing root translation loaded under the in-place policy, when played for 2 s, then the entity transform equals the interpolated sim position on every frame (animation never moves the entity).
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed with one humanoid and one non-humanoid placeholder rig, when each cycles idle → move → attack → hit-react via sim state, then the animation state probe reports each state in order and no console errors occur.
- AC-7 [perf] Given 24 animated characters (those beyond 30 m updated at reduced rate), when running for 30 s, then animation update cost ≤ 1.5 ms per frame p95 on the reference machine (High).

title: Add in-game debug console with commands, cheats and spawners
description:
## Why
Fast content creation and debugging (constitution §10) need a way to poke the running game without editing code.
## What
As a developer, I want a toggleable console with typed commands so that I can spawn, teleport, cheat and inspect instantly.
Backtick toggles an overlay console (dev builds and `?debug=1` on playtest builds); command registry (`registerCommand({name, args schema, run})`) with autocomplete, history (persisted), help. Built-ins: `help`, `spawn <contentId> [count]`, `give <itemId> [n]`, `god`, `noclip`, `kill`, `tp <x y z|bookmark>`, `timescale <n>`, `scene <id>`, `set <setting> <value>`, `seed`. Commands that mutate sim state go through the sim command queue (deterministic, recorded in replays).
## Scope
- In: Console UI, registry, parser with zod arg validation, autocomplete against content ids
- In: Built-in commands
- In: Production stripping (dynamic import behind build flag)
- Out: Entity inspector (e33-entity-inspector)
- Out: Domain-specific commands (each system registers its own)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given `spawn testprop-crate 3`, when executed, then 3 crate entities exist in the sim next tick and the command is present in the replay input log.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `spawn does-not-exist`, when executed, then the console prints "unknown content id" with the 3 closest matches and the sim is unchanged.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `give` with a non-numeric count, when executed, then argument validation fails with usage help.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given a dev build, when backtick is pressed, then the console opens, captures keyboard input (player does not move) and Esc/backtick closes it.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a production build without `?debug=1`, when backtick is pressed, then nothing opens and console modules are absent from the main bundle.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given typing `sp` + Tab, when autocomplete runs, then it completes to `spawn`.

title: Build automated perf budget suite against the hardware baseline
description:
## Why
Performance regressions are cheapest to fix the day they land; budgets make "good browser performance" (constitution §10) enforceable.
## What
A Playwright-based perf suite (`pnpm perf`) with `perf-budgets.json` citing the contract baseline: frame time p50/p95 per scene and preset, time to first frame / playable, initial transfer size, JS heap after N minutes, long tasks count. Two execution modes:
  1. **CI mode** (GPU-less runners): enforces deterministic-ish budgets — transfer size, bundle size, heap, load time under network throttling (50 Mbps), long tasks > 200 ms, and relative regression of software-rendered frame time vs main (± 15%) as a warning.
  2. **Reference mode** (`pnpm perf:ref`, manual on the M1 Pro reference machine): enforces absolute frame-time budgets and writes `perf/results/<date>-<sha>.json`; committed results feed the trend chart.
Includes a baseline stress scene in the greybox kit (N moving physics props + lights).
## Scope
- In: Perf harness (frame-time sampling via rAF + PerformanceObserver long tasks, CDP heap), budget file, reporters (JSON + job summary)
- In: CI job `perf-budget`
- In: Baseline stress scene `perf-baseline`
- Out: Creature/combat stress scene (e32-combat-stress-scene)
- Out: Cross-browser runs (e32-browser-matrix)
## Notes
- Budget numbers come only from backlog-contract §1 Hardware baseline; stories cite them rather than inventing new ones.
- Frame-time sampling excludes the first 3 s (warm-up) and uses ≥ 1,800 frames.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the `perf-baseline` scene in reference mode on the reference machine (High, 1440p-equivalent), when measured over 1,800 frames, then p95 frame time ≤ 16.7 ms or the run fails with a per-metric report.
- AC-2 [integration] Given CI mode, when initial transfer size exceeds 50 MB or throttled load-to-playable exceeds 10 s, then `perf-budget` fails naming the metric and delta vs budget.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a samples array, when percentiles are computed, then p50/p95/p99 match a committed reference implementation, and fewer than 300 samples yields an "insufficient samples" failure rather than a pass.
- AC-4 [integration] Given heap after 5 minutes idle in the testbed exceeds 1.5 GB, when measured, then the suite fails.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a PR whose software-rendered frame time regresses > 15% vs main, when CI runs, then a warning annotation appears (non-blocking).
- AC-6 [unit] Given `perf-budgets.json` with a budget lacking a `source` field citing the baseline, when validated, then it fails.

title: Create typed settings store and options menu skeleton
description:
## Why
Every accessibility and comfort feature needs one place to live, persist and notify systems of change.
## What
Add `src/game/settings`: a zod-typed settings schema with defaults and categories (controls, camera, display, audio, accessibility, gameplay/difficulty), versioned persistence in localStorage (small, sync) with migration, change subscriptions (`settings.on("camera.invertY", cb)`), and "apply immediately" semantics. Options UI skeleton: tabbed categories, generic controls (toggle, slider, select, keybind placeholder), reset category to defaults, keyboard/gamepad navigable.
## Scope
- In: Schema, defaults, persistence + version migration, subscriptions
- In: Options menu shell with generic controls generated from schema metadata (label, help text, range)
- Out: Individual settings features (other e31 items)
- Out: Graphics presets implementation (e32-quality-presets)
## Notes
- Settings are per-browser, not per-save. Difficulty assists are settings too but read by sim via an injected config (never global reads from sim).

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0 — input actions, HUD vitals and inventory UI (all P0/m1) depend on it.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given stored settings with an unknown key and an out-of-range value, when loaded, then the unknown key is dropped, the value is clamped/defaulted and a warning is logged.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a subscriber to `audio.master`, when the value changes, then the callback fires once with the new value; unchanged sets do not fire.
- AC-3 [unit] Given stored settings at schema v1 and code at v2, when loaded, then the migration maps renamed keys and preserves user values.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the options menu, when a toggle is changed and the page reloaded, then the change persists.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given "Reset to defaults" in Camera, when confirmed, then only camera settings reset.
- AC-6 [integration] Given localStorage is unavailable, when the game starts, then defaults are used in-memory and no uncaught error occurs.

title: Build Continue / Load / Save menu screens
description:
## Why
The m1 loop needs saves reachable from the title screen and pause menu.
## What
As a player, I want Continue, Load and Save screens so that I can resume and manage my saves.
Title: Continue (most recent), New Game, Load. Pause: Save, Load. Slot list shows thumbnail + metadata; confirmation dialogs for overwrite/delete; keyboard and gamepad navigable.
## Scope
- In: Title and pause menu save screens
- In: Empty/error states
- Out: Settings screens (e31-settings-framework)
## Notes
- None.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — required by the E01 grey-box vertical slice.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given one or more saves, when the title screen shows, then Continue is focused by default and loads the most recent save.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given no saves, when the title screen shows, then Continue is disabled with an accessible "no saves yet" reason and New Game is focused (reconciled with mw-e01.2 AC-2 and the slice spec, 2026-10-02).
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the slot list, when navigated by keyboard only (arrows/Enter/Esc), then every action (load, save, overwrite confirm, delete confirm) is reachable.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the storage in in-memory fallback mode, when the save screen opens, then the non-persistence warning is visible.
notes: 2026-10-02 from mw-e01.1 (docs/design/vertical-slice.md §6 F3): AC-2 here (Continue hidden with no saves) conflicts with mw-e01.2 AC-2 (Continue disabled with an accessible 'no saves yet' tooltip). The slice spec chooses disabled-with-reason, matching the locked class cards (mw-e01.15); reconcile AC-2 when this is picked up.

title: On death, offer reload of latest save or checkpoint
description:
## Why
The m1 loop requires die → reload; it must be fast so failure invites another try.
## What
As a player, I want a death screen offering "Load last save" (most recent of any slot type) and "Load…" so that I return to play within seconds.
Death screen appears after the death sequence; reload completes to playable in ≤ 3 s warm.
## Scope
- In: Death screen flow, most-recent-save resolution, full world teardown/rebuild on load
- Out: Death conditions and animation (e04-damage-model and E02)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an autosave at t=100 and a manual save at t=120, when resolving "last save", then the manual save is chosen.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the player dies in the testbed, when "Load last save" is chosen, then the game is playable in ≤ 3 s and the sim state hash equals the save's state hash.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given no saves exist at death, when the death screen shows, then it offers "Restart area" instead and does not error.
- AC-4 [integration] Given load of a corrupt latest save, when chosen from death screen, then the recovery flow (e30-corruption-recovery) offers the backup.

title: Autosave on area transitions and checkpoints into a rotating ring
description:
## Why
Failure should create stories, not lost hours; autosaves keep risk fun rather than punishing.
## What
As a player, I want the game to autosave at safe moments so that a crash or death never costs much progress.
Autosave triggers: area transition, checkpoint trigger volumes, after quest state changes, and every 5 minutes of playtime when safe. Never while in combat/alerted state, mid-air, or during dialogue — deferred until safe. Ring of 3 autosave slots, oldest overwritten. Unobtrusive HUD indicator.
## Scope
- In: Autosave scheduler with "safe to save" predicate supplied by systems
- In: Ring buffer slots
- In: HUD indicator hook
- Out: Trigger volume implementation (e03-triggers)
- Out: Alert/combat state source (e11-alert-states)
## Notes
- Safe predicate is a registry so combat/stealth/dialogue can veto without save code knowing them.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 3 autosaves exist, when a 4th autosave occurs, then the oldest is replaced and the other two remain.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an autosave trigger fires while a registered veto (combat) is active, when the veto clears 20 s later, then exactly one autosave occurs at that point.
- AC-3 [unit] Given playtime passes 5 minutes with no other autosave, when safe, then a timed autosave occurs; given another autosave happened 1 minute ago, then the timer resets.
- AC-4 [integration] Given an autosave write fails, when the next safe moment arrives, then it retries once and surfaces a non-blocking HUD warning on second failure.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the testbed with a checkpoint volume, when the player enters it, then an autosave appears in the slot list with the area name.

title: Support manual save slots with metadata and thumbnails
description:
## Why
Players experiment ("what if I anger the minotaur?"); multiple slots make experimentation safe.
## What
As a player, I want several named save slots showing class, location, playtime and a thumbnail so that I can keep parallel playthroughs.
Slot model: 10 manual slots + autosave ring + quicksave; metadata (character name, class, area name, playtime ticks, saved-at, game version, 256×144 WebP thumbnail captured from the canvas). Operations: save, load, overwrite (confirm), delete (confirm), rename.
## Scope
- In: Slot manager in game layer
- In: Thumbnail capture (render-side, excluded-coverage helper)
- Out: Menu UI screens (e30-save-load-ui)
## Notes
- None.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — required by the E01 grey-box vertical slice.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 10 filled manual slots, when the player attempts an 11th new save, then the slot manager requires choosing an overwrite target.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a slot saved with class knight in area "testbed-arena" after 3,600 ticks, when metadata is read, then it reports those values and playtime 60 s.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a thumbnail capture fails (canvas tainted or context lost), when saving, then the save still succeeds with a placeholder thumbnail.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a slot deletion, when confirmed, then the slot and its backup blob are both removed.

title: Gate save-schema changes on committed migration fixtures in CI
description:
## Why
Contract §3: versioned migration tests for every save-schema change; forgetting a migration must be impossible, not merely discouraged.
## What
Commit `test/save-fixtures/<saveSchemaVersion>/*.json` generated from representative worlds. A CI test loads every fixture through the current migration chain and asserts it validates and loads. A schema fingerprint (hash of each section's JSON Schema export) is committed in `save-schema.lock.json`; if a section schema changes without bumping its version and adding a migration + fixture, CI fails with instructions. `pnpm save:fixture` generates a fixture for the current version.
## Scope
- In: Fixture loader test, schema fingerprint lock + check, fixture generator script
- Out: Runtime migration logic (e30-save-serialization)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given fixtures for versions 1..N, when CI runs, then each loads under the current build and yields a world passing invariant checks.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a section schema field added without bumping the section version, when the lock check runs, then it fails naming the section and telling the developer to bump + add migration + fixture.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a version bump without a new fixture directory, when the check runs, then it fails.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a fixture that fails to load, when CI runs, then the failure names fixture path and the migration step that threw.

title: Persist saves to IndexedDB with atomic writes and fallbacks
description:
## Why
Browser storage is fragile (quota, private mode, eviction); saves must survive or fail loudly, never silently.
## What
Add `src/game/save/storage`: a `SaveStore` interface with an IndexedDB implementation (db `mw-saves`, stores `slots`, `blobs`) using single-transaction atomic writes (write new blob + update slot pointer in one transaction, keep previous blob as backup), `navigator.storage.persist()` request on first save, quota estimate, and an in-memory fallback when IndexedDB is unavailable with a visible "saves will not persist" warning.
## Scope
- In: IndexedDB store (idb wrapper or hand-rolled), in-memory store, shared contract tests run against both (fake-indexeddb in Node)
- In: Quota and persist-permission handling
- Out: Slot UX (e30-save-slots)
- Out: Cross-tab locking (e30-multi-tab-guard)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the IndexedDB store, when a save is written then read back, then bytes are identical (contract test runs against both implementations).
- AC-2 [integration] Given a transaction aborted mid-write (simulated), when the slot is read, then the previous save is returned intact.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a QuotaExceededError on write, when saving, then the error surfaces as a typed `SaveQuotaError`, the previous save remains, and the UI can show "free up space".
- AC-4 [e2e] Given IndexedDB throws on open (private-mode simulation), when the game starts, then the in-memory store is used and a persistent warning banner is shown.
- AC-5 [integration] Given `navigator.storage.persist` is unavailable, when first save occurs, then saving proceeds without error.

title: Define versioned save format with section registry and migrations
description:
## Why
Save-game stability is a constitution technical priority; one versioned format with a migration chain prevents "your save is incompatible" after every update.
## What
Add `src/game/save/format` (100% coverage layer): save envelope `{formatVersion, saveSchemaVersion, gameVersion, buildSha, contentHash, createdAtTick, wallClockSavedAt (injected), metadata, sections: Record<sectionId, {version, data}>, checksum}`. Systems register a section (`registerSaveSection({id, version, schema, serialize(world), deserialize(world, data), migrations})`). Serialization reuses the canonical encoder from e00-sim-state-hash; checksum over sections. Migration runner applies per-section migrations in order (vN→vN+1) before zod validation.
## Scope
- In: Envelope schema (zod), section registry, serialize/deserialize whole world
- In: Per-section migration chain + runner
- In: Checksum verification
- In: Round-trip property test: random world → save → load → identical state hash
- Out: Persistence to IndexedDB (e30-indexeddb-storage)
- Out: Fixture-based migration CI harness (e30-migration-fixtures)
- Out: World facts content (e27-world-state-store registers its own section)
## Notes
- Sections allow e17 inventory, e27 world state, e19 progression, e23 quests to own their data without a central god-schema.
- Unknown sections from a newer build are preserved verbatim on re-save (forward-compat) but flagged.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a world with 3 registered sections, when saved and loaded into a fresh world, then the sim state hash equals the original.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a section at data version 1 and code at version 3, when loaded, then migrations 1→2 and 2→3 run in order and the result validates against the v3 schema.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a save whose checksum does not match its sections, when loaded, then a typed `SaveCorruptError` is returned and the world is untouched.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a save containing a section id not registered in this build, when loaded, then load succeeds, a warning lists the unknown section, and re-saving preserves it verbatim.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a missing migration step (v1 data, only 2→3 registered), when loaded, then a typed `MissingMigrationError` names section and versions.
- AC-6 [unit] Given `saveSchemaVersion` newer than the running build supports, when loaded, then it refuses with `SaveFromNewerBuildError` rather than attempting to parse.

title: Create greybox testbed scene, level kit, scene loader and debug camera
description:
## Why
Gameplay is never blocked by art; every system needs a fast place to be tried in-engine from day one.
## What
As a developer, I want a greybox testbed and modular level kit so that I can prototype rooms, corridors and encounters in minutes.
Greybox kit primitives (floor, wall, ramp, stairs, pillar, doorway, platform, crate) with grid snapping and colour-coded materials by purpose (walkable, climbable, interactive, hazard). Scenes are data (`content/scenes/*.json`: placements + entity spawns) loaded by a scene loader into both sim and renderer. Free-fly debug camera (toggle), scene picker via `?scene=` URL param, and a default `testbed` scene (room → corridor → arena).
## Scope
- In: Level kit + scene schema (via e00-content-pipeline)
- In: Scene loader/unloader (sim entities + render objects + physics colliders)
- In: Debug fly camera, `?scene=` param, on-screen scene name + build SHA
- In: Playwright smoke loading each scene in `content/scenes`
- Out: Player controller and gameplay camera (e02-player-controller, e02-camera)
- Out: Debug console (e33-debug-console)
## Notes
- Scenes may be authored by hand in JSON or exported from Blender via glTF extras later; keep the schema simple.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given `?scene=testbed`, when the app loads, then the room→corridor→arena scene renders with zero console errors within 5 s locally.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a scene file, when loaded then unloaded, then the sim world has zero remaining scene entities and the physics world zero colliders.
- AC-3 [content] Given every file in `content/scenes`, when validated, then it passes the scene schema and all referenced kit pieces exist.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given `?scene=does-not-exist`, when loaded, then a visible error lists available scenes and the app does not crash.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the debug camera toggled on, when WASD/mouse input is sent, then the camera moves and toggling off restores the prior camera.
- AC-6 [perf] Given the testbed scene, when measured on the reference machine (High), then p95 frame time ≤ 8 ms (half budget, leaving headroom for gameplay).

title: Bind fixed-step sim to rAF rendering with interpolation
description:
## Why
Smooth visuals at any refresh rate with a deterministic sim underneath is the backbone of "responsive controls feel excellent" (E02).
## What
Add `src/game/loop`: an accumulator-based loop on requestAnimationFrame that advances `World.step` at the fixed rate, caps catch-up steps (spiral-of-death guard), exposes interpolation alpha to render sync, and pauses the sim when the tab is hidden. Render sync reads sim snapshots (read-only view) and updates scene objects. Input sampling produces per-tick command lists (hook for e02-input-actions).
## Scope
- In: Loop, accumulator, max-steps-per-frame cap, pause/resume on visibilitychange
- In: Sim→render sync interface (entity ↔ scene object binding registry)
- In: Injected time source for tests
- Out: Action mapping (e02-input-actions)
- Out: Frame pacing analytics (e32-frame-pacing)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a fake clock advancing 33.3 ms per frame at 60 Hz sim, when 60 frames run, then exactly 120 sim steps occur and alpha stays in [0,1).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a single frame delta of 2,000 ms (debugger pause), when the loop processes it, then at most 5 steps run and the excess time is dropped with a logged warning.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `visibilitychange` to hidden, when 10 s pass and the tab becomes visible, then 0 sim steps ran while hidden and no catch-up burst occurs.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a 144 Hz and a 60 Hz simulated display, when the same inputs run for 600 sim ticks, then final sim state hashes are identical.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an entity destroyed in the sim, when render sync runs, then its bound scene object is disposed within the same frame.

title: Bootstrap the chosen renderer and physics with a boot smoke test
description:
## Why
The ADR decision must become a running, measurable baseline before any visual gameplay work begins.
## What
Install the renderer and physics chosen in ADR-0001; add `src/render/bootstrap` creating canvas, renderer, scene, camera, resize/DPR handling (render scale setting hook) and a clear teardown; lazy-load the physics WASM with a loading state. Playwright smoke: app boots, first frame renders, no console errors, canvas non-blank (pixel sample check), resize works.
## Scope
- In: Renderer + physics bootstrap, dispose(), DPR cap
- In: Unsupported-browser fallback screen (WebGL2/WASM missing) — minimal version
- In: Playwright boot smoke spec with screenshot artifact
- In: coverage-exclusions.md row for render bootstrap
- Out: Full capability detection matrix (e32-capability-detection)
- Out: Greybox content (e00-greybox-testbed)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the built app, when loaded in Chromium, then the first frame renders within 3 s locally, the canvas has non-uniform pixels, and there are zero console errors or warnings from our code.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the viewport resizes from 1280×720 to 1920×1080, when the next frame renders, then canvas drawing-buffer size matches viewport × min(devicePixelRatio, cap).
- AC-3 [e2e] Given WebAssembly is disabled via init script, when the app loads, then a readable "unsupported browser" screen appears instead of a blank page or uncaught error.
- AC-4 [integration] Given `dispose()` is called, when the renderer is recreated 5 times, then WebGL context count does not grow and no errors are logged.

title: Load schema-validated content with a per-entry test harness
description:
## Why
Spells, items, creatures and puzzles are data, not code (constitution §10); designers need fast, safe iteration with errors caught before runtime.
## What
Add `src/content`: a registry of content types, each with a zod schema and a folder under `content/<type>/*.json`; a loader (Vite `import.meta.glob` in the app, fs in Node tests) that validates, reports all errors with file path + JSON path, and freezes results into a typed, id-indexed catalogue. Cross-reference helper (`ref("creature", id)`) validated after load. Content hash over canonical content for replay/save compatibility. Test harness: `describeContent("spell", (entry) => …)` generates one test per entry, and a coverage check fails if any content entry has no exercising test.
## Scope
- In: Registry, loader, error formatting, cross-ref validation, content hash
- In: Example content type `testprop` with 2 entries
- In: Per-entry test generator + "every entry exercised" check
- In: JSON Schema export from zod for editor autocompletion (`content/*.schema.json`)
- Out: Specific schemas (spells e06, creatures e12, items e17, …)
- Out: CLI validator/scaffolder and hot reload (e33-content-validator-cli, e33-content-scaffolder, e33-content-hot-reload)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a content file with a missing required field and a wrong type in two places, when loaded, then all three errors are reported with file path and JSON pointer in one run.
- AC-2 [unit] Given two entries with the same id in different files, when loaded, then loading fails naming both files.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an entry referencing `creature:goblin-archer` that does not exist, when cross-refs validate, then it fails naming source entry and missing target.
- AC-4 [unit] Given unchanged content in a different file order, when the content hash is computed, then it is identical.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a content entry with no test that exercises it, when the content-coverage check runs in CI, then it fails listing the entry id.
- AC-6 [content] Given the example `testprop` entries, when validated, then they pass and the loaded catalogue is deeply frozen.

title: Record inputs and replay them to identical state hashes in tests
description:
## Why
Contract §3 determinism policy: recorded input logs must replay to identical sim state hashes — our strongest regression net for emergent systems.
## What
Add `src/sim/replay`: a replay file format (`{formatVersion, buildSha, contentHash, seed, stepHz, inputs: per-tick command lists (run-length encoded), checkpoints: [{tick, hash}]}`), a recorder that captures commands fed to `World.step`, and a player that re-runs them asserting checkpoint hashes. Vitest helper `expectReplay("replays/foo.json")` and a `pnpm replay:record` dev hook in the game layer. Golden replays live in `test/replays/` and run in CI.
## Scope
- In: Format (zod schema), recorder, player, checkpoint every N ticks (default 60)
- In: Vitest helper + one golden replay against the core sim
- In: Clear failure output using `diffSnapshots` at the first mismatching checkpoint
- Out: Bug-report capture UX (e33-replay-bug-capture)
- Out: Game-layer keyboard/mouse capture (lives with e02-input-actions integration)
## Notes
- Replays record *sim commands* (post input mapping), not raw DOM events, so they survive key remapping.
- When content or sim changes intentionally alter outcomes, `pnpm replay:rebless` regenerates hashes and the diff must be reviewed in the PR.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a recorded 3,600-tick session, when replayed, then every checkpoint hash matches and the final hash equals the recorded final hash.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a sim change that alters one component at tick 1,234, when the golden replay runs, then it fails reporting checkpoint tick 1,260 (first after divergence) and the differing entity/field.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a replay whose `formatVersion` is newer than supported, when loaded, then it fails with a typed `UnsupportedReplayVersion` error.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a replay whose `contentHash` differs from current content, when run, then the harness reports "content changed" distinctly from a determinism failure.
- AC-5 [integration] Given `test/replays/*.json`, when CI runs unit tests, then all golden replays execute and pass.

title: Add canonical sim state serialization and hashing
description:
## Why
Replays, save verification and desync debugging all need one canonical, order-independent fingerprint of sim state.
## What
Add `src/sim/snapshot`: canonical serialization of world state (sorted entity ids, component fields in declared order, floats encoded via their IEEE-754 bits, RNG states, clock) and a fast non-cryptographic hash (e.g. xxHash32/FNV-1a 64) over it. Provide `diffSnapshots(a, b)` returning the first differing entity/component/field for debugging.
## Scope
- In: Canonical encoder, hash, diff utility
- Out: Save file format (e30-save-serialization reuses the encoder)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given two worlds with identical state built via different entity insertion orders but the same ids, when hashed, then the hashes are equal.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a single component float differing by 1 ULP, when hashed, then the hashes differ and `diffSnapshots` names the entity, component and field.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `-0` vs `+0` and two different NaN payloads, when encoded, then the documented canonicalisation rule is applied consistently (NaN canonicalised; ±0 distinct) and tested.
- AC-4 [perf] Given 5,000 entities × 3 components, when hashed in Node, then it completes in ≤ 5 ms.

title: Build deterministic fixed-step sim loop, entity store and event bus
description:
## Why
Every rule of the game (constitution: systemic world, "Wait… I can do that?") lives in one deterministic, testable simulation core.
## What
Add `src/sim/core`: `World` with fixed timestep (default 60 Hz, configurable), ordered system scheduler, entity/component store (typed component definitions, stable integer entity ids, dense storage, queries with deterministic iteration order), deferred entity creation/destruction applied at end of tick, and a typed event bus (events emitted during tick N are delivered in emission order at defined phase boundaries). `step(inputs)` is the only way time advances; inputs are a per-tick command list.
## Scope
- In: World, scheduler, component registry, queries, event bus, command/input queue
- In: Snapshot/restore API hook for components (consumed by state hash and saves)
- In: Micro-benchmarks via `vitest bench`
- Out: Canonical state hashing (e00-sim-state-hash)
- Out: Render interpolation and rAF binding (e00-game-loop-bridge)
- Out: Physics integration (per ADR-0001)
## Notes
- Entity ids are never reused within a session (generation counter) to avoid stale-reference bugs.
- Cross-browser float determinism is not guaranteed for Math.sin/cos/exp; document the policy: determinism target is same build + same engine; gameplay-critical trig goes through `src/sim/math` wrappers so a deterministic implementation can be swapped in.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given systems A, B, C registered in that order, when `step()` runs, then they execute in order A→B→C every tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an entity destroyed by system A during tick N, when system B queries in the same tick, then the entity is still visible, and from tick N+1 it is gone.
- AC-3 [unit] Given two worlds with the same seed and identical input lists for 1,000 ticks, when compared, then their component snapshots are deep-equal.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an event emitted by a handler of another event, when the bus flushes, then the nested event is delivered after the current event in FIFO order and a cycle guard throws after 10,000 events in one flush.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a query for components [Position, Flammable], when entities are added in random order, then iteration order is ascending entity id.
- AC-6 [perf] Given 5,000 entities with 3 components and 10 trivial systems, when `vitest bench` runs in Node on CI, then mean `step()` time is ≤ 1 ms.

title: Implement seeded RNG streams and injected clock for the sim
description:
## Why
Determinism starts with randomness and time being inputs, not ambient globals — required for replays, saves and reproducible bugs.
## What
Add `src/sim/rng`: a fast, serializable PRNG (e.g. PCG32 or xoshiro128**) with named sub-streams (`rng.stream("loot")`) so adding a consumer in one system does not perturb others; helpers (int range, float, chance, pick, shuffle, weighted). Add `src/sim/clock`: a sim clock advanced only by the fixed-step loop (tick count, sim time in ms as integer ticks × step).
## Scope
- In: PRNG with serialize/restore state
- In: Named stream derivation from a root seed (hash of seed + name)
- In: Sim clock type used by all systems
- Out: The loop itself (e00-sim-core)
## Notes
- Avoid Math.* transcendental functions in RNG; use 32-bit integer ops (`Math.imul`, `>>> 0`) which are specified exactly.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given seed 12345, when 1,000 values are drawn from stream "loot", then they equal a committed golden sequence.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a stream whose state is serialized after 500 draws and restored into a new instance, when 500 more draws are made, then they equal the original instance's next 500.
- AC-3 [unit] Given streams "loot" and "ai", when extra draws are added to "ai", then the "loot" sequence is unchanged.
- AC-4 [unit] Given `int(5, 5)` or `pick([])`, when called, then it returns 5 and throws a typed `EmptyChoiceError` respectively.
- AC-5 [unit] Given 1,000,000 `float()` draws, when bucketed into 10 bins, then each bin holds 10% ± 0.5%.

title: Spike: choose Three.js vs Babylon.js and physics engine (ADR-0001)
description:
## Why
The renderer and physics choice shapes every render, animation and physics story; making it on evidence against our hardware baseline avoids a costly mid-project switch.
## What
Time-box: 3 days. Question: which of Three.js + Rapier or Babylon.js + (Rapier | Havok) best serves a stylized third-person action RPG in the browser given our baseline? Build the same benchmark scene in `spikes/engine-three/` and `spikes/engine-babylon/`: greybox dungeon room, 1 skinned glTF character with 3 blended animations + 30 skinned NPCs, 200 dynamic rigid bodies (boxes/barrels) with collisions, 8 dynamic point lights + 1 shadowed directional light, 1 particle emitter, post-processing bloom. Measure on the reference machine (High, 1440p-equivalent) and a low-tier machine if available: p50/p95 frame time, gzip bundle size, time-to-first-frame, JS heap. Evaluate physics determinism: Rapier deterministic build (`@dimforge/rapier3d-deterministic`) snapshot/restore and cross-browser state-hash equality, and whether gameplay physics can live behind the `src/sim` boundary. Also score TS ergonomics, glTF/animation retargeting, inspector/debug tooling, WebGPU path, docs/community, licence.
## Scope
- In: Two spike prototypes (not production code), scripted benchmark harness, results table
- In: docs/adr/0001-engine-and-physics.md with weighted scorecard, decision, consequences, rejected option and revisit triggers
- In: docs/adr/README.md + ADR template (first ADR)
- Out: Production renderer bootstrap (e00-render-bootstrap)
- Out: 3D asset sourcing pipeline (e37-3d-pipeline-decision)
## Notes
- Keep spike code out of src/ and out of coverage; delete or archive after the ADR merges.
- Related: e37-3d-pipeline-decision should consume the glTF/animation findings.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given both prototypes, when run on the reference machine with the scripted harness, then a results table (p50/p95 frame time, bundle gz KB, TTFF, heap) for each is recorded in the ADR with browser/OS versions.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the Rapier deterministic build, when the same 600-step input script runs twice in Chrome and once in Firefox, then the ADR records whether final state hashes match, with the script committed in `spikes/`.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the evaluation, when ADR-0001 is written, then it contains a weighted scorecard, the chosen renderer and physics engine, rejected options with reasons, and explicit revisit triggers.
- AC-4 [manual] Given neither option reaches p95 ≤ 16.7 ms in the benchmark on High, when the ADR is written, then it records the gap, the mitigations assumed (e.g. LOD, instancing, fewer shadow casters) and proposes budget changes rather than silently accepting.
- AC-5 [manual] Given the ADR, when merged, then the ADR states whether gameplay physics runs inside `src/sim` (deterministic) or in `src/game` with sim-owned outcomes, and the contract's "the renderer" wording remains valid.

title: Reflect merged/open PR Closes lines in backlog.html immediately
description:
## Why
Beads are closed locally after merge, so issues.jsonl lags reality; the public page must be accurate the moment a PR merges.
## What
As a follower, I want beads referenced by merged PRs to appear as Completed (with a PR link) and beads in open PRs to appear In progress so that the page is correct even before local bead closure is pushed.
The generator gains a GitHub overlay: using `GITHUB_TOKEN`, list PRs (paginated, REST or GraphQL), parse `Closes mw-…` lines with the shared parser from e00-pr-template, and compute: merged PR → bead Completed with link "PR #N" and merge date; open PR → bead In progress with link; closed-unmerged PR → ignored. Bead closed in jsonl wins over open-PR status. The Pages workflow adds `pull_request_target` (types: opened, reopened, edited, closed) so the page updates on PR open/close; under pull_request_target it checks out the default branch only and never checks out or executes PR code.
## Scope
- In: scripts/backlog/github.mjs with injectable fetch, pagination and rate-limit handling (100% covered, fixture-based tests)
- In: Overlay merge rules + "source" badges (jsonl vs PR)
- In: Workflow trigger changes with `permissions: pull-requests: read` and explicit `ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}`
- In: Offline flag `--no-github` for local runs
- Out: Automatically closing beads in jsonl from CI (process stays local per CLAUDE.md)
## Notes
- Security: pull_request_target runs with a write-capable token in base context — never `actions/checkout` with `ref: github.event.pull_request.head.sha`, never run scripts from the PR; the PR body is treated as untrusted data (only regex-extracted ids are used).
- Cache API responses per run; cap to last 500 PRs by default.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given jsonl bead `mw-e09.3` open and a merged PR #57 whose body has `Closes mw-e09.3`, when generated, then `mw-e09.3` is in the Completed tab with a link to PR #57.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an open PR #60 with `Closes mw-e09.4`, when generated, then `mw-e09.4` shows status "in progress (PR #60)" in the Upcoming tab.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a closed-unmerged PR referencing `mw-e09.5`, when generated, then `mw-e09.5` keeps its jsonl status.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the GitHub API returns 403 rate-limited or a network error, when generated, then the page is still produced from jsonl alone with a visible "GitHub status unavailable" banner and exit code 0.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a PR body referencing an id not present in jsonl, when generated, then it is listed in an "Unknown references" footer instead of crashing.
- AC-6 [unit] Given 3 pages of PR results, when fetched, then all pages are consumed via the Link header and results merged.
- AC-7 [integration] Given the workflow file, when statically checked by a test, then no step under pull_request_target checks out a PR head ref or runs `pnpm install` from PR contents.
- AC-8 [integration] Given a PR is merged on GitHub, when the resulting workflow run completes, then the Pages site shows its beads as Completed without any local bd action.

title: Generate backlog.html from issues.jsonl and deploy to GitHub Pages
description:
## Why
A human-friendly public view of what is done and what is next keeps the project honest and lets playtesters and collaborators follow progress without installing bd.
## What
As a developer or follower, I want a single-file backlog.html with Completed and Upcoming / In progress tabs so that I can see progress per epic and milestone at a glance.
`scripts/backlog/generate.mjs` reads `.beads/issues.jsonl` and writes `site/backlog.html` (also served as `index.html`): one self-contained file (inline CSS/JS, no external requests), two tabs "Completed" and "Upcoming / In progress", grouped by epic then milestone, each bead showing ID, title, priority, status, labels, expandable ACs and description (`<details>`), and dependencies (linked in-page, with blocker status). Per-epic progress bar (closed/total). Generated-at timestamp and source commit SHA. Workflow `.github/workflows/backlog-pages.yml` builds and deploys to GitHub Pages on push to main and `workflow_dispatch`.
## Scope
- In: Generator (pure functions: parse → model → render) with 100% coverage (listed in coverage-layers.json)
- In: HTML escaping of all bead text; a safe minimal markdown subset (headings, lists, code, bold) rendered without raw HTML passthrough
- In: Pages workflow using actions/upload-pages-artifact + actions/deploy-pages with `concurrency: pages`
