- In: Light/dark theme via prefers-color-scheme; readable at 375 px width
- Out: GitHub PR overlay (merged/open PR status) and pull_request_target trigger — see e00-backlog-pr-status
- Out: Issue-editing UI (read-only page)
## Notes
- Status mapping: closed → Completed; open/in_progress/blocked/deferred → Upcoming tab with status pill; epics sorted by id, milestones m0→post-mvp, then priority, then id.
- Keep render pure and deterministic given (issues, prStatus, now, sha) so snapshot tests are stable.
- Workflow permissions: `contents: read`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a jsonl with one closed and two open beads under `mw-e09`, when generated, then the Completed tab lists 1 and the Upcoming tab lists 2 under the E09 heading with a 1/3 progress bar.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a bead title containing `<script>alert(1)</script>`, when rendered, then the output contains the escaped text and no executable script element from bead content.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a bead with acceptance criteria, when rendered, then the ACs appear inside a collapsed `<details>` element and the bead row shows ID, priority, status, labels and dependency links.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a bead depending on an id not present in the file, when rendered, then the dependency shows as "unknown" rather than throwing.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an empty issues.jsonl, when generated, then both tabs render an empty-state message and the script exits 0.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the generated file, when opened in Playwright with network disabled, then it renders fully, tab switching works by click and keyboard, and there are zero console errors.
- AC-7 [integration] Given a push to main, when backlog-pages.yml runs, then the Pages URL serves the new file within that run; `workflow_dispatch` produces the same result.
- AC-8 [integration] Given coverage runs, when complete, then `scripts/backlog/**` is at 100% lines/branches/functions/statements.

title: Protect main: squash-only, required checks, auto-delete branches
description:
## Why
Contract §1: all work via PR, squash merge only, CI green. Protection makes that a rule rather than a habit.
## What
Configure (and codify in `scripts/configure-repo.sh` using `gh api`) main branch protection: require PR, require status checks `lint`, `typecheck`, `unit`, `coverage-gate`, `coverage-ratchet`, `e2e-smoke`, `build`, `secrets`, `audit`, `beads-validate`, `pr-lint`; require branches up to date; disallow force-push and deletion; squash merge only (merge commits and rebase disabled); auto-delete head branches; linear history. Document the settings in `docs/repo-settings.md`.
## Scope
- In: configure-repo.sh (idempotent) + docs
- In: Verification script that reads settings via API and diffs against expected
- Out: Adding new checks later (each check bead updates the script)
## Notes
- Solo-maintainer project: do not require approving reviews (would block the only maintainer); rely on required checks. Revisit if contributors join.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given repository settings, when a direct push to main is attempted, then it is rejected.
- AC-2 [manual] Given a PR with a failing required check, when merge is attempted, then GitHub blocks it.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the verify script, when run against the repo, then it reports zero drift from expected settings (squash-only, required checks list, auto-delete on).
- AC-4 [manual] Given a PR merged via the UI, when it completes, then only "Squash and merge" was offered and the head branch was deleted.
- AC-5 [integration] Given configure-repo.sh run twice, when the second run completes, then it makes no changes (idempotent).
close_reason: Completed in PR #38. Applied with scripts/configure-repo.sh: verify-repo-settings.sh reports no drift (AC-3), a second configure run changes nothing (AC-5), a direct push to main was rejected with GH006 (AC-1); strict required checks block failing PRs (AC-2) and squash-only + delete-branch are verified settings (AC-4).

title: Add PR template with Closes lines and a PR-body lint check
description:
## Why
backlog.html and bead closure rely on explicit `Closes mw-…` lines; they must be present and well-formed on every PR.
## What
Add `.github/pull_request_template.md` (Summary, Closes lines, Test evidence, DoD checklist from contract §3, CHANGELOG note, coverage exclusions touched). Add a `pr-lint` job (pull_request: opened/edited/synchronize) that parses the PR body and fails if there is no `Closes mw-<id>` line (unless label `no-bead` is applied by a maintainer for trivial chores) or if a referenced id does not exist in `.beads/issues.jsonl` on the PR head.
## Scope
- In: PR template
- In: scripts/pr-body-lint.mjs (shared parser with e00-backlog-pr-status, 100% covered)
- In: pr-lint job
- Out: Closing beads after merge (process, CLAUDE.md)
## Notes
- Share the `Closes` regex with the backlog generator: `^\s*Closes\s+(mw-[a-z0-9.]+)\s*$` (case-insensitive, one id per line).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a body with lines `Closes mw-e00.3` and `closes mw-e30.1`, when parsed, then both ids are returned.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a body mentioning `mw-e00.3` only in prose (`fixes part of mw-e00.3`), when parsed, then no ids are returned.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a PR without any Closes line and without the `no-bead` label, when `pr-lint` runs, then it fails with a message showing the expected format.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a PR whose Closes line references an id not in issues.jsonl, when `pr-lint` runs, then it fails naming the id.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the PR body is edited to add a valid Closes line, when the `edited` event fires, then `pr-lint` re-runs and passes.

title: Validate .beads/issues.jsonl parses and is well-formed in CI
description:
## Why
The backlog is a project artefact that drives backlog.html; a malformed line from a bad merge must be caught before it breaks the page.
## What
Script `scripts/validate-beads.mjs` (100% covered) run in CI job `beads-validate` when `.beads/**` changes (and always on main): every non-empty line parses as JSON; each record has `id`, `title`, `status`; ids match `^mw-`; no duplicate ids (last-wins is reported as an error unless bd format allows it); dependency targets exist; epic children reference an existing epic. Emits GitHub annotations with line numbers.
## Scope
- In: validate script + tests with fixture jsonl files
- In: CI job with path filter plus always-run on main
- Out: Label/AC style linting of bead content (possible follow-up)
## Notes
- Confirm bd issues.jsonl semantics (one line per issue vs append log) when implementing; the duplicate rule must match bd behaviour.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a jsonl with a truncated line 42, when the validator runs, then it exits non-zero with an annotation pointing to line 42.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a record whose dependency references `mw-e99.7` which does not exist, when validated, then it fails naming both ids.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an empty trailing line or CRLF line endings, when validated, then it passes.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the committed `.beads/issues.jsonl`, when CI runs `beads-validate`, then it passes.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the script and fixtures, when coverage runs, then `scripts/validate-beads.mjs` is at 100% on all metrics.

title: Fail CI on CRITICAL dependency CVEs and enable Dependabot
description:
## Why
Policy: never ship libraries with known CRITICAL CVEs. A free public game still owes players a safe page.
## What
Add an `audit` CI job (`pnpm audit --audit-level critical --prod` plus dev deps reported) that fails on any CRITICAL advisory, runs on PRs, on push to main and nightly on a schedule. Add Dependabot (npm + github-actions, weekly, grouped minor/patch) and dependency-review-action on PRs to block newly-introduced critical/high-licence problems. Temporary waivers live in `audit-waivers.json` with advisory id, reason, bead and expiry date.
## Scope
- In: security.yml `audit` job + nightly schedule
- In: .github/dependabot.yml
- In: dependency-review-action with licence denylist (GPL-3.0/AGPL for runtime deps, since assets/code must permit free distribution)
- In: audit-waivers.json + validator (expired waiver fails CI)
- Out: Secret scanning (e00-secret-scanning)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a PR adding a dependency version with a known CRITICAL advisory, when CI runs, then `audit` fails listing the advisory id and package path.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a HIGH (not critical) advisory, when CI runs, then `audit` passes but writes a warning to the job summary.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a waiver whose expiry date is in the past, when the waiver validator runs, then it fails naming the advisory.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a waiver missing a bead id or reason, when the validator runs, then it fails.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the nightly schedule, when a new CRITICAL advisory affects main, then the workflow fails and opens/updates a GitHub issue titled with the advisory id.

title: Block secrets via gitleaks in CI and an optional pre-commit hook
description:
## Why
The repo is public; a leaked token is permanent. Secrets must never reach a commit.
## What
Add a `secrets` CI job running gitleaks over the PR commit range (and full history on push to main), a `.gitleaks.toml` with an allowlist mechanism that requires a comment, enable GitHub secret scanning + push protection in repo settings, and a lefthook/husky pre-commit hook running gitleaks on staged files.
## Scope
- In: .github/workflows/security.yml `secrets` job
- In: .gitleaks.toml
- In: pre-commit hook (opt-in install via `pnpm prepare`)
- In: Enable GitHub secret scanning + push protection (documented; needs-human if API token lacks admin)
- Out: Dependency CVEs (e00-dependency-audit)
## Notes
- Test the job with a fake high-entropy token in a throwaway branch; do not commit real-format tokens into fixtures — use gitleaks test fixtures generated at runtime.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a PR commit containing a string matching the GitHub PAT pattern, when CI runs, then `secrets` fails and reports file and line without echoing the full secret.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a clean PR, when CI runs, then `secrets` passes in ≤ 60 s.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a staged file containing an AWS-key-shaped string, when `git commit` runs with hooks installed, then the commit is rejected.
- AC-4 [manual] Given repository settings, when inspected, then secret scanning and push protection are enabled.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an allowlist entry without an explanatory comment, when the config lint step runs, then it fails.

title: Enforce coverage-exclusions.md as the only source of exclusions
description:
## Why
Exclusions are where coverage policies quietly rot; each one must be visible, justified and owned.
## What
Create `coverage-exclusions.md` with a machine-readable table (path glob | reason | bead | alternative verification). `scripts/check-coverage-exclusions.mjs` parses it and asserts the Vitest `coverage.exclude` list is exactly the set in the file (beyond default test/config ignores), every row has a non-empty reason and a `mw-` bead id, no glob matches `src/sim/**` or `src/content/**`, and glue-layer gaps below 100% are listed with justification. Also bans `/* v8 ignore */` / `istanbul ignore` comments outside excluded paths.
## Scope
- In: coverage-exclusions.md template + initial rows (src/render/**, bootstrap main.ts)
- In: check script + CI step in the coverage-gate job
- In: Docs section in CONTRIBUTING on how to request an exclusion
- Out: Threshold numbers themselves (e00-ci-pipeline)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given vitest excludes `src/render/**` but the markdown table does not list it, when the check runs, then it fails naming the unlisted glob.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a row with an empty reason or without a `mw-` bead id, when the check runs, then it fails naming the row.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a row excluding `src/sim/rng.ts`, when the check runs, then it fails because 100% layers cannot be excluded.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a `/* v8 ignore next */` comment in `src/game/foo.ts` (non-excluded path), when the check runs, then it fails with file and line.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the committed repo state, when CI runs the check, then it passes and the script has 100% coverage.

title: Add CI with per-layer coverage gates, ratchet and Playwright smoke
description:
## Why
The contract goal is releases trusted without reading the code; that requires CI to enforce the §3 coverage policy mechanically, not by reviewer vigilance.
## What
GitHub Actions workflow `ci.yml` on pull_request and push to main with jobs: `lint` (incl. determinism lint), `typecheck`, `unit` (Vitest + coverage), `coverage-gate`, `coverage-ratchet`, `e2e-smoke` (Playwright, Chromium), `build`. Coverage enforcement:
  1. **100% layer:** `vitest.config.ts` `coverage.thresholds` glob entries for `src/sim/**`, `src/content/**`, `src/game/save/**` (save/load), and runtime dirs registered in `coverage-layers.json` (economy, quest, dialogue runtimes, `scripts/backlog/**`) at 100 lines/branches/functions/statements with `perFile: true`.
  2. **Glue layer:** `src/game/**`, `src/ui/**`, `src/audio/**`, `src/tools/**` at ≥ 90 lines and branches (per directory).
  3. **Excluded layer:** `src/render/**`, shaders, WASM bindings, bootstrap are excluded only if listed in `coverage-exclusions.md` (validated by e00-coverage-exclusions).
  4. **Ratchet:** on push to main CI uploads `coverage-summary.json` as artifact `coverage-baseline`; PR runs download the latest main artifact and `scripts/coverage-ratchet.mjs` fails if any of the four metrics decreases (tolerance 0.01 pp) globally or for any layer in `coverage-layers.json`. If no artifact is available it falls back to committed `coverage-baseline.json` and emits a warning annotation.
## Scope
- In: .github/workflows/ci.yml, pnpm store caching, Playwright browser caching
- In: coverage-layers.json (single source for layer → globs → thresholds) consumed by vitest.config.ts and the ratchet script
- In: scripts/coverage-ratchet.mjs with 100% unit coverage
- In: Job summary table of coverage per layer vs baseline
- Out: Secret scanning and CVE audit jobs (e00-secret-scanning, e00-dependency-audit)
- Out: beads validation job (e00-beads-validate)
- Out: Cross-browser matrix (e32-browser-matrix)
- Out: Required-check configuration (e00-branch-protection)
## Notes
- Stable job names matter: branch protection references them (`lint`, `typecheck`, `unit`, `coverage-gate`, `coverage-ratchet`, `e2e-smoke`, `build`).
- Use `concurrency` to cancel superseded PR runs.
- Adding a new 100%-layer runtime directory = one line in coverage-layers.json.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a PR that adds an uncovered branch in `src/sim`, when CI runs, then `coverage-gate` fails naming the file and metric below 100%.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a PR that drops `src/ui` line coverage to 89%, when CI runs, then `coverage-gate` fails; at 90% it passes.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a baseline summary and a PR summary where global branches fell from 95.20% to 95.10%, when `coverage-ratchet.mjs` runs, then it exits non-zero and prints the metric, layer, old and new values.
- AC-4 [unit] Given no main-branch artifact is available, when the ratchet runs, then it compares against committed `coverage-baseline.json` and emits a GitHub warning annotation instead of silently passing.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a PR summary equal to baseline within 0.01 pp, when the ratchet runs, then it passes (float tolerance).
- AC-6 [integration] Given a PR with a failing Playwright smoke test, when CI runs, then `e2e-smoke` fails and uploads the trace and screenshot as artifacts.
- AC-7 [integration] Given a clean PR, when CI runs with warm caches, then the full pipeline completes in ≤ 10 minutes.

title: Lint src/sim for nondeterminism and forbidden layer imports
description:
## Why
Deterministic sim (constitution §10) is only real if it is mechanically enforced; replays and save stability depend on it.
## What
ESLint overrides scoped to `src/sim/**` banning `Math.random`, `Date.now`, `new Date()`, `performance.now`, `crypto.getRandomValues`, `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`requestAnimationFrame`, `window`/`document`/`navigator` globals, and imports from `src/{game,render,audio,ui,tools}` or renderer/physics-rendering packages. Import-boundary rules for all layers: `render` may not import `ui`, `sim` imports only `sim` + `content` types, etc.
## Scope
- In: eslint no-restricted-globals / no-restricted-properties / no-restricted-syntax rules for src/sim
- In: eslint-plugin-import (or boundaries) layer matrix for all src/* layers
- In: Fixture files under `test/lint-fixtures/` proving each rule fires
- Out: Runtime determinism checks (e00-replay-harness)
## Notes
- Allowed escape: `// eslint-disable-next-line` in src/sim is itself banned via `eslint-comments/no-restricted-disable` for these rules.
- Iteration order: prefer arrays/Maps (insertion ordered); document that `for…in` over numeric-like keys is ordered by spec but discouraged.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a fixture `src/sim` file calling `Math.random()`, `Date.now()` or `performance.now()`, when ESLint runs, then each call is reported as an error naming the injected RNG/clock alternative.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a `src/sim` file importing from `src/render` or referencing `document`, when ESLint runs, then an error is reported.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `src/game` calling `performance.now()`, when ESLint runs, then no error is reported (rule scoped to sim only).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a `src/sim` file with `// eslint-disable-next-line no-restricted-properties` above `Math.random()`, when ESLint runs, then the disable comment itself is reported as an error.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the lint fixture suite, when `pnpm test` runs, then a test programmatically lints every fixture and asserts the expected rule IDs fire.

title: Scaffold TypeScript/Vite/pnpm repo with lint, typecheck and Vitest
description:
## Why
Every other bead needs a consistent, strict toolchain; rapid iteration (constitution §10) starts with a fast, boring build.
## What
Create the project skeleton: pnpm workspace root, Vite app, TypeScript strict, ESLint (flat config) + Prettier, Vitest with v8 coverage, Playwright installed, and the `src/{sim,content,game,render,audio,ui,tools}` layout from the backlog contract §2 with a placeholder module + test in each. Scripts: `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint`, `format`, `typecheck`, `test`, `test:coverage`, `e2e`.
## Scope
- In: package.json, pnpm-lock, .nvmrc/.node-version, tsconfig (strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes)
- In: ESLint + Prettier config, EditorConfig
- In: vitest.config.ts with v8 coverage (reporters: text, json-summary, lcov)
- In: playwright.config.ts with one placeholder spec
- In: README quickstart section
- Out: CI workflows (e00-ci-pipeline)
- Out: Per-layer thresholds and ratchet (e00-ci-pipeline)
- Out: Determinism lint rules (e00-determinism-lint)
- Out: Renderer dependency (e00-render-bootstrap)
## Notes
- Pin Node LTS via .node-version and `packageManager` field; use corepack.
- Path aliases: `@sim/*`, `@content/*`, `@game/*`… mirrored in Vite and Vitest.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a fresh clone with the pinned Node, when `pnpm install && pnpm build` runs, then it exits 0 and produces `dist/index.html`.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the scaffold, when `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` runs, then all pass with at least one test per `src/*` layer.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a file with an implicit `any` or an unchecked index access, when `pnpm typecheck` runs, then it fails.
- AC-4 [integration] Given `pnpm test:coverage`, when it completes, then `coverage/coverage-summary.json` and `coverage/lcov.info` exist.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given `pnpm e2e`, when the placeholder Playwright spec opens the built app, then the page loads with zero console errors.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a Node version other than the pinned one, when `pnpm install` runs, then it fails with an engine-mismatch message (engine-strict).

title: Serialize world facts and entity deltas through the save system
description:
## Why
Save-game stability is a technical pillar; world state is the largest and most fragile part of a save.
## What
As a player, I want saving and loading to restore the whole world exactly so that I can trust my progress.

Register fact store + per-level delta sets as save sections with the e30 versioned format; lazy-load deltas for unloaded levels; version and migration hooks for fact renames/removals and component persistence changes; round-trip and migration tests.
## Scope
- In: Save section providers (facts, deltas per level), schema versions, migration functions
- In: Round-trip property tests with generated fact/delta sets
- In: Corruption handling: invalid section → recover what is valid, report
- Out: Storage/IndexedDB and save slots UI — see e30-save-serialization
## Notes
Fact renames are declared in the registry (renamedFrom) so migrations are generated, not hand-written, where possible.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 1,000 randomly generated facts and deltas (fast-check), when serialized and deserialized, then the result is deep-equal and the state hash matches.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a v1 save and a registry declaring "door.cellar.open" renamedFrom "cellar_door_open", when loaded, then the migrated fact holds the old value.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a save whose delta section for one level is corrupted, when loaded, then other sections load, that level falls back to baseline and a recoverable error is reported (edge).
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the greybox slice, when the player opens a door, loots a chest, saves, closes the browser tab and reloads the save, then the door is open and the chest empty.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a save created by the previous release fixture, when loaded by the current build, then it loads without error (migration test).

title: Persist entity changes as deltas from authored level baselines
description:
## Why
Smashed walls, burned bridges, moved crates, looted chests and dead creatures must stay that way — without saving the entire world.
## What
As a player, I want the world to be exactly as I left it when I come back so that my actions matter.

Each level has an authored baseline. Entities flagged persistent record deltas: transform (if moved beyond epsilon and at rest), destroyed/broken, burnt state, property overrides (wetness excluded if transient), mechanism state, container contents, spawned persistent entities (dropped items, debris flagged persistent), and actor life/disposition hooks. On level load, deltas apply after baseline spawn and before first tick.
## Scope
- In: Delta capture on level unload/save, delta apply on load, spawned-entity records
- In: Per-component persistence declarations (which properties persist)
- In: Stable entity ids for authored entities; generated ids for spawned ones
- Out: Policies for transient states — see e27-persistence-policies
- Out: Actor AI state persistence — see mw-e11 (supplies its component serializer)
## Notes
Authored entity ids must be stable across level edits; the level pipeline assigns GUIDs and a lint warns if a persistent entity id disappears (orphaned delta → dropped with warning).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a crate moved 5 m and at rest, when deltas are captured, then one transform delta exists; a crate nudged 1 mm produces none.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a broken wall and a looted chest, when captured and re-applied to a fresh baseline, then the wall is broken (no collider) and the chest is empty.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a persistent dropped item spawned at runtime, when captured and re-applied, then it exists at the same position with the same item id.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a delta referencing an entity id no longer present in the level baseline, when applied, then it is skipped with a warning and loading continues (edge).
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox slice, when the player burns a rope bridge, leaves the level and returns, then the bridge is still gone and replay hashes match.
- AC-6 [perf] Given 5,000 deltas, when applied on level load, then application takes ≤ 30 ms on the reference machine.
close_reason: Completed in PR #158 (AC-5 full slice round-trip split to mw-e27.15)

title: Declare world facts in a content registry validated at load
description:
## Why
Unregistered fact strings are typos waiting to break quests. A registry makes facts discoverable, typed and migratable.
## What
content/facts/*.json registry: key pattern, type, default, persistence policy (see e27-persistence-policies), description, owner system. All quest/dialogue/puzzle/level content references are cross-validated against it. Undeclared writes fail in dev/test.
## Scope
- In: Registry schema + loader + cross-reference validator for content files
- In: Dev/test strict mode: undeclared write throws; prod: logs + ignores
- Out: Quest/dialogue content — see e23-quest-runtime, e22-dialogue-runtime
## Notes
Entity-scoped fact patterns ("entity:*.opened") are declared once as templates.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the registry, when validated, then every entry has type, default and description and keys are unique.
- AC-2 [content] Given a dialogue or puzzle file referencing an undeclared fact, when validated, then validation fails naming the file and fact.
- AC-3 [unit] Given strict mode, when code writes an undeclared fact, then it throws; in production mode it logs a warning and ignores the write (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a template fact "entity:*.looted", when "entity:mine/chest-3.looted" is written, then it validates against the template type.

title: Store persistent world facts in a typed deterministic fact store
description:
## Why
Doors opened, characters helped, creatures befriended and treasures stolen must persist and be readable by every system (E27 outcome).
## What
As a developer, I want a single typed fact store so that quests, dialogue, puzzles and levels read and write world state consistently.

Facts are namespaced keys (global: "quest.missing-miller.stage", entity-scoped: "entity:<levelId>/<entityId>.opened") with typed values (bool, int, enum, string id, timestamp in sim ticks). API: get/set/increment/has, change events, transactional batch writes within a tick, deterministic iteration and a stable content hash for replays.
## Scope
- In: Fact store in src/sim with typed values, namespaces, change events
- In: Transaction batching per tick, deterministic hash
- In: Fact-setter receiver node for the e03 signal graph
- Out: Registry/schema of declared facts — see e27-fact-registry
- Out: Entity physical state persistence — see e27-entity-deltas
- Out: Serialization — see e27-save-integration
## Notes
Timestamps are sim ticks from the injected clock, never wall clock. Keep the store small and flat; it is not a general database.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an empty store, when set("door.cellar.opened", true) is called, then get returns true and one factChanged event fires with old=undefined/new=true.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a transaction that sets 3 facts and then throws, when rolled back, then no facts change and no events fire.
- AC-3 [unit] Given facts inserted in different orders on two runs, when hashed, then hashes are identical.
- AC-4 [unit] Given set with a value of the wrong type for an existing fact (string to bool), when called, then it throws a typed error and the value is unchanged (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a signal-graph fact-setter receiver, when its input goes high, then the configured fact is set on that tick.

title: Wire trigger volumes and mechanisms with data-defined signal graphs
description:
## Why
Designers must connect levers to doors and volumes to events without writing code (fast content creation, reusable interaction systems).
## What
As a designer, I want to connect a trigger volume or lever to any receiver in data so that I can build encounters and mechanisms without scripts.

Signal graph: emitters (trigger volumes with filters — actor tag, property predicate, weight, element presence; levers; plates; receivers) → wires → receivers (doors, lights, spawners, audio cues, world-fact setters). Logic nodes: AND, OR, NOT, XOR, timer/delay, pulse, latch, counter, sequence (ordered inputs), random (seeded). Evaluated deterministically once per tick in topological order with cycle detection.
## Scope
- In: Trigger volume component with enter/exit/stay and property-predicate filters
- In: Signal graph schema (zod), runtime evaluation, logic node library
- In: Validator: missing targets, cycles without delay, unused outputs
- Out: Puzzle goal evaluation — see e15-puzzle-kit
- Out: World-fact persistence — see e27-world-state-store (receiver provided there)
## Notes
Filters are property predicates ("any entity with burning=true enters"), never type ids. Cycles are allowed only through delay/latch nodes to avoid same-tick oscillation.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a trigger volume filtered to entities with burning=true, when a burning object enters, then enter fires; a non-burning player entering does not fire it.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an AND node with two lever inputs, when only one lever is on, then output is off; when both are on, output is on on the same tick.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a sequence node expecting inputs A,B,C, when inputs arrive A,C,B, then it resets and emits a failed pulse; A,B,C emits success.
- AC-4 [content] Given a signal graph with a zero-delay cycle, when validated, then validation fails naming the cycle nodes (edge).
- AC-5 [content] Given a wire referencing a missing entity id, when validated, then validation fails with the file path and id.
- AC-6 [unit] Given the same graph and inputs, when evaluated on two runs, then emitted signal order is identical.

title: Build doors, locks, levers and buttons as data-wired mechanisms
description:
## Why
The grey-box vertical slice needs room → corridor progression; the locked-tower example needs locks that thieves pick, knights break, sorcerers bypass and keys open.
## What
As a player, I want doors that open, lock, jam, break and burn so that there is always more than one way through.

Mechanism components: door (hinged/sliding/portcullis/trapdoor, open/closed/locked/jammed/broken, speed, blocks light/gas/sound when closed), lock (tier, key id, pickable tier, magical seal flag), lever/button/crank/wheel (toggle, momentary, multi-position). All are signal emitters/receivers wired via e03-triggers. Doors are also breakables/flammables via properties (a wooden door burns; an iron door does not).
## Scope
- In: Door, lock, lever, button, crank components and state machines
- In: Lock resolution: key in inventory, lockpick capability hook, break, magical unlock hook
- In: Door as field/light/sound blocker; blocked-by-object handling
- In: Greybox prefabs for each
- Out: Lockpicking minigame — see mw-e10
- Out: Pressure plates — see e03-pressure-plates
- Out: Shootable targets — see e03-shootable-mechanisms
## Notes
Key check reads e17-inventory-core. Doors opening/closing emit noise events and update light/gas occlusion. Portcullis falling onto a crate is stopped (object weight vs. crush force) — a creative way to wedge it open.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a locked door and a player holding the matching key id, when Unlock is used, then state becomes unlocked and an unlocked event with the player as source fires.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a hinged door opening into a crate, when the door opens, then it stops at the obstruction without penetrating and emits blocked; removing the crate lets it finish.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a lever wired to a portcullis, when the lever toggles, then the portcullis receives the signal and moves at its configured speed; toggling mid-motion reverses it.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a wooden door (flammable) that burns out, when resolved, then the door becomes broken/open and no longer blocks light, gas or sound.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a portcullis closing onto an object with crush resistance above the portcullis force, when resolved, then the portcullis stops above the object (wedged) (edge).
- AC-6 [unit] Given a frozen lever, when interacted with, then it does not move and emits jammed until thawed.
- AC-7 [e2e] Given the greybox slice room, when the bot pulls a lever then walks through the opened door, then it reaches the corridor with no console errors.

title: Query light level at any position from all light sources in sim
description:
## Why
Stealth needs light and darkness as numbers; puzzles need "navigating darkness" and light receivers. The renderer's lighting is not queryable or deterministic, so the sim needs its own light model.
## What
As a thief, I want shadows to genuinely hide me so that extinguishing a torch is a meaningful choice.

A sim-side light model: light emitters (point/spot/directional/ambient zones) with intensity, radius, falloff, cone; baked static occlusion (per-emitter visibility probes or cell occlusion) plus dynamic occluders (doors, large objects). lightLevel(pos) returns 0..1 with per-emitter contributions; fires and spells register emitters automatically. Includes a render-parity check.
## Scope
- In: Emitter component, ambient zones (moonlight, indoor dark), sampling API with contributions
- In: Occlusion: static bake from greybox geometry + dynamic door/large-object occluders
- In: Burning entities and light stimuli auto-register emitters
- Out: Visibility scoring — see e09-visibility-model
- Out: Light sources gameplay (extinguish/ignite) — see e03-light-sources
- Out: Beams/mirrors — see e03-light-beams
## Notes
Cache sampling in a coarse light grid (1 m) with dirty-region invalidation when emitters change. Render parity: sample positions compared against renderer luminance in Playwright to keep sim and visuals roughly aligned.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — e09-visibility-model (m1 AI fight) reads light level from it.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a point light of intensity 1.0 and radius 8 m, when sampled at 0, 4 and 8 m with no occluders, then values follow the documented falloff (1.0, 0.25±0.01, 0.0).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a wall between emitter and sample point, when sampled, then that emitter contributes 0.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a door that closes between an emitter and a room, when the door state changes, then samples in the room update on the next tick.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an entity starts burning, when sampled nearby, then its light contribution appears without any manual registration; when it stops burning it disappears.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a sample position outside all baked regions, when queried, then the ambient zone default is returned rather than an error (edge).
- AC-6 [perf] Given 64 dynamic emitters and 500 samples per tick, when running, then light sampling ≤ 0.5 ms per tick p95 on the reference machine.
- AC-7 [e2e] Given the greybox lighting room, when the Playwright parity probe samples 20 points, then sim light level and rendered luminance rank-correlate ≥ 0.8.
notes: AC-7 (render parity e2e) moved to mw-e03.37: the renderer had no point lights and scenes had no light data, so parity needs render + content + game wiring beyond this sim PR. Sim model delivers AC-1..AC-6.

title: Break fragile objects and smash weakened walls into debris
description:
## Why
"The knight might discover that an old wall can simply be smashed apart." Breaking must come from damage type vs. structural properties, so arrows, spells and thrown barrels break things too.
## What
As a knight, I want to smash cracked walls, barricades and pottery so that brute force opens new routes and reveals secrets.

Breakable component: structural hp, resistances per damage type (blunt, slash, pierce, force, fire, cold-shatter), fragile impact threshold, break result (debris pieces, contents spilled, nav/collision change, revealed passage). Weak walls are visually telegraphed (crack decal hook) and marked with a discoverable hint property.
## Scope
- In: Damage accumulation per type, impact-energy breaks for fragile objects, frozen-shatter multiplier
- In: Break results: spawn debris bodies (budgeted), drop contents, remove collider, update nav hooks
- In: Break events with source attribution and noise loudness
- Out: Weapon damage numbers — see e04-damage-model
- Out: Persisting broken state — see e27-entity-deltas
## Notes
Barricades of wood: slash-weak and flammable (burn through them). Old walls: blunt/force-weak only — so knight, Thunderclap, a rolling boulder or an explosive gas pocket all work. No per-class checks.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — e27-entity-deltas persists broken state; a breakable crate is part of the grey-box slice.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a breakable with blunt resistance 0.2 and hp 100, when it receives blunt damage totalling 125, then it breaks; the same slash damage with resistance 0.9 does not break it.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a fragile object, when an impact event exceeds its break threshold (from any source: thrown, fallen, hit), then it breaks and spills its contents.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a frozen breakable, when struck, then its effective threshold is divided by the frozen fragility multiplier.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a break, when resolved, then the collider is removed, a revealed-passage event fires if configured, and a noise event with the material break loudness is emitted.
- AC-5 [unit] Given many breaks in one tick exceeding the debris budget, when resolved, then extra debris is culled deterministically (oldest first) and breaks still complete (edge).
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox weak-wall room, when the bot uses a heavy attack placeholder on the wall, then a passage opens and the bot walks through.

title: Simulate movable, throwable and stackable physics objects in sim
description:
## Why
Crates, barrels, bottles, statues and debris are the raw material of systemic play and puzzles; they must behave consistently and deterministically.
## What
As a player, I want objects to tumble, stack and roll believably so that I can build, knock over and improvise.

A physics-object layer binding e03 properties (weight → mass, friction, restitution, buoyancy) to rigid bodies stepped inside the sim fixed timestep, with sleeping, impact events (impulse, relative speed, materials), and sim-side authority (renderer interpolates only). Impact events feed breakables, noise and damage.
## Scope
- In: Rigid body lifecycle from properties; fixed-step integration inside sim tick
- In: Impact events with energy (J) and material pair for sound/noise
- In: Stacking stability, sleeping, max-body budget, render interpolation contract
- Out: Breaking — see e03-breakables
- Out: Player carry/push — see e02-carry-throw, e02-push-pull
- Out: Levitation — see e03-liftable-levitation
## Notes
Physics engine per e00-engine-decision (Rapier WASM with enhanced determinism expected). Physics is wrapped behind an interface so unit tests can run with a deterministic reference integrator.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 10 kg crate dropped from 2 m onto stone, when simulated, then it comes to rest within 2 s and emits one impact event with energy 196 J ± 5%.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a stack of 5 crates, when simulated for 10 s with no disturbance, then no crate moves more than 1 cm (stable stacking) and all bodies sleep.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a weight property change on a body (e.g. soaked cloth heavier), when committed, then the rigid body mass updates on the next tick.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the same scene and inputs, when simulated 3,000 ticks on two runs, then physics state hashes are identical.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the active body count exceeds the budget (default 300), when a new body wakes, then the oldest distant resting bodies are forced to sleep and a budget warning is logged (edge).
- AC-6 [perf] Given 200 active bodies in the greybox scene, when simulated, then physics step ≤ 2.0 ms per tick p95 on the reference machine.
notes:
From mw-e03.3 (PR #49): src/sim/stimulus added a spatial.placement component ({x,y,z,radius} bounding sphere; placeEntity/placementOf). Physics should keep it in step with bodies rather than defining a second position source.

From mw-e00.19 (PR #73): the non-compat @dimforge/rapier3d-deterministic package has no main/exports, so plain Node/Vitest can't import it. Sim physics tests need Vitest wasm config (vite-plugin-wasm) or the -compat package in tests only; hashes must match either way.
From mw-e00.21 (greybox testbed): the scene loader writes static level geometry into a tiny sink, src/sim/physics/static-colliders.ts: StaticColliderSink { add(desc): ColliderHandle; remove(handle): void; count(): number }. Descriptors are the mw-e02.2 greybox shapes (GreyboxShape from src/sim/character/greybox.ts: axis-aligned { kind: 'box', min, max } and { kind: 'ramp', min, max, rises }), never with velocity. The Rapier port should implement this sink (fixed colliders) and replace InMemoryColliderSink in src/main.ts; unloadScene removes every handle it added (AC-2 of mw-e00.21 counts sink.count() == 0 after unload). It is add/remove only: queries stay on CollisionWorld (mw-e02.2/e02.21).

title: Ignite, burn, spread and extinguish fire from heat and properties
description:
## Why
Fire is the canonical systemic element: burning ropes, oil slicks, torched webs, scared creatures. "If ropes have flammable=true and fire spells produce heat, you have built the foundation."
## What
As a player, I want anything flammable to catch fire when hot enough and fire to spread to nearby flammables so that I can improvise with torches and spells.

Heat/fire rules over properties and the element field: entities heat up from stimuli and neighbouring cells; at ignitionPoint and not wet/frozen they ignite; burning entities consume fuel, emit heat into the field, emit light (via e03-light-field) and smoke gas, dry out neighbours, and reduce structural hp; at fuel 0 they become burnt (material → charred) or are destroyed. Water/cold/smothering extinguish. This item also establishes the propagation rule framework (rule registry, phases) that other elements plug into.
## Scope
- In: Rule framework: ordered rule phases, each rule reads/writes only properties + field
- In: Heating, ignition, burning, fuel consumption, burnout/destruction, spread via field
- In: Extinguish by wetness/cold/smother; wet objects dry by heat before igniting
- Out: Water, ice, electricity, gas specifics — see sibling e03 items
- Out: Fire visuals/audio — see e03-state-feedback-bridge
## Notes
Everything here is expressed as property rules. A lint rule forbids referencing entity archetype ids in src/sim/elements/**. Emergent examples to cover in e03-emergence-scenarios: oil puddle ignition chain, burning a rope support, torching a spider web wall.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any entity with flammable, wetness < 0.5 and not frozen, when its temperature reaches ignitionPoint, then burning=true on that tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a burning entity and a flammable neighbour within 1 cell, when ticks elapse, then the neighbour ignites within the time predicted by field heat transfer (± 1 tick) and a non-flammable neighbour never ignites.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a burning entity with fuel F, when it burns uninterrupted, then it burns out after F seconds and transitions to its burnt state (material charred or destroyed per data).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a wet flammable entity (wetness 1.0) exposed to heat, when heated, then wetness decreases first and it ignites only after wetness < 0.5.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a burning entity receives a water stimulus making wetness ≥ 0.5, when resolved, then burning=false and a steam gas puff is emitted into the field.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a fire in a closed room with limited fuel, when simulated 10 minutes, then the fire terminates (no infinite burn loop) and the field returns to ambient (edge).
- AC-7 [integration] Given a greybox scene with a line of 10 wooden crates, when the first is ignited, then all 10 burn in order and a replay reproduces identical state hashes.

title: Build a sparse spatial grid for temperature, moisture, gas and charge
description:
## Why
Fire spreading across a floor, gas filling a room, or water pooling need a medium between objects; per-object rules alone cannot express "the room is full of gas".
## What
A sparse, chunked voxel field (default 0.5 m cells, 8×8×8 chunks) storing temperature, moisture, gas concentration per gas type, and charge. Supports diffusion steps with per-cell conductivity derived from occupying materials, walls blocking flow, sleeping chunks when stable, and entity↔cell exchange.
## Scope
- In: Chunked sparse storage, activation/sleep, fixed-point or deterministic float math
- In: Diffusion kernel with blockers from static geometry
- In: Entity↔cell coupling interface used by propagation rules
- Out: Element-specific rules — see e03-element-propagation, e03-water-wetness, e03-gas-clouds, e03-electricity
## Notes
Use integer/fixed-point for cross-browser determinism. Budget target: 2,000 active cells ≤ 2.0 ms/tick (verified by e03-sim-perf-budget).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a single hot cell in an open field, when diffusion runs for N ticks, then total heat is conserved within 0.1% (minus configured ambient loss).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a wall between two cells, when diffusion runs, then no quantity crosses the wall.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a chunk whose values are within epsilon of ambient for 60 ticks, when checked, then it sleeps and costs zero update time until touched.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the same initial field on two runs, when stepped 1,000 ticks, then field hashes are identical.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a stimulus far outside any existing chunk (1 km away), when applied, then a new chunk is allocated without affecting others and memory stays bounded by the chunk cap (edge).

title: Inject heat, cold, water, charge, force and gas via one stimulus API
description:
## Why
Spells, arrows, torches, lightning, creatures and traps must all act on the world through the same door, or the combinatorial workload kills the project.
## What
As a developer, I want a single applyStimulus(shape, element, intensity, duration, source) API so that any ability produces world effects without knowing what it hits.

Stimulus shapes: point, sphere, cone, capsule/beam, box, contact (on hit). Elements: heat, cold, water, charge, force (impulse), gas (type), light, blunt/slash/pierce (for breakables). Each stimulus is recorded with source for attribution (quests, crime, telemetry). Stimuli resolve in a fixed phase of the tick.
## Scope
- In: Stimulus types + shapes, ordering rules, attribution
- In: Overlap resolution against entities with properties and against the element field
- In: Stimulus log available to debug overlay and tests
- Out: Specific spells/arrows — see e06-spell-pipeline, e05-bow-core
- Out: Propagation after injection — see e03-element-propagation
## Notes
A Fire Arrow = contact(pierce) + sphere(heat, r=0.5). A torch swing = capsule(heat, low). Thunderclap = sphere(force) + sphere(blunt). Designers compose these in data.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a sphere heat stimulus of radius 2 m, when applied, then every entity with temperature within 2 m receives heat scaled by the documented falloff and entities outside receive none.
- AC-2 [unit] Given two stimuli applied in the same tick in either order, when resolved, then resulting state is identical (order-independent via sorted resolution).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a force stimulus on a pushable 10 kg object, when applied, then an impulse proportional to intensity/weight is delivered to the physics object.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a stimulus with a source entity, when it causes a propertyChanged, then the event carries the source id (attribution).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a stimulus with intensity 0 or a zero-radius shape, when applied, then it is a no-op and does not throw (edge).

title: Provide data-defined material presets for common world objects
description:
## Why
Fast content creation: a designer should mark a crate "wood" and get sensible flammability, weight density, sound and fragility for free.
## What
As a designer, I want to pick a material preset (wood, dry-wood, stone, iron, copper, cloth, rope, paper, oil, water, ice, glass, straw/hay, flesh, bone, ivy, earth) so that objects get consistent properties with per-object overrides.
## Scope
- In: content/materials/*.json presets with property defaults + footstep loudness + impact sound id
- In: Override merge rules (object value > preset > global default)
- In: Material docs table generated from data
- Out: Visual materials/shaders — see mw-e37 / mw-e29
## Notes
Example values: wood ignition 300°C, fuel 60 s/kg-ish scalar; iron conductive, non-flammable; oil ignition 210°C, spreads as liquid; glass fragile threshold low; straw impactAbsorb 0.8, very flammable.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given every material preset, when validated, then all fields pass schema and physically inconsistent combos (flammable + ignitionPoint missing) are rejected.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an object with material=wood and override weight=3, when resolved, then weight is 3 and all other properties come from the wood preset.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an object referencing an unknown material id, when loaded, then load fails with the id and file path (edge).
- AC-4 [content] Given the presets, when the docs generator runs, then docs/design/materials.md lists every material and property value.
notes: From mw-e03.1 (PR #41): world property 'material' is a plain kebab-case id string; this bead should turn it into ref('material') and may add cross-field checks to worldPropertiesSchema (e.g. burning implies flammable, as findPropertyViolations does in the sim).

title: Define typed world-property components for systemic interactions
description:
## Why
The single most important architectural principle: interactions come from properties (flammable=true), never "Fireball + Rope" scripts. Every system in the game reads and writes these.
## What
As a designer, I want to give any object a set of physical/elemental properties so that it automatically reacts to fire, water, cold, electricity, force and light.

A typed property component set in src/sim with schema in src/content: material, temperature (°C), ignitionPoint, fuel (burn seconds), burning, wetness (0..1), frozen, freezePoint, conductive, charge, weight (kg), fragile (breakThreshold J), hp/structural, buoyancy/density, climbable (grade), liftable, pushable, hideable, reflective, transparent, opaque, lightEmitter, soundDamping, friction, impactAbsorb, ownership tag. Derived queries (isFlammableNow = flammable ∧ ¬wet>0.5 ∧ ¬frozen).
## Scope
- In: Property component definitions + zod schemas + defaults
- In: Query helpers and change events (propertyChanged{entity, key, old, new})
- In: Deterministic ordered iteration over entities with a property
- Out: Material defaults — see e03-material-presets
- Out: Propagation behaviour — see e03-element-propagation and siblings
## Notes
Keep the property set closed and versioned (adding a property is a schema bump tracked by e30 migrations). A CI guard (see epic exit criteria) forbids type-pair checks in interaction rules. Actors (player, creatures) use the same components — see e03-actor-properties.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an entity with flammable, wetness=0.8, when isFlammableNow is queried, then it returns false; at wetness=0.2 it returns true.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a property write that changes a value, when committed, then exactly one propertyChanged event fires with old/new values; writing the same value fires none.
- AC-3 [content] Given an entity data file with an unknown property key or out-of-range value (wetness 1.4), when validated, then validation fails naming the path.
- AC-4 [unit] Given 1,000 entities with the flammable property created in random order, when iterated, then iteration order is by entity id and stable across runs.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a frozen=true entity with temperature above freezePoint, when invariants are checked, then the validator reports an inconsistent state (edge).

title: Expose stance and movement profiles for stealth noise and visibility
description:
## Why
Stealth cannot be crouching + an eye icon: stance and speed must feed visibility and noise as numbers (Thief constitution).
## What
As a thief, I want my stance and speed to meaningfully change how visible and loud I am so that careful movement is rewarded.

The controller publishes a MovementProfile each tick: stance (standing/crouched), gait (still/walk/run/sprint), silhouette height, and normalised noise and visibility multipliers from data. A "slow walk" modifier (hold key / light stick) gives the quietest gait.
## Scope
- In: MovementProfile type and data table per stance × gait
- In: Slow-walk modifier action
- In: Armor/encumbrance multiplier hook (value supplied by inventory)
- Out: Visibility scoring — see e09-visibility-model
- Out: Noise propagation — see e09-sound-propagation
## Notes
Default multipliers: stand-sprint noise 1.0, stand-run 0.6, stand-walk 0.3, crouch-walk 0.15, slow-walk 0.08, still 0.0. Related: e09 consumes; do not implement scoring here.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — visibility and noise at m1 need crouch/walk/run profiles.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a crouched player moving at crouch speed, when the profile is read, then noise multiplier is 0.15 and silhouette height matches the crouch capsule.
- AC-2 [unit] Given sprint pressed while crouched, when resolved, then the player stands (if space allows) and profile becomes stand-sprint; if a ceiling blocks standing, sprint is ignored (edge).
- AC-3 [unit] Given an encumbrance multiplier 1.5 from armor, when walking, then noise multiplier is 0.45 and clamped to ≤ 1.0 overall.
- AC-4 [content] Given the stance profile table, when validated, then every stance × gait combination is defined.

title: Support gamepad input with deadzones and remappable bindings
description:
## Why
Gamepad is second after KB/M (Technical constitution). Action RPG combat is commonly played on a pad.
## What
As a player, I want to plug in a standard gamepad and play with sensible defaults so that I can play from the couch.

Gamepad API polling mapped into the same ActionFrame: radial deadzone, response curve, right-stick look with acceleration, default standard-mapping bindings, rebinding, hot-plug, and last-used-device prompt glyph switching.
## Scope
- In: Standard mapping (Xbox/PS layouts) defaults, radial deadzone 0.15 configurable, look curve
- In: Hot-plug connect/disconnect, device-switch detection for prompt glyphs
- Out: Aim assist — see e05-bow-core / e02-lock-on
- Out: Haptics — P3 later
## Notes
Browser Gamepad API differs across Chrome/Firefox/Safari; test standard mapping only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given stick input magnitude 0.10, when processed with deadzone 0.15, then move vector is (0,0); at magnitude 1.0 it is length 1.0.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the stick at magnitude 0.575 (midway between deadzone and full), when processed, then output magnitude is 0.5 ± 0.01 (rescaled radial deadzone).
- AC-3 [unit] Given both KB and gamepad produce move input in one tick, when merged, then the larger-magnitude vector wins and length never exceeds 1.0.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a gamepad disconnects mid-sprint, when the next frame is sampled, then all gamepad-held actions release and the game pauses per settings.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the last input came from the gamepad, when the interact prompt renders, then it shows the gamepad glyph.
notes: 2026-09-29 owner decision: gamepad moved up to P0/m1, to do right after mw-e02.4. The owner plays with an Xbox controller, so Xbox glyphs are the default and it's the test device. Include right-stick rate-based camera look (mw-e02.4 makes look device-agnostic) and amend CONSTITUTION §10 'Keyboard + mouse comes first, gamepad second' to treat them as equal first-class inputs.

title: Lock controller determinism with golden replay tests in CI
description:
## Why
Determinism is a constitution-level technical goal; controller regressions are silent and must be caught automatically.
## What
Record golden input logs on the greybox traversal course (run, jump, crouch, slopes, steps, later mantle/climb/swim) and assert final and periodic state hashes in CI. Provide a script to re-bless goldens intentionally with a diff report.
## Scope
- In: 3 golden logs (basic, slopes/steps, stress with rapid direction changes)
- In: Periodic hash checkpoints every 60 ticks to localise divergence
- In: Re-bless script with human-readable diff
- Out: Replay harness itself — see e00-replay-harness
## Notes
Extend goldens as traversal items land (each traversal item adds a clip).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given each golden log, when replayed in CI, then every checkpoint hash matches the committed golden.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a deliberate 1% change to runSpeed, when replayed, then the test fails and reports the first divergent checkpoint tick.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a log recorded at a different frame rate (30 vs 144 Hz render), when replayed, then sim hashes are identical (render rate independence).

title: Drive character animation from sim locomotion state and events
description:
## Why
Animation must reflect the sim exactly (no sliding feet, no "floaty" jumps) without leaking renderer concerns into the sim.
## What
As a developer, I want the sim to publish a locomotion state snapshot and discrete animation events so that any renderer/animation set can play matching clips.

The sim emits: locomotion state (idle/walk/run/sprint/crouch/airborne/landing/climb/mantle/swim), normalised speed, turn rate, and events (jumpStart, land{impactSpeed}, footstep{foot}, mantleStart, ledgeGrab). src/game maps these to an animation state machine on grey-box/Mixamo rigs.
## Scope
- In: LocomotionSnapshot type + event stream in sim
- In: Blend-tree driver in render using speed/turn rate; root motion NOT authoritative
- In: Grey-box capsule-man placeholder rig
- Out: Combat animation layers — see e04-melee-core
- Out: Final character rigs — see e37-3d-pipeline-decision
## Notes
Footstep events are produced from sim stride distance, not from animation curves, so they stay deterministic (consumed by e02-footstep-events).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a player accelerating from idle to run, when snapshots are sampled, then state transitions idle→walk→run occur at documented speed thresholds (0.2, 2.5 m/s).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a fall of 3 m, when landing, then exactly one land event fires with impactSpeed within ±2% of the analytic value.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player is pushed sideways while idle (external impulse), when sampled, then state is not "walk" unless input is present (no false locomotion).
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the bot runs and jumps, then the placeholder rig plays run and jump clips (animation state probe) and there are no console errors.
- AC-5 [perf] Given 20 animated characters in the greybox scene, when running for 30 s, then animation update cost ≤ 1.0 ms per frame p95 on the reference machine (High).

title: Focus and interact with world objects via contextual prompts
description:
## Why
The world rewards curiosity: bookshelves, levers, chests, bodies, statues must all respond to one consistent interact verb.
## What
As a player, I want to look at an object and press Interact to use it so that exploring feels natural and I always know what I can do.

Objects expose interaction affordances (open, pull, pick up, read, search, hide, climb, talk…) declared as components. A focus selector in src/sim scores candidates by distance, view angle and line of sight and picks one focus target; the UI shows a contextual prompt. Affordances may be gated by class/capability or item (locked → "Pick lock" for thief, "Unlock" with key).
## Scope
- In: Interactable component with affordance list, range, required capability/item predicate
- In: Deterministic focus scoring + LOS check, hysteresis to prevent flicker
- In: Interaction event dispatch to owning systems; contextual prompt model for UI (text + binding glyph)
- In: Hold-to-interact durations
- Out: Prompt visuals — see mw-e31/ui work
- Out: Specific affordances (doors, containers) — see e03-doors-locks-switches, e03-hiding-containers
## Notes
Scoring: score = w_d*(1 - d/range) + w_a*cos(angle); range default 2.5 m, max angle 45°. Ties broken by entity id for determinism. Unavailable affordances are still shown greyed with the reason (e.g. "Locked — needs Iron Key") to hint at alternate routes.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given two interactables at 1.0 m (30° off-axis) and 2.0 m (straight ahead), when focus is computed, then the selection matches the documented scoring and is identical across runs.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an interactable behind a wall within range, when focus is computed, then it is not selected (LOS).
- AC-3 [unit] Given focus on A and a new candidate B scoring within 10% of A, when computed, then focus stays on A (hysteresis).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a locked door and a player without the key or lockpicking capability, when focused, then the prompt shows the affordance as unavailable with the reason and Interact dispatches nothing.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a hold-to-interact affordance (1.0 s), when Interact is released at 0.8 s, then the interaction is cancelled and no event fires.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the bot faces a lever and presses Interact, then the lever event fires and the prompt DOM element displays the bound key.

title: Follow the player with a colliding, orbiting third-person camera
description:
## Why
A camera that clips into walls or loses the player breaks exploration and combat. Camera options are also an accessibility concern (E31).
## What
As a player, I want a smooth third-person camera I control with the mouse so that I can always see my character and surroundings.

Orbit camera with shoulder offset, pitch limits, sensitivity/invert options, zoom, collision pull-in against level geometry (never inside walls), and smooth recovery. Camera yaw feeds the controller as data so movement is camera-relative but still deterministic.
## Scope
- In: Orbit + shoulder offset, pitch clamp (-70°..+60°), zoom 2–6 m, sensitivity + invert Y
- In: Sphere-cast collision pull-in, recovery easing, transparency fade of occluders near the camera
- In: Camera yaw injected into ActionFrame for camera-relative movement
- Out: Lock-on framing — see e02-lock-on
- Out: Bow aim camera — see e05-bow-core
- Out: Motion sickness options UI — see mw-e31
## Notes
Camera lives in src/game/src/render (presentation), but the yaw consumed by sim is quantised into the ActionFrame so replays are exact. Default FOV 70°.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given pitch input beyond the clamp, when applied, then pitch stays within -70°..+60°.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a wall between the ideal camera position and the player, when resolved, then the camera is placed ≥ 0.2 m in front of the wall on the same frame (no clipping frame).
- AC-3 [unit] Given the occluder disappears, when recovering, then the camera returns to the ideal distance over 0.3 s ± 0.05 without overshoot.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the camera yaw is 90°, when move=(0,1), then the player moves along the camera forward vector (camera-relative).
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the Playwright bot walks the player along a narrow corridor with pillars, then no rendered frame has the near plane inside geometry (depth probe) and there are no console errors.
- AC-6 [manual] Given a playtest, when 3 testers orbit and move for 5 minutes, then none report nausea or losing sight of the character.
notes: Merged in PR #82; AC-6 manual playtest pending

title: Move controller tuning values into schema-validated content data
description:
## Why
Feel is found by iteration (rapid iteration is a technical pillar). Designers must tune speeds, jump arcs and camera feel live without code changes.
## What
Controller and camera parameters live in a zod-validated content file (content/controller/*.json) with per-class overrides (e.g. thief crouch faster, knight in heavy armor slower). The debug console can live-edit values and dump the modified file.
## Scope
- In: Schema + default file + per-class override merge
- In: Debug console commands: ctl.get, ctl.set, ctl.dump
- In: Hot reload in dev
- Out: Armor weight effects on movement — see mw-e17 (supplies modifiers)
## Notes
Values documented with units in the schema description fields.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the controller data file, when validated, then every numeric field has declared units and range and the default file passes.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a class override that sets only crouchSpeed, when merged, then all other values come from the base profile.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an out-of-range value (negative gravity), when loaded, then validation fails with the field path in the error.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the debug console, when ctl.set runSpeed 6 is executed, then the next tick uses 6.0 m/s and ctl.dump outputs a valid file.

title: Move the player with a deterministic third-person kinematic controller
description:
## Why
Movement is the verb the player uses every second; if it feels mushy nothing else matters. Keeping it in src/sim means replays, AI and tests share the exact rules the player feels.
## What
As a player, I want tight, weighty walk/run/sprint, jump and crouch movement so that exploring the world feels excellent.

A kinematic capsule controller in src/sim consumes ActionFrames and the camera yaw, resolves collisions against the physics world, handles slopes, steps, ground snapping, jump arcs, coyote time and jump buffering, and exposes a movement state (grounded/airborne/crouched/sprinting) plus the capsule shape (crouch lowers it). Climb/traverse extension points are defined here and filled in by later items.
## Scope
- In: Walk/run/sprint with accel/decel curves, air control, gravity, jump, coyote time (≤ 120 ms), jump buffer (≤ 150 ms)
- In: Slope limit, step-up, ground snapping, moving-platform carry
- In: Crouch stance with reduced capsule and uncrouch obstruction check
- In: Traversal hook interface (climb, mantle, swim) for later items
- Out: Ledges/climbing — see e02-ledge-mantle, e02-climb-surfaces
- Out: Stance stealth modifiers — see e02-stance-profiles
- Out: Dodge roll — see e04-melee-core
## Notes
Starting numbers (all in content data, tunable): run 5.0 m/s, sprint 7.5 m/s, crouch 2.2 m/s, reach max speed in 0.15 s, stop in 0.10 s, jump apex 1.2 m, step height 0.35 m, slope limit 45°. Physics queries go through a thin collision-world interface so the sim is unit-testable with a fake world; the Rapier implementation follows e00-engine-decision.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a grounded player at rest on flat ground, when move=(0,1) is held, then speed reaches 5.0 m/s ± 0.05 within 0.15 s and releasing stops the player within 0.10 s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a grounded player, when jump is pressed, then apex height is 1.2 m ± 0.02 and the player lands on the same tick count on every run.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player walked off a ledge 100 ms ago, when jump is pressed, then the jump executes (coyote time); at 130 ms it does not.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a 0.30 m step, when walking into it, then the player steps up without losing more than 10% speed; given a 0.40 m step, then the player is blocked.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a 50° slope, when walking up it, then the player slides back down and cannot ascend; a 40° slope is climbable at ≥ 80% speed.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a crouched player under a 1.2 m ceiling, when crouch is released, then the player stays crouched until the obstruction clears (edge).
- AC-7 [integration] Given the greybox traversal course and a recorded input log, when replayed twice, then final sim state hashes are identical.
close_reason: Completed in PR #75 (input taken as the MovementActions/CharacterInput subset, since mw-e02.1 is still open)

title: Map remappable KB/M input to deterministic per-tick action frames
description:
## Why
Keyboard + mouse comes first (Technical constitution). Everything downstream — controller, combat, spells, replays, AI-driven test bots — must consume abstract actions, not raw keys, so the sim stays deterministic and remapping is free.
## What
As a player, I want every game action bound to remappable keys and mouse buttons so that I can play comfortably and the game reacts identically every time.

An action map (Move, Look, Jump, Sprint, Crouch, Interact, LockOn, CycleTarget, PrimaryAttack, SecondaryAttack, Ability1–4, Inventory, Pause, …) turns DOM input into an immutable ActionFrame sampled once per fixed sim tick (digital buttons with pressed/held/released edges, analog move vector, look delta). The sim only ever sees ActionFrames.
## Scope
- In: Action registry (data-defined), default KB/M bindings, runtime rebinding API with conflict detection
- In: ActionFrame sampling aligned to e00-sim-core ticks; pointer lock handling
- In: Bindings persisted through the settings store
- Out: Gamepad — see e02-input-gamepad
- Out: Remapping UI screen — see mw-e31 (uses this API)
## Notes
ActionFrame is plain data so e00-replay-harness can record/replay it verbatim. Keep raw DOM handling in src/game; the frame type lives in src/sim. Related: mw-e31 accessibility remapping UI.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the default binding set, when W and Space are pressed in the same tick, then the ActionFrame contains move=(0,1) and jump.pressed=true, and on the next tick jump.held=true, jump.pressed=false.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a rebind of Jump to F, when F is pressed, then Jump fires and Space no longer does.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a rebind that collides with an existing binding in the same context, when applied, then the API returns a conflict listing both actions and leaves bindings unchanged.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a key pressed and released within a single tick (between samples), when the frame is sampled, then pressed=true and released=true are both reported so taps are never lost.
- AC-5 [integration] Given pointer lock is lost (Esc / window blur), when the next frame is sampled, then all held actions are released and look delta is zero (no stuck keys).
- AC-6 [integration] Given bindings saved via e31-settings-framework, when the page reloads, then custom bindings are restored.
notes:
AC-6 (persist bindings) is split out to mw-e02.22, which depends on mw-e31.1. This bead ships an in-memory bindings API.
mw-e02.2 (PR #75) consumes CharacterInput = { actions: MovementActions, cameraYaw } from src/sim/character/controller.ts. ActionFrame must satisfy MovementActions structurally, or be mapped in characterControllerSystem's input selector. Walk is partial stick deflection, not a separate action.

title: VFX cue sheets map sim events to effects
description:
## Why
Effects should follow events from data, sharing audio's matcher so sound and visuals stay in sync.

## What
A game-layer bridge reusing the generic rule matcher from e28-cue-sheets: `{event, match:{...}, effect, socket, orientTo:"hitNormal"|"attackerForward", scaleBy}`. Effects attached to an entity detach and finish gracefully when it is destroyed (no orphaned loops).

## Scope
- In: VFX rule schema, bridge, attachment lifecycle, initial rules
- Out: Specific effects (per-feature items)

## Notes
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given generic and material-specific rules for `DamageApplied`, when a metal-on-metal hit occurs, then the specific effect spawns oriented to the hit normal.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a looping effect attached to an entity, when the entity is destroyed, then emission stops and existing particles finish within their lifetime.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a 60 s combat replay with VFX on and off, when compared, then sim state hashes are identical every tick.
- AC-4 [content] Given a VFX rule referencing an unknown effect id, when validated, then it warns (placeholder allowed) with the rule index.

title: Procedural placeholder VFX textures keyed by final asset ids
description:
## Why
Effects must be tunable before final art exists; placeholders under final ids make integration a swap.

## What
A tool (`tools/vfx/gen-placeholders`) generating soft circle, spark streak, smoke puff (noise), ring, shard and flame flipbook textures, saved under final asset ids with `placeholder: true` manifest flags, plus a report listing remaining placeholders.

## Scope
- In: Generator, initial texture set, manifest flags, report
- Out: Final VFX textures via GPT image prompts (asset group, e37)

## Notes
Ids listed in the combat plan summary for the asset group.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given all effect definitions, when validated, then every referenced texture id resolves to a manifest entry.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the generator with a fixed seed, when run twice, then outputs are byte-identical.
- AC-3 [content] Given the placeholder set, when measured, then total size ≤ 1.5 MB.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the report command, when run, then it lists all `placeholder: true` textures with a count.

title: Data-driven VFX framework with pooling and particle budgets
description:
## Why
Impacts, magic and destruction establish the visual identity; one budgeted framework keeps spectacle within the performance baseline (E29 outcome).

## What
Renderer-agnostic VFX interface (implemented in src/render/vfx after e00-engine-decision). Effect definitions as content data: emitters (rate/burst, lifetime, velocity cone, size/colour/alpha curves, texture/flipbook id, blend mode), sockets, duration/loop, quality tiers. Instanced particle rendering with pooling (no per-spawn allocations after warm-up). **Budget manager** (pure TS in src/game/vfx, unit-testable): global cap 4000 particles High / 1500 Low, per-effect priority, distance culling at 60 m, LOD tiers. API: `spawn(effectId, {position | entity+socket, rotation, scale, params}) → handle`. Presentation RNG only — never the sim RNG.

## Scope
- In: Effect schema, runtime, pooling, budget manager, socket attachment, debug stats overlay
- Out: Event→effect mapping (e29-vfx-cue-sheets)
- Out: Specific effects (per-feature VFX items)
- Out: Final textures (asset group)

## Notes
Render-specific code is covered by Playwright smoke + perf; budget/pool logic sits in src/game for ≥ 90% unit coverage.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given an effect definition with a negative lifetime or unknown blend mode, when validated, then it fails with the path.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the High cap of 4000 and a request that would exceed it, when evaluated, then lower-priority effects are culled first and the new effect is admitted only if its priority is higher.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a pool warmed to 64 instances of an effect, when 64 spawn and expire repeatedly for 1000 cycles, then no new allocations occur (pool counter unchanged).
- AC-4 [unit] Given an effect 70 m from the camera, when spawned, then it is culled without consuming budget.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an unknown effect id, when spawned, then a null handle returns, dev builds show a magenta marker, and nothing throws.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed in Chromium, when 20 test effects spawn, then they render with no console errors and a screenshot sanity check passes.
- AC-7 [perf] Given 50 simultaneous effects at the High cap, when measured, then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms on the reference machine.
notes: Superseded numbers: owner decided 2026-09-29 (mw-e29.16) that caps are 2000 High / 800 Low per style bible §13.1. The 4000/1500 figures in the description and AC-2 are historical; AC-2's culling rule was tested at a 4000 cap.

title: Data-driven cue sheets map sim events to sounds
description:
## Why
Sounds must follow game events without hard-coded calls scattered across code, and must never influence the deterministic sim.

## What
A game-layer bridge subscribing to sim events and resolving **cue sheet** rules (content data): `{event, match:{...tags}, cue, variants, pitchJitter, volumeJitterDb, cooldownMs, priority}`. Most-specific match wins. A separate presentation RNG handles variation (never the sim RNG). Identical cues on the same entity within 30 ms are de-duplicated. The rule matcher is generic so e29-vfx-cue-sheets reuses it.

## Scope
- In: Rule schema, matcher, bridge, presentation RNG, de-dupe, initial rules for combat events
- Out: Specific sound sets (per-feature audio items)

## Notes
Put the matcher in src/game/cues so VFX shares it.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given rules for `DamageApplied` generic and `DamageApplied{weapon:"metal", target:"bone"}`, when a metal-on-bone hit occurs, then the specific cue plays.
- AC-2 [unit] Given two identical cue requests on one entity 20 ms apart, when processed, then only one plays.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a 60 s combat replay run with audio enabled and disabled, when compared, then sim state hashes are identical every tick.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a rule with 4 variants and pitch jitter ±5%, when triggered 1000 times, then all variants occur and pitch stays within ±5%.
- AC-5 [content] Given a cue sheet referencing an unknown sim event type, when validated, then it fails with the rule index.

title: Placeholder sound pack keyed by final asset ids
description:
## Why
Gameplay is never blocked by final audio; placeholders named with final ids make swapping in real assets a file replacement.

## What
A script (`tools/audio/gen-placeholders`) synthesising simple placeholder sounds (filtered noise bursts, tones, clicks) or pulling CC0 clips, written under the final asset ids (e.g. `sfx-knight-parry-metal-01`). Manifest entries flagged `placeholder: true`. A dev report lists remaining placeholders so the asset group can prioritise prompt beads.

## Scope
- In: Generator script, initial placeholder set for combat/archery/footsteps/UI, manifest flags, placeholder report
- Out: Final SFX creation (art/audio group, e38)

## Notes
Initial ids are listed in the combat plan summary for the asset group. Licences for any CC0 clips go in assets/CREDITS.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given all cue sheets, when validated, then every referenced sound id resolves to a manifest entry (placeholder or final).
- AC-2 [content] Given the placeholder set, when measured, then total size ≤ 2 MB.
- AC-3 [content] Given any CC0-sourced placeholder, when validated, then it has a licence/provenance line in assets/CREDITS.md.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the placeholder report command, when run, then it lists every id with `placeholder: true` and a total count.

title: Web Audio engine: registry, buses, voice pool, positional audio
description:
## Why
Every weapon, footstep and creature needs a robust, browser-safe audio core before feedback can feel satisfying (E28 outcome).

## What
A `src/audio` engine: lazily created `AudioContext`, resumed on first user gesture (autoplay policy) with a queue that plays requests younger than 2 s and drops older ones. Sound registry from a content manifest (id → url(s), variants, bus, spatial, loop, priority). Decode + LRU cache (cap 64 MB decoded). Bus graph: master → music, sfx (subgroups combat, footsteps, creatures), ambience, ui. Positional audio via `PannerNode` (HRTF on High, equalpower on Low), inverse distance, ref 2 m, max 40 m.
