Listener follows the camera each render frame. Voice pool max 48 (Low 24) with priority + distance stealing. API: `play(cueId, {position|entity, volume, pitch}) → handle` with stop/fade.

## Scope
- In: Context lifecycle, registry, cache, buses, panner, listener, voice pool, handle API
- In: Fake AudioContext test double for ≥ 90% coverage of src/audio
- Out: Mapping sim events to sounds (e28-cue-sheets)
- Out: Volume settings UI (e28-mixer-settings)
- Out: Sound asset creation (art/audio group)

## Notes
Presentation only: nothing in src/audio may write to sim state. Related: stealth noise simulation is owned by e09-sound-propagation.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a suspended AudioContext, when `play` is called before any gesture, then the request is queued; on resume, requests younger than 2 s play and older ones are dropped.
- AC-2 [unit] Given 48 active voices, when a higher-priority request arrives, then the lowest-priority, farthest voice is stolen; when a lower-priority request arrives, then it is rejected.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a sound attached to a moving entity, when the entity moves, then the panner position updates in the same frame.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unknown cue id, when played, then a null handle is returned, one warning is logged per id, and nothing throws.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a corrupt audio file, when decoding fails, then the id is marked failed and dev builds substitute a placeholder beep; production stays silent.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, when the page is clicked and a test cue plays, then `AudioContext.state` is `running` and no console errors occur.
- AC-7 [perf] Given 48 positional voices on moving entities, when measured, then main-thread audio update ≤ 0.5 ms per frame p95 on the reference machine.

title: Creatures attack via the move system with readable telegraphs
description:
## Why
Enemies are creatures, not dummies: their attacks must share the player's rules (parry, block, poise) and telegraph clearly for Zelda-like readability.

## What
As a designer, I want creature attacks defined as move data with enforced telegraphs so that every creature is parryable, dodgeable and readable by the same rules as the player.
Creature schema references moves; the combat layer exposes `canUseMove`, `rangeFor(move)`, cooldowns and `inRange` queries for AI (e11). Readability rules: every creature attack has a windup ≥ 18 ticks (300 ms) before active frames; `unblockable`/grab moves ≥ 30 ticks (500 ms) and must declare a distinct telegraph cue (audio + VFX). `TelegraphStarted` event fires on the move's `telegraphTick`.

## Scope
- In: Creature move references, AI query API, telegraph rules/events, greybox skeleton 3-move set for validation
- Out: AI decision-making (e11)
- Out: Bestiary content (e13)
- Out: Creature animation/art

## Notes
Greybox skeleton moves: overhead chop (parryable), 2-hit slash (parryable), lunging thrust (unparryable, blockable). Related: bestiary skeleton (e13) should adopt these.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — required by the E01 grey-box vertical slice.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given a creature move with startup 12 ticks, when validated, then it fails the readability rule (minimum 18).
- AC-2 [content] Given an `unblockable` creature move with no telegraph cue or startup < 30 ticks, when validated, then it fails.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature executing a move with telegraphTick 4, when tick 4 runs, then exactly one `TelegraphStarted` event is emitted with the move's cue ids.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature move on cooldown 120 ticks, when `canUseMove` is queried at tick 60, then it returns false with reason `cooldown`.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox skeleton's overhead chop, when the knight parries it in the window, then the skeleton enters Parried exactly as the dummy does.

title: Combat HUD: health and stamina bars with damage feedback
description:
## Why
The player must read health and stamina at a glance without numbers cluttering the screen (Zelda-like readability).

## What
As a player, I want clear health and stamina bars and a hint of where damage came from so that I can make decisions mid-fight.
Health bar with delayed "chip" segment (lost health shown in a lighter colour that drains after 500 ms); stamina bar that flashes when an action is rejected for stamina; low-health pulse below 25%; off-screen damage direction indicator (arc toward source for 1.5 s); HUD scale from settings. UI reads sim state through the game layer only — no rules in UI.

## Scope
- In: Health/stamina bars, chip, rejection flash, low-health pulse, damage direction indicator, HUD scale setting
- Out: Target/lock-on HUD (e04-hud-target)
- Out: Screen shake/vignette (e29-screen-feedback)
- Out: Stealth HUD (stealth group)

## Notes
Placeholder UI art until the style bible (e37-style-bible) lands; integration of final UI art is a separate asset bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given health 100→70 on one hit, when rendered, then the bar shows 70 filled and a 30-wide chip segment that begins draining at 500 ms and is gone by 1000 ms.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an `ActionRejected{reason:"stamina"}` event, when processed, then the stamina bar enters its flash state for 300 ms.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a hit from a source 120° behind the camera forward, when processed, then the damage indicator arc points to 120° and fades out at 1.5 s.
- AC-4 [unit] Given health at 24% of max, when rendered, then the low-health pulse is active; at 25% it is not.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the combat sandbox, when the player takes a dummy hit, then the DOM/engine HUD health value matches sim health within one rendered frame.
- AC-6 [unit] Given HUD scale set to 150% in settings, when the HUD mounts, then bar dimensions are 1.5× baseline and remain within the viewport at 1280×720.

title: Combat sandbox scene with dummy creatures and frame-data overlay
description:
## Why
Combat feel is tuned by iteration; a dedicated sandbox makes every timing change testable in seconds and gives e2e tests a stable arena.

## What
As a developer, I want a combat sandbox scene with configurable dummies and live frame data so that I can tune and verify timing without playing through levels.
Contents: a training dummy (infinite-health toggle, configurable resistances/poise/hurtbox regions), an attacker dummy that performs a selected move on a metronome (default every 2.0 s; parryable/unblockable toggle) for parry and dodge practice, a frame-data overlay (current move, phase, tick, i-frame/hyperarmor highlights, hitboxes/hurtboxes), DPS/poise readouts, debug slow-motion (sim steps at 0.25× wall time; sim tick count unchanged), and spawners via e33-debug-console.

## Scope
- In: Scene, dummies, overlay, slow-mo, console commands
- In: Deterministic scene seed for e2e tests
- Out: Archery range layout (e05-archery-range)
- Out: Real creature AI (e11)

## Notes
Scene is loaded via e00-greybox-testbed's scene loader under /dev/combat.
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the sandbox, when `spawn dummy --poise 60 --resist slash=0.5` is entered, then a dummy with those values exists in sim state.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the attacker dummy set to a 2.0 s metronome, when 10 s elapse, then exactly 5 swings start, each on a tick multiple of 120.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the sandbox loaded in Chromium, when the frame overlay is toggled, then it shows move id, phase and tick matching sim state and no console errors occur.
- AC-4 [unit] Given slow-motion 0.25×, when 4 s of wall time pass, then exactly 60 sim ticks have run and frame data is unchanged versus normal speed.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a dummy with infinite health, when 10,000 damage is dealt, then it never emits `Died` and health display resets after 3 s.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: From mw-e04.8: when the sandbox wires attackers into the game, add hitVolumeSystem after the player's action timeline (installPlayer with combat) and pass invulnerable: iframeRule(moves); in src/main.ts it currently runs before the player's systems, which would check i-frames one tick stale.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: From mw-e04.7: placeholder hit-reaction tuning to tune in the sandbox — creature reactions.knockdownImpulse 900 N·s and reactions.launchSpeed 2 m/s (content defaults), and the player's DEFAULT_REACTION_PROFILE mass 80 kg. Wire the sandbox with installHitReactions({ moves, damage, pushers: [pushCharacter, pushPhysicsObject] }), register HIT_VOLUME_COMPONENTS (facing) and pass reactions: true to simAnimReader.

title: Dodge roll and backstep with invulnerability frames
description:
## Why
A precise dodge with honest i-frames is the souls-like skill expression that makes dangerous enemies fair.

## What
As a knight, I want to roll through or away from attacks with a short invulnerability window so that timing, not stats, keeps me alive.
Roll (directional, relative to camera or lock-on): 36 ticks, 20 stamina, i-frames ticks 2–14 (13 ticks ≈ 217 ms) at medium defaults, 3.0 m travel. Backstep (no direction held): 24 ticks, 12 stamina, i-frames 2–7. Roll recovery cancellable into a roll-attack from tick 28. Hits landing during i-frames apply no damage, poise or reaction and emit `DodgedHit` (feedback + telemetry). Rolling off ledges is allowed; rolling into a wall stops displacement but i-frames continue.

## Scope
- In: Roll, backstep, i-frames, roll-attack cancel, `DodgedHit` event
- Out: Load-class variations (e04-armor-weight)
- Out: Archer quickstep (e05-mobile-archery)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a roll started on tick 0, when a hit lands on tick 14, then no damage/poise applies and `DodgedHit` is emitted; when a hit lands on tick 15, then it applies normally.
- AC-2 [unit] Given no movement input, when dodge is pressed, then a backstep executes costing 12 stamina with i-frames on ticks 2–7 only.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a roll toward a wall 1 m away, when stepped, then displacement stops at the wall and i-frames still run through tick 14.
- AC-4 [unit] Given attack pressed at roll tick 26 (inside the buffer), when tick 28 arrives, then the roll-attack move starts.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a replay of the attacker dummy swinging and a roll timed 1 tick early vs on time, when replayed, then outcomes differ exactly as recorded and hashes are deterministic across 100 runs.
- AC-6 [manual] Given the sandbox attacker dummy, when three playtesters practise for 3 minutes, then each reports dodges "felt fair" (no hits they believed they had dodged) — any counterexample is logged with a replay file.

title: Sim-chosen hit reactions: flinch, stagger, knockback, knockdown
description:
## Why
Readable reactions tell the player what their hit did; knockback into ledges and hazards lets combat interact with the world.

## What
As a player, I want enemies (and me) to react differently to light hits, poise breaks and heavy impacts so that I can read the fight and exploit openings.
The sim selects a reaction tier from poise state, hyperarmor and impulse: `none` (hyperarmor absorbed), `flinch` 12 ticks (interrupts startup only), `stagger` 45 ticks (on `PoiseBroken`), `knockback` 60 ticks + physics displacement (impulse ≥ 300 N·s equivalent), `knockdown` 90 ticks grounded then wake-up with 20 i-frame ticks. Direction quadrant (front/back/left/right) from hit vector vs facing. Creature schema may override tiers (e.g. trolls never knocked down). Displacement goes through physics so a shoved creature can fall off ledges or into fire.

## Scope
- In: Reaction selection, durations, direction, displacement via physics, `HitReaction` event with reaction id for render/audio
- Out: Animation assets (render/art)
- Out: Critical/riposte states (e04-parry-riposte)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature with 40 poise and no hyperarmor, when a 15-poise hit lands during its startup, then a 12-tick flinch interrupts the attack.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a hit that emits `PoiseBroken`, when resolved, then the reaction is `stagger` for 45 ticks and the victim's current action is cancelled.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a hit from behind the victim, when resolved, then the reaction direction is `back`; given a hit at 80° to the right, then `right`.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a victim in a hyperarmor window with remaining cap 40 and a 30-poise hit, when resolved, then reaction is `none` but damage still applies.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a creature standing 0.5 m from a ledge in the greybox testbed, when a knockback hit lands toward the ledge, then the creature falls off and environmental fall damage rules apply.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a knocked-down entity, when it wakes up, then it is invulnerable for 20 ticks and cannot be re-knocked-down during them.

title: Knight light attack chain and shield block with guard break
description:
## Why
This is the first playable fight of the vertical slice: a sword chain that feels weighty and a shield that makes defence a choice (Knight fantasy: weight, impact, mastery).

## What
As a knight, I want a three-hit sword chain and a shield block so that I can trade blows deliberately and defend against frontal attacks.
Chain: L1 12/4/18 ticks, 12 stamina, 20 slash, 15 poise; L2 10/4/20, 14 stamina, 22 slash, 15 poise; L3 16/5/26, 18 stamina, 30 slash, 30 poise. The chain resets to L1 after 30 idle ticks past recovery. During startup the knight may rotate up to 360°/s toward the lock-on target (from e02-camera); during active frames rotation is locked (commitment).
Block (hold): shield becomes active after 6 ticks (100 ms); covers a frontal 120° arc; movement at 50% speed. Wood shield absorbs 85% physical / 30% fire, stability 60: stamina loss = attack `staminaDamage` × (1 − stability/100). If stamina reaches 0 while blocking, **Guard Break**: 60-tick stagger, `GuardBroken` event, and the unabsorbed remainder of that hit applies.

## Scope
- In: Light chain, block, guard break, lock-on tracking during startup, initial wood shield data
- Out: Parry and riposte (e04-parry-riposte)
- Out: Dodge (e04-dodge-iframes)
- Out: Heavy/charged (e04-heavy-charged)
- Out: Shield bash (e04-shield-bash)

## Notes
Anchor e04-melee-core: this item delivers the minimum fight for M1. Parry and dodge (also in the anchor's meaning) land as sibling items e04-parry-riposte and e04-dodge-iframes so dependents are not blocked on them.
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an idle knight with 100 stamina, when attack is pressed three times inside each buffer window, then L1→L2→L3 execute, 44 stamina is spent, and the next press starts L1 again.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a knight whose shield has been raised ≥ 6 ticks, when a frontal 30-slash hit with staminaDamage 20 lands, then health drops by 4.5 and stamina by 8.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a blocking knight, when a hit arrives from outside the frontal 120° arc, then full damage applies and no stamina is drained by the block.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the shield raised only 3 ticks, when a frontal hit lands, then the block is not yet active and full damage applies.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a blocking knight with 8 stamina, when a hit with staminaDamage 20 lands, then stamina is 0, `GuardBroken` is emitted, the knight is staggered for 60 ticks and the unabsorbed damage is applied.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the combat sandbox dummy, when L1 connects, then `DamageApplied` appears on the sim event bus on a tick within L1's active window (ticks 12–15).
- AC-7 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed in Chromium, when Playwright issues the attack action three times, then the dummy's health drops by 72 (20+22+30) and no console errors are logged.
- AC-8 [manual] Given a 5-minute sandbox session, when three playtesters use the chain, then median rating for "swings feel heavy and committed" is ≥ 4/5 and none describe attacks as floaty.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: From mw-e04.7 (hit reactions): for guard break call applyHitReaction(world, knight, { kind: 'stagger', ticks: 60, direction, instigator, source }, { moves }) from src/sim/combat/reactions. It replaces any reaction playing; the DamageApplied of the unabsorbed remainder then resolves to a weaker reaction and is suppressed ('weaker'), so the 60-tick stagger stands.

title: Stamina pool governs attacks, blocks, dodges and sprint
description:
## Why
Stamina gives fights rhythm — attack, breathe, defend — which is the backbone of weighty souls-like combat.

## What
As a knight, I want a stamina bar that my attacks, blocks, dodges and sprinting draw from so that fights have a readable push-and-pull rhythm.
Max 100. Regenerates 40/s after a 30-tick (500 ms) delay since the last spend; while blocking regen ×0.35. Costs come from move data. An action is allowed whenever stamina > 0 and may drive it to 0 (the "last action" rule). Reaching 0 triggers **Exhausted**: regen delay becomes 72 ticks (1.2 s) and sprint is disabled until stamina ≥ 20. Sprint drains 10/s.

## Scope
- In: Stamina component, regen rules, exhaustion, action gating, `ActionRejected{reason:"stamina"}` event
- Out: HUD bar (e04-hud-vitals)
- Out: Armor-weight regen modifiers (e04-armor-weight)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 100 stamina, when a 12-cost attack starts, then stamina is 88 and does not regenerate for 30 ticks, after which it rises 40/s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given 5 stamina, when a 20-cost dodge is requested, then it executes and stamina becomes 0 (not negative) and Exhausted is set.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 0 stamina, when attack is pressed, then the action is rejected and `ActionRejected{reason:"stamina"}` is emitted once per press.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an Exhausted knight, when sprint is held, then sprint is refused until stamina ≥ 20.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a knight holding block, when 60 ticks pass after the regen delay, then stamina regenerates at 14/s (40 × 0.35).
- AC-6 [manual] Given a 5-minute sandbox session, when a playtester fights the attacker dummy, then they can describe when they are "out of breath" without looking at the HUD (audio + animation cues suffice).

title: Action timeline FSM with input buffer, cancel windows and local time
description:
## Why
Souls-like weight comes from committed startup/active/recovery phases; a fair 150 ms input buffer keeps that weight from feeling unresponsive.

## What
A deterministic per-entity action state machine that executes `MoveDef`s: phases, cancel windows, chain transitions, interruption by hit reactions, and a per-entity **local time scale** (used for hit-stop). Input buffer: an action pressed up to 9 ticks (150 ms) before it becomes legal executes on the first legal tick; the most recent buffered input wins. Consumes abstract actions from e02-input-actions, never raw keys.

## Scope
- In: Timeline runner, buffer, cancel rules, interrupt API, local time scale, action-rejected events
- Out: Specific knight moves and their tuning (e04-melee-core and siblings)
- Out: Hit-stop amounts (e04-hit-stop)

## Notes
Stamina is spent on the first startup tick and is not refunded if interrupted (souls convention).
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a move with startup 12 / active 4 / recovery 18, when executed from tick 0, then phase transitions occur at ticks 12, 16 and 34 exactly.
- AC-2 [unit] Given attack pressed 8 ticks before recovery ends, when recovery ends, then the chained move starts that tick; given it pressed 12 ticks before, then the input is dropped.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a move with a dodge cancel window starting at recovery tick 6, when dodge is pressed at recovery tick 4, then the dodge executes on recovery tick 6.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an entity interrupted during startup, when the interrupt resolves, then no hitbox spawns and the stamina already spent is not refunded.
- AC-5 [unit] Given local time scale 0 for 4 ticks during an active phase, when time resumes, then the phase continues from the same offset and total move duration is extended by exactly 4 ticks.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a recorded input log of a 3-hit chain with a dodge cancel, when replayed 100 times through e00-replay-harness, then every tick's state hash is identical.

title: Data schema for attack moves: frames, costs, hitboxes, flags, cues
description:
## Why
Combat must be data-driven so knights, creatures and archers share one move format and designers tune timing without code changes (Technical constitution).

## What
A zod schema for `MoveDef`: `id`, frame data (`startup`, `active`, `recovery` ticks), `cancelWindows` (into dodge/attack/block by tick range), `staminaCost`, damage packet template, `poiseDamage`, `staminaDamage`, hitbox track id, `reach` class, `swing` (`horizontal`|`vertical`|`thrust`), flags (`parryable`, `blockable`, `unblockable`, `hyperarmor` tick range + poise cap, `iframes` tick range, `interruptible`), `telegraphTick`, `chainNext`, and presentation ids (`anim`, `audioCue`, `vfxCue`). Initial data: knight sword light 1–3, heavy, charged, shield bash, kick, dodge roll, backstep; training-dummy swing.

## Scope
- In: Schema, validators, initial knight move file, loader to runtime tables
- Out: Executing moves (e04-action-timeline)
- Out: Creature-specific move sets (e13 bestiary, via e04-creature-attack-hooks)

## Notes
Unknown presentation cue ids warn (placeholder assets may lag) but never fail validation.
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the knight move file, when validated, then all moves pass and `sword-light-1` resolves to startup 12 / active 4 / recovery 18 ticks.
- AC-2 [content] Given a move whose i-frame or hyperarmor range extends beyond startup+active+recovery, when validated, then it fails with the move id and field path.
- AC-3 [content] Given a move whose `chainNext` references a missing move id, when validated, then it fails listing the dangling reference.
- AC-4 [content] Given a move flagged both `parryable` and `unblockable` without `parryable` override note, when validated, then a warning is emitted (legal but unusual).
- AC-5 [content] Given a move with an unknown `audioCue` id, when validated, then validation passes with one warning naming the id.

title: Swept hitboxes and region-tagged hurtboxes in the sim
description:
## Why
Hits must land where the player sees them land and never tunnel through fast swings; region tags make heads and weak points matter for every class.

## What
Sim-side collision shapes independent of the renderer: hurtboxes (capsule/sphere/box) attached to entity sockets with a region tag (`weakpoint` > `head` > `torso` > `limb`, plus `armored` flag) and multiplier; hitboxes driven by authored socket tracks from move data and **swept** from previous to current tick pose so a 2 m sword arc over 4 active ticks cannot skip a thin target. One hit per target per active window. Faction/friendly-fire rules per move so creatures can be tricked into hitting each other. The render animation follows sim poses, never the other way round.

## Scope
- In: Shape types, swept capsule tests, region priority, per-swing hit registry, friendly-fire flags
- In: Debug draw data exposed to the greybox testbed overlay
- Out: Projectile swept tests (e05-arrow-projectile reuses the query)
- Out: Animation authoring (render)

## Notes
Region priority resolves overlapping hurtboxes. Keep shape math in src/sim/geom so arrows and spells share it.
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a sword hitbox sweeping a 2.0 m arc over 4 active ticks and a 0.4 m-radius target capsule mid-arc that no single tick pose overlaps, when stepped, then exactly one hit registers on the tick whose sweep intersects it.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a hitbox overlapping the same target for all 4 active ticks, when stepped, then exactly one hit event is emitted for that swing and target.
- AC-3 [unit] Given overlapping head and torso hurtboxes both intersected on the same tick, when resolved, then the hit carries region `head` and its multiplier.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a sweep crossing an ally with `friendlyFire: true` in the move, when stepped, then the ally is damaged; with `friendlyFire: false`, then the ally is ignored.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an attacker destroyed during its active window, when the next tick runs, then its hit volumes are removed and no further hits are emitted.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the greybox testbed with the hitbox overlay enabled, when a swing plays, then the drawn shapes hash-match the sim shapes for every rendered frame.
- AC-7 [perf] Given 24 active hitboxes and 40 hurtboxes, when the hit query runs, then it takes ≤ 0.5 ms per tick p95 on the reference machine.

title: Deterministic damage model: damage types, resistances, poise, death
description:
## Why
Every class and creature must resolve harm through one rule set so knight swings, arrows, backstabs, spells and falling rocks compose systemically (Combat constitution; "enemies reward understanding behaviour" via weaknesses).

## What
A pure `src/sim/combat/damage` module. A `DamagePacket` carries `instigator`, `source`, per-type amounts (`slash`, `pierce`, `blunt`, `fire`, `frost`, `shock`, `arcane`, `poison`), `poiseDamage`, `staminaDamage`, `impulse`, `impactForce` and `tags` (e.g. `critical`, `backstab`, `weakpoint`, `riposte`, `environment`). Resolution runs an ordered **modifier pipeline**: attacker modifiers → hit-region multiplier → defender resistances → guard/block → armor flat absorption → clamp. Other groups register modifiers (e.g. thief backstab ×N, spell amplifiers) without editing core code. Components: `Health`, `Poise` (max, current, regen delay, regen rate), `Resistances`. Emits `DamageApplied` (with per-type breakdown), `PoiseBroken`, `Died` on the sim event bus. Amounts use integer hundredths to avoid float drift in replays.

## Scope
- In: Damage packet, damage types, resistance multipliers, modifier pipeline API, health, poise accumulation/regen, death event
- In: Zod schema fragment for resistances/poise reused by e12-creature-schema
- Out: Hit detection volumes (e04-hit-volumes)
- Out: Hit reaction selection (e04-hit-reactions)
- Out: Environmental damage sources (e04-environmental-damage)
- Out: Thief backstab rules (thief group, consumes modifier API)
- Out: Spell damage authoring (e06-spell-pipeline)

## Notes
Poise defaults: poise regenerates at 25% of max per second after 2.0 s (120 ticks) without poise damage. Resistance multipliers in [0, 3]; 0 = immune. Example: skeleton blunt 1.5, pierce 0.5, poison 0.
This is the anchor other groups depend on. Related: thief backstab bonus (e10), sorcerer spell damage (e06), archer weak points (e05-weak-points) all register modifiers here.
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a defender with slash resistance 0.5 and no armor, when a 40-slash packet resolves, then health decreases by exactly 20.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a packet of 30 blunt + 20 fire against resistances blunt 1.5 / fire 1.0, when resolved, then total damage is 65 and `DamageApplied` lists the per-type breakdown {blunt: 45, fire: 20}.
- AC-3 [unit] Given two modifiers registered at stages `attacker` (×2 when tagged `backstab`) and `defender` (−10 flat), when a tagged 20-pierce packet resolves, then result is 30 and stage order is stable by (stage, registration id) across 1000 seeded runs.
- AC-4 [unit] Given poise max 50, when three 20-poise hits land within 120 ticks, then `PoiseBroken` is emitted exactly once on the third hit and poise resets to 50; given the same hits 150 ticks apart, then no break occurs because poise regenerated.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a creature with 5 health, when a 1000-damage packet resolves, then health clamps to 0, `Died` is emitted exactly once, and later packets on the dead entity are ignored (no second `Died`, no negative health).
- AC-6 [unit] Given a resistance of 0 for a damage type, when only that type is dealt, then 0 damage is applied and `DamageApplied.immune` is true so feedback can show "no effect".
- AC-7 [content] Given creature data with resistances, when validated, then unknown damage types or multipliers outside [0, 3] fail with the offending JSON path.
- AC-8 [unit] Given the combat sim module, when the coverage suite runs, then src/sim/combat/damage reports 100% lines/branches/functions/statements.

title: E01 — Playable Vertical Slice
description:
## Outcome
A player can start the game from a title screen, pick a class, spawn into a grey-box room, walk a corridor, fight a skeleton, loot it, save, die, respawn and reload — end to end, in a browser, verified by an automated e2e test. At m2 a grey-box class gauntlet proves every class's core verbs in one course.

## Scope
- In: title → class select → spawn flow; the pause menu (resume / settings / save / load / quit to title); the m1 grey-box slice level; the player death & respawn loop (consumes the combat Died event and e30-death-reload); contextual respawn rules used later by the Knot (wake in the Fold); area transitions between scenes; the m1 "slice plays start-to-finish" e2e + perf test; the m2 class-fantasies gauntlet level and its per-class e2e runs.
- Out: the systems themselves (controller E02, combat E04, saves E30, inventory E17, loot E18); final art/audio (E37/E38); the real MVP levels (E24–E26).

## Exit criteria
- The m1 slice e2e passes in CI on Chromium on every PR.
- Death → respawn/reload returns to play in <= 3 s warm.
- The m2 gauntlet is completed by a scripted replay for each of the four classes using only that class's verbs.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 [e2e] Given a clean browser profile, when the slice e2e runs, then it reaches "slice complete" with zero console errors.
- EC-2 [e2e] Given each of the four classes, when its gauntlet replay runs, then the course is completed using only that class's capabilities.

title: E17 — Inventory & Equipment
description:
## Outcome
Weapons, armor, books, keys, consumables, quest objects and unusual artifacts are manageable without inventory busywork. Equipment changes what the player can *do* (new verbs, altered stealth/noise, light, traversal), not only numbers. All rules live in `src/sim` with data in `src/content`.
## Scope
- In: Item definition schema + validator, inventory model, equip slots, keyring, consumables, pickup/drop/throw, equipment-granted verbs, inventory/equipment UI, save integration, debug commands
- In: Encumbrance decision via spike (weightless vs light encumbrance)
- Out: Loot tables and containers (mw-e18)
- Out: Spell learning from books (e07-spellbook-learning; we only model books as items)
- Out: Shops and prices (mw-e20)
- Out: Specific item content lists for Briar Glen (world-content group)
## Exit criteria
- Player can pick up, inspect, equip, use, drop and throw items in the greybox testbed with keyboard+mouse and gamepad.
- At least 3 equipment items grant a new verb or systemic property (e.g. light source, noise reduction, climb anchor) through the capability registry, verified by tests.
- Inventory and equipment round-trip through save/load with zero diffs across 100 randomized inventories.
- src/sim inventory/equipment modules and src/content item schema at 100% coverage.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 Player can pick up, inspect, equip, use, drop and throw items in the greybox testbed with keyboard+mouse and gamepad.
- EC-2 At least 3 equipment items grant a new verb or systemic property (e.g. light source, noise reduction, climb anchor) through the capability registry, verified by tests.
- EC-3 Inventory and equipment round-trip through save/load with zero diffs across 100 randomized inventories.
- EC-4 src/sim inventory/equipment modules and src/content item schema at 100% coverage.

title: E18 — Loot & Treasure
description:
## Outcome
Exploration produces interesting, handcrafted discoveries rather than endless statistically interchangeable equipment. Loot is data (tables + placements), deterministic under seeded RNG, persistent in world state, and aware of ownership so theft is a real, systemic act.
## Scope
- In: Loot table schema + deterministic roller + validator, containers, placed/hidden treasure, creature drops, ownership + stolen flag, unique artifacts with verbs, container/loot UI, treasure design guide, loot audit tool
- Out: Random affix/stat-stick generation (explicitly rejected by the anti-grind rule)
- Out: Lockpicking and trap disarming mechanics (mw-e10) — containers only expose lock/trap hooks
- Out: Specific treasure placements for Briar Glen/Labyrinth (world-content group)
## Exit criteria
- A container in the greybox testbed can be opened, looted, and stays looted after save/reload.
- Taking an owned item while witnessed flags it stolen and emits a crime event consumed by AI; unwitnessed theft flags it stolen without a crime event.
- The loot validator rejects any table referencing a missing item, a duplicated unique, or a cyclic nested table.
- Roller is deterministic: same seed + same table yields identical results in 10,000-roll replay tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 A container in the greybox testbed can be opened, looted, and stays looted after save/reload.
- EC-2 Taking an owned item while witnessed flags it stolen and emits a crime event consumed by AI; unwitnessed theft flags it stolen without a crime event.
- EC-3 The loot validator rejects any table referencing a missing item, a duplicated unique, or a cyclic nested table.
- EC-4 Roller is deterministic: same seed + same table yields identical results in 10,000-roll replay tests.

title: E12 — Creature Framework
description:
## Outcome
Creatures are data: unique senses, locomotion, attacks, property-driven vulnerabilities, factions/relationships, dispositions, fears/morale, personalities, needs and non-hostile interaction affordances are all declared in validated content and consumed by AI and stealth systems — ready for the bestiary (E13) and social creatures (E14).

## Scope
- In: creature schema, sense profiles, grey-box fixtures, spawner, attack definitions, locomotion, vulnerabilities via world properties, factions, dispositions, fears/morale, personality traits, needs hooks, interaction affordances, creature save state, auto smoke-test harness, authoring guide.
- Out: specific bestiary creatures (E13), social creature content and dialogue (E14/E22), final models/animations (E37 asset beads).

## Exit criteria
- A new creature can be added with data only and passes the auto smoke harness.
- Schemas and runtime at 100% coverage.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 [content] Given any creature data file, when validated and smoke-tested, then it passes with no code changes required.
- EC-2 [unit] Given creature modules, when coverage runs, then `src/sim` and `src/content` creature code is at 100%.
- EC-3 [manual] Given the authoring guide, when a designer follows it, then a new creature is added in ≤ 30 min.

title: E11 — Enemy AI
description:
## Outcome
Enemies patrol, perceive, investigate, communicate, fight, retreat, search and return to believable routines through a deterministic, data-driven behaviour runtime and the six-state alert machine (Unaware → Suspicious → Investigating → Searching → Alerted → Combat). Enemies never know the player position except through their senses.

## Scope
- In: architecture spike + runtime, scenario test harness, navigation, perception, awareness, alert states, memory/LKP, patrol, investigate, search, communication/alarms, combat, retreat/flee, return to routine, AI tuning data, debug visualisation, AI perf budget.
- Out: creature data schema (mw-e12), stealth inputs (mw-e09), boss/bestiary-specific behaviours (E13/E26), social dialogue (E14/E22).

## Exit criteria
- Grey-box fight (m1) uses this AI; stealth scenarios (m2) pass.
- No-omniscience enforced by architecture tests.
- 24 agents within the AI perf budget.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 [unit] Given the AI modules, when an architecture test scans imports, then no behaviour/memory module reads ground-truth player transforms.
- EC-2 [perf] Given the AI stress scene, when run on the reference machine, then AI+perception+sound cost p95 ≤ 3 ms per tick.
- EC-3 [integration] Given the AI scenario suite, when run, then every scenario is deterministic and green.
- EC-4 [e2e] Given the grey-box fight room, when the player fights fixture guards, then guards patrol, detect, fight and search without errors.

title: E00 — Project Foundation
description:
## Outcome
A trustworthy engineering foundation: every change lands through a green, coverage-gated, security-scanned PR; the sim core is deterministic and replayable; content is schema-validated; a greybox testbed boots in the chosen engine; and a public backlog.html always shows what is done and what is next.
## Scope
- In: Repo scaffold (TS strict, Vite, pnpm), lint/format/typecheck, Vitest + Playwright
- In: CI pipeline with per-layer coverage thresholds, ratchet, determinism lint, secret scanning, dependency CVE gate
- In: Branch protection, PR template with Closes lines, CHANGELOG, coverage-exclusions.md process
- In: backlog.html generator + GitHub Pages deploy
- In: Engine ADR spike (Three.js vs Babylon.js incl. physics/Rapier)
- In: Deterministic sim core, state hashing, replay harness, content pipeline, greybox testbed
- Out: Gameplay systems (E02+)
- Out: Save/load (mw-e30)
- Out: Perf budget suite beyond the baseline scene (mw-e32)
- Out: Debug console and content tools (mw-e33)
## Exit criteria
- A PR that lowers coverage, calls Math.random in src/sim, leaks a secret, or adds a CRITICAL CVE dependency is blocked by required checks.
- backlog.html on GitHub Pages reflects a merged PR's Closes lines within one workflow run of the merge.
- ADR-0001 records the engine + physics choice with measured evidence from the reference machine.
- The greybox testbed boots in Chrome, Firefox and Safari with zero console errors and a replay test reproduces identical sim state hashes.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 A PR that lowers coverage, calls Math.random in src/sim, leaks a secret, or adds a CRITICAL CVE dependency is blocked by required checks.
- EC-2 backlog.html on GitHub Pages reflects a merged PR's Closes lines within one workflow run of the merge.
- EC-3 ADR-0001 records the engine + physics choice with measured evidence from the reference machine.
- EC-4 The greybox testbed boots in Chrome, Firefox and Safari with zero console errors and a replay test reproduces identical sim state hashes.

title: E30 — Save/Load
description:
## Outcome
Browser-safe saves reliably preserve character and world state across sessions, browser restarts and game updates; a corrupted or interrupted save never costs the player all their progress.
## Scope
- In: Versioned save envelope, sim-state serialization via a section registry, migrations
- In: IndexedDB storage with fallback, slots, autosave, quicksave, death→reload flow
- In: Corruption recovery, multi-tab guard, export/import, save/load UI
- Out: Cloud saves / accounts (post-MVP, not planned)
- Out: World-fact modelling itself (see e27-world-state-store)
## Exit criteria
- Every save schema change ships with a migration and a committed fixture that CI loads successfully.
- Killing the tab mid-write never leaves zero loadable saves (automated test).
- Save/load code paths have 100% coverage.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 Every save schema change ships with a migration and a committed fixture that CI loads successfully.
- EC-2 Killing the tab mid-write never leaves zero loadable saves (automated test).
- EC-3 Save/load code paths have 100% coverage.

title: E27 — Dynamic World State
description:
## Outcome
Meaningful actions persist: doors opened, walls smashed, ropes burned, chests looted, creatures befriended, treasures stolen, characters helped. A typed, deterministic world-fact store plus per-entity deltas against authored baselines captures the world as the player left it and flows through e30 save serialization. Quests, dialogue, puzzles and level variants all read the same facts.
## Scope
- In: Typed world-fact store (e27-world-state-store) with registry, change events and deterministic ordering
- In: Entity delta persistence (moved/broken/burned/looted/dead) relative to authored level baselines
- In: Save/load integration and migrations via e30, fact query/condition API shared by quests/dialogue/puzzles
- In: Persistence policies (permanent/rest-reset/transient), offscreen elapsed-time catch-up, fact-gated world variants
- In: Ownership/theft facts, debug inspector, size/perf budgets
- Out: Save file format, IndexedDB storage and migration framework — see e30-save-serialization
- Out: Quest and dialogue runtimes — see e23-quest-runtime, e22-dialogue-runtime (they consume facts)
- Out: Crime/witness reactions — see mw-e11 / mw-e10
## Exit criteria
- Smashing a wall, burning a rope bridge, looting a chest and befriending a creature, then save → reload (and full browser restart) restores all four exactly (e2e).
- World state for 10,000 facts + 5,000 entity deltas serializes in ≤ 50 ms and ≤ 1 MB compressed.
- Every fact written at runtime is declared in the content fact registry; undeclared writes fail tests.
- src/sim world-state code and save integration at 100% coverage with round-trip and migration tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 Smashing a wall, burning a rope bridge, looting a chest and befriending a creature, then save → reload (and full browser restart) restores all four exactly (e2e).
- EC-2 World state for 10,000 facts + 5,000 entity deltas serializes in ≤ 50 ms and ≤ 1 MB compressed.
- EC-3 Every fact written at runtime is declared in the content fact registry; undeclared writes fail tests.
- EC-4 src/sim world-state code and save integration at 100% coverage with round-trip and migration tests.

title: E02 — Core Character Controller
description:
## Outcome
Movement, camera, jumping, climbing, stance, interaction, targeting and animation hooks feel excellent and responsive on keyboard + mouse (gamepad second). All movement rules live in src/sim as a deterministic kinematic controller driven by abstract input actions, so replays, AI and tests share the exact same rules the player feels.
## Scope
- In: Remappable input action layer (KB/M, then gamepad) producing deterministic per-tick action frames
- In: Kinematic third-person controller: walk/run/sprint, jump, gravity, slopes, steps, crouch stance
- In: Traversal verbs: ledge mantle/grab, climbable surfaces, wading/swimming, walking on ice, external impulses
- In: Third-person camera with collision, lock-on targeting, contextual interact/focus verb, carry/push objects
- In: Animation state + footstep event hooks, controller tuning data, latency and determinism verification
- Out: Combat moves (attack/block/parry/dodge) — see mw-e04 (e04-melee-core)
- Out: Bow aiming camera specifics — see mw-e05 (e05-bow-core)
- Out: Stealth visibility/noise scoring — see mw-e09 (consumes stance and footstep hooks from this epic)
- Out: Final character models and animation clips — see mw-e37
## Exit criteria
- Input-to-motion latency ≤ 100 ms (p95) measured by Playwright on the reference machine; controller sim cost ≤ 0.3 ms per tick.
- A recorded 60 s traversal replay (run, jump, mantle, climb, crouch, swim) reproduces an identical sim state hash on every CI run.
- All controller rules in src/sim at 100% coverage; every tuning value lives in schema-validated content data.
- A playtester can traverse the greybox traversal course (e00-greybox-testbed) using only KB/M and, separately, only a gamepad.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 Input-to-motion latency ≤ 100 ms (p95) measured by Playwright on the reference machine; controller sim cost ≤ 0.3 ms per tick.
- EC-2 A recorded 60 s traversal replay (run, jump, mantle, climb, crouch, swim) reproduces an identical sim state hash on every CI run.
- EC-3 All controller rules in src/sim at 100% coverage; every tuning value lives in schema-validated content data.
- EC-4 A playtester can traverse the greybox traversal course (e00-greybox-testbed) using only KB/M and, separately, only a gamepad.

title: E03 — Systemic Interaction Engine
description:
## Outcome
Doors, switches, movable objects, breakables, fire, water, ice, electricity, gas, light, physics and triggers form one reusable, property-based world simulation. Nothing is scripted pairwise: objects declare properties (flammable, wet, frozen, conductive, weight, fragile, climbable, liftable, hideable, reflective…) and elements propagate by rules over those properties, so a spell, an arrow, a torch, a creature and a puzzle all touch the same systems. This is the architectural heart of "Wait… I can do that?".
## Scope
- In: Typed world-property components + data-defined material presets
- In: A single stimulus API that spells, arrows, weapons, creatures and environment all use to inject heat, water, cold, charge, force, gas and light
- In: Element propagation rules: fire/heat, water/wetness, freezing/melting, electricity, gas, wind/force
- In: Light field (queryable light level per position), extinguishable/ignitable light sources, redirectable light beams
- In: Physics objects (movable, throwable, stackable, breakable, liftable/levitatable, buoyant), ropes/supports
- In: Doors, locks, levers, pressure plates, shootable mechanisms, trigger volumes and data-wired signal logic
- In: Hiding places and containers; climbable surface markup; actor participation in properties
- In: Interaction-matrix property-test harness, emergence scenario replays, debug overlays and perf budgets
- Out: Specific spells/arrows/abilities — see mw-e06/e08, mw-e05, mw-e10 (they emit stimuli through this epic)
- Out: Stealth scoring and AI perception — see mw-e09/mw-e11 (they query the light field and receive world noise events)
- Out: Puzzle authoring and solvability — see mw-e15
- Out: Persistence of world changes — see mw-e27
## Exit criteria
- No code path in src/sim or src/content references a pair of specific object types to produce an interaction; a lint/grep check in CI enforces that interaction rules read only properties.
- The interaction-matrix harness property-tests every element × property combination and runs in CI in ≤ 60 s.
- The greybox "chaos room" scenario library (≥ 12 emergent combos) replays deterministically to identical state hashes.
- Element simulation costs ≤ 2.0 ms per tick p95 with 2,000 active cells on the reference machine.
- src/sim portions at 100% coverage.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 No code path in src/sim or src/content references a pair of specific object types to produce an interaction; a lint/grep check in CI enforces that interaction rules read only properties.
- EC-2 The interaction-matrix harness property-tests every element × property combination and runs in CI in ≤ 60 s.
- EC-3 The greybox "chaos room" scenario library (≥ 12 emergent combos) replays deterministically to identical state hashes.
- EC-4 Element simulation costs ≤ 2.0 ms per tick p95 with 2,000 active cells on the reference machine.
- EC-5 src/sim portions at 100% coverage.

title: E04 — Knight Combat
description:
## Outcome
Sword/shield gameplay supports attack chains, blocks, parries, dodges, stagger, heavy/charged attacks, shield bashes, weapon reach, armor trade-offs and satisfying hit reactions — and a greybox skeleton fight is fun with no rewards. The shared damage model underpins every class.

## Scope
- In: damage model (types, resistances, poise, modifiers), hit volumes, move data, action timeline, stamina, light chain, block, parry/riposte, dodge/i-frames, heavy/charged, shield bash, reach classes, armor weight, hit-stop, hit reactions, knight world verbs (smash, kick), environmental damage, creature attack hooks, combat sandbox, combat HUD, golden replays, assists, fun validation.
- Out: thief backstab/stealth attacks (thief group), spells (magic group), creature AI decisions (e11), bestiary content (e13), final animation/art/audio assets (art/audio group).

## Exit criteria
- All combat rules live in src/sim/combat with 100% coverage and golden replays.
- Skeleton fun validation spike passes, or its tuning beads are complete and a re-run passes.
- Combat sandbox covers every knight verb for manual tuning.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 src/sim/combat reports 100% coverage and the golden combat replay suite is green in CI.
- EC-2 docs/playtests/skeleton-fun-01.md (or a later re-run) records PASS against the stated bar.
- EC-3 A knight can break a weak wall, kick a brazier into flammables and shove a creature off a ledge in the greybox testbed without scripted pairings.

title: Owner review: accept or reject ADR-0006 (pure-TS navmesh vs recast-navigation-js)
description:
## Why
mw-e11.4 (PR #162) shipped a pure-TypeScript navmesh bake and A* and recorded the choice as ADR-0006, status Proposed.

## What
Owner reads docs/adr/0006-navmesh-and-pathfinding.md and accepts (flip status to Accepted) or rejects (file a migration bead to recast-navigation-js).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1 [manual] ADR-0006 status is Accepted or Rejected with the owner's decision recorded.

title: Run creature AI on the scene's navmesh in the game loop
description:
## Why
mw-e11.4 delivers navmesh paths and navmeshNavigation (an AiNavigation port), but the game does not run creature AI in scenes yet, so nothing in play uses them.

## What
When a scene with a baked navmesh loads, build a NavMesh from content navmesh/<scene>, door states from the loaded door spawns (worldNavDoors), and install AI with navmeshNavigation so patrols and investigations walk real paths through doors and up climbs.

## Scope
- In: scene-load wiring in src/game, unload/reload, a Playwright check that a patrolling creature goes through a doorway
- Out: new behaviours (mw-e11.9+)

## Notes
Related: src/sim/nav/navigation.ts, src/sim/nav/doors.ts, src/game/scene/scene-loader.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the testbed with a patrolling creature whose route crosses a doorway, when the scene runs 30 s headless, then the creature passes through the doorway and never leaves the navmesh.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the grey-box testbed in the browser, when a creature patrols, then no console errors occur and its position stays on the navmesh.

title: Install noise propagation at scene load and route AI emit-noise through noiseEmitted
description:
## Why

mw-e09.3 built sound propagation in the sim, but nothing in the running game installs it, and AI behaviours' emit-noise step raises its own AiNoiseEmitted instead of the shared noiseEmitted channel, so guards' noises are not propagated.

## What

When a scene loads, the game builds its sound graph (soundGraphFromScene) and installs noise propagation with the shipped stealth noise tuning and door materials; a level change swaps the graph. The AI emit-noise primitive raises noiseEmitted (kind ai, source the agent) so its noises propagate like any other.

## Scope

- In: Game wiring at scene load and unload
- In: AI emit-noise on the shared channel
- Out: Listener perception (mw-e11.5)
- Out: Audio occlusion playback (mw-e28.10)

## Notes

Replay fixtures may need re-recording if the AI change alters event order.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the mechanism room loaded in the game, when a pot breaks in the west closet with its door shut, then a listener in the hall receives noiseHeard via west-doorway.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a behaviour with an emit-noise step, when it runs, then a noiseEmitted with the agent as source is raised.

title: Integration test: burnt rope bridge stays gone across a level round-trip
description:
## Why
mw-e27.3 AC-5 was covered only partially in PR #158 (weak-wall room, scene reload) because the slice has no rope bridge or area transitions yet.

## What
Once area transitions (mw-e01.11) exist and the greybox slice has a burnable rope bridge, add the integration test: burn the bridge, leave the level, return; bridge still gone and replay hashes match.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1 [integration] Given the greybox slice, when the player burns a rope bridge, leaves the level and returns, then the bridge is still gone and replay hashes match.

title: Assign stable GUIDs to scene placements and lint orphaned persistent ids
description:
## Why
mw-e27.3 (PR #158) keys authored-entity deltas by placement index (piece:<n>), so reordering placements in a scene orphans their deltas. The bead's notes require GUIDs assigned by the level pipeline and a lint that warns when a persistent entity id disappears.

## What
Give every scene placement an authored, stable id (GUID) assigned by tooling; switch sceneAuthoredEntities to use it; add a content lint that diffs ids against the previous build and warns on removed persistent ids.
acceptance_criteria:
AC-1 [unit] Reordering placements in a scene leaves every authored entity id unchanged.
AC-2 [content] Removing a placement that had an id in the committed lock produces a lint warning naming it.
AC-3 [unit] Existing piece:<n> deltas migrate to GUID ids via the save migration runner.

title: Bind the four quick slots to default keys and pad buttons
description:
## Why
mw-e17.6 shipped four quick slots (sim: Consumables.useSlot, useQuickSlotCommand) but no buttons use them: keys 1-4 and the d-pad are already ability1-4 (docs/design/controls.md), so binding them needs an owner layout decision.
## What
Pick the default keyboard and pad bindings for quick slots 1-4 (e.g. a modifier + 1-4, F1-F4, or d-pad with abilities moved), add quickSlot1-4 actions to the ActionFrame registry, and have the consumables system read them (consumablesSystem input option).
## Scope
- In: actions, default bindings, remapping conflicts, controls doc
- Out: quick-slot HUD (mw-e17.10)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Pressing the quick slot 1 binding uses quick slot 1 (item.used with slot 0).
- AC-2 [unit] The default bindings have no conflicts in the gameplay context.

title: Grant item capabilities while carried through the capability registry
description:
## Why

Tools such as the climbing hook declare grants with `while: carried` (ADR-0004), but nothing grants them yet: mw-e17.3's inventory model holds items without touching capabilities (discovered while implementing mw-e17.3).

## What

When the first unit of a definition with `while: carried` grants enters an actor's inventory, grant each capability through CapabilityRegistry (src/sim/progression/capabilities.ts) with source `tool:<defId>`; revoke when its last unit leaves. Driven by item.added / item.removed or inside InventoryRules.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an actor without verb.climb.rough, when a climbing hook is added, then the actor has it from source tool:<id> and capability.gained is emitted once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given two hooks carried, when one is removed, then the capability stays; when the second is removed, capability.lost is emitted.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an inventory with carried grants, when saved and loaded, then capability sources and inventory agree and the state hash matches.

title: Stop replay goldens conflicting on contentHash in every content PR
description:
## Why
Every PR that touches content changes the content hash stored in each replay golden and in tests/integration/fixtures/testbed-player.replay.json. With parallel PRs this forces a rebase + rebless on every merge (PRs #139-#146 each rebased 2-3 times just for this), and costs CI minutes.

## What
Decouple outcome checking from the content hash: e.g. store the content hash in a single generated file, or have goldens record per-system content fingerprints only for content they use, or warn (not fail) on a hash mismatch when replayed outcomes and final state hashes are identical. Keep detection of real behaviour changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given two PRs that each add unrelated content, when the second is rebased onto the first, then no replay golden or fixture file conflicts.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a content change that alters a replay's outcome, when tests run, then the replay check still fails.

title: hasCapability must honour replacing unlocks (subsumed capabilities stay usable)
description:
## Why
ADR-0004 says a replacing unlock must subsume the capability it replaces (Telekinesis still pulls levers like Mage Hand). PR #143 (mw-e19.3) revokes the replaced capability's learned source and only UnlockBook.knows follows the replacement chain; hasCapability used by puzzles, traversal and other checks does not. Authoring any replacement chain today would break checks on the replaced id.

## What
Make the registry's capability query treat a capability as held when a held capability replaces it (transitively), or keep the replaced grant; one source of truth for every caller.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given spell.telekinesis learned as a replacement of spell.mage-hand, when a puzzle checks hasCapability(actor, spell.mage-hand), then it returns true.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a replacement chain A→B→C with only C held, when any caller queries A, then it is held.

title: Placeholder audio pack is at ~2000 of its 2048 KB budget
description:
## Why
PR #142 (mw-e04.20) left the generated placeholder SFX pack at about 2000 KB of its 2048 KB budget. The next few cue additions will fail CI.

## What
Shrink the placeholders (lower sample rate/bit depth or shorter durations for placeholder-only sounds, or dedupe shared ones) or, if the budget itself is wrong for the placeholder phase, raise it with a recorded reason. Placeholders must still be keyed by final asset ids.
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [content] Given the placeholder audio pack, when CI's audio placeholder check runs, then the pack uses at most 60% of its budget and every cue still resolves to a sound.

title: Record owner review of ADR-0003 to ADR-0005
description:
## Why
The owner reviewed the three ADRs from the 2026-10-02 spikes and changed one number; the ADR files and dependent beads must match.

## What
ADR-0003: non-knight armor capacity 23 kg (plate Heavy for all classes); fix heading numbering. ADR-0004: fix cross-references. ADR-0005: status Accepted. Update mw-e17.13 to 23 kg.
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [content] Given the ADRs, when read, then ADR-0003 uses 23 kg non-knight capacity with recomputed load tables, all three headings match their file numbers, and ADR-0005 is Accepted.

title: Lint behaviour definitions: unreachable states, dead activities, no exit
description:
## Why
ADR-0003 makes creature behaviour pure data (HFSM alert states + utility activities). Data mistakes that load fine but strand a guard (a state nothing reaches, an activity no state lists, a state with no way out) would only show up in playtests; a thief exploiting a guard stuck in Suspicious forever is a bug, not a story.

## What
As a designer, I want behaviour definitions checked for structural mistakes when content is validated so that a broken behaviour fails CI instead of a playtest. A content check over every behaviour file (and the tuning it resolves) that reports, with the behaviour id and the offending name: states unreachable from `initial`; states with neither a timeout nor any outgoing transition (except Combat, which must have a lost-target exit); activities not listed by any state; listed activities whose considerations can never score above 0 (a step or linear curve that is 0 over the input's declared range); `done`/`failed` conditions naming an activity the state does not list.

## Scope
- In: Content check run by `pnpm content:schemas`/content tests, input ranges declared by the input registry
- In: Fixture behaviours that trigger each error
- Out: Runtime loading errors for unknown names (mw-e11.2 AC-2)
- Out: Fuzzing the transition table at runtime (mw-e11.7 AC-6)

## Notes
Related: docs/adr/0003-ai-architecture.md (Consequences, runtime semantics). Pure functions over the parsed definition, 100% covered like the rest of src/content.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given a behaviour whose Searching state is listed but no transition or timeout leads to it, when validated, then validation fails naming the behaviour id and "searching" as unreachable.
- AC-2 [content] Given a non-Combat state with no timeout and no transitions, when validated, then validation fails naming the state as having no exit.
- AC-3 [content] Given an activity defined but listed by no state, when validated, then validation fails naming the activity.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an activity whose only consideration is a step curve returning 0 across the input's declared range, when checked, then it is reported as never selectable.
- AC-5 [content] Given a transition `{ "done": "investigate" }` in a state that does not list `investigate`, when validated, then validation fails naming both.
- AC-6 [content] Given every shipped and fixture behaviour definition, when validated, then no error is reported.

title: Offer a one-time health, stamina or mana boon choice at shrines
description:
## Why
ADR-0004 grows health, stamina and mana only from one-time shrines and found boon items. `mw-e19.6` implements the stat layers and fixed-stat sources; nothing yet offers the shrine's choice, which is the player's only say in how their supporting stats grow.

## What
As a player, I want to find a shrine and choose whether it strengthens my health, stamina or mana so that a rare discovery fits how I play.

A shrine is a world entity with `once: true`. Interacting opens a choice of +10 health, +10 stamina or +10 mana; a stat at cap is shown but unavailable. Choosing applies the step through `mw-e19.6`, records a world-state fact so the shrine stays spent across save and load, and emits `stat.boon`. A shrine is a discovery, not a rest point.

## Scope
- In: Shrine component and schema, choice flow on the minimal UI, spent fact, events, a grey-box shrine in the testbed
- Out: Stat model and boon items (`mw-e19.6`); shrine art and story names (`mw-e37`, `mw-e39`); world placement (content epics)

## Notes
MVP budget: 8 shrines. Story names must not reuse "relic" (Vane's shipments).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an unspent shrine and max stamina 100, when the player chooses stamina, then max stamina is 110, current stamina rises by 10 and stat.boon is emitted once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a spent shrine, when the player interacts, then no choice is offered and stats are unchanged.
- AC-3 [unit] Given max health at its cap of 200, when the shrine choice opens, then health is listed as unavailable and cannot be chosen (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given all three stats at cap, when the player interacts, then the shrine is not spent and reports at-cap.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a spent shrine, when the game is saved and loaded, then the shrine is still spent.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the grey-box testbed shrine, when the player chooses mana, then the mana HUD maximum increases by 10 with no console errors.

title: Enforce the cross-class simple-capability rule in the learn API
description:
## Why
ADR-0004 allows a knight to read an easy spellbook and a sorcerer to learn a basic shield bash, but only for *simple* capabilities. The rule must live once in the shared learn API, not be re-implemented in each channel (`mw-e19.7`–`mw-e19.10` each say "per the ADR cross-learning rule").

## What
As a knight, I want to learn an easy spell from a book I found so that my curiosity is rewarded, while the sorcerer's deeper chains stay hers.

`learn(capId, channel)` checks, for a learner whose class differs from the capability's affinity: the capability is a chain root, its unlock sets `crossClass: true`, it is within the channel bound (book: difficulty ≤ 0.3, mana cost ≤ 20, licensed school; trainer: stamina cost ≤ 25, no proficiency; schematic: shop-sold materials, any bow; trick: no tool or trick required; tool: grant flagged crossClass) and it is not in the home class's signature list. A refusal returns reason `off-class` with an in-fiction explanation key, and the source (book, schematic, note) is not consumed.

## Scope
- In: Cross-class check in the learn API, refusal reasons and text keys, class `signature` list in class data
- Out: Content validation of crossClass flags (`mw-e19.15`); channel adapters' own tests (`mw-e19.7`–`mw-e19.10`)

## Notes
See `docs/adr/0004-progression-model.md`, "Cross-class learning: the simple rule".
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a knight and a crossClass root spell with difficulty 0.2 and mana cost 15, when learned from a book, then the capability is granted with channel book.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a knight and spell.flame-jet (has prerequisites), when learned from a book, then learning fails with reason off-class and the book is not consumed.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a sorcerer and the knight's signature technique.parry, when offered by a trainer, then learning fails with reason off-class and no gold is deducted.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a thief and a crossClass schematic whose arrow needs shop-sold materials, when read, then the arrow is learned with channel schematic.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an off-class learner and an unlock without crossClass: true that otherwise meets every bound, when learned, then it fails with reason off-class (edge).

title: Validate progression content against the ADR-0004 anti-grind rules
description:
## Why
ADR-0004 defines eight content rules (P1–P8) that keep progression about verbs. `mw-e19.3` AC-6 covers numeric-only unlocks and cycles and `mw-e07.8` covers spell chains; the rest (narrow `supporting`, one-time stat sources, cross-class bounds, no exclusive unlocks, reachability, no XP fields) have no validator yet, so content could quietly reintroduce grind.

## What
As a designer, I want `pnpm content:check` to reject progression data that breaks the anti-grind rule so that a bad unlock fails in CI with the rule id, entry and file.

Implement rules P2 and P4–P8 from `docs/adr/0004-progression-model.md` and generalize P3 (each chain step is a new verb) from spells to techniques, arrows, tools and tricks. Every message names the rule id, the entry id and the file.

## Scope
- In: Validator rules over capability, unlock, trainer, schematic, tool, trick, deed, stat-source and class data; fixtures for each rule
- Out: The P1 numeric-only rule and cycle check already in `mw-e19.3`; spell chain check in `mw-e07.8`; runtime learn API (`mw-e19.16`)

## Notes
MVP stat budget is 8 shrines and 6 boon items; stat steps are exactly +10; caps 200 (ADR-0004 stats table).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given a stat source entry granting +15 max health, when validated, then validation fails with rule P5 naming the entry and file.
- AC-2 [content] Given an unlock flagged supporting: true that targets spell.firebolt, when validated, then validation fails with rule P2.
- AC-3 [content] Given a technique chain step whose move, ops and stimuli equal its predecessor's and differ only in damage, when validated, then validation fails with rule P3.
- AC-4 [content] Given a crossClass: true unlock with a prerequisite, or one listed in its class's signature capabilities, when validated, then validation fails with rule P6.
- AC-5 [content] Given an unlock declaring excludes, or a replacing unlock with no subsumes, when validated, then validation fails with rule P7.
- AC-6 [content] Given a capability that no book, trainer, schematic, tool, trick, deed, item or class grants, when validated, then validation fails with rule P8 naming the capability.
- AC-7 [content] Given any content entry with an xp, level or skillPoints field, when validated, then validation fails with rule P4.

title: Handle carried world objects on stagger, climbing, scene exit and save
description:
## Why
ADR-0003 keeps crates, bodies and statues out of the inventory: they are carried physically. Carrying already exists as a verb (`mw-e02.17`, `mw-e10.5`), but the edge cases the ADR lists (stagger, ladders, scene exits, saves, lost quest objects) have no owner, and failure should create a new situation rather than a stuck one.

## What
As a player, I want a carried crate or body to behave predictably when I am hit, try to climb, leave the area or save so that carrying never traps me or loses the quest.

- A hit that breaks poise or staggers the carrier drops the held object at their feet.
- Grabbing a ladder, rope, ivy or ledge while carrying is refused with "Hands full"; picking up a second world object while carrying is refused the same way; taking a small item goes to the pack.
- Exiting a scene while carrying drops the object at the threshold on the near side.
- A save written while carrying stores the object placed at the carrier's feet; on load the player is not carrying.
- Quest-critical world objects declare a `recovery` anchor; destroyed or out of bounds, they return there and emit `object.recovered`.
- Shoulder-carry (bodies, `bulky`) moves at ×0.5 for every class; hand-carry at ×0.85 with no sprint. Multipliers stack with the armor load class.

## Scope
- In: Drop-on-stagger, traversal and pickup refusals, scene-exit drop, save placement, recovery anchors and their validator check, shared carry speed values
- Out: Lift, throw and push mechanics (`mw-e02.17`, `mw-e02.18`); hiding bodies (`mw-e10.5`)

## Notes
Related: `mw-e10.5` AC-1 states ×0.6 for bodies; ADR-0003 sets ×0.5 for all classes, so that AC is updated when this lands.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player hand-carrying a crate, when a hit staggers them, then the crate is released at their feet in the same tick and the carry state ends.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player carrying a body, when they interact with a ladder, then the grab is refused with reason hands-full and the body stays carried.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player carrying a crate across a scene exit, when the new scene loads, then the crate exists in the origin scene at the threshold and the player is not carrying.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the player carrying a body, when the game is saved and loaded, then the body is a placed world object at the save position and the player is not carrying.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a quest-critical world object that falls below the scene kill plane, when resolved, then it reappears at its recovery anchor and emits object.recovered once.
- AC-6 [content] Given a world object flagged questCritical without a recovery anchor, when validated, then validation fails naming the entity and file.
- AC-7 [unit] Given a Heavy-load knight shoulder-carrying a body, when running, then speed is 2.25 m/s ± 0.01.

title: Apply armor load class to speed, sprint, jump, climbing and armor swaps
description:
## Why
ADR-0003 makes armor the only weight in the game: the heavy knight should be slower, tire sooner and lose rope and ivy routes, while the thief in leather keeps every verb. `mw-e04.16` covers rolls, regen, poise and noise; nothing yet applies the load class to running, sprinting, jumping, climbing or armor swaps.

## What
As a knight, I want my armor's load class to change how I move and climb so that putting on plate is a real choice, not a bigger number.

From the derived `EquipmentState.loadClass` (`mw-e17.4`), apply the ADR-0003 table: run/sprint/crouch speed multipliers (Medium ×0.95, Heavy ×0.9, Overloaded walk only ≤ 2.4 m/s), sprint drain (×1.15 / ×1.3 / no sprint), climb drain (×1.25 / ×1.5 / ×2.0), jump height (×0.95 / ×0.85 / ×0.7), climbing allowed surfaces (Heavy and Overloaded: ladders only, others refused "Too heavy to climb"). Armor and shield equip changes are refused while in Combat (reason `in-combat`) or while climbing, hanging or carrying (reason `busy`); weapons, ammo and tools still swap.

## Scope
- In: Load class multipliers in controller, stamina and climb tuning as content data; climb surface gate; armor-swap refusal rules
- Out: Roll profiles, regen, poise and noise (`mw-e04.16`); pull-up refusal (`mw-e02.34`); footstep noise (`mw-e09.5`)

## Notes
Numbers and the table live in `docs/adr/0003-encumbrance-model.md`. Load ratio = equipped armor kg / class armor capacity (knight 30, others 23).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a Heavy load class, when the player runs and sprints, then horizontal speed is 4.5 m/s and 6.75 m/s ± 0.01 and sprint drains stamina at 13/s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an Overloaded load class, when sprint is held, then the player stays at walk speed ≤ 2.4 m/s and no stamina is drained for sprinting.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a Heavy load class, when the player walks into ivy or a rope, then the grab is refused with reason too-heavy; a ladder grab succeeds and drains climb stamina at 7.5/s.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a Medium load class, when the player jumps, then apex height is 0.95 × the Light apex height ± 1%.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a creature in Combat with the player, when body armor is equipped, then it fails with reason in-combat and equipment is unchanged; a weapon swap in the same state succeeds.
- AC-6 [unit] Given the player is climbing, when a shield is unequipped, then it fails with reason busy (edge).
- AC-7 [content] Given the load class tuning data, when validated, then every load class defines every multiplier and all multipliers are in (0, 1].

title: Show a slice-complete card and return to the title
description:
## Why
The slice must end on a clear beat. Without one a player who walks through the exit wonders whether they finished, and the e01-slice-playtest measure "reached slice complete" needs a moment testers can see.

## What
As a player, I want a short "Slice complete" card when I walk through the exit so that I know I finished and can go back to the title.

When the world fact `slice.complete` becomes true, input is released to the UI and a grey-box card shows "Slice complete", the run time and the class, with "Return to title" focused. The sim keeps no further state. The completion autosave (e01-slice-save-points) happens before the card shows, so Continue from the title loads the completed slice.

## Scope
- In: Card on the e00-ui-framework kit, run timer readout, return to title, keyboard/gamepad focus
- Out: Ending screens, credits and music (E39/E38)
- Out: The slice.complete trigger and fact (e01-slice-greybox-level, mw-e01.4)

## Notes
Spec: docs/design/vertical-slice.md §3 (beat B8). The e2e pass condition is the fact, not this card.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given slice.complete flips to true, when the next frame renders, then the card shows with "Return to title" focused and player input no longer moves the knight.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a run from New Game at tick 0 to completion at tick 9000 (60 Hz), when the card renders, then it shows 2:30.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the card, when "Return to title" is chosen, then the title shows with zero console errors and Continue loads the completion save.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the completion autosave is vetoed or fails, when the card shows, then it states that the run was not saved instead of claiming it was (edge).

title: Restart the slice from its start when the player dies with no save
description:
## Why
"Failure creates stories" (CONSTITUTION §2), and failure must never strand the player. A death before the slice's first checkpoint (or with no save at all) leaves no save to reload; e30-death-reload then offers "Restart area", and in the slice that button needs a defined result.

## What
As a player, I want "Restart area" on the death screen to put me back at the slice's start with my class kit so that dying before any save never leaves me stuck.

Restart area tears the world down and runs the same hand-off New Game uses (e01-title-new-game-flow): load `game.startScene` at its player-start spawn and apply the class chosen this session (e19-class-selection), with fresh world facts. It writes no save itself; the slice's first checkpoint then autosaves as normal.

## Scope
- In: Restart-area action in the slice, re-use of the New Game hand-off, class kept from the session
- Out: Death screen and option ordering (e30-death-reload, mw-e30.7)
- Out: Respawn-rule resolver (e01-death-respawn-loop, mw-e01.8)

## Notes
Spec: docs/design/vertical-slice.md §6 (failure F2). In normal play the slice's first checkpoint (CP-1, the spawn-room door) autosaves within seconds, so this path is mostly reached with the debug console's kill command or a fresh profile where storage failed.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given no saves exist and the knight dies in the spawn room, when "Restart area" is chosen, then the slice reloads at player-start, player.class = knight, the knight kit is equipped and every slice fact has its default.
- AC-2 [integration] Given Restart area completes, when the sim state hash is taken, then it equals the hash of a New Game as knight at tick 0 (same seed).
- AC-3 [e2e] Given a clean profile and a death before CP-1, when "Restart area" is chosen, then the slice is playable within 3 s warm with zero console errors.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the session has no chosen class (state lost or corrupted), when Restart area runs, then it returns to the title screen instead of throwing and logs a warning (edge).

title: Wire the bow and arrows into the game world with the aim camera
description:
## Why

The bow rules (mw-e05.3) and arrow ballistics (mw-e05.2) run in the sim, but nothing in the game world flies arrows yet, so the archer fantasy (precision at range) cannot be felt or tested in a browser.

## What

As an archer, I want to take out the bow in the testbed and shoot so that draw, aim and release can be felt and tuned.
Install the arrow system (installArrows) in the game world with the physics collision query; give the testbed player the shortbow and a quiver (installPlayer `combat.bow`); render loosed and stuck arrows as grey-box shafts; ease the orbit camera's FOV from 70 deg to the bow's `aim.fov` (55 deg) over `aim.time` while `isDrawing`, and back out on release; show the selected arrow type and quiver count in the `?frames` overlay.

## Scope

- In: game/render wiring of arrows and the bow, aim-mode camera FOV, quiver readout.
- Out: sway and reticle (mw-e05.5), the archery range (mw-e05.14), final arrow art and VFX (mw-e29.11).

## Notes

Discovered from mw-e05.3. The sim side (BowComponent, bowSystem, lookAim, bowLocomotionScale) is done; this is glue in src/game, src/render and src/main.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the testbed player with the shortbow, when the toggle is pressed and fire is held 48 ticks and released, then an arrow entity flies from the nock point and an ArrowFired event is emitted.
