- AC-2 [unit] Given the bow drawn, when the camera updates, then its vertical FOV eases from 70 deg toward the bow's aim.fov (55 deg), reaching about two thirds of the way in aim.time seconds, and eases back after release.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the testbed in Chromium, when Playwright takes out the bow and looses an arrow at a wall, then the arrow renders stuck in the wall and no console errors occur.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an empty quiver for the selected type, when fire is pressed, then the overlay shows 0 for that type and no arrow renders.

title: Creatures stand on the ground and get knocked back through a character controller
description:
## Why

Spawned creatures (mw-e12.4) are placed entities: they have no body in the controller or physics world, so they do not fall to the ground from a raised spawn, and hit reactions compute knockbacks and launches for them that nothing applies (the pushers act on the player's CharacterController and physics objects only). The constitution wants creatures that are creatures, not target dummies.

## What

Give each spawned creature a kinematic character body sized from its nav agent (radius, height, step height, max slope) so it stands on and collides with the level, and apply hit-reaction pushes to it like the player's. Locomotion speeds stay AI's (e11) business.

## Scope

- In: per-creature controller capsule from its locomotion; gravity; knockback/launch pushes.
- Out: pathfinding (mw-e11.4), AI steering.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given fixture-hound spawned 2 m above the floor, when 60 ticks pass, then it stands on the floor.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a knockback-tier hit on fixture-guard, when the reaction plays, then the guard moves away from the attacker and never through a wall.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the same seed and inputs, two runs hash identically.

title: Knight's light swing passes over short creatures like the 0.9 m fixture hound
description:
## Why

Found while wiring creature spawning (mw-e12.4): the knight's light attack, swung at a fixture-hound (0.9 m tall, hurtbox capsule 0–0.9 m) standing 1.2 m in front of him, never connects, while the same swing at the 1.8 m fixture-guard at the same distance does. Hounds, rats, goblins and other low creatures must be hittable with the knight's basic attack, or the player has no answer to them.

## What

Decide (owner/design) how low creatures are hit: angle the light chain's socket track lower, add a downward/low attack, or auto-aim the swing's height at the locked target. Then make it so.

## Scope

- In: knight melee reaching low targets; a test with a short creature.
- Out: creature hurtbox regions per rig (asset beads).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given fixture-hound 1.2 m in front of the knight, when he performs the light attack (locked on or not), then it deals damage to the hound.
- AC-2 [integration] Given fixture-guard at the same distance, the light attack still hits as today.

title: Bind arrow flight and impact events to the cue sheets for audio and VFX
description:
## Why

Arrow impacts must be heard and seen: a thunk into wood, a clang off stone, a flyby past your head. The sim now emits them (mw-e05.2) but no cue sheet can bind them yet.

## What

Add `ArrowFired` and `arrowImpact` (src/sim/combat/arrows/events.ts, which follow physicsImpact's conventions: entity, other, material, hardness, outcome, energy, impulse, speed, normal, position) to the cue event table (src/content/cue-events.ts) and the game's cue bindings (src/game/cues/events.ts), with the arrow id, outcome and surface impact class as facts, so audio (e28) and VFX (e29.11) cue sheets can pick sounds and puffs by arrow and surface.

## Scope

- In: cue event specs and bindings for arrow fired/impact, contract tests.
- Out: the sounds themselves (e38.28–31), arrow VFX (e29.11).

Discovered from mw-e05.2.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an arrowImpact on stone, when bound, then the cue event carries anchors entity/other/at and facts arrow, outcome, surface impact class, energy and speed.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a cue sheet rule on arrowImpact with outcome ricochet, when a standard arrow ricochets off stone in a sim run, then the rule fires once.
- AC-3 [unit] Given ArrowFired, when bound, then the cue event is anchored at the arrow and carries the arrow id.

title: Parry and riposte cues that are never stolen
description:
## Why

A parry must ring out above everything (Combat is intrinsically fun); mw-e28.4 shipped the impact matrix but the sim has no parry event yet.

## What

When mw-e04.12 emits its parry event, bind it in src/content/cue-events.ts and add a combat cue-sheet rule playing sfx-knight-parry-metal at voice priority 100 (the riposte accent already plays on the riposte tag).

## Scope

- In: cue event binding, cue rule, saturation test
- Out: final parry SFX (mw-e38.12)
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [integration] Given a successful parry during a 48-voice saturation test, when it fires, then the parry cue plays (not stolen) and a lower-priority voice is dropped (carried over from mw-e28.4 AC-2).

title: physics-objects bench p95 near 2.0 ms budget on CI (was 1.24 ms at merge)
description: PR #94 merged tests/bench/physics-objects.bench.ts at ~1.24 ms p95 on CI (budget 2.0 ms). On PR #110's branch CI measured 2.016 and 2.17 ms twice, then passed after rebase. Check CI bench history on main since 6e5bb89 for drift (candidates: onRemove hooks PR #99, scene physics, hit reaction pushers, locomotion). Fix any real regression; if it's runner variance, make the bench measurement robust (retained samples, warm-up) without loosening the budget.

title: Physics-objects bench flakes over its 2.0 ms budget on CI runners
description:
## Why
The mw-e03.10 AC-6 bench (tests/bench/physics-objects.bench.ts, 200 bodies, p95 ≤ 2.0 ms) passes locally at ~0.8 ms but on GitHub runners ranges 0.94–2.18 ms across unrelated branches (main 0.94 and 1.78; feat/knockback-fall-damage 2.02; feat/lock-on 1.56, 2.04, 2.06, 2.18), so PRs fail the unit job at random.

## What
As a developer, I want the perf budget to measure the sim, not runner noise, so that CI failures mean regressions.

## Scope
- In: make the CI measurement stable (warm-up, more ticks, median-of-runs, or a CI-specific reference factor as other benches do) without loosening the reference-machine budget.
- Out: physics performance work itself unless the profile shows a real regression.

## Notes
Found while merging mw-e02.16 (PR #102).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given 10 consecutive CI runs on main, when the bench runs, then none fails while the reference-machine p95 stays ≤ 2.0 ms.
- AC-2 [perf] Given a deliberate 50% slowdown of the physics-object system, when the bench runs on CI, then it fails.
close_reason: Duplicate of mw-w3d; completed in PR #115

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: Seen on PR #107 (mw-e02.15/e04.19): PR-run p95 2.009/2.046/2.022/2.032/2.041 ms (one pass at 1.99) while the same bench locally is 0.80–0.91 ms on both the branch and main (no difference), and other PRs' runs 1.29–1.79. Every bench in those runs was ~2x slower (line of sight 0.28 vs 0.16 ms), so it is runner speed, not the code.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: Duplicate of mw-w3d; fixed by PR #115 (p95 over a fixed 3000-tick window after warm-up). CI after: 1.094 ms on the slow runner class.

title: Investigate vfx-system bench at 13-16 ms locally (was 0.13 ms at merge)
description: PR #92 merged tests/bench/vfx-system.bench.ts at ~0.13 ms p99 (2000 particles). A full local pnpm bench on 2026-09-30 measured 13-16 ms against its 1-2 ms budgets. Could be machine load (load avg ~25-30) or a real regression from later merges (animation driver, physics poses as VFX anchors in PR #99, etc). Bisect on a quiet run; check CI's bench numbers for recent main commits. Fix the regression if real; if it's load-only, document and close.
close_reason: Load-only: CI p99 flat at 0.13-0.21 ms across all main commits since e1d8975; local main == e1d8975 (~0.11 ms p99); base commit reproduces multi-ms p99 under load spike. No code change.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: Load-only, no regression. (1) CI unit job bench p99 for VfxSystem.update() on every main commit e1d8975..7152e1a (12 runs): 0.13-0.21 ms at 2000 particles, 0.25-0.45 ms at 4000; flat, no step change across PR #99 (c5d3728), #104 (3252df1) etc. (2) Local, vfx bench alone, alternating e1d8975 vs origin/main 8ce8a8a, 3 runs each at load avg 17-23 on 10 cores: both ~0.11-0.12 ms p99 at 2000 and ~0.22-0.24 ms at 4000 -- identical. One e1d8975 run during a load spike FAILED with p99 4.09 ms (max 50 ms, rme +/-22%), reproducing the symptom on the pre-regression commit, so it is OS preemption, not code. (3) Full pnpm bench on main at load 15: all 13 files pass, vfx p99 0.11/0.22 ms; same with --no-file-parallelism, so bench files don't contend with each other. The 13-16 ms reading came from load avg 25-36 on the machine. The bench is not fragile in itself; a p99 wall-clock gate can't be protected from 3x core oversubscription without loosening budgets, which the contract forbids. Re-run pnpm bench on a quiet machine if a local failure appears.

title: Feed the lock-on target into the knight's attack facing
description:
## Why
mw-e04.6 lets the knight turn at up to 360°/s toward a lock-on target during attack startup, via PlayerMeleeOptions.target (faceTarget). Lock-on (mw-e02.16) is not merged yet, so the testbed passes no target and the knight tracks its look direction instead.
## What
When lock-on lands, pass its current target to installPlayer's combat.melee.target.
## Scope
- In: wiring the lock-on target into the facing rule
## Notes
Follow-up from mw-e04.6.
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [unit] Given a locked-on target 90° to the side, when a light attack starts, then the knight turns 6° per startup tick toward it and is locked from the first active tick.
notes: 2026-09-30 from mw-e02.16 (PR #102): lock-on's target is LockOnComponent.target (src/sim/targeting). Not wired in #102: faceTarget reads PlacementComponent on the target, which the arena's lock-on dummies (SceneTransform only) lack, and the room combat dummy is not targetable yet (mw-e02.32). Do both together: pass target: (w, e) => w.get(e, LockOnComponent)?.target ?? undefined and make faceTarget fall back to the lock's ViewAnchor point or give targets a Placement.

title: Wire guard breaks and blocked hits into hit reactions
description:
## Why
Guard breaks (mw-e04.6) lock the blocker's timeline for 60 ticks and emit GuardBroken, and blocked hits arrive as DamageApplied tagged `blocked` / `guard-break` with 0 poise damage. Hit reactions (mw-e04.7) must not flinch on a blocked hit and should turn GuardBroken into a readable guard-break stagger reaction (HitReaction event) for animation and audio.
## What
Map GuardBroken to a guard-break reaction (60 ticks, no second interruptAction), and skip or use a block-recoil reaction for DamageApplied tagged blocked.
## Scope
- In: reaction selection for blocked/guard-break hits
- Out: parry (mw-e04.12)
## Notes
Follow-up from mw-e04.6.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a blocked hit (tag blocked), when reactions resolve, then no flinch interrupts the blocker.
- AC-2 [unit] Given GuardBroken, when reactions resolve, then a guard-break reaction of 60 ticks is emitted and the timeline is not re-locked.

title: Wake-up i-frames make hit volumes emit DodgedHit, like dodge i-frames
description:
## Why

Hit reactions (mw-e04.7) make a knocked-down entity invulnerable for 20 wake-up ticks through a damage-model modifier (wakeIframesModifier), so a hit in that window still emits HitboxHit and a 0-damage DamageApplied. Dodge i-frames (mw-e04.8) instead turn such hits into DodgedHit in the hit-volume system. One invulnerability rule keeps feedback and telemetry consistent.

## What

As a developer, I want the hit-volume system's invulnerability rule to include wake-up i-frames so that every invulnerable hit is a DodgedHit whatever made the target invulnerable.

## Scope

- In: compose hasWakeIframes (src/sim/combat/reactions) with iframeRule in the hit-volume options; keep wakeIframesModifier for damage that does not come through hit volumes (projectiles, hazards).
- Out: new invulnerability sources.

## Notes

hasWakeIframes(world, entity) already has the InvulnerabilityRule shape.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an entity 5 ticks into its wake-up i-frames, when a hitbox sweeps it, then DodgedHit is emitted and no HitboxHit, DamageApplied or HitReaction follows.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same entity one tick after its i-frames, when a hitbox sweeps it, then HitboxHit is emitted and the hit applies.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a rolling entity inside its dodge i-frames and no knockdown, when swept, then DodgedHit is emitted exactly as before this change.

title: Let interaction reach ignore physics objects' own colliders in the game
description:
## Why
Property-derived affordances (liftable → pick up, pushable → push) must work on physics objects, but a crate's own Rapier collider blocks the reach ray to its centre, so it could never take focus.

## What
As a player, I want to focus and pick up a loose crate so that physics props are interactable like any other object.

When the game installs physics objects (mw-e03.10 wiring), pass the sim's `physicsBodiesOf` as the interaction `bodiesOf` (setupTestbedPlayer `interaction.bodiesOf`) so an object's own body and bound collider never block reach to it.

## Scope
- In: wiring `physicsBodiesOf` in src/main.ts and the testbed replay world once physics-object components are registered there
- Out: pick-up/carry behaviour itself (mw-e02.17)

## Notes
`physicsBodiesOf` lives in src/sim/interaction/system.ts (mw-e02.5); ColliderHandle and the sight world's BodyId share one sequence.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a liftable physics crate in the testbed in reach and view, when focus is computed, then the crate is focused (its own collider does not block reach).
- AC-2 [integration] Given the same crate behind a wall, when focus is computed, then it is not focused.

title: Creature attack executor honours dodge i-frames
description:
## Why
mw-e04.8 made hits during a dodge's i-frames become DodgedHit in the hit-volume system (hits/system.ts, iframeRule). The creature attack executor (src/sim/combat/attacks/executor.ts, mw-e12.5) still tests its own bounding-sphere hurtboxes and applies damage directly, so a creature attack run through it ignores i-frames.

## What
Either route executor hits through the hit-volume system (likely part of mw-e04.20) or have the executor ask the same InvulnerabilityRule and emit DodgedHit instead of damage.

## Scope
- In: executor melee and projectile hits respect i-frames
- Out: new dodge rules

## Notes
iframeRule(moves) and isInvulnerable in src/sim/combat/dodge/dodge.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a knight rolling on tick 0, when an executor melee attack's active tick lands on tick 14, then no damage applies and DodgedHit is emitted; on tick 15 it applies.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a projectile reaching a knight during i-frames, then it is DodgedHit and the projectile behaves as a miss.

title: Playtest dodge fairness in the combat sandbox (e04.8 AC-6)
description:
## Why
mw-e04.8 AC-6 is a manual feel check that needs the combat sandbox's attacker dummy (mw-e04.9), which did not exist when the dodge shipped.

## What
As a player, I want dodges that feel fair so that timing, not luck, keeps me alive. Once the sandbox exists, three playtesters practise rolling through the attacker dummy's metronome swing for 3 minutes each.

## Scope
- In: the playtest, logging counterexamples with replay files
- Out: tuning changes (file separately with evidence)

## Notes
Dodge rules: src/sim/combat/dodge; numbers in src/content/data/move/dodge-roll.json and backstep.json. Golden replays of an on-time vs one-tick-early roll: tests/replays/dodge-*.json.
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [manual] Given the sandbox attacker dummy, when three playtesters practise for 3 minutes, then each reports dodges "felt fair" (no hits they believed they had dodged); any counterexample is logged with a replay file.

title: Remove physics body automatically when a physics-object entity is destroyed
description: From PR #94: removePhysicsObject must be called manually before destroying a physics-object entity or its Rapier body leaks in the world. Hook entity destruction so the body is removed automatically; test that destroying the entity leaves no body behind and state hash matches.

title: Play impact sounds from physicsImpact events via cue sheets
description: mw-e03.10 emits physicsImpact { entity, other, materials, energy, impulse, speed, normal, position } but it is not in the cue-sheet event table (src/content/cue-events.ts CUE_EVENTS) nor bound in src/game/cues/events.ts, so no sound plays for tumbling crates. Add the event with material facts (like HIT_FACTS) and energy as a volume-scaling number, and a default cue rule using each material's impactSound. ACs to be written per the backlog contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a physicsImpact payload, when its cue binding reads it, then it offers the anchors entity, other and at, and the facts entity/other (impact class of each side's material), entityMaterial/otherMaterial (material ids) and energy, impulse, speed (numbers).
- AC-2 [unit] Given the physics cue sheet, when a wood crate lands on stone through the world event bus, then the cue bridge plays sfx-impact-wood at the crate, and a harder impact (more energy) plays louder than a soft one.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a cue rule for physicsImpact, when content loads, then it may match the material facts and scale volume by energy, and matching an unknown fact or a number fact is rejected naming the rule.

title: Spawn scene props as physics objects in the game and render them from their sim pose
description: mw-e03.10 added the sim physics-object layer (installPhysicsObjects, addPhysicsObject, physics.object pose component, bindCollider) but nothing in the game uses it yet. Wire it in src/main.ts / src/game: install physics objects on the game world, spawn scene spawns whose prop is a movable object (crates, barrels) as physics objects with their material properties, bind level colliders to stone entities so impacts name a material, bind render objects that read physics.object position/rotation through RenderSync, and log physicsBudgetExceeded warnings to the console/debug overlay. ACs to be written per the backlog contract.
acceptance_criteria:
AC-1: Loading a scene with physics spawns every spawn whose prop has a body (content testprop.body: box size + material) as a sim physics object standing on its spawn, with the prop's mass as weight and its material's world properties; markers and props without a body stay static.
AC-2: Every solid level-kit piece becomes a stone entity (level material configurable) owning its static colliders via bindCollider, so an impact on the level names the piece entity and ['wood','stone'].
AC-3: Movable props are drawn from their sim pose (physics.object position/rotation) through RenderSync, interpolated between the last two ticks; drawing never changes sim state.
AC-4: physicsBudgetExceeded warnings are logged (console.warn + data-physics-budget debug attribute); the budget focus follows the player.
AC-5: Unloading a scene leaves no bodies or colliders behind; loading and stepping is deterministic (testbed player replay re-recorded).
AC-6: In the browser the testbed spawns its two movable props as physics objects (data-physics-objects=2) with zero console errors.

title: Decide the live-particle caps: 2000/800 (style bible) or 4000/1500 (mw-e29.1)
description:
## Why

Two sources disagree on the global live-particle cap. The style bible §13.1 per-frame scene budget (which e32-perf-budgets enforces and other beads such as mw-e37.73 cite, e.g. ≤ 800 on Low) says High ≤ 2000 / Low ≤ 800. The mw-e29.1 description says 4000 High / 1500 Low.

## What

mw-e29.1 shipped VFX_PARTICLE_CAPS = { high: 2000, low: 800 } (src/game/vfx/budget.ts), following the style bible, and tested the budget rule at the 4000 cap the bead's AC-2 names. The runtime measured about 0.25 ms per frame p99 at 4000 particles in Node and a 2.9 ms frame p95 with 50 effects at the 2000 cap on an M1 Pro (headed Chromium), so either number fits the frame. The owner picks one; the constant, the style bible table and perf-budgets.json (e32) must then agree.

## Scope

- In: the decision, VFX_PARTICLE_CAPS, style bible §13.1, the vfx-test-stress effect and the ?vfx=stress count if the cap changes.
- Out: auto-degrade (mw-e29.15).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the chosen caps, when the style bible §13.1 table and VFX_PARTICLE_CAPS are compared, then they match.
- AC-2 [perf] Given ?vfx=stress at the chosen High cap, when measured on the reference machine, then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms.
close_reason: Owner decided 2026-09-29: keep style bible §13.1 caps, 2000 High / 800 Low (already shipped in VFX_PARTICLE_CAPS, PR #92). Revisit only with e32 reference-machine measurements.

title: Socket track content type: author the arcs move hitboxes sweep along
description:
## Why

Moves name a socket track (hitbox.track, e.g. knight-sword-arc-light-1) but no track data exists yet. mw-e04.2 added the sim side: SocketTrack (key 0 = pose before the first active tick, key k = active tick k) and hitboxFromMove(move, track, aim), so today callers must build tracks in code.

## What

A socket-track content type (src/content/data/socket-track/<id>.json): per-key socket poses (position + rotation) in the attacker frame, validated so a track has 1 … active+1 keys; a ref check that every move's hitbox.track exists; compiled into a lookup the knight attacks (e04.6) and creature attacks use with hitboxFromMove. Author tracks for every move id that names one (knight sword arcs light 1-3, heavy, shield bash, kick, dummy swing).

## Notes

Tracks are sim data; the render animation follows them (never the reverse). Keep keys at tick resolution; sweeps interpolate between keys.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a move whose hitbox.track names a missing track, when content loads, then validation fails naming the move and track.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a track with more keys than the move's active ticks + 1, when content loads, then validation fails.
- AC-3 [integration] Given every shipped move with a hitbox, when its track is looked up and swept through its active ticks, then the hitbox sweeps a non-empty arc and each key is finite.

title: Render sim light sources and check sim/render light parity
description:
## Why

The sim's light model (mw-e03.15) decides whether a thief is seen; players judge that from what they see on screen. If sim light and rendered light disagree, shadows lie to the player and stealth feels unfair.

## What

As a thief, I want the shadows I see to be the shadows guards use so that hiding in a dark corner works when it looks like it should.

Render the sim's light sources in the greybox renderer and prove they agree: a greybox lighting room (scene with torches, a burning prop, a moonlit window), renderer point/spot lights driven from the sim's `LightField` emitters (intensity and radius mapped from the same falloff), the level's static geometry handed to `LightField.statics` alongside physics at scene load, and a Playwright parity probe.

## Scope

- In: greybox lighting-room scene; scene-file light environment (ambient zones, directional lights) loaded into `LightField.setEnvironment`; game wiring (`installLightField`, `lightFieldSystem`, a sink that feeds both physics and light statics); renderer lights from sim emitters; Playwright parity probe
- Out: the light model itself (done in mw-e03.15); visibility scoring (mw-e09.2); light debug overlay (mw-e33.10)

## Notes

Split out of mw-e03.15 (its AC-7): the renderer had no point lights and scenes had no light data, so parity needed render and content work beyond the sim PR. Probe idea: project each sample point to screen, read floor luminance from a canvas screenshot, compare with `LightField.levelAt` via Spearman rank correlation.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the greybox lighting room, when the Playwright parity probe samples 20 points, then sim light level and rendered luminance rank-correlate ≥ 0.8.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a scene with light environment data, when it loads, then its ambient zones and directional lights are in the LightField and its static geometry blocks light.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given a torch entity in the lighting room, when it stops burning, then its rendered light goes out on the same tick the sim level drops.

title: Save and load the sim's physics state in the world save section
description:
## Why

Since mw-e03.35 a World with physics carries PhysicsState (engine id plus Rapier's snapshot as base64 and a handle table) in its WorldSnapshot, and restore() requires it. The save world section's schema (src/game/save/format/registry.ts) is a strictObject without a physics field, so saving a world that has physics would be rejected, and physics would be lost across save/load.

## What

Add the optional physics field to the world section (a new section version with an identity migration, like facts in v2), with round-trip and fixture tests. Consider compressing the Rapier bytes (ADR-0001: about 350 KB per 200 bodies) and whether static level geometry should be rebuilt from the level rather than saved (mw-e27.3 baselines).

## Scope

- In: world section schema/version, save fixtures, round-trip test with a physics world
- Out: dynamic bodies (mw-e03.10)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a World with Rapier physics and a loaded scene, when saved and loaded into a new World, then the state hash is identical and stepping on matches the uninterrupted run.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a save from before this change (no physics), when loaded into a World without physics, then it loads unchanged.

title: Persist custom key bindings through the settings store
description:
## Why
Split from mw-e02.1: AC-6 there needs the settings framework (mw-e31.1), which depends on the UI layer (mw-e00.23). Input mapping ships first with an in-memory bindings API.
## What
Save and restore mw-e02.1's bindings via the mw-e31.1 settings store.
## Scope
- In: bindings serialisation, migration of unknown actions, wiring to settings store
- Out: rebind UI (options menu)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given bindings saved via e31-settings-framework, when the page reloads, then custom bindings are restored.
- AC-2 [unit] Given stored bindings that reference an unknown action or key code, when loaded, then those entries are dropped and defaults fill the gap.

title: Autosave at a testbed checkpoint volume shows in the slot list (e2e) and HUD indicator
description:
## Why
mw-e30.5 shipped the autosave scheduler as API only: its AC-5 [e2e] (checkpoint volume in the testbed -> autosave in the slot list with the area name) is proven at the sim level in src/game/save/autosave/autosave.integration.test.ts because the greybox testbed (mw-e00.21) and HUD layer (mw-e00.23) do not exist yet.

## What
Wire AutosaveScheduler into the game loop (update between sim steps, reset after load), mark a testbed checkpoint volume via autosaveAtCheckpoints, render the HUD saving indicator and the non-blocking failure warning from scheduler.subscribe, and add the Playwright test.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the testbed with a checkpoint volume, when the player enters it, then an autosave appears in the slot list with the area name.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given an autosave write fails twice, then a non-blocking HUD warning is shown and play continues.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the testbed with a checkpoint volume, when the player enters it, then an autosave appears in the slot list with the area name.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given an autosave write fails twice, then a non-blocking HUD warning is shown and play continues.

title: Validate signal-graph entity bindings against level entity ids
description:
## Why

mw-e03.21 signal graphs bind nodes to level entities by name ("entity": "lower-lock-gate"). Nothing checks those names at content load yet because levels are not content; a typo only fails when the graph is placed at runtime.

## What

As a designer, I want the content loader to reject a graph whose bindings name entities missing from the level that places it, so that typos fail in CI rather than in play.

## Scope

- In: cross-reference check from the level/placement data to signal-graph bindings, with file path and pointer
- Out: the level format — see mw-e01.4 greybox level

## Notes

The sim already throws on a missing binding when the graph is placed (addSignalGraph).
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [content] Given a level placing a graph whose node binds an entity id absent from the level, when validated, then validation fails naming the id and the level file.

title: Out-of-breath cues when the knight is Exhausted
description:
## Why

mw-e04.5 AC-6: running out of stamina must be readable without the HUD (souls-like fairness). The sim now emits StaminaExhausted / StaminaRecovered (src/sim/combat/stamina.ts) but nothing presents them yet.

## What

As a knight, I want to hear and see that I am out of breath so that I stop swinging before the HUD tells me.
On StaminaExhausted: heavy-breathing loop on the player bus and a hunched/winded idle and slower recovery pose; on StaminaRecovered: breath settles and the loop stops. ActionRejected{reason:"stamina"} plays a short strained grunt (once per press). Placeholder assets via e28 cue sheets until final audio lands.

## Scope

- In: cue-sheet entries and game-layer bindings for the three events, placeholder animation state, manual playtest
- Out: HUD stamina bar (mw-e04.10), final SFX/animation assets (audio/art beads)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a StaminaExhausted event, when the game layer processes it, then the breathing cue starts once and stops on StaminaRecovered.
- AC-2 [unit] Given ActionRejected{reason:"stamina"}, when processed, then the strain cue plays once.
- AC-3 [manual] (carried from mw-e04.5 AC-6) Given a 5-minute sandbox session, when a playtester fights the attacker dummy, then they can describe when they are "out of breath" without looking at the HUD.

title: Make simMath transcendentals bit-identical across platforms
description:
## Why

Golden replays must pass on developer machines and CI alike. While building the replay harness (mw-e00.17) the first golden, recorded on macOS arm64, diverged in CI on Linux x64 at tick 60 by 1 ULP in a velocity fed by simMath.sin/cos: Node 24's Math.sin/cos are not bit-identical across OS/CPU even on the same Node version. Any sim feature using trig (controller headings, arcs, AI facing) will make its goldens platform-dependent.

## What

Replace the Math-backed wrappers in src/sim/math.ts with pure-JS implementations built only from IEEE-exact ops (+ - * / sqrt), e.g. an fdlibm port for sin/cos/tan/atan2/exp/log/pow/hypot, and pin their outputs with golden vectors.

## Scope

- In: deterministic simMath functions, golden vectors checked in CI, perf bench
- Out: changing call sites (they already route through simMath)

## Notes

The core replay scenario (src/sim/replay/scenarios/core.ts) avoids trig until this lands; once it does, reintroduce trig there and re-bless.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a table of golden input/output bit patterns for every simMath function, when run on Node in CI (Linux x64) and on macOS arm64, then every output is bit-identical to the table.
- AC-2 [unit] Given 10,000 random inputs, when compared with Math, then every result is within 1 ULP.
- AC-3 [perf] Given 1,000,000 sin+cos calls, when benchmarked, then they take no more than 3x the Math.sin/cos time.

title: Story bible: retitle to The Vesper Bell; stone river trade and imperial silver
description:
## Why

The bible still opens with the retired 'Merlin's Wrath' evaluation, and the owner has updated the world's economy: stone was the valley's original wealth, quarried and barged down the Wend to the sea for export abroad; silver, later found at the heart of the mine, is now the empire's cash cow and the root of its dominance over neighbouring states.

## What

Replace §1 with The Vesper Bell (per ADR-0002); rewrite the world, history, factions and locations sections for the stone trade and imperial silver; make Wendmouth visibly built on stone (quays, breakwater, warehouses and civic buildings of massive dressed stone); fix everything downstream (cast, quests, glossary, canon facts).

## Scope

- In: docs/narrative/story-bible.md; style bible harbour visual notes if they conflict
- Out: re-planning asset beads (follow-up if needed)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] No 'Merlin' references remain in the story bible except the codename note.
- AC-2 [content] The stone trade, the river's role carrying stone to the sea, and imperial silver are consistent across all sections and the canon-facts list.
- AC-3 [content] The Wendmouth section describes a harbour of big stone structures clearly built from the stone trade.

title: Perf-pass and playtest Wendmouth on both presets
description:
## Why
Crowds, water, a ship and a brawl in one scene are a perf risk; hijinks must be discovered, not explained.

## What
Perf suite runs on market day, the Tidefair brawl and night heist scenes on reference and low-tier machines; a 5-tester playtest (one per class plus one free): do they find a hijink and a gear upgrade unprompted within 30 minutes? Findings in docs/playtests/wendmouth.md with beads.

## Scope
- In: Perf captures and fixes, playtest, findings
- Out: Global perf (E32)

## Notes
Related: e32-reference-runbook.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given market day with 40 crowd agents on the Stone Wharf, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).
- AC-2 [perf] Given the Tidefair brawl on Low, when measured, then p95 <= 16.7 ms at 1080p on the Low preset on an Intel Iris Xe / base M1 8 GB class machine, with p99 <= 33.3 ms (30 fps floor) during worst-case combat.
- AC-3 [perf] Given a warm cache, when arriving by barge, then the harbour is playable in <= 3 s and heap stays <= 1.5 GB.
- AC-4 [manual] Given 5 testers, when playing 30 minutes in Wendmouth, then >= 4 buy or earn a gear upgrade and >= 4 attempt a hijink or heist unprompted.

title: Light and score Wendmouth for market day, night and the tavern
description:
## Why
Loud and cheerful by day, lantern-lit and sneaky by night: the harbour's mood changes the play.

## What
As a player, I want Wendmouth to sound busy by day and to have dark pools of shadow at night so that both hijinks and heists feel right.
Lighting per phase (dock lanterns, ship lamps, lighthouse sweep on the breakwater), music cues (harbour day/night, Drowned Gull diegetic, Tidefair, heist tension), ambience bindings (gulls, rigging creak, surf), reverb zones for cellars.

## Scope
- In: Lighting, music bindings, ambience/reverb bindings
- Out: Audio assets (E38)

## Notes
Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. Gameplay never waits on this item. Related: e28-ambience, e28-reverb-zones and e29-environment-fx are P2 in the combat plan; bind ambience beds, reverb zones and fog/firefly FX here when they land, otherwise ship lighting + music only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the clock crosses dusk, when the phase event fires, then lighting blends to night within 5 s and music switches to the harbour night cue.
- AC-2 [integration] Given night lighting, when sampled along the warehouse heist routes, then >= 40% of each route has light <= 0.3 (edge: stealth viable).
- AC-3 [perf] Given night with all lanterns lit and the Tern's lamps, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

title: Art-dress Wendmouth with glenstone harbour assets and the Tern
description:
## Why
Colossal glenstone quays, vaulted warehouses, net lofts and a three-master: Wendmouth must look loud, cheerful and built like a city next to quiet Briar Glen.

## What
As a player, I want Wendmouth to look like a crooked, salt-weathered port built from the valley's stone so that arriving feels like a change of air.
Monumental glenstone harbour kit (stepped quays, mason-marked block breakwater, vaulted warehouses, columned Customs House, treadwheel cranes on stone piers, block yards) with timber net lofts and sheds perched on the stone, props, the Gilded Tern hero model, crowd variants, water surface materials; keep collision and gameplay ids intact.

## Scope
- In: Art swap for the harbour, the Tern, interiors, crowd visuals
- Out: Asset creation (E37)

## Notes
Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. Gameplay never waits on this item.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the dressed harbour, when all E40 route and heist replays run, then they pass unchanged.
- AC-2 [perf] Given the Stone Wharf on market day with the Tern in view, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent) and draw calls <= 1500.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the art review, when compared to the style bible, then interactable affordances (climbable nets, cuttable ropes) remain legible against dressing (edge).

title: Place Wendmouth rumours, lore texts, secrets and treasure
description:
## Why
Rumours 13–18 must lead somewhere; every vaulted warehouse and net loft should hide something.

## What
As a curious player, I want harbour gossip that points at real places so that talking in Wendmouth leads to mischief.
Bind rumours 13–18 to sources (Mags, Nell, Old Reed, Tidemarket gossip) with produced resolve facts; place the Lantern Court notice, the bay nine manifest copies, the foundry invoice, Mr. S—'s sealed letter; 10–14 treasures incl. smugglers' stashes and gull hoards.

## Scope
- In: Rumour source bindings, fact producers, lore/treasure placements
- Out: Texts (e39-harbor-rumors-texts)

## Notes
River rumour 16 resolves in e25-weeping-adit; 18 in e40-breakwater-sea-door.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given rumours 13–18, when validated, then each has >= 1 source and a resolvesWhen fact produced by placed content (no warnings).
- AC-2 [integration] Given rumour 15 heard, when the player enters the Undertow, then it resolves.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a stash looted, when saved and reloaded, then it stays empty (edge).

title: Declare Wendmouth obstacles and class routes in the registry
description:
## Why
Sneakiness is richly rewarded, but every class must get its hijinks; the audit has to see the harbour.

## What
As a player of any class, I want every harbour obstacle to offer my class a route so that Wendmouth plays to my fantasy.
Registry entries and replays for: customs strongroom, bay nine, boarding the Tern, the Undertow entry, the crate (six routes), and the Tidefair (one event per class flavour). Obstacles are marked mandatory within their quest (the town itself is optional).

## Scope
- In: Registry entries, route affordances added where missing, replays
- Out: Audit gate (e16-route-audit)

## Notes
Target 4 classes for bay nine and the Tern.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the registry, when validated, then every E40 quest-mandatory obstacle has >= 3 class routes and bay nine and the Tern have 4.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each declared route, when replayed, then the obstacle exit fact is set.
- AC-3 [integration] Given an obstacle whose only thief route needs the P2 disguise, when audited without it, then >= 3 other routes still pass (edge).

title: Place The Crate for Mr. S— heist with all six solution routes
description:
## Why
The harbour's centrepiece: a stealth-first heist that every class can solve its own way.

## What
As a player of any class, I want to take Vane's relic crate by heist, paper, net, force, ice or leverage so that I win the name-stone and the manifest my way.
Wire the bible §6.1 quest 6 routes into the level: heist (case, roof/skylight entry, dodge the watchman, swap contents for ballast, re-seal with the stamp); paper (swap/forge the manifest so Cray seizes the crate legally, needing Quell's honest manifest or the dead clerk's seal); net (cut the net mid-hoist so the crate drops into the harbour, fish it out at low tide before the Low Tide Company); force (dockside brawl with Nell's crew and the watch; Cray arrives at the end); ice (freeze the pool at night and take it from the hold, or Gust the hoist so it lands on the wharf); leverage (confront Quell with the foundry invoice). Outcomes: name-stone, manifest, sealed letter facts.

## Scope
- In: Hoist sequence timing, crate entity with contents state, route wiring, outcome facts, low-tide retrieval spot
- Out: Quest graph (e39-harbor-heist-quest)
- Out: Disguise entry (Related: e40-dockhand-disguises, P2)

## Notes
Crate contents per canon: 40 horn-coins, 3 carved stones, 1 name-stone. The name-stone is a befriend-Horn trigger (Related: e14-horn-befriend-help).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given each of the six routes, when its replay runs, then the crate outcome fact is set to the route id and the name-stone is obtainable.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the perfect heist (contents swapped, seal re-stamped, no alert), when the Tern sails, then heist.perfect is set and no one in Wendmouth reacts.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the crate dropped into the harbour, when the Low Tide Company reaches it first at low tide, then the crate moves to the Undertow and remains obtainable there (edge: failure relocates).
- AC-4 [integration] Given Act III starts before any route resolves, when evaluated, then crate.shipped is set and the customs manifest copy still proves the shipments.

title: Add the harbour watch, Low Tide Company and Tern crew as humans
description:
## Why
Wendmouth adds no creature types: its opposition is human and social — bribe, trick, drink with, out-brawl.

## What
As a player, I want harbour people who arrest, throw me off the pier or brawl instead of killing me so that getting caught in Wendmouth is a story.
Human creature data on e12: harbour watch (non-lethal by default; arrest via e22-crime-bounty or subdue → thrown off pier), Low Tide Company smugglers (clubs, knives, nets, whistles; alarms via whistles), Tern crew (deck patrols, belaying-pin clubs). Factions and relationships (Low Tide vs watch), bribe/drink affordances, retreat/surrender.

## Scope
- In: Three human archetypes as creature data, move sets, faction table entries, affordances, subdue outcomes
- Out: Crime/bounty (e22-crime-bounty)
- Out: Dialogue (e39-dialogue-harbor-folk, e39-dialogue-harbor-trade)

## Notes
Readability rules apply to human attacks too. Knives are lethal only if the player draws steel first (escalation fact).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the three human archetypes, when validated, then they pass CreatureDef and all moves pass readability.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the watch subdues the player without a bounty, when resolved, then the player is thrown off the pier (breakwater wake) rather than jailed.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a Low Tide smuggler blows a whistle, when heard by allies within range, then they converge on the whistle location.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the player bribes a watchman with enough coin, when accepted, then that watchman ignores trespass for 10 game minutes (edge: expires).

title: Fill the harbour with pickpocketable crowds that give stealth cover
description:
## Why
Pickpocketable crowds make the thief's playground; market days should feel packed.

## What
As a thief, I want dense market-day crowds I can blend into and pick pockets from so that sneaking in plain sight is rewarded.
Crowd NPC sets on schedule windows (market days denser), each with a small pocket loot table; crowd volumes reduce the player's visibility score while moving at walk speed inside them; bumping a crowd NPC at run speed emits a noise/complaint.

## Scope
- In: Crowd schedule data, pocket loot tables, crowd-cover visibility modifier volumes, bump barks
- Out: Disguises (e40-dockhand-disguises)
- Out: Pickpocket mechanics (e10-pickpocketing)

## Notes
Crowd cover is a visibility modifier volume on e09-visibility-model inputs, not a new stealth system.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player walking inside a crowd volume, when a watchman's visibility score is computed, then it is reduced by the configured crowd factor versus open ground.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a crowd NPC pickpocketed unseen, when checked, then an item from its pocket table is taken and no crime is recorded.
- AC-3 [perf] Given a market-day crowd of 40 agents on the Stone Wharf, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent) and p95 <= 16.7 ms at 1080p on the Low preset on an Intel Iris Xe / base M1 8 GB class machine, with p99 <= 33.3 ms (30 fps floor) during worst-case combat (edge: crowd LOD).

title: Build the breakwater, sunken figurehead, sea-door and harbour tides
description:
## Why
Getting thrown off the pier should land you somewhere new: the figurehead and the smugglers' sea-door.

## What
As a player, I want being thrown off the pier to wash me up by a secret door so that failure in Wendmouth opens a route.
Stone breakwater, the sunken figurehead (debunks the sea-serpent rumour 18 by diving), the smugglers' sea-door into the Undertow tunnels. Harbour tide: two standing-water levels scheduled on the world clock (high/low); low tide exposes the sea-door and the crate-drop spot. Wake rule: "thrown off the pier" (subdued in Wendmouth) → surface at the breakwater.

## Scope
- In: Breakwater area, figurehead dive spot, sea-door, two-state tide schedule, wake rule content
- Out: Flowing water / waves (not planned)

## Notes
Tide is two scheduled water-level states, not simulation.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player is subdued by dockhands or the watch in Wendmouth, when resolved, then they surface at the breakwater and harbor.thrownOffPier increments.
- AC-2 [integration] Given low tide on the clock schedule, when the harbour loads, then the sea-door is above water and enterable; at high tide it is reachable only by swimming (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player dives to the figurehead, when reached, then rumour 18 resolves as false.

title: Build the Gilded Tern: rigging, hold, cabin, locked berth, departure
description:
## Why
The merchantman is the heist's destination, a shanghai wake point and a ship you can climb.

## What
As a player, I want to board the three-masted Tern by lighter, swim, rigging line, a frozen pool, Tereza's favour or signing on as crew so that the ship becomes a playground.
Ship at anchor in the pool: climbable rigging and yards, deck, hold (crates, shanghai wake spot), Captain Hesketh's cabin, the locked berth of Mr. S—'s agent (never opens in the MVP; interact hooks), crew patrols. World variant: when Act III begins the Tern is gone (fact tern.sailed) with or without Vane's crate.

## Scope
- In: Ship scene/area, rigging climb routes, hold and cabin, locked berth, boarding routes, sailed variant
- Out: Crew behaviour (e40-harbor-opposition)
- Out: Hesketh dialogue (e39-dialogue-harbor-trade)

## Notes
The pool is standing water: freezing it at night makes a walkable path to the hull (bible sorcerer route).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the pool frozen by any cold stimulus at night, when walked, then the Tern's hull ladder is reachable on foot.
- AC-2 [integration] Given fact act3.started, when the harbour loads, then the Tern is absent and tern.sailed is set; the crate outcome is recorded as shipped if not resolved.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player is on board when Act III starts, when the harbour next loads, then they are placed on the wharf, never stranded at sea (edge).
- AC-4 [content] Given the obstacle registry, when validated, then boarding the Tern declares >= 4 class routes.

title: Build a continuous rooftop and net-loft route across the waterfront
description:
## Why
Climbers should cross the whole harbour above the crowd — and archers need rigging-shot vantages.

## What
As a thief, I want a roof route from the Stone Wharf to the breakwater via net lofts so that I can reach skylights, the customs roof and the Tern's rigging line unseen.
Connected roofs and net lofts (hanging nets climbable and flammable), plank bridges, gull-hoard ledges, archer vantage points over the pool and the Tern's rigging.

## Scope
- In: Roof surfaces with acoustic tags, climbable nets, plank bridges, vantage points
- Out: Climbing mechanics (E10/E02)

## Notes
Tarred roofs are quiet; tin roofs are loud (acoustic tags).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the rooftop replay, when a thief crosses from the Stone Wharf to the breakwater, then they never touch street navmesh.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a climbable net ignited, when it burns, then the route segment closes and an alternative segment remains (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given an archer at a vantage point, when aiming at the Tern's hoist rope, then it is within effective bow range and unobstructed.

title: Build the Undertow black market and its smugglers' tunnels
description:
## Why
The Undertow sells what the Tidemarket can't — the thief's best tools — and links the harbour underground.

## What
As a thief, I want a black market in the smugglers' cellars with tunnels to the tavern and the harbour wall so that I can equip myself and move unseen.
Cellars beneath the fish market; tunnels to the Drowned Gull trapdoor and the breakwater sea-door; Nell Gannet's fence/merchant data: smuggler thief tools (tide-silk rope, glue-soled boots, smoke pearls, skeleton-key ring, customs-seal stamp), fenced goods, and the dockhand disguise kit item. Access: trust, the trapdoor, or the sea-door.

## Scope
- In: Cellar scene, tunnels, fence merchant data, thief tool item data (on e10 tool schema)
- Out: Tool mechanics (E10)
- Out: Disguise behaviour (e40-dockhand-disguises)

## Notes
Tool items reuse existing verbs: tide-silk rope → rope anchor, glue-soled boots → quieter footsteps on wet surfaces, smoke pearls → smoke escape, skeleton-key ring → lockpick bonus, customs-seal stamp → re-seal action.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given Nell's merchant file, when validated, then isFence is true and every tool references an existing capability or tool type.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player enters by the sea-door, when first arriving, then the Undertow merchants are Wary rather than Hostile and trade is allowed after one exchange (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the customs-seal stamp bought, when used on a broken seal, then the seal reads intact (ties to e40-bonded-warehouse).

title: Author the Tidemarket: Tereza's arms stall and the foreign book cart
description:
## Why
Everyone can equip themselves better in Wendmouth than in Briar Glen; the Tidemarket is where.

## What
As a player of any class, I want an import market with foreign steel, light armour, exotic arrows and rare spellbooks so that the trip downriver upgrades my kit.
Merchant data on e20: Tereza Maelo's arms stall (curved Saltmarch sabres, harpoon-spears, lacquered round shields, sharkskin brigandine; an under-the-counter tier gated by duel/Tidefair facts); exotic arrows as foreign variants of MVP arrow types (whistling = noise, grapple = rope; data only); spice/silk/oddities stall. Foreign bookseller's cart authored on the e21 bookshop template (Storm, Illusion and Gravity texts; restricted ones subject to customs).

## Scope
- In: Covered market interior, three merchant files, one bookshop file, under-the-counter conditions
- Out: Arrow mechanics (E05)
- Out: Merchant dialogue (e39-dialogue-harbor-trade)
- Out: Tereza's duel (e40-tereza-duel)

## Notes
Related: e05-trick-arrows-extended (P3) — netting, tar and glass-headed arrows appear only if that lands. Mirela pays well for anything the cart won't sell (Related: e24-lamplit-stacks buyback).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the Tidemarket stock, when compared with all Briar Glen merchants, then every class has >= 2 purchasable items not sold in Briar Glen.
- AC-2 [content] Given the foreign book cart, when pnpm validate:bookshops runs, then it passes and no unique book is duplicated with the Lamplit Stacks.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the under-the-counter tier, when neither the duel nor a Tidefair win fact is set, then it is hidden (edge); with either, it appears.
- AC-4 [content] Given the arrow stock, when validated, then every arrow item references an existing e05 arrow type.

title: Stage the Tidefair Gull Shoot and the Pocket Race
description:
## Why
Archers win shooting contests and thieves lift ribbons from five marks — one of them the Inspector.

## What
As an archer, I want to hit wooden gulls on a swinging boom and then the live gull that stole the ribbon; as a thief, I want to lift a ribbon from each of five marked contestants without being caught.
Gull Shoot: boom-mounted targets on a swinging rope (moving-target scoring), then a live harbour gull target that flees to the rooftops. Pocket Race: five marked NPCs wandering the wharf crowd (one is Cray), each carrying a ribbon; caught = out.

## Scope
- In: Two contest definitions, swinging boom prop, live-gull chase target, five marked contestants
- Out: Archery and pickpocket mechanics (E05/E10)

## Notes
Sabotage is possible: cut the boom rope, or plant a ribbon on a rival. Both have consequences via cheat rules.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the boom swinging, when an arrow hits a wooden gull, then the hit scores and the gull drops.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the Pocket Race, when the player lifts all five ribbons unseen, then they win; if Cray notices a lift, then she files a note (fact cray.noticedThief) but does not arrest.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the live gull flees to a rooftop, when the player follows, then its hoard location becomes reachable and the ribbon is retrievable (edge: prize never lost).

title: Stage the Tidefair arm-wrestling bout and the Gull brawl
description:
## Why
Knights get hijinks too: beat Big Oona, then survive the free-for-all when someone loses badly.

## What
As a knight, I want to arm-wrestle and brawl at the Tidefair so that strength and timing win me coin and friends.
Arm-wrestling: a timed hold contest scored from stamina management and timed pushes (reuses e04 stamina). The Gull brawl: a non-lethal free-for-all on the wharf using melee and hit reactions with a knockout tag; environment pushes into the water are allowed. Both run on the contest framework with cheat rules (magic, dirty tricks) and a lose-gracefully branch (Oona buys you a drink).

## Scope
- In: Two contest definitions, arm-wrestle input/stamina binding, brawl non-lethal rules, participants
- Out: Combat systems (E04)
- Out: Quest rewards (e39-side-quests-harbor)

## Notes
Any class may enter; knights have the flavour advantage (poise, stamina).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the arm-wrestling contest, when the player outlasts Oona's stamina, then contest win fires and the Tidefair reputation fact increments.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the brawl, when any participant reaches 0 health, then they are knocked out (not killed) and leave the brawl.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player is shoved into the harbour during the brawl, when they surface, then they are out of the contest and may climb back via a ladder (edge).

title: Build the Drowned Gull: arm-wrestling, dice, drinking and the trapdoor
description:
## Why
Nell's tavern is the harbour's social hub, the thief's drop point and a place where losing lands you somewhere new.

## What
As a player, I want a rowdy tavern where I can arm-wrestle Big Oona, drink, gamble, start or end a brawl and find the trapdoor to the Undertow so that Wendmouth's people become my allies or rivals.
Interior on the breakwater end: arm-wrestling table (contest), dice table, drinking contest (losing wakes you shanghaied in the Gilded Tern's hold via a wake-in-place rule), brawl trigger (non-lethal brawling), the thief commission drop with Nell (deliver the coin, keep it, or deliver a fake), and the trapdoor (found by search or granted by Nell's trust).

## Scope
- In: Interior, contest instances (arm-wrestling, dice, drinking), brawl trigger, drop interaction facts, trapdoor, wake rule
- Out: Nell and Oona dialogue (e39-dialogue-harbor-folk)
- Out: Tidefair brawl (e40-tidefair-strength)

## Notes
Brawls use non-lethal damage tags: knocked-out, never killed, for everyone involved.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player loses the drinking contest, when it resolves, then they wake in the Tern's hold, fact tern.shanghaied is set and no reload occurs.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the thief delivers a fake horn-coin to Nell, when evaluated, then commission.fakeDelivered is set and the payout still occurs.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a brawl started in the tavern, when it ends, then no participant has died and the watch is not called (dockhands settle it).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the trapdoor is found without Nell's trust, when used, then the Undertow is reachable but Nell's disposition drops one band (edge).

title: Run data-defined contests with entry, scoring, cheating and bets
description:
## Why
The Tidefair and the Drowned Gull need contests; no other plan owns a contest runner, and bespoke scripting per event would not scale.

## What
A small data-driven contest runner in src/sim built on the condition/effect DSL and quest objective trackers: contest definitions {id, entry conditions, fee, participants, scoring from sim events, win/lose conditions, cheat rules (condition → detected-if-observed-by), betting book (odds, throw-the-match option), rewards/effects}. Emits contest.started/ended with placement.

## Scope
- In: Contest schema + validator, runner, cheat detection via perception of watchers, betting hook, outcome effects
- Out: Individual events (Tidefair items, e40-drowned-gull)
- Out: Quest graphs (e39-side-quests-harbor)

## Notes
Cheating is always possible and always has a consequence (bible §6.1 quest 7). Losing gracefully is a valid outcome with its own effect.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a contest with a scoring rule "hits on target tag gull", when 3 matching hit events occur, then the player score is 3 and ties break by earliest completion.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a cheat rule "magic used" and Cray perceiving the cast, when it occurs, then contest.cheatDetected fires and the disqualify effect applies; unobserved, no detection (edge).
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player accepts Nell's bet to throw the match, when they lose, then the payout effect applies; if they win, the betting-book grudge effect applies.
- AC-4 [content] Given contest data, when validated, then every contest has entry, win and lose conditions and references existing effects.

title: Build the Bonded Warehouse: bay nine, skylights, hoists and manifests
description:
## Why
The warehouse is the thief's showcase: a sealed bay, a watchman and a desk full of paper.

## What
As a thief, I want a warehouse with skylights, hoist beams and a manifest desk so that I can case it and choose my way in.
Sealed bays; bay nine (Vane Deepworks) with a customs-seal entity (intact / broken / re-sealed, stamp-verifiable); skylights (climb, rope-arrow anchor); hoist beams (traversable, can lower crates); the night watchman's patrol and lantern; the manifest desk (swap or forge the bay nine manifest); Jasper Quell's office (foundry invoice, honest manifest, Mr. S— letters).

## Scope
- In: Interior, seal state entity, skylight and beam routes, watchman patrol data, manifest desk and Quell's office items
- Out: Heist outcomes (e40-crate-heist)
- Out: Quell dialogue (e39-dialogue-harbor-trade)

## Notes
The seal records who stamped it; the dead clerk E. Ardley's stamp is evidence (bible canon).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the watchman's night patrol, when the stealth replay enters via a skylight, then bay nine can be reached with the watchman never exceeding Suspicious.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the bay nine seal broken, when re-sealed with the customs-seal stamp item, then the seal reads intact to inspection; without the stamp it reads broken.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the watchman finds a broken seal on his round, when perceived, then he raises the alarm and the harbour watch investigates (edge: failure creates pursuit, not reload).
- AC-4 [content] Given the obstacle registry, when validated, then bay nine declares >= 3 class routes.

title: Build the Customs House, its strongroom and Cray's book confiscation
description:
## Why
Inspector Cray is the MVP's only on-screen Lantern Court official; confiscation turns carrying books into a story.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a customs inspector who confiscates restricted books I carry openly so that smuggling them becomes my own heist.
Customs House: cargo scale, Cray's office (the well-read shelf, confiscated romances), the manifest copy of bay nine, the strongroom of confiscated goods (skylight/roof route, locked door). Inspection: at the barge berth and the customs gate, any book item with legality restricted and no writ in the player's visible inventory is moved to the strongroom as an owned-by-customs item (never forbidden-plot items). Recovery: buy back with a writ, steal back (a crime via e22-crime-bounty), or charm back (Contraband Pages).

## Scope
- In: Interior, strongroom container, inspection trigger + legality check, writ condition, confiscation facts
- Out: Contraband Pages quest graph (e39-side-quests-harbor)
- Out: Cray dialogue (e39-dialogue-harbor-trade)
- Out: Crime/bounty rules (e22-crime-bounty)

## Notes
Related: e21-stolen-forbidden-stock (P2) for reselling recovered restricted books. Stowaway arrivals (e25-barge-travel) and sneaking past the gate skip inspection.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player carries a restricted book without a writ, when inspected, then the book moves to the strongroom container and fact customs.confiscated.<bookId> is set.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a book flagged as a plot item, when inspected, then it is never confiscated (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given a confiscated book stolen back from the strongroom while witnessed, when reported, then a Wendmouth crime is recorded via e22-crime-bounty.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the player holds a writ fact, when inspected, then nothing is confiscated and Cray's disposition is unchanged.

title: Build the Stone Wharf with working cranes, cargo nets, crates and block yards
description:
## Why
The wharf is the harbour's toybox: swinging loads, cuttable nets and crate and block-yard mazes for every class.

## What
As a player, I want cranes I can operate, nets I can cut and crates and stone blocks I can climb or hide behind so that the wharf invites hijinks.
The great stepped glenstone quay where stone barges unload: two treadwheel cranes on stone piers (operable winch + jib rotation, suspended loads on ropes), cargo nets (rope supports: cuttable, flammable, shootable), block yards of dressed glenstone in rows (climbable, hiding spots), stacked crates (climbable, hiding spots, pushable), the Lantern Court notice board, the open flagstones marked for Tidefair events, and at the far end the Silver Quay behind an iron gate and imperial guards (a non-enterable set piece: seen, not entered).

## Scope
- In: Crane mechanisms, net/rope entities, crate stacks and block yards with material presets, Tidefair space markers, the gated Silver Quay backdrop
- Out: Tidefair event logic (Tidefair items)
- Out: Heist hoist sequence (e40-crate-heist)

## Notes
Everything via properties: a net drops when its supporting rope is cut, burnt or shot — never scripted per weapon.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a loaded cargo net hanging from a crane, when its rope is severed by any means, then the load falls under physics and lands or splashes into the water volume below.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the crane jib rotated with a load swinging, when the load strikes a creature, then impulse damage applies via the damage model.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a crate stack pushed over, when it collapses onto the only walkway, then a climb or push route over the debris remains (edge: no softlock).

title: Block out Wendmouth harbour in grey-box with every named place
description:
## Why
Wendmouth is where shenanigans ensue; its layout decides every sightline, rooftop and heist route.

## What
As a player, I want a crooked, crowded harbour I can read in one visit so that I can plan mischief.
Grey-box (~200×160 m): Stone Wharf (great stepped quay, barge berth, block yards, open Tidefair flagstones, and the gated Silver Quay at its far end — seen, not entered), the columned Customs House, the vaulted Bonded Warehouse, the fish market over the Undertow, the Tidemarket, net lofts, the breakwater with the Drowned Gull at its end, the pool with the Gilded Tern at anchor, towpath and barge arrival points. Massing is monumental glenstone (stepped quays, block breakwater, vaulted warehouses) with timber net lofts and sheds perched on the stone; the pool and quay edges are standing-water volumes.

## Scope
- In: Harbour scene, building shells and entries, navmesh, water volumes, connectivity nodes, arrival spawns
- Out: Per-place content (other E40 items)
- Out: Art (e40-harbor-art-dress)

## Notes
Wendmouth is optional (bible §3.6): no main-quest edge may require it. The river does not flow in the sim; the harbour pool is standing water.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the scene, when validated, then every bible §3.6 place exists as a named node linked in connectivity.json.
- AC-2 [content] Given connectivity.json, when the main-quest critical path is computed, then no required edge passes through a Wendmouth node (edge: optional town).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the navmesh, when queried, then every building entry is reachable from both the barge berth and the towpath arrival.
- AC-4 [perf] Given the grey-box harbour from the Stone Wharf, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

title: Playtest the full dungeon per class and replay each critical path
description:
## Why
The MVP's defining scenario must be completable and memorable for every class.

## What
Automated critical-path replays per class from the mine gate to "Vespers rung"; one internal playtest per class through the whole dungeon; findings to docs/playtests/dungeon.md with beads.

## Scope
- In: 4 critical-path replays, 4 playtests, findings
- Out: External playtests (e35-external-round-1)

## Notes
Replays must cover two different macro-routes per class across the four runs.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a save at the mine gate, when each class's critical-path replay runs, then vespers.rung is set with zero console errors.
- AC-2 [manual] Given one tester per class, when finished, then each rates the dungeon >= 4/5 for "my class mattered".
- AC-3 [manual] Given testers who got stuck > 5 minutes, when observed, then each stuck point has a bead or accepted note (edge).

title: Perf-pass every dungeon area on both presets
description:
## Why
The dungeon hosts the heaviest fights and effects; it must hold budgets everywhere.

## What
Perf suite scenes for the goblin hall, scriptorium fire, Ossuary fight, Chapel, Horn's Hall, Cradle and the climb; captures on reference and low-tier machines; fixes within budget; area load times.

## Scope
- In: Perf scenes, captures, fixes, report
- Out: Engine-level perf (E32)

## Notes
Related: e32-reference-runbook, e32-memory-leak-test.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given each listed dungeon perf scene, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).
- AC-2 [perf] Given the Cradle fight on Low, when measured, then p95 <= 16.7 ms at 1080p on the Low preset on an Intel Iris Xe / base M1 8 GB class machine, with p99 <= 33.3 ms (30 fps floor) during worst-case combat.
- AC-3 [perf] Given warm caches, when transitioning between any two adjacent dungeon areas, then load <= 3 s and heap <= 1.5 GB after 30 transitions (edge).

title: Light and score the dungeon: mine, priory, Knot and the finale
description:
## Why
Darkness is a stealth system and a mood; the song must be heard growing.

## What
As a player, I want each dungeon layer to have its own light and sound so that descending feels like going deeper into a dream.
Lighting per area (lamps in the mine, moonlight in the priory, rune glow in the Knot), ambience beds (mine drips and creaks, priory wind, Knot hum, Chapel echoes), music cues per area plus the song layer driven by song.intensity, set-piece audio (sour bell, Horn's Hall, Cradle, climb, Vespers ring).

## Scope
- In: Lighting, ambience zones, reverb zones, music cue bindings, set-piece cue wiring
- Out: Audio assets (E38)

## Notes
Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. Gameplay never waits on this item. Related: e28-ambience, e28-reverb-zones and e29-environment-fx are P2 in the combat plan; bind ambience beds, reverb zones and fog/firefly FX here when they land, otherwise ship lighting + music only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given song.intensity changes, when evaluated, then the song music layer gain follows within 2 s.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the Vespers ring, when triggered, then all other music ducks and the bell cue plays uninterrupted.
- AC-3 [integration] Given dungeon lighting, when sampled along each thief route, then at least 40% of each route has light <= 0.3 (edge: stealth remains viable).
- AC-4 [perf] Given the Chapel with 3 Hushlings and all area lights, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

title: Art-dress the Knot with Hornfolk stone, runes and dream visuals
description:
## Why
The Knot is a sentence carved as corridors; its art must make runes legible and the Cradle dreamlike.

## What
As a player, I want the labyrinth's walls to be written in Hornfolk runes and the Cradle to shimmer so that the place feels ancient and alive.
Hornfolk stone kit, rune band decals (readable, with landmark faces), bone niches, chapel acoustics visuals, Fold moss, Cradle dream-leak shaders.

## Scope
- In: Art swap for Knot scenes, rune decals, Cradle shaders
- Out: Asset creation (E37)

## Notes
Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. Gameplay never waits on this item.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the dressed Knot, when rune-navigation tests and all Knot replays run, then they pass unchanged.
- AC-2 [perf] Given the Cradle fight with dream shaders, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).
- AC-3 [manual] Given 3 testers, when asked to follow runes, then >= 2 identify the rune to follow from art alone (edge: legibility).

title: Art-dress the Deepworks and Bellwater Priory with final assets
description:
## Why
Timbered galleries and a roofless nave must read instantly as different places.

## What
As a player, I want the mine and the priory to look like the story bible so that each layer of the dungeon has its own identity.
Swap grey-box for mine kit (pale cut-glenstone galleries, timber supports, rails, block carts, frost-bright silver seams, goblin junk) and priory kit (Vesperine stone, singing statues, bell); keep gameplay ids and collision.

## Scope
- In: Art swap for Deepworks and priory scenes, LODs, decals
- Out: Asset creation (E37)

## Notes
Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. Gameplay never waits on this item.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the dressed scenes, when all E26 route and puzzle replays in these areas run, then they pass unchanged.
- AC-2 [perf] Given the goblin hall and the nave, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).
- AC-3 [manual] Given the art review, when compared to the style bible, then silhouettes of interactables remain readable against dressing (edge).

title: Build the four endings' level states across town and dungeon
description:
## Why
Endings are assembled from world facts; the world itself should show the ending.

## What
As a player, I want the world to visibly change after my ending so that my choices feel real.
Fact-gated variants (e27-world-variants): Vespers Rung (bell rung each dusk by goblins/Hale/Tansy, bread at the mine gate, wolves howl again if breach sealed); The Last Warden (Horn's absence, goblin watch or Clatter humming, lantern and footprints at the gate); The Hireling's Silence (mine reopened, Vane prosperous, sleepwalker sitting up); The Long Vespers (sleeping valley, goblin with a stick in the Cradle).

## Scope
- In: Variant entity sets per ending in town, gate, Fold, Cradle; epilogue camera anchors
- Out: Ending logic and text (e39-main-quest-data, e39-intro-endings-text)

## Notes
Epilogue slides are text over these level states.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the facts for each ending, when the town and gate load, then the matching variant set is active and no other ending's variants are.
- AC-2 [integration] Given breach.sealed with Vespers Rung, when night falls in the Briarwood, then wolf howls resume.
- AC-3 [integration] Given contradictory facts (horn.killed and horn.befriended), when evaluated, then killed takes precedence and a content warning is logged (edge).

title: Author first-pass class routes through every dungeon area
description:
## Why
The knight forces, the thief infiltrates, the archer manipulates distant mechanisms, the sorcerer alters the dungeon.

## What
As a player of any class, I want each dungeon area to offer my class a route so that the Labyrinth plays differently for me.
Per area: knight (weak walls, heavy doors, holding chokepoints), archer (distant mechanisms, open-chamber dominance, rope anchors), sorcerer (freeze/levitate/blink/illusion affordances), thief (vents, crawlspaces, hidden passages, dark routes). Registry entries and replays.

## Scope
- In: Route affordances across mine/priory/Knot, registry entries, replays
- Out: Gap closing after audit (e16-gap-pass-dungeon)

## Notes
Every thief hidden passage should be discoverable by others too (with effort) — secrets are for everyone.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the registry, when validated, then every E26 mandatory obstacle has >= 3 class routes declared.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each declared route, when replayed, then the obstacle exit fact is set.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a thief hidden passage, when a non-thief searches the wall, then it can be found with a light or search action (edge).

title: Wire dungeon shortcuts: crypt, cistern, cage lift and one-way doors
description:
## Why
Every loop is a shortcut the player can open; the dungeon should fold back on itself.

## What
As a player, I want to open doors from the far side and ride lifts back up so that returning to earlier areas is fast.
Shortcuts: crypt passage Knot ↔ priory (Horn opens, or pry from below), cistern ↔ priory (gate from the priory side), winch cage mine top ↔ bottom, supply-tunnel arrival ↔ goblin hall, Outer Ring ↔ Deepworks breach bypass. One-way doors with a visible "barred on this side" state.

## Scope
- In: Shortcut doors/lifts, facts, connectivity updates
- Out: Transition engine (e01-area-transitions)

## Notes
Each shortcut fact persists and shows on the world map notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a one-way door approached from the locked side, when interacted, then it shows the barred state and does not open.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each shortcut opened, when saved and reloaded, then it remains open.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the cage lift at the bottom and the player at the top, when the call lever is used, then the cage returns (edge: never stranded).

title: Ring the Vesper Bell: hang the tongue, mend it and wake the sleepers
description:
## Why
The solution is a lullaby. Ringing the cracked bell — wrong and beautiful — is the climax.

## What
As a player, I want to hang the bronze tongue and ring the bell so that the Nightjar sleeps and the missing wake.
Belfry finale: hang tongue (or Oswin's recast), optional mend first (Frostglass/Alteration-class property effect sets bell.mended for a truer note), ring. Song falters (song.intensity → 0), Hushlings dissolve, the Fold sleepers wake (sleepers.woken), Tansy asks who you are. Sets vespers.rung.

## Scope
- In: Tongue hang interaction, mend option, ring sequence, facts, dissolve/wake hooks
- Out: Endings text (e39-intro-endings-text)
- Out: Ending level states (e26-ending-states)

## Notes
Mend is systemic: any freeze or alteration effect applied to the crack entity counts.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the tongue hung, when the bell is rung, then vespers.rung is set, song.intensity becomes 0 and all Hushlings dissolve.
- AC-2 [integration] Given bell.mended before ringing, when rung, then the truer-note variant plays and fact bell.trueNote is set.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the tongue was destroyed and no recast exists, when the belfry is reached, then Oswin's recast path is signposted (edge: never unwinnable).

title: Build the Sounding Shaft climb with defenders and chase variants
description:
## Why
With the tongue recovered, the bell must ring: a vertical ascent with the song rising behind.

## What
As a player, I want to climb from the Cradle to the belfry on ropes, counterweights and old bell-ropes so that the finale is a set piece.
Shaft interior: ledges, bell-rope climbs, counterweight lifts, a collapsing stair section. Variants by facts: Horn holds the foot (horn alive and healed/befriended); goblins or Clatter hold it; knight holds while restored Clatter climbs (sacrifice beat); nobody → chase with Hushlings climbing. Archer shortcut: rope line skips half the climb.

## Scope
- In: Shaft scene, climb routes, defender variants, chase spawner, archer shortcut
- Out: Ally behaviours (e14-horn-befriend-help)

## Notes
Falling during the chase drops the player to the last ledge checkpoint, not the bottom (anti-frustration).
acceptance_criteria:
