Dialogue, quests, shops, loot and deeds all need "if X then do Y" without bespoke scripting; one validated DSL prevents five incompatible mini-languages and eval().
## What
JSON-serializable, zod-validated expression language in src/sim/logic. Conditions: `all/any/not`, `fact`, `factCmp`, `hasItem`, `hasCapability`, `playerClass`, `disposition`, `questState`, `objectiveState`, `gold`, `timeOfDay`. Effects: `setFact`, `giveItem`, `takeItem`, `gold`, `disposition`, `startQuest`, `completeObjective`, `resolveQuest`, `failQuest`, `learnCapability`, `emit` (sim event), `revealRumor`. Evaluator is pure over a context interface; effects apply as an atomic batch (all or nothing). Extensible registry so other epics add condition/effect kinds with their own validators.
## Scope
- In: Schema, evaluator, atomic effect applier, registry for extension, reference validation hooks, human-readable describe() for tooling/UI
- Out: Dialogue graph (e22-dialogue-runtime)
- Out: Quest graph (e23-quest-runtime)
## Notes
No string expressions, no eval. Describe() output powers "requires: …" hints for locked options.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given `all[hasItem(key-a), not(fact(door.open))]` and a context with key-a and door closed, when evaluated, then result is true.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an effect batch [takeItem(x), giveItem(y)] where takeItem fails, when applied, then neither effect is applied and the failure reason is returned.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an unknown condition kind in data, when validated, then validation fails naming the kind and path.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a registered extension condition, when used in content, then it validates and evaluates like built-ins.
- AC-5 [unit] Given any condition, when describe() is called, then it returns a non-empty localized-key string (tested for every built-in kind).

title: Build shop UI with merchant identity, buy/sell and price breakdown
description:
## Why
Merchants must feel like characters, and players must understand why prices are what they are.
## What
As a player, I want a shop screen that shows the merchant's face and personality, clear buy/sell lists and why an item costs what it does so that trading is quick and characterful.

Layout: merchant portrait slot + greeting bark; tabs Buy / Sell / Buyback / Services; item rows with price, specialty badge, stolen marker (sell tab), comparison vs equipped; price tooltip shows modifier breakdown (disposition, specialty, haggle); Haggle button (when available); quantity selector for stacks; confirm for expensive (> 25% of gold) purchases.
## Scope
- In: Shop screen, tabs, breakdown tooltip, quantity selector, confirmation, keyboard/gamepad, text-size support
- Out: Haggle flow UI (uses dialogue UI)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: shop panel frame, merchant portrait frame, specialty badge icon, gold icon, stolen marker icon, buyback icon.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a merchant with specialty "books", when the Sell tab lists a book, then a specialty badge shows and the tooltip lists the specialty modifier.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a purchase costing > 25% of player gold, when confirmed, then a confirmation dialog appears; cheaper purchases complete in one input.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a stolen item on the Sell tab at a non-fence, when displayed, then the row is disabled with the refusal reason.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the greybox merchant, when the player buys an item and sells it back via Buyback, then gold and inventory match the pre-buy state.
- AC-5 [unit] Given text size 150%, when the shop renders, then price columns remain aligned and no row text is clipped.

title: Add purchasable services as meaningful gold sinks
description:
## Why
Gold has meaningful uses beyond items: healing, lodging, translation of books, bribes and donations create choices and stories.
## What
As a player, I want to pay for services (heal, rest at the inn, translate an untranslated book, bribe a guard, donate to the shrine) so that gold opens doors, not just inventory slots.

Service schema: `{id, providerNpcId, price or priceFormula, conditions, effects}` reusing the effect DSL; invoked from dialogue. Bribes/donations can change disposition or facts.
## Scope
- In: Service schema + validator, purchase via dialogue effect, atomic gold deduction
- Out: Trainer techniques (e19-knight-trainer-channel uses this)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a translate-book service costing 40 and an untranslated book in inventory, when purchased, then 40 gold is removed and the book instance gains `translated`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given insufficient gold, when purchasing, then nothing changes and the dialogue receives `insufficient-gold`.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a service whose conditions are unmet (e.g. no untranslated book), when listed, then it is hidden or shown locked per its `showWhenLocked` flag.
- AC-4 [content] Given service data, when validated, then every provider NPC and effect reference resolves.

title: Support fences and merchant reactions to stolen goods
description:
## Why
Stolen goods need an outlet and consequences; offering a merchant their own stolen silver should be memorable (and funny).
## What
As a thief, I want to sell stolen goods to a fence at a discount, and face consequences if I try to sell them to their owner so that theft is a complete loop.

Fences buy stolen items at the economy-doc discount. Non-fences refuse stolen items; if the merchant (or their faction) is the owner, emit `crime.theft.recognized` → disposition drop and optional guard alert. Fences can "launder" at a fee (clear stolen flag) if the design doc enables it.
## Scope
- In: Fence rules, owner recognition, disposition/crime events, optional laundering
- Out: Guard arrest/bounty behaviour (mw-e11)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a stolen item worth 100 and a fence with discount 0.4, when sold, then the player receives the price model result for a fence (breakdown includes stolen discount).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a merchant who owns a stolen item the player tries to sell, when attempted, then the sale is refused, disposition drops by the configured amount and `crime.theft.recognized` is emitted.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a stolen item owned by someone else, when offered to a non-fence, then the sale is refused with no crime event.
- AC-4 [unit] Given laundering enabled, when paid, then the stolen flag clears and gold is deducted atomically.

title: Restock merchant inventories on world-time ticks deterministically
description:
## Why
Living shops change over time; rotating stock gives reasons to return (and underpins bookshop rotation in E21).
## What
As a player, I want merchants to restock and occasionally carry new things so that revisiting shops is worthwhile.

On world day tick: restock entries flagged `restock` up to their counts, roll `rotating` loot-table entries with seed (merchantId, day), refill gold toward reserve, clear buyback. Unique items never restock. Condition-gated stock (e.g. after a quest outcome) appears when conditions become true.
## Scope
- In: Restock scheduler, rotation rolling, conditional stock, gold refill
- Out: Bookshop regional/rare/secret rules (e21-bookshop-system)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a restock entry of count 3 with stock 0, when a day tick passes, then stock is 3.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same merchant and day, when rotation rolls twice (e.g. across reload), then the rotating stock is identical.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a sold-out unique item, when any number of day ticks pass, then it never reappears.
- AC-4 [unit] Given stock gated on fact `bridge.repaired`, when the fact becomes true, then the entry appears on the next tick.

title: Implement merchant buy/sell transactions with persistent stock
description:
## Why
Gold needs meaningful uses and merchants need living inventories; transactions must never duplicate or lose items or gold.
## What
As a player, I want to buy and sell with merchants whose stock and gold are finite and remembered so that shops feel like real places.

Atomic transactions: buy (player gold ≥ price, stock > 0) and sell (merchant gold ≥ price, merchant buys category, not refused). Buyback: last 10 sold items repurchasable at the sell price until restock. Stock, gold and buyback stored in world-state store. Emits `shop.bought`/`shop.sold` events for quests/telemetry.
## Scope
- In: Transaction engine, merchant runtime state, buyback, persistence, events
- Out: Restocking (e20-restock-rotation)
- Out: UI (e20-shop-ui)
- Out: Haggling (e20-haggling)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given player gold 100 and an item priced 80 with stock 1, when bought, then player gold is 20, the item is in inventory, merchant gold +80 and stock 0.
- AC-2 [unit] Given stock 0, when a buy is attempted, then it fails with `out-of-stock` and no state changes.
- AC-3 [unit] Given merchant gold 30 and a sell priced 50, when sold, then it fails with `merchant-cannot-afford` (or offers 30 if the economy doc enables partial) and state is unchanged on failure.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an item just sold, when bought back before restock, then the price equals the sell price.
- AC-5 [unit] Given 1,000 random buy/sell sequences (seeded), when executed, then total gold across player+merchant and total item count are conserved.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a transaction, when saved and reloaded, then merchant stock, gold and buyback are unchanged.

title: Implement pure price model with disposition and stolen modifiers
description:
## Why
Prices must respond to relationships and context, be deterministic, and be 100% tested (contract §3: economy at 100%).
## What
Pure function `price({item, instance, merchant, direction: buy|sell, disposition, haggleModifier, worldFacts})` → integer gold with a breakdown of applied modifiers. Modifiers: base value, merchant markup/buyRate, specialty bonus, disposition band multiplier, stolen (fence discount; non-fence refuses), quest items unsellable, floor of 1 gold, sell price never exceeds buy price for the same merchant.
## Scope
- In: Price function, breakdown for UI, exhaustive tests incl. property tests
- Out: Transactions (e20-shop-system)
- Out: Haggle flow (e20-haggling)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an item of value 100, merchant markup 1.2 and neutral disposition, when pricing a buy, then the price is 120 and the breakdown lists base and markup.
- AC-2 [unit] Given friendly vs cold disposition bands, when pricing the same buy, then the friendly price is lower by the economy doc multipliers.
- AC-3 [unit] Given any item/merchant/disposition combination (property test, 10,000 cases), when pricing, then sell price ≤ buy price and price ≥ 1.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a stolen item and a non-fence merchant, when pricing a sell, then the result is `refused: stolen`.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a quest item, when pricing a sell, then the result is `refused: quest-item`.

title: Define merchant schema with identity, specialty and stock rules
description:
## Why
Merchants need identities, inventories and specialties (QfG5 personality, Elder Scrolls living shops) authored as data.
## What
Zod schema `merchant`: `id`, `npcId` (dialogue speaker), `personalityTags` (e.g. greedy, gossipy, suspicious), `specialties` (item categories/tags bought at better rates), `buysCategories`, `stock: [{item | lootTable, count, restock?}]`, `goldReserve` + `goldRestock`, `markup`/`buyRate` bands, `isFence`, `hours?` (world time hook), `barkSet` id. Validator checks references and bands against economy doc.
## Scope
- In: Schema, validator, 2 grey-box fixture merchants (general goods, fence)
- Out: Bookshop specialisation (e21-bookshop-system extends this)
- Out: Briar Glen merchants (world-content group)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 2 fixture merchants, when validated, then validation passes.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a merchant with markup outside the economy doc band, when validated, then validation fails naming merchant and field.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a merchant whose stock references a missing item or loot table, when validated, then validation fails with the reference.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a merchant with `isFence: false` and `buysStolen: true`, when validated, then validation fails (only fences buy stolen goods).

title: Write economy design: gold income, meaningful sinks, price bands
description:
## Why
Gold must have meaningful uses; without a budget the MVP will either drown the player in gold or starve the bookshop.
## What
docs/design/economy.md: gold income sources (loot, quests, selling, theft), meaningful sinks (spellbooks, trainer techniques, arrow materials, thief tools, services, bribes, donations/deeds), price bands per item tier, target gold curve across the MVP (e.g. can afford 1 of 3 premium books on first bookshop visit), merchant markup ranges, disposition and stolen-goods modifier ranges, haggle limits.
## Scope
- In: Doc with numeric targets consumed by e20-price-model and e20-economy-balance-tool
- Out: Merchant content (world-content group)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the doc, when reviewed, then it lists every sink category with a price band in gold.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the doc, when reviewed, then it defines a target obtainable-gold : sink-cost ratio band for the MVP region (e.g. 0.6–0.8) used by the balance tool.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the doc, when reviewed, then it gives numeric ranges for disposition, specialty, stolen and haggle modifiers.

title: Build capabilities screen and "new verb learned" feedback
description:
## Why
Players must notice and remember new verbs, otherwise capability progression is invisible.
## What
As a player, I want a screen listing what I can do, grouped by source, with hints about what I might learn next, and a clear moment when I learn something new so that I try my new verbs.

Screen: capabilities grouped (Class, Learned, From Gear, Temporary), each with icon, description and input hint. "Rumoured" section shows known-but-unlearned capabilities from rumors/books glimpsed. Learn moment: banner with verb name, one-line usage hint, and input glyph; optional short practice prompt.
## Scope
- In: Capabilities screen, learn banner, input glyph binding, rumoured hints
- Out: Spellbook-specific UI (mw-e07)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: capability/verb icons per class (placeholder shapes first), learn banner frame, input glyph set (KB/M + gamepad).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given capabilities from class, learning and an equipped lantern, when the screen opens, then each appears under the correct group with its icon.
- AC-2 [integration] Given `capability.gained` from a learn action, when fired, then the learn banner appears within 1 frame and shows the currently bound input glyph for that verb.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player remaps the verb's input, when the screen reopens, then the new glyph is shown.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a temporary capability expires while the screen is open, when it expires, then it is removed from the list without closing the screen.

title: Grant thief verbs from tools and tricks learned from contacts
description:
## Why
Thief growth is about tools and tricks (lockpicks, grapples, smoke, disguises); owning a tool is owning a verb.
## What
As a thief, I want new tools and tricks to open new routes so that my arsenal grows in options, not numbers.

Tools are items with `grants` (via e17-equipment-verbs on the toolBelt, or passive when carried per ADR). Tricks (e.g. `trick.feign-death`, `trick.shadow-step`) are learned from notes/contacts via the shared learn API with channel `trick`. Tool degradation per ADR (e.g. lockpicks can break — failure creates stories).
## Scope
- In: Tool-carried capability grants, trick learning channel, optional breakage rule hook
- Out: Tool mechanics (mw-e10)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given lockpicks on the tool belt, when checked, then `tool.lockpick` is granted; removing the lockpicks revokes it.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a trick note read by a thief, when read, then the trick is learned with channel `trick`.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a breakable tool with 1 durability, when a breaking event occurs, then the tool is removed and its capability revoked with a `tool.broke` event.
- AC-4 [unit] Given two lockpick stacks, when one breaks, then the capability remains while any stack remains.

title: Unlock archer trick arrows via schematics and trick-shot techniques
description:
## Why
Archers control space through specialized arrows and trick shots; new arrow types are new verbs.
## What
As an archer, I want to find fletching schematics and learn trick shots so that my quiver gains new ways to solve problems (rope arrows, water arrows, noise arrows).

Fletching schematic item → `learn(arrow.<type>, channel: schematic)`; once known, arrows of that type can be assembled at rest points from simple materials (count-limited, no crafting tree). Trick-shot techniques (e.g. ricochet, pinning) learned from deeds or trainers via the shared channels.
## Scope
- In: Schematic item handling, simple arrow assembly (materials → arrows), trick-shot unlock via deed/trainer
- Out: Arrow physics and effects (mw-e05)
- Out: General crafting system (not MVP)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an archer reading a rope-arrow schematic, when read, then `arrow.rope` is learned with channel `schematic` and the schematic is consumed.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `arrow.rope` known and 2 rope + 2 shafts, when assembling at a rest point, then 2 rope arrows are added and materials removed.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `arrow.rope` not known, when assembling, then the recipe is unavailable even with materials.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a non-archer reading a schematic, when read, then behaviour follows the ADR cross-learning rule and is covered by a test.

title: Let trainers teach knight techniques through dialogue services
description:
## Why
Knights master techniques; learning them from a character (for gold, a deed, or a duel) is more memorable than a skill point.
## What
As a knight, I want to learn new techniques from trainers who demand payment, proof or a test so that each new move has a story.

Trainer = NPC with `teaches: [{capability, price?, requires: conditions, test?: questId}]`. Dialogue effect `learnCapability` (via e22 DSL) and a service listing in the trainer's dialogue. Supports technique chains (shield bash → shield charge → shield vault) and non-gold prices (a favour quest).
## Scope
- In: Trainer data schema, dialogue effect binding, gold deduction via shop transactions, test-quest gating
- Out: Technique mechanics (mw-e04)
- Out: Specific trainer NPCs (world-content group)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a trainer teaching `technique.shield-charge` for 50 gold and a knight with 60 gold and the prerequisite, when learned, then gold is 10 and the capability is granted with channel `trainer`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given insufficient gold, when the learn effect runs, then it fails atomically (no gold removed, no capability).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a technique gated by a test quest not yet resolved, when offered in dialogue, then the option is shown as locked with its requirement text.
- AC-4 [content] Given all trainer data, when validated, then every taught capability exists and every test quest id resolves.

title: Wire spellbook learning into progression prerequisites
description:
## Why
Magic is learned primarily from books (constitution §4). Book learning must respect progression prerequisites and class rules defined in the ADR.
## What
As a sorcerer, I want reading a spellbook to teach me its spell when I understand the prerequisites so that books become exciting and school knowledge matters.

Adapter from e07-spellbook-learning to `progression.learn(spell, channel: book)`. Handles: missing prerequisite (book stays readable, shows what knowledge is missing), non-sorcerer readers per ADR cross-learning rule, damaged/untranslated books gated by conditions.
## Scope
- In: Adapter, failure explanations, cross-class rule enforcement
- Out: Book reading UI and spell data (mw-e07, mw-e08)
- Out: Bookshop inventories (e21-bookshop-system)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a sorcerer reading a book for a spell whose prerequisites are met, when read, then the spell capability is granted with source `learned` and channel `book`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a knight reading a sorcerer-only spellbook, when read, then no capability is granted and the result explains per ADR (e.g. "The runes swim before your eyes.").
- AC-3 [unit] Given a book whose spell is already known, when read, then no duplicate grant occurs and the book is flagged `read`.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the greybox testbed, when a sorcerer picks up and reads a test spellbook, then the new spell appears in the capabilities list and can be cast.

title: Implement minimal supporting stats and rare stat growth sources
description:
## Why
Stats can exist but must support rather than define progression (constitution §3); keep them few and legible.
## What
As a player, I want a small set of stats (e.g. health, stamina, focus) that grow from rare discoveries so that finding a heart-container-like relic feels special without turning into grind.

Stats per ADR (≤ 5), with base from class, modifiers from equipment and temporary effects, and permanent increments from data-defined sources (relic items, shrines, deeds). Hard caps. No per-kill XP.
## Scope
- In: Stat model with base/modifier/permanent layers, caps, sources, events, save section
- Out: Combat consumption of stamina/poise (mw-e04)
- Out: Mana/focus spending (mw-e06)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given base health 100 and a relic granting +10 permanent max health, when consumed, then max health is 110 and current health increases by 10.
- AC-2 [unit] Given max health at its cap, when another permanent increment is applied, then it is clamped and the source is not consumed (returns `at-cap`).
- AC-3 [unit] Given an equipment modifier of -10 stamina, when unequipped, then stamina max returns to its prior value.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature is killed, when resolved, then no stat changes occur (no per-kill XP).

title: Write treasure design guide for handcrafted loot
description:
## Why
World-content authors need a shared rule set so loot stays meaningful across the town, wilderness and labyrinth.
## What
docs/design/treasure.md: treasure tiers (junk-with-jokes, useful consumables, tools, books, artifacts), placement density guidelines ("interesting-looking places usually contain something"), ratio of handcrafted vs table-rolled, gold budget per area (links to economy doc), ownership conventions, humour guidelines for flavour text.
## Scope
- In: Guide doc with examples and anti-patterns
- Out: Actual placements (world-content group)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the guide, when reviewed, then it defines each treasure tier with one example and an anti-pattern.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the guide, when reviewed, then it states numeric density targets (e.g. discoveries per room/area) and the handcrafted:rolled ratio.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the guide, when reviewed, then it references the economy gold budget from e20-economy-design.

title: Add unique artifacts with active verbs and lore
description:
## Why
Handcrafted discoveries with verbs are the reward that replaces stat-sticks; artifacts should make players say "wait, I can do that?"
## What
As a player, I want rare artifacts that do strange, useful things so that finding one changes how I play.

Artifact = item with `flags.unique` and either passive `grants` or an `activate` block (cooldown/charges, effects via the shared effect vocabulary and world properties). Examples for grey-box tests only: a compass that points to the nearest hidden placement, a bell that emits a loud noise event at a distance, a cold stone that gives `frozen` to touched water. Uniqueness enforced world-wide.
## Scope
- In: Activate verb, charges/cooldown, uniqueness guarantee, lore text field, 3 grey-box test artifacts
- Out: The MVP artifact roster (world-content group)
## Notes
Artifacts must express effects via properties (e03) — never artifact-specific code paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an artifact with 3 charges and recharge-on-rest, when activated 4 times without rest, then the 4th activation fails with reason `no-charges`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a unique artifact already obtained, when any table or placement tries to grant another, then no second instance is created.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the bell test artifact activated, when resolved, then a noise event with the configured loudness is emitted at the target point and nearby guards react via e11.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the cold-stone test artifact touching a `wet`/water volume, when resolved, then the volume gains `frozen` via e03 propagation.
- AC-5 [content] Given all artifact data, when validated, then each has a non-empty lore text key and at least one grant or activate effect.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: mw-e18.1 note: the loot roller treats a unique item as obtained when the fact item.<id>.obtained is true (obtainedFactKey in src/sim/loot/tables.ts), or via LootContext.isObtained. Nothing writes that fact yet: the uniqueness guarantee here should set it on first pickup (and declare it in the fact registry, which throws on undeclared writes in dev/test).

title: Drop what creatures actually carry, plus data-driven extras
description:
## Why
Creatures are not target dummies or loot piñatas; what they carry should be visible and plausible (the goblin with the lantern drops the lantern).
## What
As a player, I want defeated or robbed creatures to hold the gear I saw them using so that loot feels grounded.

Creature schema extension: `carried` inventory (equipped items shown on the creature) + optional `dropTable` for pouch contents. On death the corpse becomes a container; on pickpocket (mw-e10) the carried inventory is the source. Wolves drop nothing but pelts-as-quest-materials only if data says so.
## Scope
- In: Carried inventory on creatures, corpse-as-container, owned-by-creature flags (robbing a living goblin is theft)
- Out: Pickpocket mechanics (mw-e10)
- Out: Harvesting/crafting (not planned for MVP)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature with carried [rusty-sword, lantern], when killed, then its corpse container holds exactly those plus the rolled drop table results.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature with no carried items and no drop table, when killed, then no corpse container is created (no empty loot prompt).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a living intelligent creature, when an item is taken from it, then the item is flagged stolen with the creature as owner.
- AC-4 [content] Given every creature data file, when validated, then all carried/dropTable references resolve.

title: Track item ownership and flag stolen items on witnessed theft
description:
## Why
Stealing must be a real systemic act with consequences (thief fantasy, Elder Scrolls living world) and feed shops, disposition and AI.
## What
As a thief, I want taking things that belong to others to be tracked and only punished when someone notices so that careful theft pays off and sloppy theft creates stories.

Ownership on containers, placements and world items (`ownerId` NPC or faction). Taking an owned item marks the instance `stolen` with owner. At the moment of taking, witnesses are evaluated via e11 perception/e09 visibility: witnessed theft emits `crime.theft` (value, owner, witnesses) consumed by e11-alert-states and disposition; unwitnessed theft emits nothing but the item remains flagged. Owner discovers missing high-value items later (optional fact `owner.noticedMissing`).
## Scope
- In: Ownership data, stolen flag assignment, witness check, crime event, returning stolen items clears the flag
- Out: Guard responses/bounty (mw-e11)
- Out: Fence pricing (e20-fences-stolen-goods)
- Out: Pickpocket minigame (mw-e10)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an owned item in a container and no witness able to see the player, when taken, then the instance is stolen with the ownerId and no `crime.theft` event is emitted.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an NPC with the player in sight cone and visibility ≥ its threshold, when an owned item is taken, then `crime.theft` is emitted listing that NPC as witness.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a stolen item given back to its owner (via dialogue effect or putting it back in the owner's container), when returned, then the stolen flag clears.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unowned item, when taken in full view, then no stolen flag or crime event occurs.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox guard watching a chest, when the player takes an item, then the guard enters at least the Suspicious alert state.

title: Support designer-placed and hidden treasure with discovery rules
description:
## Why
The world rewards curiosity: wells hide tunnels, loose bricks hide stashes. Handcrafted placement beats random drops.
## What
As a designer, I want to place specific items in the level and optionally hide them behind discovery conditions so that curious players find hand-authored rewards.

Placement data: `{id, itemOrTable, transform, hidden?: {revealWhen: property-based conditions}}`. Reveal conditions are systemic: light level above threshold (e03-light-field), capability present (e.g. `sense.detect-magic`), object moved/broken (e03 events). Looted placements persist.
## Scope
- In: Placement schema, reveal condition evaluation, persistence, greybox examples: stash under a movable crate, item only visible in light
- Out: Hidden passages / secret doors (mw-e03 / mw-e15)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a hidden placement with `revealWhen: lightLevel >= 0.6`, when light at its position rises to 0.7, then it becomes interactable and a `treasure.revealed` event fires once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a placement hidden under a movable object, when the object is moved off its footprint, then the placement is revealed.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a looted placement, when the level reloads, then the placement does not respawn.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a reveal condition referencing an unknown capability, when content is validated, then validation fails.

title: Add debug console commands to give, remove and inspect items
description:
## Why
Fast content iteration and bug reproduction require spawning items without playing to them.
## What
Debug console commands: `item.give <id> [count] [--stolen owner]`, `item.remove`, `item.list [category]`, `equip <id>`, `gold <n>`, with id auto-complete from the item catalogue.
## Scope
- In: Commands, autocomplete, error messages
- Out: Loot/quest commands (their own epics)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the console, when `item.give healing-draught 3` runs, then the inventory gains 3 and the console prints the new count.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an unknown item id, when `item.give` runs, then the console prints the 3 closest ids by edit distance and changes nothing.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `item.give silver-ring 1 --stolen mayor`, when executed, then the added instance has stolen=true and ownerId=mayor.

title: Add equipment paper-doll view with verb and stealth comparison
description:
## Why
Equipment choices should be legible as trade-offs in verbs, noise and light, not just damage numbers.
## What
As a player, I want to see what I'm wearing and how swapping gear changes my noise, light and available verbs so that I can dress for the job (stealthy thief vs. armored knight).

Paper-doll with slot silhouettes, compare panel showing deltas for noise, weight class, light, granted/lost verbs, and key combat values. Non-proficiency penalties shown clearly.
## Scope
- In: Equipment view, compare panel, slot filters, gamepad support
- Out: 3D character preview rendering (optional, render group later)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: slot silhouette icons (head, body, hands, feet, main, off, trinket, ammo, tool), comparison up/down indicators.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given heavy armor equipped and soft leather hovered, when comparing, then the panel shows noise decrease and weight class change using derived EquipmentState values.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an item that grants a verb, when hovered, then the compare panel lists the verb under "Gains"; unequipping an item lists its verbs under "Loses".
- AC-3 [integration] Given a sorcerer hovering plate armor, when compared, then the non-proficiency penalty is shown with a warning style.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an empty slot, when rendered, then its silhouette placeholder is displayed and is focusable for gamepad navigation.

title: Let equipment grant verbs and systemic properties
description:
## Why
Zelda-style meaningful items: equipment should unlock verbs (a lantern makes light, a grappling hook enables anchors, soft boots quiet footsteps), not just add stats.
## What
As a player, I want gear that changes what I can do so that finding a new item feels like finding a new ability.

Equipped items with `grants` register capabilities as source `equipment:<instanceId>` in the capability registry; unequipping revokes them. Items may also emit properties: `lightRadius` (feeds e03-light-field), `noiseModifier`, `carriesFire`, etc. Interaction prompts query capabilities so new options appear on world objects.
## Scope
- In: Grant/revoke on equip change, property emitters, prompt refresh event
- In: Three grey-box sample items: lantern (light), soft boots (noise), climbing hook (anchor verb)
- Out: The verbs' mechanics themselves (owned by their epics, e.g. climbing in mw-e10)
## Notes
Same registry as progression so dialogue/quests/puzzles check "can the player do X" regardless of source.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an item granting `verb.anchor-climb`, when equipped, then `hasCapability("verb.anchor-climb")` is true; when unequipped, it is false.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player already has a capability from progression and equips an item granting the same one, when the item is unequipped, then the capability remains (source-counted).
- AC-3 [integration] Given an equipped lantern, when the light field is sampled at the player position, then light level increases by the item's `lightRadius` contribution.
- AC-4 [integration] Given soft boots equipped, when the player walks on stone, then emitted footstep noise is reduced by the item's `noiseModifier`.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an item granting an unknown capability at runtime (content bypass), when equipped, then equip succeeds, the grant is skipped and an error event is logged.

title: Grey-box thief infiltration challenge with multiple scripted routes
description:
## Why
Milestone m2 requires the thief fantasy proven in grey-box; a perfect infiltration must feel as good as a hard fight.

## What
A grey-box vault infiltration `greybox/thief-vault`: guarded courtyard, lit halls, a locked vault with a key carried by a patrolling guard, climbable exterior wall, alarm bell, hiding places. At least 3 distinct solution routes (pickpocket key; climb + pick window lock; distraction + extinguish + takedown), each covered by a scripted e2e/scenario test. Records a “ghost” (never detected) flag on completion.

## Scope
- In: Level data, routes, scripted solution tests, completion flag
- Out: Final dungeon (E26)
- Out: Art

## Notes
Fixture creatures only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given route A (pickpocket), when the scripted scenario runs, then the vault opens and no guard exceeds Suspicious.
- AC-2 [integration] Given route B (climb + lockpick window), when run, then the vault is reached and the completion flag is set.
- AC-3 [integration] Given route C (distract + extinguish + takedown), when run, then the vault opens with one unconscious guard hidden and no alarm.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a scripted failure (player spotted in the courtyard), when run, then the alarm escalates the zone and the scripted escape via smoke + hiding place still completes the level.
- AC-5 [manual] Given 3 playtesters, when completing the vault undetected, then ≥ 2 rate satisfaction ≥ 4/5.

title: Smoke bombs and flash powder break line of sight for escapes
description:
## Why
Escape tools turn failed stealth into a chase instead of a death — the thief’s disengagement fantasy.

## What
As a thief, I want to throw a smoke bomb so that I can break line of sight and slip away. Smoke bomb creates a gas volume (via element propagation, drifts and dissipates over 12 s) tagged `occlusion: partial:0.1` for LOS; creatures inside have sight disabled and cough (noise). Flash powder: instant stun for creatures facing it within 5 m (sight-dependent — blind/life-sense creatures unaffected). Losing LOS feeds LKP rules, so guards search where you vanished.

## Scope
- In: Smoke gas volume + LOS occlusion + dissipation
- In: Flash stun rule by sense profile
- In: Integration with memory/LKP
- Out: Gas propagation engine (e03-element-propagation)
- Out: VFX art (placeholders)

## Notes
Smoke is a gas: a Gust effect should clear it via the same gas rules (property-based).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a smoke volume between guard and player, when LOS is queried, then visible fraction ≤ 0.1.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a smoke volume, when 12 s pass without wind, then it has dissipated and LOS is restored.
- AC-3 [unit] Given flash powder within 5 m and a guard facing it, when detonated, then the guard is stunned 3 s; a creature without sight senses is not stunned.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a Combat guard chasing the player, when the player throws smoke and runs 10 m sideways, then the guard enters Searching with LKP at the smoke cloud, not the player’s position.
- AC-5 [unit] Given any gas-clearing wind effect through the smoke volume, when applied, then the volume moves/dissipates per gas rules.

title: Detect and disarm world traps; failures trigger them
description:
## Why
Triggered traps should create new situations rather than reloads; spotting and disarming them is thief expertise.

## What
As a thief, I want to notice and disarm pressure plates, tripwires and dart traps so that I can open safe routes — and accept the chaos when I fail. Traps have a `concealment` value; the player perceives them via a proximity/light-based check (thieves have a bonus; sneaking slower improves it) which reveals a subtle highlight. Disarm is an in-world timed action (like lockpicking) with a failure chance by trap quality; failure triggers the trap. Disarmed traps can be picked up (become placeable items where data allows).

## Scope
- In: Trap detection check, reveal highlight, disarm action, fail-trigger
- In: Salvage to item
- Out: Trap mechanics/effects themselves (e03-triggers / e03-doors-locks-switches)
- Out: Dungeon trap placement (E26)

## Notes
Detection uses light-field at trap position: dark traps are harder to spot.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a trap with concealment 0.5 in light 0.8, when a thief sneaks within 3 m, then it is detected within 1 s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same trap in light 0.1, when a knight walks within 3 m, then it is not detected.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a disarm attempt that fails (seeded), when resolved, then the trap triggers its normal effect.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a successfully disarmed pressure plate, when a creature steps on it, then nothing triggers.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a disarmed tripwire, when salvaged, then a tripwire kit item is added to inventory.

title: Climb tagged surfaces, ledges and ropes with stamina
description:
## Why
Climbing is how the thief reaches the window, the rooftop and the rafters — the class-specific alternate route.

## What
As a thief, I want to climb rough walls, vines, ladders and ropes so that I can take routes other classes cannot. Surfaces with property `climbable` (with difficulty) allow climbing; ledges allow shimmy and mantle; placed ropes (from items) create temporary climbable lines. Climbing drains stamina per difficulty; running out causes a fall (noise + damage by height). Class/progression gates higher difficulties. Climbing is quiet (−10 dB vs walk) but you are silhouetted on walls (contrast rule).

## Scope
- In: Climb state machine on top of controller climb hooks
- In: Stamina drain + fall
- In: Rope placement creating climbable volume + nav link for climbers
- Out: Core controller physics (e02-player-controller)
- Out: Climbing animations (placeholders)

## Notes
Climb routes also produce off-mesh links usable by climber creatures (e11-navigation).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a `climbable` difficulty-2 wall and a thief with max climb difficulty 3, when climb is initiated, then the player enters Climbing state.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a knight with max climb difficulty 1, when attempting the same wall, then climb is refused with a reason prompt.
- AC-3 [unit] Given stamina reaches 0 while climbing 4 m up, when the tick runs, then the player falls, takes fall damage per curve and a landing noise is emitted.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a rope placed on an anchor point, when complete, then a climbable volume and an off-mesh climb link exist until the rope is retrieved.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the stealth course vertical hall, when the player climbs to the rafters, then the player stands on the rafter platform within 10 s of input with no console errors.

title: Pickpocket and plant items on creatures from behind
description:
## Why
Pickpocketing creates emergent solutions: steal a key instead of picking a lock, plant evidence, lift a guard’s disguise pass.

## What
As a thief, I want to lift items from, or plant items on, unaware creatures so that I can solve problems without violence. Available when target is Unaware/Suspicious, not perceiving the player, within 1.2 m behind/side arc. Opens a compact in-world list of visible pockets (creature inventory items flagged `pocketable`). Each attempt takes time by item weight; success chance falls with target awareness and item weight; a failed attempt raises target awareness sharply (Alerted if it turns and sees you). Theft is recorded (disposition/faction events for witnesses).

## Scope
- In: Pickpocket and plant actions, success model, witness events
- In: Creature inventory integration
- In: Compact UI (placeholder)
- Out: Creature loot tables (e18-loot-tables)
- Out: Crime/bounty (Related: crime system)

## Notes
Success probability formula documented in tuning data; seeded RNG.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an Unaware guard with a `pocketable` key, when the player attempts from behind at 1 m, then the item transfers on success and the attempt takes the weight-scaled duration.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a failed attempt, when resolved, then the target’s awareness increases by the configured spike and it turns toward the player.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a witness guard perceives the theft, when resolved, then a `witnessed-theft` event fires applying disposition and faction modifiers.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a target with no pocketable items, when the prompt is evaluated, then the verb is offered but the list shows “Nothing to take” (still allows planting).
- AC-5 [unit] Given the target walks out of range mid-attempt, when resolved, then the attempt cancels without a transfer or awareness spike.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the player plants an item on a guard, when saved and loaded, then the guard’s inventory contains the planted item.

title: Pick locks as an in-world, interruptible, noisy action
description:
## Why
Locked doors and chests are the thief’s signature alternate routes; picking them in the world while guards patrol creates tension.

## What
As a thief, I want to pick locks while staying aware of my surroundings so that opening a door is a tense, skilful choice rather than a menu. Implements the ADR: locks carry quality (1–5), pin count, jam chance; picking is an in-world action (player stays visible and hearable, camera third-person) consuming lockpick durability; skill layer per ADR with an accessibility no-timing mode. Failures emit small noises and may break a pick; jamming a lock makes it unpickable (bash/magic still work). Progression hooks raise max quality.

## Scope
- In: Lock component extension, pick action, noise, durability, jam
- In: In-world UI overlay (placeholder)
- In: Accessibility mode
- Out: Door/lock base mechanics (e03-doors-locks-switches)
- Out: Unlock spells/bashing (E06/E04, same component)

## Notes
Default noise per failed pin 18 dB; broken pick 25 dB.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a quality-2 lock and one lockpick set, when the pick action completes successfully, then the lock is unlocked and durability decreases by 1.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a failed pin attempt, when resolved, then an 18 dB noise event is emitted at the lock.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a lock jams (seeded chance), when evaluated, then further pick attempts are refused with reason `jammed` while other unlock methods still work.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player is attacked or moves > 0.5 m while picking, when resolved, then the action is interrupted and progress is lost.
- AC-5 [unit] Given lock quality above the player’s unlocked max, when the prompt is evaluated, then picking is not offered and the prompt says why.
- AC-6 [integration] Given accessibility no-timing mode, when picking a quality-3 lock, then it completes after the documented duration without input timing.
- AC-7 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box door maze, when the player picks a locked door, then the door opens and the navmesh link becomes traversable.

title: Spike: systemic lockpicking design that stays in the world
description:
## Why
The constitution prefers world systems over disconnected minigames. Lockpicking must keep the player in the world, exposed to guards and noise, while still involving skill.

## What
Time-box 1 day. Question: how can lockpicking be an in-world, interruptible action with a light skill layer (e.g. timing tension clicks while the camera stays third-person) instead of a full-screen minigame? Prototype 2 variants in the grey-box (A: timed hold with pin-click timing windows; B: pure duration by lock quality vs tool/skill with noise risk), evaluate readability, tension with nearby guards, accessibility (a no-skill option), and progression hooks. ADR with recommendation.

## Scope
- In: Two prototypes in `spikes/lockpicking/`
- In: ADR with lock data shape (quality, pins, noise per failure, jam chance)
- Out: Production lockpicking (e10-lockpicking)

## Notes
Must remain compatible with sorcerer/knight alternatives (Unlock spell, bashing) via the same lock component from e03-doors-locks-switches.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the ADR, when reviewed, then it records the choice, rejected alternatives, and a data shape for lock quality.
- AC-2 [manual] Given 3 internal testers, when trying both prototypes near a patrolling guard, then preferences and time-to-open are recorded in the ADR.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it specifies an accessibility mode that removes timing requirements.

title: Carry and hide unconscious or dead bodies
description:
## Why
Hiding bodies is how thieves cover their tracks; a body left in the light should cause the alarm the player earned.

## What
As a thief, I want to pick up and hide bodies so that patrols do not discover what I did. Pick up unconscious/dead humanoid-size creatures (size class limit), carry at reduced speed (−40%) and no sneak-sprint, higher visibility (+profile), drop or place into hiding places with `body-capacity` (chests, wardrobes, deep shadow, water). Placed bodies inside containers are invisible to anomaly detection; bodies in darkness depend on visibility. Unconscious creatures carried keep their wake timer.

## Scope
- In: Carry state, movement modifiers, drop/place
- In: Body containers
- In: Integration with anomaly detection
- Out: Ragdoll physics beyond placeholder (Related: physics/animation)
- Out: Looting bodies (e17 / E18)

## Notes
Dropping a body emits a thud noise scaled by surface (e.g. 35 dB on stone).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an unconscious guard, when the player picks it up, then player speed is ×0.5 (ADR-0003, matches mw-e02.17) and the visibility profile term increases by the configured amount.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player carrying a body, when placed into a container with body capacity 1, then the body is hidden and the container is full.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a body placed in a container, when a guard perceives the container, then no body anomaly is raised unless the guard opens it.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature larger than the carry size limit, when pickup is attempted, then it is refused with reason `too-heavy`.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the unconscious carried guard’s wake timer expires, when it wakes while carried, then it is dropped, enters Alerted and the player is staggered 0.5 s.

title: Backstabs and non-lethal takedowns on unaware targets
description:
## Why
Opportunistic combat is the thief’s combat fantasy: ambushes and takedowns reward patience and positioning.

## What
As a thief, I want to backstab or knock out an unaware enemy from behind so that a clean infiltration can thin the guard without a fight. Conditions: target alert state ∈ {Unaware, Suspicious}, player within rear arc (±60°) and 1.5 m, target does not perceive the player this think. Lethal backstab: damage multiplier from damage model (lethal on humanoids by default). Non-lethal (sap/choke): target becomes `unconscious` for a data-defined duration (default 10 min sim) unless woken. Creature schema flags (`immune-to-knockout` for undead/constructs, `no-backstab` for huge creatures) gate the verbs. Takedown emits noise (choke 20 dB, backstab 35 dB). Failed attempts (target turns) cause a scuffle: target enters Combat staggered.

## Scope
- In: Prompt availability, execution, outcomes, noise
- In: Creature flags gating
- In: Failure scuffle outcome
- Out: Environmental takedowns (e10-environmental-takedowns)
- Out: Animations (placeholder snaps)

## Notes
Unconscious bodies are carriable (e10-body-carry-hide) and anomalies (e09-anomaly-detection).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an Unaware humanoid and the player 1 m behind within 60°, when takedown is evaluated, then both backstab and knockout verbs are available.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same target in Investigating or higher, when evaluated, then no takedown verb is available.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature flagged `immune-to-knockout`, when evaluated, then only backstab is available.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a knockout, when executed, then the target is `unconscious` for 600 s sim and a 20 dB noise is emitted at its position.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the target perceives the player during the 0.5 s wind-up, when the takedown resolves, then it fails, the target enters Combat and is staggered for 0.8 s.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the patrol-yard scenario, when the player knocks out a guard out of sight of others, then the other guards remain Unaware.

title: Extinguish and relight light sources to reshape the shadows
description:
## Why
Extinguishing lights lets thieves create their own darkness, and any system that affects light (water, wind, frost magic) should work too.

## What
As a thief, I want to snuff candles and douse torches so that I can create shadows where I need them. Light sources with property `extinguishable` go out from: interact (pinch/snuff, quiet), any `wet`/water effect via element propagation (thrown water flask, rain), strong wind/gust effects, frost. `ignitable` light sources relight from any fire source. Light-field updates immediately; extinguishing emits a small noise and creates an anomaly (e09-anomaly-detection).

## Scope
- In: Light source state + property-based rules
- In: Interact snuff action
- In: Light-field update + anomaly record
- Out: Light-field implementation (e03-light-field)
- Out: Water arrows (E05) — works automatically via property

## Notes
Magical lights may be tagged non-extinguishable; that is data.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any `extinguishable` light within a water/wet effect volume, when the effect applies, then the light turns off and the light-field level at 2 m drops to the ambient value within 1 tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an `ignitable` unlit torch in contact with any fire source, when 0.5 s passes, then it relights.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a light tagged non-extinguishable, when water hits it, then it stays lit.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the player snuffs a candle via interact, when complete, then a ≤ 15 dB noise is emitted and an anomaly `light-out` is registered for that light.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a guard walking past a torch the player extinguished, when perceived, then the guard enters Suspicious with cause `light-out`.

title: Throw objects to create noise distractions guards investigate
description:
## Why
Thrown distractions are the thief’s first verb in the progression ladder (Sneak → distractions → …) and a classic stealth tool.

## What
As a thief, I want to throw a coin or bottle so that guards look away or walk over to investigate. Any `throwable` item or physics object can be aimed (trajectory preview arc) and thrown; on impact it emits a noise event = item impact dB + surface offset; `fragile` items shatter (louder, leave shards as `glass-shards` surface). Guards perceive the propagated noise and investigate the perceived position. Thrown object remains in the world (anomaly if found near a post repeatedly — hook).

## Scope
- In: Throw aim + arc preview + release
- In: Impact noise via sound propagation + surface
- In: Pickup-able thrown objects (non-fragile)
- Out: Combat throwing damage (E04)
- Out: Arrows (E05)

## Notes
Uses physics objects for the throw; the noise rule is property-based (`throwable`, `fragile`), never item-specific.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a coin (impact 45 dB) landing on stone 10 m from a guard with threshold 30 dB, when propagated, then the guard receives a heard-noise stimulus and enters Suspicious.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a bottle tagged `fragile` landing, when it hits any surface, then it shatters, emits the fragile-break loudness and adds a `glass-shards` surface patch.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a coin landing on carpet, when propagated to the same guard, then perceived loudness is reduced by the carpet offset and the guard stays Unaware.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the distraction-room scenario, when the player throws a bottle behind a guard, then the guard turns and investigates the impact location within 2 s.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a throw into water, when it lands, then a `splash` noise kind is emitted and the object sinks (not retrievable unless shallow).
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box course, when the player aims, then a trajectory arc renders and the landing marker matches the actual landing point within 0.5 m.

title: Define thief tool item data: lockpicks, throwables, smoke, traps
description:
## Why
Thief tools are data-driven items so shops, loot and progression can hand them out without code.

## What
Item definitions (in the inventory schema) for: lockpick set (durability), coin/pebble/bottle throwables (impact noise, breakable), smoke bomb, flash powder, noisemaker trap, tripwire kit, caltrops, rope, water flask (extinguish), sap/blackjack (non-lethal), disguise items referencing faction. Each carries world properties (weight, fragile, noise) and tags consumed by E10 features.

## Scope
- In: Item data files + tests
- In: Tags: `tool:lockpick`, `throwable`, `trap:*`, `disguise:<faction>`
- Out: Loot/shop placement (E18/E20)
- Out: Icons (asset beads)

## Notes
Placeholder icon ids: `icon-tool-lockpick`, `icon-throw-coin`, `icon-throw-bottle`, `icon-smoke-bomb`, `icon-trap-noisemaker`, `icon-trap-tripwire`, `icon-caltrops`, `icon-water-flask`, `icon-sap`.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given each thief item file, when validated, then it passes the inventory item schema and carries its required tags.
- AC-2 [content] Given a throwable without an impact noise value, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a lockpick set with durability 10, when resolved, then durability is 10 and it stacks to max 5 sets.
- AC-4 [content] Given every thief item, when the content harness runs, then each has at least one automated test (spawn into inventory + use).

title: Deterministic infiltration replay scenarios with asserted guard states
description:
## Why
Releases must be trusted without reading code. Scripted infiltrations with asserted guard states prove the stealth systems work together and stay working.

## What
A suite of ≥ 10 headless scenarios using the AI scenario harness on the stealth course layouts, each with a scripted player path and asserted guard states over time. Scenarios: shadow sneak (never above Suspicious), sprint on gravel (Suspicious ≤ 1 s), closed-door muffling, thrown distraction lure, break LOS and hide (guard ends Searching then postAlert Unaware), body discovery → Alerted, alarm → zone level 2, rafters crossing, hiding-place seen-enter, ally communication chain. Each records a state-hash sequence as a regression baseline.

## Scope
- In: Scenario files, baselines, CI job
- In: Readable failure timelines
- Out: Browser e2e (course e2e ACs)

## Notes
Scenarios reference fixture creatures only so bestiary tuning never breaks them.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the shadow-sneak scenario, when run, then no guard exceeds Suspicious for the full 60 s.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the break-LOS scenario, when run, then the guard sequence is Combat → Searching → Unaware(postAlert) with the Searching phase starting within 5 s of LOS break.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the closed-door scenario, when the same noise is made with the door open vs closed, then the guard enters Suspicious only in the open case.
- AC-4 [integration] Given every scenario, when run twice, then state-hash sequences are identical to each other and to the committed baseline.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a deliberately broken rule (test-only flag doubling light weight), when the suite runs, then at least 3 scenarios fail (the suite actually detects regressions).
- AC-6 [perf] Given the full suite, when run in CI, then it completes in ≤ 30 s.

title: Build the stealth grey-box course covering every stealth input
description:
## Why
Stealth systems need one playable space that exercises light, sound, surfaces, doors, verticality and hiding for e2e tests and tuning playtests.

## What
A grey-box level `greybox/stealth-course` with labelled stations: light/dark gradient hall, surface strip (carpet/stone/gravel/creaky wood/water), door maze (open/closed/locked), vertical hall with rafters and ledges, hiding place gallery, distraction room, patrol yard with 3 fixture guards, alarm bell zone with reserve guards. Includes a baked navmesh, room/portal graph and patrol routes.

## Scope
- In: Level data, placeholder props, patrol routes, spawn points
- In: Console `tp station <n>`
- Out: Final dungeon content (E26)
- Out: Art

## Notes
Used by e09 e2e ACs, e09-infiltration-scenarios and e10 thief challenge.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the course, when loaded in the browser, then all 8 stations are reachable and no console errors appear.
- AC-2 [content] Given the course data, when validated, then navmesh, portal graph and patrol routes pass validation.
- AC-3 [integration] Given `tp station 3`, when entered, then the player is at the door maze start.
- AC-4 [perf] Given the course with all guards active, when measured on the reference machine (High), then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms.

title: Failed stealth escalates into new situations, not reload screens
description:
## Why
Failure creates stories. Being spotted should cause lockdowns, reinforcements, changed patrols or a chase — situations the player can still play through.

## What
As a thief, I want getting caught to change the level rather than end my run so that I can improvise an escape. Area alarm levels (0 calm, 1 wary, 2 alarm, 3 lockdown) per zone driven by alarms, bodies found and combat. Data-defined responses per zone and level: lock specified doors, light extra lights, reinforce posts from a reserve pool (pre-placed, activated — not spawned from nowhere), release hounds, shift patrols; decay back after N minutes of calm to a stable “wary” level, never fully reset. Responses recorded in world state.

## Scope
- In: Zone alarm model + response data + decay
- In: Integration with doors, lights, reserve creatures
- In: World state persistence
- Out: Crime/bounty system across settlements (Related: E22/E27 crime; not in this epic)
- Out: Specific dungeon zone authoring (E26)

## Notes
Reserve pool creatures are placed in level data with `reserve: <zone>`; activation paths them in from their barracks so the player can see them come.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given zone Z at level 0, when an alarm device activates in Z, then Z becomes level 2 and all level-2 responses fire once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a level-3 response `lock-doors: [d1, d2]`, when triggered, then d1 and d2 are locked via the door system and pathfinding reflects it.
- AC-3 [unit] Given no alarm triggers for 5 sim minutes at level 2, when the decay rule runs, then Z drops to level 1 (never to 0 once an alarm has occurred).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a reserve creature already killed or knocked out by the player, when reinforcements are called, then it is not activated and no replacement is spawned.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a save while Z is at level 2, when loaded, then Z is at level 2 with its responses applied.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the stealth grey-box course, when the player is spotted and the alarm rung, then the course remains completable via at least one alternate route (scripted e2e path succeeds).

title: Text barks and audio stingers on alert state transitions
description:
## Why
Players read enemy minds through barks ("Who’s there?", "Must be rats…"). With no voice in MVP, text barks plus audio stingers carry this.

## What
As a thief, I want guards to mutter and call out as their state changes so that I understand what they think without a UI meter. Bark tables per behaviour profile map (transition, cause) → weighted lines, shown as floating subtitle text near the speaker within hearing range; audio stinger per escalation (placeholder tones) via the audio engine; cooldowns prevent spam. Barks also enable stealth-layer music hooks.

## Scope
- In: Bark table schema + selection (seeded)
- In: Floating text renderer with distance fade
- In: Stinger cue ids + cooldowns
- Out: Voice acting (no voice in MVP)
- Out: Adaptive music system (Related: E28/E38 music layering)
- Out: Final bark writing (narrative pass, Related: e39-story-bible tone)

## Notes
Stingers: `sfx-stealth-suspicious-01`, `sfx-stealth-alerted-01`, `sfx-stealth-combat-01`, `sfx-stealth-lost-01` — placeholder beeps until asset beads land.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a Unaware→Suspicious transition with cause `heard`, when a bark is selected with a fixed seed, then it comes from the `suspicious.heard` table and is deterministic.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same agent barked 2 s ago with cooldown 5 s, when a new transition occurs, then no bark is shown.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a speaker 40 m away beyond hearing range, when a bark would show, then it is suppressed for the player.
- AC-4 [integration] Given an escalation to Alerted, when it occurs, then exactly one stinger cue is played via the audio engine.
- AC-5 [content] Given a bark table referencing an unknown transition key, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Directional awareness indicators showing each enemy’s alert state
description:
## Why
Players must see who is noticing them, from where, how close to detection, and why — without the omniscient radar that kills tension.

## What
As a thief, I want directional indicators for enemies becoming aware of me so that I can react before being caught. For each agent with awareness > 0 of the player: an indicator near the agent (on-screen) or screen-edge chevron (off-screen) that fills with awareness and changes shape per alert state (6 distinct shapes, not colour alone), plus a cause glyph (eye = saw, ear = heard, hand = anomaly). Indicators only appear for agents the player could plausibly perceive (on-screen or heard), preserving uncertainty.

## Scope
- In: Indicator model from awareness + state + dominant cause
- In: On-screen and off-screen rendering
- In: Colour-blind-safe shapes
- Out: Text barks (e09-alert-barks)
- Out: Last-known-position ghost (e09-lkp-ghost)

## Notes
Indicators for agents the player has not perceived (behind walls, silent) are hidden unless an accessibility assist enables them (e09-stealth-assists).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an agent at awareness 0.45 in Suspicious caused by hearing, when the indicator model is built, then fill = 0.45, shape = `suspicious`, glyph = `ear`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an agent behind a wall that has not been seen or heard by the player, when the model is built with assists off, then no indicator is produced.
- AC-3 [unit] Given each of the six states, when shapes are resolved, then six distinct shape ids are returned.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box course, when a guard off-screen to the left becomes Suspicious from a noise, then a left-edge chevron appears within 1 frame of the state change.
- AC-5 [unit] Given 12 aware agents, when the model is built, then at most 6 indicators are shown, prioritised by awareness × proximity.

title: Stealth HUD: light exposure, noise ring and stance readout
description:
## Why
Stealth cannot be an eye icon: the player needs to read the inputs — how lit they are and how loud they are — to make decisions.

## What
As a thief, I want to see how exposed and how loud I am so that I can make informed choices. Elements: light-exposure gem (continuous, 5 visual bands, driven by self-visibility), noise ring around the character footprint that pulses at each emitted noise scaled to its audible radius for a typical guard, stance/gait indicator, and optional diegetic cue (character material darkens in shadow). All toggleable and scalable via settings.

## Scope
- In: HUD components in `src/ui`, data binding from sim
- In: Placeholder art (CSS/SVG shapes)
- In: Settings toggles
- Out: Per-enemy awareness (e09-awareness-indicators)
- Out: Final UI art (asset beads)

## Notes
Noise ring radius = distance at which the emitted noise drops to the baseline humanoid hearing threshold in open space.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given self-visibility 0.05, when the HUD model is computed, then the gem shows band 1 of 5; at 0.95 band 5.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a 40 dB footstep and a 30 dB baseline threshold, when the noise ring is computed, then its radius is ≈ 3.2 m (10^(10/20)).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the settings toggle `hud.stealth=false`, when the HUD renders, then no stealth elements are present.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box course, when the player walks from a lit area into shadow, then the gem band decreases within 250 ms.
- AC-5 [manual] Given a playtest with 3 players, when asked to explain the gem and ring without instructions after 5 min, then at least 2 describe both correctly.

title: Guards notice world anomalies: bodies, open doors, dark torches
description:
## Why
A thief’s actions leave traces; guards noticing a doused torch or a missing colleague creates tension and new situations.

## What
As a thief, I want guards to notice what I changed so that covering my tracks is part of the craft. Anomalies are world facts compared against an agent’s expected state (routine knowledge): unconscious/dead bodies, doors open that are normally closed, lights extinguished that are normally lit, missing valuables from a watched spot, blood/broken objects, a colleague missing from post for > N s. Each anomaly type has data: detection via sight (uses visibility of the anomaly), suspicion weight, resulting state (Suspicious for an open door, Alerted for a body).

## Scope
- In: Anomaly registry + expected-state baseline per area/agent
- In: Perception integration (seen-anomaly stimulus)
- In: Data-driven anomaly types + weights
- Out: Relighting/closing on return (e11-return-to-routine)
- Out: Body carrying (e10-body-carry-hide)

## Notes
Expected state captured at level load and updated when guards themselves change things. Hidden bodies (in containers or darkness below visibility threshold) are not perceived.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a door normally closed is open, when a guard perceives it, then it becomes Suspicious and investigates the door.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a guard perceives an unconscious body, when evaluated, then it enters Alerted, investigates the body and may wake it (unconscious ally wakes after 3 s interaction).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a body placed in a container or in light ≤ 0.1 beyond 6 m, when a guard walks its route, then the body is not perceived.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a torch normally lit is extinguished, when a guard perceives the dark torch, then it becomes Suspicious (not Alerted) with cause `light-out`.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a guard itself opened a door on its route, when it later perceives that door open, then no anomaly is raised.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a scenario where the player knocks out guard A and leaves the body in a lit corridor on guard B’s route, when guard B passes, then guard B enters Alerted within 2 s of the body entering its view.

title: Hiding places: wardrobes, barrels, tall grass and shadowed alcoves
description:
## Why
Hiding places are a constitution stealth input and give failed stealth a recovery move rather than a reload.

## What
As a thief, I want to duck into a wardrobe, crouch in tall grass or press into an alcove so that I can break pursuit if I am quick and unseen. Two kinds: enter-able containers (wardrobe, barrel, under-bed — interact to enter/exit, player hidden, limited view) and concealment volumes (tall grass, curtains, alcoves — visibility multiplier while inside and stationary/crouched). Data: concealment factor, entry noise dB, entry time, capacity, `searchable` flag. AI that saw you enter knows; AI searching may check (e11-search-behaviour). Being found inside = instant Combat at close range with a brief stagger window to flee (failure creates a story).

## Scope
- In: Hiding place component + data
- In: Enter/exit via interaction with timing and noise
- In: Concealment volumes feeding visibility model
- In: Being-discovered outcome
- Out: Hiding bodies in containers (e10-body-carry-hide)
- Out: Hiding prop art (placeholder boxes)

## Notes
Entering while observed must be tracked as a memory `saw-enter:<hidingPlaceId>`.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player inside a wardrobe, when any observer computes visibility, then the result is 0 unless the wardrobe is opened by that observer.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player crouched still in tall grass (concealment 0.3), when visibility is computed, then it is multiplied by 0.3; moving at run speed removes the bonus.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a guard observes the player entering a barrel, when the guard searches, then the barrel is checked first (via memory `saw-enter`).
- AC-4 [unit] Given an occupied single-capacity hiding place, when a second entity attempts to enter, then entry is refused with a prompt reason.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a guard opens the wardrobe the player is in, when discovered, then the guard enters Combat and the player gets a 0.6 s stagger window during which exiting is possible.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box course, when the player enters and exits a wardrobe via the interact action, then the camera switches to the hiding view and back without errors.

title: Verticality rules: limited upward vision and height advantage
description:
## Why
Verticality is a stealth input: rafters, balconies and rooftops should be real thief highways because guards rarely look up.

## What
As a thief, I want to be harder to notice above or below a guard’s eye line so that rafters and ledges become routes. Vertical sight: per-profile vertical half-angles up/down (humanoids look up poorly by default, e.g. +20° up, −45° down) with an extra falloff; creatures with `looks-up` tag (e.g. spiders, fliers) ignore it; Searching agents perform occasional look-up scans. Height difference affects noise via floor transmission (already in propagation) and adds a visibility penalty when the target is above a lit area but itself in dark rafters.

## Scope
- In: Vertical cone limits + falloff
- In: Look-up scan in Searching/Investigating when LKP is elevated
- In: Tuning data
- Out: Climbing movement (e10-climbing)
- Out: Flying creature navigation (post-MVP)

## Notes
LKP elevation > 2 m above agent eye triggers look-up scan behaviour.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a humanoid guard with vertical up half-angle 20°, when the target is 30° above horizontal at 8 m, then no sight stimulus is produced while the guard is Unaware.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature tagged `looks-up`, when the same target is evaluated, then a sight stimulus is produced.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a Searching guard whose LKP is 4 m above its eye height, when it reaches the LKP area, then it performs a look-up scan that widens its up half-angle to 60° for 3 s.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a scenario where the player crosses rafters above 2 patrolling guards in a lit hall, when simulated, then neither guard exceeds Suspicious.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the target directly overhead (90°), when evaluated, then no division-by-zero or NaN occurs and visibility follows the vertical rule.

title: Author stealth tuning data: light weights, stance, noise, doors
description:
## Why
Stealth feel must be tunable by designers without code, and defaults pinned by tests.

## What
A `StealthTuning` schema and default file: light-term curve, stance multipliers, motion bands, distance falloff, contrast bonus, gait base dB, surface table link, door-state and wall/floor transmission defaults, global audibility floor, hiding-place concealment defaults. Hot reload in dev; difficulty presets can override a whitelisted subset.

## Scope
- In: Schema, defaults, hot reload, pinned default tests
- In: Difficulty override whitelist (consumed by e09-stealth-assists)
- Out: AI thresholds and timers (e11-ai-tuning-data)
- Out: Sense ranges (e12-sense-profiles)

## Notes
Curves are piecewise-linear point lists for easy editing.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the default file, when validated, then all curves are monotonic in the documented direction.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a difficulty preset overriding a non-whitelisted key, when loaded, then loading fails naming the key.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a dev build, when the stance multiplier is edited, then the visibility HUD reflects the change within 1 s.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the shipped defaults, when the pinned-default test runs, then documented values match.

title: Emit footstep noise from speed, stance, surface and equipment weight
description:
## Why
Silent movement must be a skill: running on gravel in plate armour should wake the keep; creeping barefoot over carpet should not.

## What
As a thief, I want my footsteps to be as loud as my choices make them so that moving slowly and choosing my path pays off. Each footstep (from controller gait cadence) emits a noise event: base dB by gait (sneak/walk/run/sprint) + surface offset + equipment noise (sum of equipped item `noise` values, e.g. plate clank) + landing impulse for jumps/falls (by fall height). Also emitted for any creature with footsteps, so the player can hear guards.

## Scope
- In: Footstep emission rule shared by player and creatures
- In: Landing and falling impacts
- In: Equipment noise aggregation (reads item data)
- Out: Progression perks that reduce noise (e10-silent-movement)
- Out: Audio playback (e28)

## Notes
Emit at step cadence, not per tick. Defaults: sneak 25, walk 40, run 55, sprint 65 dB at 1 m.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player sneaking on carpet with no noisy equipment, when a step occurs, then the event loudness is 15 dB (25 − 10).
- AC-2 [unit] Given sprinting on gravel wearing items with total noise +10 dB, when a step occurs, then loudness is 65 + gravel offset + 10.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a fall of 3 m onto stone, when landing, then an impact event with loudness per the fall-height curve is emitted once.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player standing still, when 5 s pass, then no footstep events are emitted.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a scenario where the player sneaks past a guard 6 m away on carpet, when simulated, then the guard stays Unaware; the same path sprinting on gravel makes the guard Suspicious within 1 s.

title: Tag surfaces with acoustic materials that change footstep noise
description:
## Why
Surfaces are a constitution stealth input: carpet muffles, gravel crunches, a creaky board betrays you, a puddle splashes.

## What
Acoustic material tags on walkable colliders and level regions (`stone`, `wood`, `wood-creaky`, `carpet`, `gravel`, `metal-grate`, `water-shallow`, `grass`, `leaves`, `glass-shards`): loudness offset dB, per-step variance, and sfx set id. Materials can change dynamically via world properties (a `wet` or `frozen` surface changes its offset; scattered glass shards become `glass-shards`). Query API `surfaceAt(position)`.

## Scope
- In: Material table (content data), collider/region tagging, dynamic modifiers from world properties
- In: Grey-box painter support: tag via level JSON
- Out: Footstep emission rule (e09-footstep-noise)
- Out: Final footstep audio (asset beads)

## Notes
Creaky boards: probability per step of an extra +12 dB creak (seeded).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a position on a `carpet` region, when `surfaceAt` is queried, then material is `carpet` with offset −10 dB (default table).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a `wood` surface that gains the `frozen` property, when queried, then the frozen-surface modifier applies per the table.
- AC-3 [unit] Given overlapping regions, when queried, then the higher-priority region wins deterministically.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a position with no surface tag, when queried, then the default `stone` material is returned and a dev warning is logged once per region.
- AC-5 [content] Given the material table, when validated, then each material has an offset in −20..+20 dB and a sfx set id.
- AC-6 [content] Given the material table, when compared with the footstep surface set in audio bible §7.3, then the material ids match exactly (a test fails on any id present in only one list).

title: Perf budget: 24 active AI agents within sim frame budget
description:
## Why
The hardware baseline requires steady 60 fps; AI perception, pathing and sound propagation are the likeliest sim hot spots.

## What
Add an AI stress scene and budget tests: 24 agents (mixed fixtures) in Alerted/Searching with continuous noise events and a moving target. Budgets: total AI+perception+sound sim cost p95 ≤ 3 ms per tick on the reference machine; ≤ 5 ms on the Low-preset class machine. Includes LOS cache and level-of-detail think rates (agents > 40 m from player think at 2 Hz).

## Scope
- In: Stress scene, budget assertions, AI LOD think rates, LOS result caching
- Out: Render perf (E32)

## Notes
Numbers cite the contract hardware baseline.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the AI stress scene with 24 agents, when run for 60 s headless on the reference machine, then AI+perception+sound cost p95 ≤ 3 ms per tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an agent 50 m from the player with LOD enabled, when 60 ticks run, then it thinks 2 times; within 40 m it thinks 10 times.
