- AC-3 [unit] Given AI LOD, when an out-of-range agent receives a noise stimulus above threshold, then it is promoted to full think rate on the next tick (no missed alerts).
- AC-4 [perf] Given the stress scene in the browser (High), when measured, then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms.

title: Author AI tuning data: thresholds, decay timers, search durations
description:
## Why
Stealth feel is tuned constantly; all numbers must be data so designers can iterate without code and tests can pin defaults.

## What
A `AiTuning` schema and default files per behaviour profile: awareness thresholds per state, accumulation rates per sense, grace and decay timers, state timeouts (Suspicious 6 s, Investigating 20 s, Searching 60 s, Alerted 120 s defaults), post-alert multiplier and duration, search radius growth, token budgets, think rates. Profiles inherit (`guard-default` → `guard-lazy`). Hot-reload in dev.

## Scope
- In: Schema, inheritance, defaults, hot reload in dev builds
- In: Pinned default-value tests
- Out: Sense ranges (e12-sense-profiles)
- Out: Stealth emitter tuning (e09-stealth-tuning-data)

## Notes
Changing defaults requires updating pinned tests deliberately — that is the point.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the default tuning files, when validated, then every state has a positive timeout and thresholds are strictly increasing Suspicious < Investigating < Detected.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `guard-lazy` inheriting from `guard-default` overriding only Searching timeout 30 s, when resolved, then all other values equal the parent.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an inheritance cycle, when loaded, then loading fails naming the cycle.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a dev build, when a tuning file is edited, then running agents use the new values within 1 s without reload.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the shipped defaults, when the pinned-default test runs, then each documented default matches.

title: Guards return to routines, visibly changed by what happened
description:
## Why
Failure creates stories: after an alert guards should go back to work, but the world should remember — lit torches, doubled posts, grumbling barks.

## What
As a thief, I want guards to settle back down after an alert but stay changed so that my mistakes reshape the level instead of resetting it. On de-escalation: path back to routine, apply post-alert adjustments from data (e.g. relight extinguished lights on route, close opened doors, patrol in pairs, add a checkpoint post, carry a torch), keep heightened awareness for a duration. Adjustments are data-driven per behaviour profile and recorded as world facts.

## Scope
- In: Return behaviour, post-alert adjustment list, persistence via world state
- In: Barks cue on return
- Out: Level lockdowns/reinforcements (e09-failed-stealth-outcomes)

## Notes
Adjustments list example: `relight-seen-extinguished-lights`, `close-seen-open-doors`, `pair-up`, `carry-torch`.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a guard de-escalates with `postAlert=true`, when simulated, then it resumes its route within 5 s and awareness rate multiplier is 1.5 for 300 s, then 1.0.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a guard with the `relight-seen-extinguished-lights` adjustment that perceived an extinguished torch during the alert, when returning, then it paths to the torch and relights it before resuming.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the torch was destroyed (not merely extinguished), when the adjustment runs, then the guard skips it and switches to `carry-torch` if declared.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a save after an alert with `pair-up` applied, when loaded, then the paired patrol persists.

title: Creatures retreat, flee to allies and cower based on morale
description:
## Why
Enemies that retreat, regroup or flee make fights and scares feel alive and allow non-lethal victories.

## What
As a player, I want frightened or wounded creatures to disengage so that encounters end in more ways than death. Consumes `Flee`/`Cower` intents from e12-fears-morale and health thresholds: flee away from the fear source toward allies, safe zones or a lair point; cower when cornered; regroup and re-enter Alerted/Searching when morale recovers. Fleeing creatures may shout (communication) and drop carried items (hook).

## Scope
- In: Flee destination scoring, cower, regroup
- In: Surrender intent event (hook for E14 dialogue)
- Out: Morale model (e12-fears-morale)
- Out: Surrender dialogue (E14/E22)

## Notes
Flee destination scoring: distance from threat, ally proximity, darkness preference per creature.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature with a `Flee` intent and threat at T, when fleeing, then after 3 s its distance from T has increased and its path does not pass within 2 m of T.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a fleeing creature with no escape path (dead end), when cornered, then it enters `Cower` within 1 s.
- AC-3 [unit] Given morale recovers above the regroup threshold, when the intent clears, then the creature enters Searching with the threat’s last-known position.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature tagged `fearless` (morale disabled), when at 1 health, then it never flees.

title: Allies share alerts by shouts, sight signals and alarm devices
description:
## Why
Enemies that communicate make a single mistake escalate believably, and give players targets — silence the shouter, cut the bell rope.

## What
As a thief, I want guards to call for help through the world rather than telepathy so that I can prevent or exploit alarms. Channels: shout (emits a loud noise event via sound propagation carrying a report: LKP, state), visual signal (allies in LOS within 25 m receive the report), alarm device (agents path to a nearest `alarm` object and activate it via the interaction/mechanism system, broadcasting Alerted to a faction zone). Only allies (faction relation ally/friendly) accept reports. Group roles in Alerted/Searching: one caller, others flank/search.

## Scope
- In: Report message type, shout/visual/alarm channels
- In: Faction filtering
- In: Basic role assignment (caller, searcher, guard-post-holder)
- Out: Reinforcement spawning (e09-failed-stealth-outcomes)
- Out: Speech/voice (text barks only — e09-alert-barks)

## Notes
Alarm objects are world mechanisms with an `alarm` property; if destroyed or jammed, the AI must fall back to shouting. Related: alarm bell mechanism may be authored with E03 switches.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a guard entering Alerted, when it shouts, then a noise event of the configured loudness is emitted and allies whose perceived level exceeds their hearing threshold receive the report.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a guard behind 2 closed doors whose shout is attenuated below an ally’s threshold, when shouting, then that ally receives nothing.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature of a hostile faction within hearing, when a shout occurs, then it does not receive the report (it may still perceive the noise as a stimulus).
- AC-4 [unit] Given an alarm object that has been disabled (jammed or destroyed), when a guard attempts to use it, then it falls back to shouting within 2 s.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a scenario with 3 guards and one alarm bell, when the first guard spots the player and reaches the bell, then all guards in the bell’s zone enter Alerted within 1 tick of activation.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a guard is knocked out mid-path to the alarm, when the tick runs, then no alarm activation occurs.

title: Search patterns around last-known position, including hiding spots
description:
## Why
A convincing search — fanning out, checking corners and wardrobes — makes escaping feel earned, and gives up plausibly so failure does not force a reload.

## What
As a thief, I want searching guards to check plausible places near where they lost me so that hiding well matters and hiding badly gets me caught. Searching generates candidate points around LKP (+ bounded prediction): nav-reachable points ranked by distance, cover/darkness, and whether the point is out of sight from LKP; plus hiding spots within radius. Agents claim points (no two agents search the same point), check hiding spots with a probability based on whether they saw the target enter it, expand radius over time, then give up.

## Scope
- In: Candidate generation, ranking, claiming, radius expansion
- In: Hiding-spot checks with probability rules
- In: Diligence trait scaling of duration
- Out: Hiding place mechanics (e09-hiding-places)
- Out: Alarm raising (e11-communication)

## Notes
Probability of checking a hiding spot: 1.0 if target was seen entering; otherwise base 0.25 scaled by proximity to LKP. Seeded RNG.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a Searching guard with LKP L, when candidates are generated, then all lie within the current radius, are nav-reachable and the first 3 are sorted by the ranking function.
- AC-2 [unit] Given two guards searching the same LKP, when they claim points, then no point is claimed by both.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the guard saw the target enter a hiding spot, when searching, then it checks that spot first with probability 1.0.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a hiding spot not seen being entered, 10 m from LKP, when evaluated with a fixed seed, then the check decision matches the documented probability formula.
- AC-5 [unit] Given no reachable candidates (LKP on an isolated ledge), when searching, then the guard looks toward LKP from the nearest point, then de-escalates at the search timeout without error.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a scenario where the player hides in darkness 8 m from LKP and stays still, when a single guard searches for 60 s, then the guard ends Searching without entering Combat in the scripted seed.

title: Guards investigate suspicious stimuli at their perceived location
description:
## Why
Distractions only work if guards go and look. Investigation is the core lever for thrown objects, noises and glimpses.

## What
As a thief, I want a guard to walk over and check a noise or glimpse so that I can lure him away from his post. In Suspicious: stop, turn toward stimulus, text bark cue. In Investigating: path to stimulus position at walk (or cautious) gait, look around on arrival with a scan pattern, inspect the source object if perceived (e.g. a thrown bottle), then decide: nothing found → de-escalate; more stimuli → escalate. Multiple stimuli: most recent strong one wins; weaker stimuli queue up to 3.

## Scope
- In: Investigate behaviour, scan pattern, source inspection, stimulus queue
- In: Cautious gait when postAlert
- Out: Group investigation roles (e11-communication)
- Out: Search around LKP (e11-search-behaviour)

## Notes
Investigation position is the perceived position (may be offset by sound routing), not the true source.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an Investigating guard with target position 12 m away, when simulated, then it arrives within (12 / walkSpeed + 1) s and performs a scan of ≥ 3 look directions.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a second, louder stimulus while investigating, when perceived, then the guard retargets to the new position and the first is queued.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an unreachable stimulus position (on a roof), when investigating, then the guard moves to the closest reachable point, looks toward the position for the scan duration, then de-escalates.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a scenario where a noise occurs behind a closed door, when the guard investigates, then it opens the door (if unlocked) before scanning the room.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a queue already holding 3 stimuli, when a 4th weaker stimulus arrives, then the weakest is dropped.

title: Auto-generate smoke tests for every creature data file
description:
## Why
The test policy requires every creature to have at least one automated test; generating them keeps the bestiary cheap to extend.

## What
A Vitest harness that discovers every `CreatureDef` and runs a standard smoke battery in a headless sim: spawn, tick 10 s, perceive a scripted stimulus (alert state leaves Unaware), execute each declared attack once against a dummy, take lethal damage and die (or respect immunity), despawn. Creature files can opt into extra scenario tests.

## Scope
- In: Discovery, battery, readable per-creature test names
- In: CI integration
- Out: Balance testing (E13 / E34 telemetry)

## Notes
Test names follow `creature:<id> smoke — <step>` so failures point to data.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given N creature files, when the suite runs, then N × (battery size) named tests execute.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a creature whose attack references a missing hitbox, when the suite runs, then only that creature’s attack step fails with the ref name in the message.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a creature immune to all damage types, when the lethal-damage step runs, then the step asserts survival instead of death.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature with no attacks, when the battery runs, then the attack step is skipped and reported as skipped, not passed.

title: Declare non-hostile creature interactions (feed, talk, calm) in data
description:
## Why
Not everything exists solely to be killed. Social creatures (E14) need a framework hook: feeding, talking, intimidating, petting or trading must be declarable per creature.

## What
As a designer, I want to declare which non-hostile verbs a creature accepts and under what conditions so that E14 can build social creatures without new engine code. `interactions`: list of {verb (`talk`, `feed`, `intimidate`, `calm`, `pet`, `trade`, `give`), conditions (disposition range, alert state ∈ {Unaware, Suspicious}, item tag required), outcome event id}. Available verbs surface as contextual prompts via the interaction system; executing emits a typed sim event consumed by dialogue/disposition rules.

## Scope
- In: Schema, condition evaluation, prompt surfacing, outcome events
- In: Alert-state gating (cannot pet a creature in Combat)
- Out: Dialogue trees (e22-dialogue-runtime)
- Out: Specific social creatures and their outcomes (E14)

## Notes
Outcome events feed e12-dispositions modifier rules, e.g. `feed` with any `edible` item applies the `fed` modifier.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P1 — befriending/helping creatures (Brother Horn, the goblins, Clatter) is an MVP constitution pillar and depends on this.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature declaring `feed` requiring item tag `edible:meat`, when the player holds no such item, then the `feed` verb is not offered.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same creature in Combat state, when the player holds meat, then `feed` is not offered.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the grey-box testbed and a fixture creature declaring `feed`, when the player feeds it, then the item is removed from inventory, a `CreatureInteracted{verb: feed}` event fires and disposition rises by the `fed` modifier.
- AC-4 [content] Given an interaction with an unknown verb, when validated, then validation fails listing allowed verbs.
- AC-5 [unit] Given two verbs with overlapping conditions, when prompts are built, then both are offered in declared order.

title: Creature fears and morale that trigger fleeing and cowering
description:
## Why
Creatures have fears. Frightening a wolf pack with fire or breaking goblin morale by felling their leader are non-lethal solutions the constitution wants.

## What
As a player, I want to exploit what creatures fear so that I can win encounters without killing everything. `fears`: list of {stimulus property or faction or event, intensity}. Morale 0–100 per creature, reduced by fear stimuli, ally deaths, low health, leader death; restored over time and near allies. Below thresholds the creature emits `Cower` or `Flee` intents for the AI.

## Scope
- In: Fear stimulus matching via properties (e.g. anything `burning` or light level > X)
- In: Morale model + thresholds + recovery
- In: Group morale shock when a `leader`-tagged ally dies
- Out: Flee movement behaviour (e11-retreat-flee)
- Out: Intimidation dialogue (E14)

## Notes
Fear stimuli are perceived — the creature must sense the burning object (via e11-perception) for it to count.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature with fear {property `burning`, intensity 30} and morale 50, when it perceives a burning object within 5 m, then morale drops to 20 and a `Flee` intent is emitted (flee threshold 25).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a fear stimulus the creature cannot perceive (behind a wall), when evaluated, then morale is unchanged.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a `leader`-tagged creature dies, when allies within 20 m perceive it, then each ally loses the configured leader-shock morale once.
- AC-4 [unit] Given morale 10 and no stimuli, when 30 s pass near 2 allies, then morale recovers by the configured rate and the `Flee` intent clears once above 35 (hysteresis).
- AC-5 [content] Given a fear with intensity outside 0–100, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Per-creature disposition toward the player with event modifiers
description:
## Why
Some creatures can be tricked, helped, befriended or angered; that needs a persistent per-individual attitude, not just a faction flag.

## What
Disposition value −100..100 per creature toward the player, seeded from def + faction. Data-driven modifier rules map sim events to deltas (`attacked: -40`, `fed: +15`, `witnessed-theft: -20`, `helped-ally: +25`). Thresholds map to stances (hostile < −50 ≤ wary < −10 ≤ neutral ≤ 10 < friendly ≤ 50 < devoted). Decay toward baseline is optional per creature.

## Scope
- In: Runtime value, modifier rules, thresholds, decay
- In: Events for UI/dialogue to consume
- In: Save serialization of values
- Out: Dialogue conditions using disposition (e22-dialogue-runtime)
- Out: Social creature content (E14)

## Notes
Modifier rules are content data so E14 can add new event types without code changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature at disposition 0, when the player attacks it, then disposition becomes −40 and stance becomes `wary`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given disposition 95, when a +15 modifier applies, then it clamps to 100.
- AC-3 [unit] Given decay rate 1/min toward baseline 0, when 10 sim minutes pass from 20, then disposition is 10.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a modifier rule for an event type that never fires, when the sim runs 10,000 ticks, then disposition is unchanged (no drift).
- AC-5 [integration] Given a saved game with a creature at −37, when loaded, then disposition is exactly −37.

title: Faction table and relationship queries between creatures
description:
## Why
Goblins that fight skeletons, wolves that avoid trolls and guards that tolerate a disguised thief all need one relationship model.

## What
Faction data (`factions.json`): id, default stance toward each other faction (`ally`, `friendly`, `neutral`, `wary`, `hostile`, `prey`, `predator`) and toward the player. Runtime API `relation(a, b)` combining faction stance, per-creature overrides and dynamic modifiers (e.g. the player attacked this faction). Relationship changes emit events.

## Scope
- In: Faction schema + symmetric/asymmetric stances
- In: Dynamic faction-wide modifiers stored in sim state (save-compatible)
- In: Query API used by perception/alert/combat
- Out: Individual disposition toward player (e12-dispositions)
- Out: Story-specific factions (E39/E13 content)

## Notes
Asymmetry is allowed (wolves see sheep as prey; sheep see wolves as predator).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given faction A hostile to B, when `relation(a, b)` is queried for members, then it returns `hostile`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an asymmetric definition A→B `prey` and B→A `predator`, when queried both ways, then each direction returns its own stance.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature-level override making one member of A friendly to the player, when queried, then that creature returns `friendly` and other A members keep the faction default.
- AC-4 [content] Given a faction referencing an undefined faction id, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the player kills a member of faction A witnessed by another A member, when the rule runs, then A’s dynamic stance toward the player worsens one step and a `FactionRelationChanged` event is emitted once.

title: Drive creature vulnerabilities from world properties, not pairings
description:
## Why
The constitution requires systemic interactions: a creature tagged `flammable` should burn from any fire source, and `undead` should respond to any light effect, without scripted spell/creature pairs.

## What
As a player, I want creatures to react to the same world properties as objects so that my experiments transfer. Creatures carry world-property tags (from e03-world-properties) plus `vulnerabilities`/`resistances` keyed by damage type or property effect (e.g. `heat: x2`, `frozen: immune`, `light: stagger`). A sim rule applies element-propagation effects to creatures exactly as to objects, then applies the creature multiplier.

## Scope
- In: Property tags on creatures participate in element propagation
- In: Multiplier + immunity + special reaction (stagger, flee trigger) data
- In: Resolution order documented
- Out: New element types (E03)
- Out: Specific creature weaknesses (E13)

## Notes
Express everything as properties; tests must use property names, never spell names. Reactions can emit a `FearStimulus` consumed by e12-fears-morale.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any creature tagged `flammable` inside an active fire volume, when 1 s of sim time passes, then it gains the `burning` state.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature with `resistances.heat: immune`, when inside a fire volume, then it takes 0 heat damage and does not gain `burning`.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature with `vulnerabilities.cold: 2.0`, when it receives a 10-point cold packet, then it loses 20 health.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature with reaction `light: stagger` and light level at its position rising above the configured threshold within 1 tick, then it enters stagger once and not again until light falls below the threshold (no re-trigger spam).
- AC-5 [content] Given a vulnerability keyed by an unknown property or damage type, when validated, then validation fails listing known keys.
notes: mw-e12.1 (PR #40) defined creature resistances as ONE map: damage type → multiplier 0–3 (0 = immune, >1 = vulnerable), matching mw-e04.1. Adapt this bead to that shape rather than adding separate vulnerabilities/immune fields.

title: Run a playtest narrative-comprehension check and fix gaps
description:
## Why
A twist no one notices is not a twist. The story must be understandable without a wiki, through play alone.

## What
As the narrative designer, I want observed playtests with a short comprehension questionnaire so that I know which beats land and which need clearer delivery. 5+ testers (mix of classes) play through; afterwards they answer: who was taking people and why, what Horn is, who the "friend below" was, what the bell does, what their class did differently. Findings become fix beads or immediate text edits.

## Scope
- In: docs/narrative/playtest-comprehension.md (script, questionnaire, results)
- In: text fixes for beats scoring < 60% comprehension
- Out: fun/feel validation (Related: E35 MVP fun validation)
- Out: telemetry dashboards (Related: E34)

## Notes
Do not prompt testers about the twist during play; observe only. Record at least one tester per class.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given ≥ 5 testers covering all 4 classes, when the questionnaire is scored, then results per question are recorded in docs/narrative/playtest-comprehension.md.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the results, when ≥ 4 of 5 testers explain the minotaur twist and the bell solution in their own words, then the check passes; otherwise fixes are made and the check repeated with new testers.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the results, when any beat scores < 60% comprehension, then a text fix or a follow-up bead is created and linked in the results doc.
- AC-4 [content] Edge: given a tester reaches an ending the designer did not expect, when analysed, then the fact trail is recorded and checked against the ending rules in e39-main-quest-data.

title: Add narrative lint for names, canon facts and dangling IDs
description:
## Why
Parallel writers drift: names misspelled, the Long Vespers happening 60 or 62 years ago, notes pointing at rooms that don't exist. An automated pass keeps canon trustworthy without re-reading everything.

## What
As a designer, I want a CI lint that checks narrative content against the canon glossary so that contradictions fail the build. Checks: proper-noun spelling against glossary.json (with a near-miss detector), canon numbers from bible §11.3, all ID references resolve (NPCs, quests, facts, locations, items), class-variant coverage warnings, banned-tone list (modern slang, fourth-wall phrases), and British-leaning spelling in player-facing text. Followed by one manual consistency read of all content against the bible.

## Scope
- In: src/tools/narrative-lint (runs in CI)
- In: glossary-driven checks
- In: one manual full-content consistency pass with fixes
- Out: schema validation itself (e00-content-pipeline)
- Out: localisation (post-MVP)

## Notes
Depends only on the P1 content; P2 content (side quests, rumours, books, spellbook flavour, descriptions, all Wendmouth content) is linted automatically in CI as it lands, and its authors fix lint errors in their own PRs. Tooling code in src/tools needs ≥ 90% coverage per backlog contract §3. Near-miss detector example: "Mirella" or "Kettlebach" → error with suggestion.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a fixture containing "Mirella", when linted, then an error names the file, line and suggests "Mirela".
- AC-2 [unit] Given a fixture stating the Long Vespers was "sixty years ago", when linted, then a canon-fact error is reported citing bible §11.3.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a dialogue node referencing a non-existent fact or location ID, when linted, then a dangling-reference error is reported.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a fixture with a banned-tone phrase, when linted, then a warning is reported with the matched phrase.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the full src/content narrative set, when the lint runs in CI, then it completes in ≤ 10 s with zero errors.
- AC-6 [manual] Given the manual consistency pass, when complete, then every discrepancy found is fixed in content or recorded in the bible change log.

title: Write harbour rumours and in-world texts (manifest, notice, tolls)
description:
## Why
Rumours and documents are how the harbour hands the player leads and evidence; a cargo manifest is a better clue than a quest marker.

## What
As a player, I want Wendmouth gossip and paperwork that point at real secrets so that snooping in the harbour pays off. Harbour rumours 13–18 (bible §6.2) with sources (Mags, Nell, Old Reed, Tidemarket gossip), truth values and targets; texts: the Gilded Tern cargo manifest (customs copy and Quell's honest copy), the Lantern Court port notice, the Kestrel Lock toll board, the foundry invoice, the one readable line of Mr. S—'s sealed letter.

## Scope
- In: rumor-13..18 data entries
- In: book-/note- entries for the harbour texts with placements
- In: evidence tags on manifest, invoice and seal used by quest conditions
- Out: town rumours 1–12 (e39-rumor-set)
- Out: general books (e39-books-lore)

## Notes
Canon numbers must match bible §11.3 exactly (40 horn-coins, 3 carved stones, 1 name-stone; 40 brass trinkets; clerk E. Ardley dead a year). The sea-serpent rumour is false and needs a debunk path.

**Integration note:** Owner wants the river and Wendmouth in the MVP (P1). It stays optional to the main quest.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the harbour rumour entries, when validated, then there are 6 rumours (13–18), each with source, truth value and a target resolving to an existing ID.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the manifest and invoice texts, when checked by the narrative lint canon rules, then all quantities and names match bible §11.3.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the honest manifest item, when a quest condition checks evidence tags, then it satisfies both Framed in Brass and The Crate for Mr. S— evidence requirements.
- AC-4 [content] Given the sea-serpent rumour, when reviewed, then it is marked false and has a debunk path (diving to the figurehead or asking Mags).
- AC-5 [unit] Edge: given the player never visits Wendmouth, when Dot's rumour pool is evaluated, then harbour rumours 13–18 may be heard only as second-hand lines and never mark a harbour target as visited.

title: Script harbour side quests The Tidefair and Contraband Pages
description:
## Why
Non-thief classes need harbour hijinks of their own, and the sorcerer needs a Lantern Court foil; both quests also unlock the harbour's better gear.

## What
As a knight, archer, sorcerer or thief, I want a harbour contest that suits my class and a scrape with the customs house so that Wendmouth is fun for everyone, not only sneaks. The Tidefair: four events any class may enter — arm-wrestling/Gull brawl (knight flavour), the Gull Shoot (archer), the Regatta with unenforced "no magic" rule (sorcerer), the Pocket Race with Cray as a mark (thief); win, cheat, throw a match for Nell's book, or lose gracefully. Contraband Pages: recover impounded books (Mirela's order, the player's own) via failed bribe, romance-novel trade, writ (Vane or forged seal), strongroom theft, inspector impersonation, or bay-nine evidence.

## Scope
- In: quest-tidefair and quest-contraband-pages data
- In: facts: tidefair.results.<event>, tidefair.cheated, cray.disposition, books.impounded, mirela.order.delivered
- In: reward hooks: Tereza under-counter stock, foreign spellbook, discounts
- Out: contest mechanics (Related: E04/E05/E06/E10 class systems)
- Out: shop inventories (Related: E20/E21)

## Notes
Losing a Tidefair event must still give a warm outcome (Oona buys a drink) — failure creates stories. Cray's disposition from Contraband Pages gates her help in The Crate for Mr. S—.

**Integration note:** Owner wants the river and Wendmouth in the MVP (P1). It stays optional to the main quest.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given both quest files, when validated, then they pass; The Tidefair has 4 events each with win/cheat/throw/lose outcomes and Contraband Pages has ≥ 5 resolutions.
- AC-2 [unit] Given each class, when the Tidefair is joined, then the class-flavoured event is highlighted and all 4 events remain enterable.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a Regatta win using magic while Cray is present, when resolved, then the win is voided, tidefair.cheated is set and a fine branch plays.
- AC-4 [unit] Given Contraband Pages completes with the bay-nine evidence route, when Cray is next spoken to, then cray.disposition is at least "grateful" and her seizure route in The Crate for Mr. S— is available.
- AC-5 [unit] Edge: given the player loses every Tidefair event, when the quest completes, then a consolation outcome is granted and Wendmouth reputation does not decrease.
- AC-6 [manual] Given playtests with a knight, archer and sorcerer, when each plays the Tidefair, then each tester names their class event as a highlight of the harbour.

title: Script the heist side quest The Crate for Mr. S—
description:
## Why
A perfectly executed infiltration should feel as satisfying as a hard fight (constitution §5). The bonded-warehouse heist is the harbour's showpiece and links Wendmouth to Vane, Horn and the Mr. S— hook.

## What
As a thief (or any class willing to try), I want to intercept Vane's relic crate before the Gilded Tern sails so that I gain evidence against Vane and a gift for the minotaur. Resolutions per bible §6.1 quest 6: stealth heist with ballast swap and re-seal (thief-favoured), paper route via forged/swapped manifest and Cray's legal seizure, archer net-cut into the harbour, knight force (brawl with Low Tide Company and harbour watch), sorcerer freeze-the-pool or Gust-the-hoist, leverage on Quell. Outcomes: name-stone, honest manifest, Mr. S—'s sealed letter; or the Tern sails.

## Scope
- In: quest-crate-for-mr-s data
- In: facts: crate.intercepted, crate.method, heist.undetected, manifest.honest.obtained, namestone.obtained, tern.sailed
- In: undetected-heist variant where the Tern sails with ballast
- Out: stealth/disguise mechanics (Related: E09 stealth, E10 thief toolkit)
- Out: warehouse and ship level geometry (Related: world-content planners, E26-style level beads)

## Notes
Heist timing is stage-based, not real-time: the Tern sails when Act III begins (bible §11.3). The name-stone is a befriend-Horn trigger consumed by e39-dialogue-horn.

**Integration note:** Owner wants the river and Wendmouth in the MVP (P1). It stays optional to the main quest.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the quest file, when validated by the quest validator, then it passes and exposes ≥ 5 resolutions, each setting crate.method.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the heist completes with heist.undetected = true, when Act III begins, then tern.sailed is set, crate.intercepted is true and no alarm or Low Tide hostility fact is set.
- AC-3 [unit] Given crate.method = force, when the quest completes, then lowtide.standing becomes hostile and Cray's arrival branch is flagged.
- AC-4 [unit] Given namestone.obtained, when Horn's first-meeting node is evaluated, then the befriend branch is offered.
- AC-5 [unit] Edge: given Act III begins before the crate is intercepted, when the quest updates, then it resolves as "sailed", the customs manifest copy remains obtainable and the main quest is unaffected.
- AC-6 [manual] Given a playtest by a thief, when the undetected heist is completed, then the tester rates it at least as satisfying as the watchtower fight on a 5-point scale.

title: Write dialogue for Inspector Cray, Tereza Maelo, Quell and Hesketh
description:
## Why
The customs inspector, the import merchant and Vane's shipping agent tie the harbour to the main plot and give each class a foil (Cray for sorcerers, Tereza for knights, Quell for thieves).

## What
As a player, I want the harbour's officials and traders to react to my class and to evidence I carry so that Wendmouth can change what happens to Vane. Inspector Prudence Cray (book confiscation, search-on-sight for sorcerers, romance-novel weakness, bay-nine suspicion, legal seizure route), Tereza Maelo (arms trade, knight duel challenge, foreign spellbook for a story, Tern access via debt of honour), Jasper Quell (nervous denials, collapse under evidence, honest manifest, head-start bargain), Captain Hesketh of the Gilded Tern (crew hiring, shanghai scene).

## Scope
- In: npc-cray, npc-tereza, npc-quell, npc-hesketh dialogue data
- In: evidence-gated branches (foundry invoice, honest manifest, dead-clerk seal)
- In: Tereza duel challenge/accept/decline/win/lose branches
- In: Cray disposition states used by Contraband Pages and The Crate for Mr. S—
- Out: duel combat rules (Related: E04 knight combat)
- Out: Tidemarket stock (Related: E20/E21)

## Notes
Cray is incorruptible: every bribe attempt fails and is recorded. Cray never confiscates plot-critical or forbidden-plot items. No human character's surname may begin with S (bible §11.1).

**Integration note:** Owner wants the river and Wendmouth in the MVP (P1). It stays optional to the main quest.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the four dialogue files, when validated, then all pass with zero unreachable nodes.
- AC-2 [unit] Given any bribe option to Cray, when chosen, then it fails, sets cray.bribe.attempted and lowers disposition; no branch lets a bribe succeed.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player holds the foundry invoice or honest manifest, when Quell is confronted, then the collapse branch is offered and can hand over crate access and the manifest.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player class is knight, when Tereza is first met, then the duel challenge is offered; given win or loss, the matching branch sets tereza.duel.result.
- AC-5 [content] Given the four files, when searched, then no option lets Cray confiscate an item tagged plot-critical.
- AC-6 [unit] Edge: given Quell was given a head start and has left Wendmouth, when his location is visited, then his absence is handled by a note/bark and no dialogue references him as present.

title: Write dialogue for Mags Oakum, Nell Gannet, Big Oona and Old Reed
description:
## Why
Wendmouth is where "shenanigans ensue"; its river and dockside characters sell the tone shift from frightened Briar Glen to a loud, cheerful port on the make.

## What
As a player, I want the bargewoman, the smuggler queen and the dockside regulars to be characters with their own angles so that the harbour feels rowdy and alive. Mags Oakum (barge rides, river lore, Weeping Adit route, her crate-carrying secret and pocketed horn-coin), Nell Gannet (Drowned Gull, Low Tide Company jobs, Undertow access, the thief-commission drop, relic-skimming secret), Big Oona (arm-wrestling champion, Tidefair barks), Old Reed (Kestrel Lock keeper, tolls in gossip). Voice per bible §5.13.

## Scope
- In: npc-mags, npc-nell, npc-oona, npc-reed dialogue data
- In: class-variant greetings and ≥ 2 class-specific branches for Mags and Nell
- In: barge-ride booking lines (morning only; refuses night runs)
- In: thief commission drop branch (deliver / keep / fake coin)
- Out: Undertow stock and prices (Related: E20 economy, E21 bookshops)
- Out: quest objectives (e39-harbor-heist-quest, e39-side-quests-harbor)

## Notes
Mags must never run the barge at night. Nell knows what is in bay nine but only reveals it at high disposition or to a thief. Related: Wendmouth level layout (world-content planners).

**Integration note:** Owner wants the river and Wendmouth in the MVP (P1). It stays optional to the main quest.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the four dialogue files, when validated by the dialogue validator, then all pass with zero unreachable nodes.
- AC-2 [unit] Given each class, when Mags and Nell greet the player for the first time, then a class-specific greeting is selected (4 distinct lines each).
- AC-3 [unit] Given the in-game time is night, when the player asks Mags for a barge ride, then the refusal branch plays and no travel is started.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player class is thief and holds the commission horn-coin, when Nell is spoken to, then deliver, keep and fake-coin options are offered and each sets commission.outcome.
- AC-5 [unit] Edge: given the player has never visited Wendmouth, when any Briar Glen NPC references Nell or Mags, then only hearsay lines are used (no line implies the player has met them).
- AC-6 [manual] Given a read-through, when compared to bible §5.13 and the tone guide, then harbour voices read as rowdier and more cheerful than Briar Glen without modern slang.

title: Write failure-state narratives: the Fold, jail, capture, sour bell
description:
## Why
"Failure creates stories." Death, capture and botched actions should land the player somewhere new and be remembered.

## What
As a player, I want failures to move the story sideways so that I keep playing instead of reloading. Content and fact wiring per bible §4.5 and §9: waking in the Fold after dying in the Knot (pre- and post-reveal text; goblin camp or Forgotten variants if Horn is dead), waking at the Sleeping Ox after a forest death, jail with the drain escape, goblin capture, ringing the tongueless bell, misfired Lull dream, NPCs remembering embarrassments; Wendmouth: thrown off the pier (breakwater sea-door), losing the drinking contest (wake in the Gilded Tern's hold), books confiscated at customs (customs strongroom).

## Scope
- In: narrative/failure data: wake-up texts and conditions
- In: facts: player.rescues.byHorn, player.jailed.count, player.captured.byGoblins, bell.rung.sour
- In: NPC remark hooks for embarrassment facts
- Out: respawn mechanics and save rules (Related: E01/E30)
- Out: jail/escape level geometry (Related: E24)

## Notes
Kettleback's "carrying fee" must never exceed what the player can pay (take a trinket if broke).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a death in the Knot with horn.fate = alive and quest before the reveal, when the wake-up is resolved, then the eerie Fold text plays and player.rescues.byHorn increments by 1.
- AC-2 [unit] Given horn.fate = dead, when a death in the Knot occurs, then the goblin-camp variant plays if goblins.standing ≥ wary, else the Forgotten variant.
- AC-3 [unit] Edge: given the player has 0 gold, when Kettleback charges the carrying fee, then a trinket is taken instead, or waived if none, and no negative gold results.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the bell is rung without its tongue, when resolved, then bell.rung.sour is set and the Hushling/Horn-approach encounter flag is raised.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the player is caught by dockhands in Wendmouth, when resolved, then the thrown-off-the-pier text plays, the player is placed at the breakwater and harbor.seadoor.discovered is set; given restricted books are confiscated, then they move to the customs strongroom container, never destroyed.
- AC-6 [manual] Given a playtest, when a tester dies in the Knot twice, then they describe the Fold wake-up as intriguing rather than as a punishment.

title: Write class-specific arrivals, routes and signature beats
description:
## Why
Classes change possibilities; the story must acknowledge each class's fantasy at key beats, not just in combat.

## What
As a knight, archer, sorcerer or thief, I want the story to notice who I am so that my class feels like a role, not a stat block. Content per bible §4.3: four arrival reasons (Oath for Hire, Silent Wolves, Letter from the Lamplit Stacks, Commission from the City), class-flavoured interaction prompts at signature beats (formal relief, signal mirror, reading Horn's axe, sneaking into the Fold, plus one Wendmouth hijinks beat per class per bible §4.3), and class-specific climax lines.

## Scope
- In: per-class arrival text and journal entries
- In: class-variant prompt/bark text for ≥ 4 signature beats per class
- In: audit sheet mapping each bible §4.3 beat to its content ID
- Out: the mechanics behind class routes (Related: E16 class-specific solutions)
- Out: NPC dialogue branches already owned by e39-dialogue-* items

## Notes
The thief's commission comes from "Mr. S—", Vane's buyer (post-MVP hook; do not resolve).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given each class, when a new game starts, then the matching arrival text and first journal entry are selected.
- AC-2 [content] Given the audit sheet, when checked, then every class moment in bible §4.3 maps to an existing content ID.
- AC-3 [unit] Given each class, when the class-variant lookup is run for every signature beat, then each class has ≥ 4 unique entries and no beat falls back to generic text unintentionally.
- AC-4 [unit] Edge: given a class-variant entry is missing for a beat, when looked up, then the "all" fallback is returned and the lint reports a warning.

title: Write opening, first-night and ending/epilogue text
description:
## Why
The first ten minutes must hook (a child sleepwalking toward a horned shadow) and the ending must reflect what the player actually did.

## What
As a player, I want a strong opening and an ending that remembers my choices so that the adventure feels whole. Text for the arrival and bounty board, the first-night sequence (including failure variants), the title/intro card, and the 4 headline endings with epilogue slides assembled from world-state facts (Horn, abbot, Vane, breach, Clatter, goblins, Tansy, Hale), plus optional harbour slides (crate intercepted → name-stone home; Tern sailed → the far-city crate hook). Also the barge-ride travel narration between Briar Glen Quay and Wendmouth.

## Scope
- In: narrative/intro and narrative/endings data
- In: epilogue slide conditions
- In: first-night variants: followed, lost her, blocked by wolves
- Out: class-specific arrival text (e39-class-variants)
- Out: cutscene staging/camera (E01/E24)

## Notes
Text-only in MVP; each slide ≤ 60 words. The Long Vespers ending must end "on a doorway, not a grave" (bible §4.4).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the endings data, when evaluated against every combination of the 7 ending facts, then each combination yields exactly one headline ending and ≥ 3 epilogue slides.
- AC-2 [unit] Given each first-night variant, when triggered, then it ends with the horned-shadow beat.
- AC-3 [unit] Given each slide, when measured, then it is ≤ 60 words.
- AC-4 [unit] Edge: given a fact is unset (e.g. Clatter never met), when epilogue slides are selected, then a neutral slide is used and no slide references an unmet character.
- AC-5 [manual] Given a playtest, when the opening completes, then ≥ 4 of 5 testers can state what they are trying to do next.

title: Write the Sleepless Abbot's notes, temptations and Cradle dialogue
description:
## Why
The second twist — the helpful "friend below" is the abbot — gives the story its Souls-like sting and re-reads earlier notes in a new light.

## What
As a player, I want the notes that helped me to turn out to be manipulation so that I feel the twist and want to re-read them. Content: 6–8 "a friend below" notes (genuinely useful), the Act III reveal speech, class-targeted temptations (Somnomancy for sorcerers, duty for knights, the hunt for archers, treasure for thieves), Cradle dialogue for fight/trick/persuade/join, and the persuade-to-rest scene with Clatter.

## Scope
- In: npc-abbot dialogue data
- In: note-friend-below-01..08 note items
- In: persuade branch gated on clatter.restored
- Out: wraith combat (E13)
- Out: the Lull spell mechanics (E08/E06)

## Notes
Voice: courteous, never raises his voice. Notes must be re-readable after the reveal; include at least two lines that read differently once the player knows.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the abbot dialogue file, when validated, then it passes and each of the 4 Cradle resolutions sets abbot.fate.
- AC-2 [unit] Given clatter.restored is false, when the Cradle dialogue is evaluated, then the persuade-to-rest option is not offered.
- AC-3 [unit] Given each class, when the temptation node is evaluated, then the class-specific temptation line is selected.
- AC-4 [content] Given the friend-below notes, when validated as items, then there are 6–8 notes and each references only locations that exist in the glossary.
- AC-5 [unit] Edge: given the sorcerer accepted Lull, when Horn or Mirela is next spoken to, then the "dreamer mark" fact is readable by their dialogue conditions.

title: Write dialogue for Clatter, Mother Kettleback and Snig
description:
## Why
A skeleton who remembers and goblins you can talk to are explicit constitution examples; they carry the game's humour and warmth in the dark.

## What
As a player, I want the skeleton and the goblins to be people so that the dungeon has characters, not just enemies. Clatter: memory fragments that grow as The Name on the Bones progresses, apology barks when hostile, rest/join choice. Mother Kettleback: negotiation after capture or approach, Horn arrangement, Duggan crate, trade lines. Snig: bookshop burglar scenes, reading attempts, vouching for the player.

## Scope
- In: npc-clatter, npc-kettleback, npc-snig dialogue data
- In: memory-stage variants for Clatter (0–3 pieces recovered)
- In: goblin standing variants (hostile, wary, friendly)
- Out: goblin camp AI (E11/E14)
- Out: side quest objectives (e39-side-quests-*)

## Notes
Goblins cannot read and do not dream (canon). Clatter loses recovered memories if the song swells before he is restored.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the three dialogue files, when validated, then all pass with zero unreachable nodes.
- AC-2 [unit] Given clatter.memories = 0..3, when Clatter is spoken to, then a distinct memory-stage line set is used for each value.
- AC-3 [unit] Given goblins.standing = hostile, wary and friendly, when Kettleback is approached, then the matching opening branch plays.
- AC-4 [unit] Edge: given the player was captured by goblins while hostile, when brought to Kettleback, then the negotiation branch is available (capture never ends in a game-over).
- AC-5 [content] Given Snig's lines, when linted, then none depict a goblin successfully reading full sentences before the Bookshop Burglar "lessons" outcome.

title: Write Brother Horn's dialogue across all Warden resolutions
description:
## Why
The minotaur twist is the emotional core of the MVP and the constitution's flagship "fight, trick, befriend or help" creature.

## What
As a player, I want the minotaur to speak with me differently depending on how I reached him so that the reveal feels earned. Dialogue for Horn: the yield line, spare/kill choice, post-trick confrontation in the Fold, befriend triggers (Vesper hymn, horn-ring, vouching by Snig or Clatter, lowered weapon), the knight's Trial of Horns, help/heal/seal-the-breach lines, rescue-count remarks after player deaths, Act III shaft-defence barks, and ending lines.

## Scope
- In: npc-horn dialogue data
- In: class-specific first-meeting lines (bible §4.3)
- In: rescue-count lines for 1, 2, 3 and 5+ rescues
- Out: Horn combat behaviour (E14 social creatures, E13 bestiary)
- Out: quest state logic (e39-main-quest-data)

## Notes
Voice: slow, short, plain sentences with pauses; never roars words. "The monks called me Brother Horn. It was a kindness. I have kept it." Related: E14 social creature hooks for yield/befriend.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given Horn's dialogue file, when validated, then it passes and each of the 6 Warden resolutions has at least one terminal node that sets horn.fate.
- AC-2 [unit] Given each befriend trigger fact independently, when the first-meeting node is evaluated, then the befriend branch is offered.
- AC-3 [unit] Given player.rescues.byHorn = 1, 2, 3 and 6, when Horn is spoken to, then the matching rescue-count line is selected.
- AC-4 [unit] Edge: given the player tricked Horn and then flees the Fold confrontation, when Horn is next met, then the "angry, then weary" re-entry branch plays instead of the first-meeting branch.
- AC-5 [manual] Given a playtest of the reveal, when the Fold is entered, then the reveal is understood from the scene before Horn explains it (confirmed in e39-playtest-comprehension).

title: Write dialogue for Vane, the Pells, Juniper, Oswin and Duggan
description:
## Why
The mine owner's grey morality, the baker's grief and the merchants' personalities make Briar Glen a living town rather than a quest dispenser.

## What
As a player, I want the rest of Briar Glen to react to the crisis and to me so that the town feels lived-in. Dialogue for Harrow Vane (bounty, charm, confrontation with ledger/Duggan, confess/bribe/flee outcomes), Hollis Pell (grief, family Bible, reunion with Tansy), Tansy Pell (post-rescue), Juniper Fenn (wolves, sleep-draught guilt, merchant lines), Oswin Brand (merchant, bell-tongue mould), Duggan Marl (crate captive, testimony).

## Scope
- In: npc-vane, npc-hollis, npc-tansy, npc-juniper, npc-oswin, npc-duggan dialogue data
- In: Vane confrontation branch with 4 outcomes (exposed, confesses, bribes, flees)
- In: merchant greeting/farewell lines with class variants
- Out: shop mechanics (e20-shop-system — Related, not anchor-linked here)
- Out: side quest objective data (e39-side-quests-*)

## Notes
Vane is redeemable (bible §5.3); avoid moustache-twirling. Oswin's mould enables a recast tongue if the original is destroyed — must match main quest fallback.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the six dialogue files, when validated, then all pass with zero unreachable nodes.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the facts vane.ledger.obtained and duggan.testimony, when the confrontation is evaluated with each combination, then the available Vane outcomes match the table in the file header.
- AC-3 [unit] Given tansy.saved is true, when Hollis is spoken to after the quest, then the reunion branch plays; given false, the grief branch plays.
- AC-4 [unit] Edge: given the Vesper Bell tongue was destroyed, when Oswin is spoken to, then the recast-tongue option is offered exactly once.
- AC-5 [manual] Given a read-through, when compared to bible §5.3–5.7, then voices match and Vane reads as morally grey rather than purely villainous.

title: Write dialogue for Mirela, Dot and Captain Hale
description:
## Why
The bookseller, the rumour-monger and the guard captain are the investigation hub; memorable, reactive town NPCs are the QfG/DOS2 heart of the game.

## What
As a player, I want the three hub NPCs to remember me, react to my class and point me at real places so that talking feels as rewarding as exploring. Dialogue graphs for Mirela Thorne (Lamplit Stacks: shop banter, restricted-shelf access, Nine Sleeps secret, Mortimer), Dot Farrow (Sleeping Ox: rumour trading hook, fence for thieves, Fitch), and Captain Hale (missing-persons list, sleepwalking secret, jail dialogue, Act III testimony). Voice per bible §5.1, §5.2, §5.4.

## Scope
- In: npc-mirela, npc-dot, npc-hale dialogue data
- In: class-variant greetings and ≥ 2 class-specific branches per NPC
- In: disposition-gated lines
- In: post-quest reactions to each headline ending
- Out: rumour content itself (e39-rumor-set)
- Out: shop inventory rules (e21-bookshop-system)

## Notes
Mirela must never sell Nine Sleeps. Hale must not know he delivered the "friend below" note until The Captain's Boots reveals it.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the three dialogue files, when validated by the dialogue validator, then all pass and every node is reachable from an entry node.
- AC-2 [unit] Given each class in turn, when each NPC greets the player for the first time, then a class-specific greeting line is selected (4 distinct lines per NPC).
- AC-3 [unit] Given the fact hale.sleepwalking.revealed is false, when any Hale node is evaluated, then no line references him delivering the note.
- AC-4 [content] Given Mirela's dialogue, when searched, then no option transfers the book-nine-sleeps item to the player.
- AC-5 [unit] Edge: given Mirela's disposition is "banned" (Mortimer caught the player), when the player talks to her, then the banned branch plays and access resets after the documented condition (biscuits or one in-game day).
- AC-6 [manual] Given a read-through, when the narrative designer compares lines to bible §5 voice samples, then each NPC's voice is consistent and no line breaks the tone guide (§2.4).

title: Script the main quest graph with four endings as quest data
description:
## Why
The MVP scenario must exercise the constitution through one adventure with multiple resolutions; the quest runtime should carry it with data, not bespoke scripts.

## What
As a player, I want the Labyrinth Beneath Briar Glen quest to track what I actually did so that my choices about the minotaur, the abbot and Vane produce different outcomes. Encodes bible §4.1 beats 1–16 as quest stages/objectives: the first night, investigation hub (any order) with the optional Wendmouth thread, six entry routes into the Deepworks (including the Weeping Adit river route), the Warden encounter with six resolutions (kill, spare, trick, befriend, help, Trial of Horns), abbot resolutions (fight, trick, persuade, join), the Climb, Vespers, the morning after, and the four headline endings assembled from world-state facts.

## Scope
- In: quest-labyrinth-beneath-briar-glen data file(s)
- In: world-state facts: horn.fate, abbot.fate, vane.fate, breach.sealed, tansy.saved, clatter.restored, goblins.standing, wendmouth.visited, crate.intercepted, tern.sailed
- In: the Gilded Tern sailing trigger at Act III start
- In: ending selection rules for the 4 headline endings and their epilogue-slide variants
- In: quest-graph tests reaching every ending
- Out: dialogue lines (e39-dialogue-* items)
- Out: intro/ending prose (e39-intro-endings-text)
- Out: encounter/level layout (E26)

## Notes
Investigation hub objectives must be completable in any order (bible §4.1 beat 4). Wendmouth is optional (bible §3.6): no main-quest objective may require it; harbour facts only add evidence, a befriend trigger (name-stone) and epilogue slides. Horn yields rather than dying at low health; killing requires an explicit choice. Related: E26 first dungeon for spatial placement.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the quest data, when validated by the quest runtime validator, then it passes with zero errors and every referenced world-state fact is registered.
- AC-2 [unit] Given scripted fact sets, when the ending rules are evaluated, then each of the 4 headline endings is reachable (including with wendmouth.visited = false throughout) and each fact set maps to exactly one ending.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the investigation hub, when its objectives are completed in each of 3 different orders, then the quest advances to "Getting in" identically.
- AC-4 [unit] Given any of the 6 Deepworks entry routes is completed, when the quest updates, then the "Getting in" stage completes and the route used is recorded.
- AC-5 [unit] Edge: given Horn is killed, when Act III begins, then the Climb uses the goblin or Clatter defender variant if available, else the chase variant, and the quest never soft-locks.
- AC-6 [unit] Edge: given Act III begins with crate.intercepted = false, when the stage starts, then tern.sailed is set and no Wendmouth objective blocks progress.
- AC-7 [unit] Edge: given Tansy is not intercepted in Act III, when the Cradle stage starts, then the hostage variant activates and all abbot resolutions remain available.
- AC-8 [manual] Given a full playthrough per class, when the quest completes, then the narrative designer confirms beats 1–16 play in order with no missing objective text.

title: Set narrative content layout, ID scheme and class-variant tagging
description:
## Why
Many narrative items are written in parallel; without one file layout and ID scheme, the lint and validators cannot catch dangling references and class variants will be inconsistent.

## What
As a designer, I want a documented, validator-backed convention for narrative data so that every dialogue, quest, rumour, book and description file is found, referenced and tested the same way. Defines: directory layout under src/content (dialogue/, quests/, rumors/, books/, descriptions/, narrative/), ID prefixes from bible §11.1 (npc-, quest-, book-, rumor-NN-, desc-), a class-variant field convention (knight|archer|sorcerer|thief|all), world-state fact naming (e.g. horn.fate, clatter.restored), and a canon glossary data file consumed by the lint.

## Scope
- In: docs/narrative/content-conventions.md
- In: src/content/narrative/glossary.json (names, places, canon facts)
- In: one worked example file per content kind passing the existing validators
- Out: the dialogue/quest schemas themselves (e22-dialogue-runtime, e23-quest-runtime)
- Out: the lint tool (e39-narrative-lint)

## Notes
World-state fact keys must be registered with the world-state store (e27-world-state-store). Keep in-game text British-leaning, code identifiers US spelling (bible §11.1).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the conventions doc, when read, then it defines directory, ID prefix, class-variant field and world-state fact naming for all six content kinds.
- AC-2 [unit] Given each worked example file, when run through the content pipeline validators, then it validates with zero errors.
- AC-3 [unit] Given glossary.json, when validated, then every principal NPC, location, creature type and canon number from bible §5, §3.5, §8 and §11.3 is present exactly once.
- AC-4 [unit] Edge: given an example dialogue line tagged with an unknown class value (e.g. "paladin"), when validated, then validation fails naming the file and field.

title: Decide the shipping title and record it as an ADR
description:
## Why
"Merlin's Wrath" is a working title; Merlin is not in the story and "wrath" signals the wrong tone. The title shapes asset prompts, the title screen and discoverability.

## What
The owner chooses between retaining the codename and the bible's shortlist (top pick: "Nightjar — The Labyrinth Beneath Briar Glen"; runner-up "The Vesper Bell"). A basic name-collision search (games stores, trademark databases, domain/handle availability) is done for the top 3. The decision is recorded as an ADR.

## Scope
- In: collision search for the top 3 candidates
- In: ADR at docs/decisions/NNNN-game-title.md
- In: updating the bible title section and backlog-contract working-title line
- Out: renaming the repository (optional follow-up)
- Out: logo/title art (E37 prompt beads)

## Notes
Options and rationale: story-bible §1. If the codename is kept, the bible suggests the "Merlin Watch" (falcon) retrofit so the name means something in-world.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the ADR, when read, then it states the chosen title, the alternatives considered, the collision-search results for each of the top 3, and the rationale.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the collision search, when a candidate collides with an existing game or trademark in the same class, then it is marked rejected in the ADR with the evidence link.
- AC-3 [content] Given the decision, when merged, then story-bible §1 and the backlog-contract working-title line reflect the chosen title.
- AC-4 [content] Edge: given the owner defers the decision, when the ADR is written, then it records "codename retained until <milestone>" and the bead stays open.
notes:
2026-09-27 owner USPTO search (live marks) for NIGHTJAR: 2 results, neither in game classes. (1) NIGHTJAR, serial 50124009, pending, IC 011 lamps, individual owner. (2) NIGHTJAR, serial 90804908, registered, IC 025/034/035 clothing etc., Nightjar Holdings LLC. No live NIGHTJAR mark found in IC 009 (game software) or IC 041 (online games). Still to check: existing games with the name (e.g. the 2011 iOS audio game 'The Nightjar'), Steam/itch/app stores, domain and social handles; consider keeping the subtitle 'The Labyrinth Beneath Briar Glen' as part of the title. Not legal advice.
2026-09-27 web check: 'The Nightjar' is crowded. Deborah Hewitt's fantasy novel The Nightjar (Tor, 2019) has nightjars guarding human souls, very close to our premise; 'The Nightjar' (2011) is a BAFTA-nominated iOS audio game; plus a well-known London bar. Recommendation: keep the Nightjar as the in-world creature name, not the headline title. 'The Vesper Bell': no games found; one YA magical-realism novel (Leah Erickson) and an unrelated horror anthology 'Vesper's Bell'. Less crowded, different genre.
close_reason: Completed in PR #2 (owner decided the title ahead of the full story-bible sign-off mw-e39.1)

title: Owner review and sign-off of the story bible; lock MVP canon
description:
## Why
Every dialogue line, quest, book and asset prompt depends on stable canon. The constitution values memorable NPCs and creatures-as-characters; the bible defines them once so parallel work stays consistent.

## What
The owner reviews the drafted `docs/narrative/story-bible.md` (premise, world history, factions, main quest beat sheet and endings, cast, side quests, rumours, creature lore, failure-creates-stories rules, naming conventions, glossary, canon quick-reference facts) and either signs it off or requests changes. The title section is reviewed and handed to the title decision bead. Signed-off canon is marked with a "Status: CANON v1" header and a change log.

## Scope
- In: owner read-through and comments
- In: revisions requested by the owner
- In: marking canon v1 and adding a change-log section
- In: confirming the 12 principal NPCs, 10 creature types, 5 side quests and 4 headline endings
- Out: the final title choice (see e39-title-decision)
- Out: writing any content data (later e39 items)

## Notes
Draft exists at docs/narrative/story-bible.md. Canon changes after sign-off require a bible change-log entry and a lint update (e39-narrative-lint). Related: art style bible (e37-style-bible) and audio bible (e38-audio-bible) should read §3.5 Locations and §5 Cast.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the drafted bible, when the owner has reviewed it, then every owner comment is resolved or recorded as an open question in the bible.
- AC-2 [content] Given the signed-off bible, when opened, then its header reads "Status: CANON v1" with a date and a change-log section exists.
- AC-3 [content] Given the bible, when checked, then §11.3 lists every canon number (timeline, counts, ages, bounty) that the narrative lint will enforce.
- AC-4 [content] Given the bible, when checked, then it names exactly the principal cast, creature roster, side quests and endings that downstream e39 items reference, with no TBD placeholders.
- AC-5 [manual] Edge: given the owner rejects a core element (e.g. the minotaur twist), when revised, then the beat sheet, cast and endings sections are updated together so no section contradicts another.

title: Provide a bookshop authoring template, validator and fixture shop
description:
## Why
The world-content group must author the Briar Glen bookshop (and future ones) purely as data.

## What
Template src/content/bookshops/_template.json with every field documented, a CLI/dev validator (pnpm validate:bookshops) reporting stock simulation over 10 rotations, and a non-Briar-Glen fixture shop ("Testbed Tomes") in the greybox testbed exercising every rule.

## Scope
- In: template, validator CLI with stock simulation report, fixture shop, authoring notes in docs/design/bookshops.md
- Out: Briar Glen bookshop content (world-content group, E24)

## Notes
Report flags pools that can never appear (all conditions unsatisfiable) and uniques duplicated across shops.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the template, when validated, then it passes the bookshop schema.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the fixture shop, when the validator simulates 10 rotations, then it prints stock per period and exits 0.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a shop whose rare book condition references a fact no content ever sets, when validated, then the validator warns "unreachable stock".
- AC-4 [content] Given two shops listing the same unique book, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Browse bookshop shelves with covers, previews and known markers
description:
## Why
The bookshop should feel like browsing a magical shop, not a spreadsheet.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to browse books by shelf/school with cover art, price, a first-page preview, comprehension estimate and "already known"/"stolen"/"forbidden" markers so that choosing a book is exciting and informed.
Extends the generic shop UI with book-specific panels; sell tab shows sell-back prices and wanted-book highlights.

## Scope
- In: bookshop UI panels, preview (reuses reader component), markers, sell tab highlights, keyboard/gamepad navigation
- Out: generic shop UI (E20)
- Out: final cover art (asset prompt beads per book)

## Notes
Placeholder covers: school-coloured leather with title text until art arrives.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a stocked shop, when the UI opens, then books are grouped by school shelf with price and cover (placeholder if no art).
- AC-2 [integration] Given a book teaching a known spell, when listed, then it shows an "Already known" marker.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the preview action, when used, then the first page renders via the reader component (garbled if language unknown).
- AC-4 [integration] Given insufficient gold, when attempting to buy, then the buy button is disabled with a reason and no transaction occurs.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed fixture shop, when a scripted player buys a book, then it appears in inventory and gold decreases by the listed price.

title: Give booksellers identity profiles, wants and rumour hooks
description:
## Why
Merchants have identities (E20); a bookseller who wants a specific tome or gossips about a rare book elsewhere drives exploration.

## What
As a designer, I want a bookseller profile (personality tags, favoured/disliked schools, wanted books list, rumours about books elsewhere, greeting variants keyed on player class and known spells) so that the dialogue group can make each bookseller memorable.
Exposes conditions/variables to the dialogue runtime: bookseller.wants(bookId), bookseller.rumour(), player.knowsSchool(school). Wanted books pay a bonus or unlock rare stock.

## Scope
- In: profile schema, dialogue variables/conditions, wanted-book bonus, rumour selection rule (points to books in other shops or dungeons)
- Out: actual dialogue writing and NPC characters (world-content/narrative groups)

## Notes
Rumours reference book ids + a location hint string authored in content; they add entries to the grimoire "rumoured spells" section (e07-grimoire-ui).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a profile with wantedBooks [X], when the player sells book X, then the bonus price applies and world fact "delivered_X" is set.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the dialogue runtime queries bookseller.rumour(), when the player already owns the rumoured book, then a different rumour is chosen or none.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a rumour is heard, when resolved, then the rumoured spell appears in the grimoire rumoured list with its location hint.
- AC-4 [content] Given a profile referencing an unknown book id in wantedBooks, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Price books by rarity, condition, legality, region and disposition
description:
## Why
Gold should have meaningful uses (E20); expensive books are aspirational goals.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want book prices that reflect rarity, condition, forbidden premium, regional demand and my relationship with the bookseller so that saving up for a grimoire matters.
price = base(rarity, tier) × condition × legality premium × region demand(school) × disposition modifier; sell-back price for books the player sells (booksellers pay more for books in their specialty).

## Scope
- In: pricing function (pure, data-configured), sell-back pricing, integer rounding rules
- Out: generic currency/transactions (e20-shop-system)

## Notes
All arithmetic in integer copper to avoid float drift; 100% coverage as an economy rule.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given base 200, damaged ×0.5, forbidden ×1.8, region ×1.0 and neutral disposition, when priced, then the price is 180.
- AC-2 [unit] Given friendly disposition −10% modifier, when priced, then the price is reduced by 10% (rounded to nearest copper).
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player sells a book in the shop's specialty school, when priced, then sell-back is the specialty rate (e.g. 40% of buy) instead of the default (25%).
- AC-4 [unit] Given any combination of modifiers, when priced, then the result is an integer ≥ 1 (property test).
- AC-5 [content] Given a pricing config with a negative multiplier, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Stock rare and unique books gated by world state conditions
description:
## Why
Rare books are the thrill of a bookshop: the one copy of a legendary grimoire appearing after you help the bookseller.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want rare books that appear only under conditions (quest completed, disposition level, day of week, region event) and unique books that exist once in the world so that bookshop visits can surprise me.
Conditions evaluated against the world state store and dialogue disposition; unique books tracked globally; a rare book may be "reserved" for the player for N days.

## Scope
- In: condition evaluation, unique registry, reservation window
- Out: secret back-room stock (e21-secret-stock)

## Notes
Conditions reuse the shared condition language from E22/E23 if available; otherwise a minimal condition set with a migration note.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a rare book conditioned on world fact "helped_bookseller", when the fact is false, then the book is not stocked; when true, it appears at next shop open.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a unique book already looted from a dungeon, when a shop would stock it, then it is skipped.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a reserved rare book with a 5-day window, when 5 days pass without purchase, then it leaves stock and returns to the rare pool.
- AC-4 [content] Given a rare entry with an unknown condition key, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Rotate bookshop stock on an in-game schedule
description:
## Why
Rotating inventory gives a reason to return to the bookshop after each expedition.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want the bookshop's non-staple shelves to change every few in-game days so that revisiting is worthwhile.
Rotation period in in-game days; rotating slots re-roll from pools excluding books the player already owns or knows (configurable); sold-out items restock only at rotation; state persists.

## Scope
- In: rotation scheduler, exclusion rules, persistence of current stock and last rotation
- Out: rare/unique books (e21-rare-stock)

## Notes
Rotation triggers on in-game time crossing the boundary, including while the player is away (lazy evaluation on shop open).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a rotation period of 3 days, when in-game time advances 3 days and the shop opens, then rotating slots re-roll exactly once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given in-game time advances 9 days while away, when the shop opens, then stock equals what 3 sequential rotations would produce (deterministic).
- AC-3 [unit] Given excludeKnown=true, when rotating, then no book teaching an already-known spell appears in rotating slots.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a pool smaller than the slot count after exclusions, when rotating, then remaining slots are filled with lore books or left empty — never duplicates.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a save mid-period, when reloaded, then stock and next rotation time are unchanged.

title: Generate bookshop stock from regional pools and school specialties
description:
## Why
Bookshops should be genuinely exciting destinations with different inventories per settlement (constitution §4).

## What
As a designer, I want to author a bookshop as data (region, specialties, pools, rules) on top of the generic shop system so that each settlement's bookshop feels distinct without code.
BookshopDefinition: shopId (E20), region, specialtySchools[] with weight multipliers, staplePool (always stocked), regionalPool, rarePool, secretPool, rotation rules, bookseller profile id. Stock generation is deterministic from world seed + shop id + rotation period.

## Scope
- In: bookshop schema, stock generator for staples/regional/specialty, integration with e20 shop buy/sell
- Out: rotation (e21-rotating-stock)
- Out: rare/secret (own beads)
- Out: Briar Glen shop content (world-content group, E24)

## Notes
The same book may appear in multiple regional pools; uniques are tracked globally so a unique book only ever exists once.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a bookshop with 3 staple books and a regional pool of 10, when stock is generated, then all 3 staples plus N regional books (per rule) are present.

title: Build the spell combination test suite and greybox spell gallery
description:
## Why
Emergent combinations are the point of magic; a suite proves they emerge from properties and catches regressions when E03 rules change.

## What
A generated integration test matrix: for every pair of stimulus types emitted by catalogue spells (heat, cold, force, light, moisture, charge, life, decay) applied in both orders to a fixture set of property-tagged generic objects and creatures, assert deterministic, rule-consistent outcomes (golden snapshots). Plus curated scenario tests (Wellspring → Arc Lash chain, Wellspring → Frostglass bridge, Gravity Well → Thunderclap scatter, Gust → Fire spread, Polymorph → Telekinetic Throw) expressed via properties. Plus a greybox "spell gallery" room exhibiting every property for e2e/manual play.

## Scope
- In: combination matrix generator, golden snapshots, curated scenario tests, greybox gallery scene, e2e smoke of the gallery
- Out: E03 rule changes (Core group) — the suite reports, it does not fix

## Notes
Golden updates require an explicit reviewed flag in the PR. Suite runs headless in < 60 s.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given every ordered pair of catalogue stimulus types and the fixture object set, when run, then outcomes match golden snapshots and two runs produce identical hashes.
- AC-2 [integration] Given Wellspring then Arc Lash on 3 creatures in the puddle, when resolved, then all receive charge damage (conduction through wet).
- AC-3 [integration] Given Wellspring then Frostglass on a pit filled with water, when resolved, then a walkable ice surface exists across the pit.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a new spell added to the catalogue emitting an unseen stimulus type, when the suite runs, then it fails listing the missing pair coverage.
- AC-5 [perf] Given the full suite, when run in CI, then it completes in ≤ 60 s.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox spell gallery, when a scripted run casts every P1 spell at its gallery station, then no console errors occur and each station reports its expected property change.
- AC-7 [manual] Given a 30-minute playtest in the gallery, when testers experiment freely, then they report at least 3 combinations nobody told them about.

Constitution example; force + gas-clearing gives a cheap, flexible physics verb.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a cone of wind that pushes creatures and loose objects and disperses gas and smoke so that I can shove foes off ledges or clear poison.
Cone force impulse scaled by weight; displaces gas volumes; fans existing fires (spreads heat downwind) and blows out small flames.

## Scope
- In: Gust spell
- In: spell JSON + book item JSON, unit tests for effects, integration tests for world interactions, placeholder cue ids
- Out: final VFX/SFX/icon/book cover (asset prompt beads)
- Out: world placement of the book (E24–E26)

## Notes
School: Storm. Placeholder cues: vfx-spell-gust-cone, sfx-spell-gust-whoosh. Icon: icon-spell-gust. Book cover: ui-book-cover-gust.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell data file, when validated and loaded, then it has a school, book item, vfxCue and sfxCue and casts in the headless sim.
- AC-2 [integration] Given loose objects of 5 kg and 80 kg in the cone, when Gust fires, then the 5 kg object is thrown ≥ 4 m and the 80 kg object moves ≤ 0.5 m.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a poisonous gas volume in the cone, when Gust fires, then the gas concentration in the cone drops by ≥ 80% and relocates downwind.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a small flame (candle-scale light source) in the cone, when Gust fires, then it is extinguished; a large fire instead spreads 1 m downwind.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a creature near a ledge, when pushed past the edge, then it falls and takes fall damage per creature rules.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a creature tagged anchored/heavy, when hit, then it staggers but is not displaced.

title: Add Wellspring: conjure a burst of water that soaks an area
description:
## Why
Conjured water is the connective tissue for combinations: douse fires, fill basins, soak foes for frost and lightning.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to conjure a splash of water at a point so that I can extinguish fires, make things wet and fill containers.
AoE moisture stimulus 3 m; creates a temporary puddle (`waterSurface`) for 15 s; fills container-tagged objects (basins, scales) with water weight.

## Scope
- In: Wellspring spell
- In: temporary puddle volume
- In: container fill via moisture
- In: spell JSON + book item JSON, unit tests for effects, integration tests for world interactions, placeholder cue ids
- Out: final VFX/SFX/icon/book cover (asset prompt beads)
- Out: world placement of the book (E24–E26)

## Notes
