- AC-2 [integration] Given telemetry disabled, when exported, then the bundle omits telemetry and the manifest says so.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the bundle manifest schema, when an exported bundle is parsed by the analysis tooling, then it validates.

title: Add an in-game feedback hotkey capturing context and a note
description:
## Why
Players' moments of delight or confusion are best captured in the moment, tied to where and when they happened.
## What
As a playtester, I want to press a key, type a quick note and tag it (bug / confusing / fun / idea) so that my feedback carries its context.
Captures screenshot, area, position, tick, recent 60 s of events (if enabled), optional bug bundle (e33-replay-bug-capture); stored locally and included in the playtest export.
## Scope
- In: Feedback overlay, local storage, inclusion in export
- Out: Uploading (e34-opt-in-upload)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the feedback key pressed, when the overlay opens, then the game pauses and resumes on close.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given a submitted note tagged "fun", when exported, then the bundle contains the note, tag, screenshot and area/tick.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a note longer than 2,000 characters, when submitted, then it is truncated with an indicator.

title: Capture uncaught errors locally for playtest bundles
description:
## Why
Playtesters rarely report console errors; capturing them locally makes crashes diagnosable without third-party services.
## What
Global `error`/`unhandledrejection` handlers record `{message, stack (sanitized of URLs query strings), buildSha, area, tick}` into a small local error log (always on, local only, max 200 entries) shown in the bug/feedback bundle and "View my data".
## Scope
- In: Handlers, sanitizer, local log
- Out: Remote error reporting services (not used)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a thrown error with a stack containing `?token=abc`, when sanitized, then query strings are stripped.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given an unhandled promise rejection, when it occurs, then an entry is logged and the game continues running.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 250 errors, when logged, then only the latest 200 are kept and repeated identical errors are counted rather than duplicated.

title: Emit core gameplay events: deaths, encounters, spells, puzzles
description:
## Why
E34 outcome names these signals explicitly: deaths, abandoned encounters, spell usage and puzzle completion.
## What
Instrument: `session_start/end` (class, build), `death` (cause type, killer content id, area, position bucketed to 2 m), `encounter_start/complete/abandon` (encounter id, duration, resolution: combat/stealth/social/avoid), `spell_cast` (spell id, target type, outcome tags), `puzzle_start/solve/abandon` (puzzle id, solution path id), `ability_used` (class verb id), `setting_changed` (difficulty/assist ids only), `item_acquired` (source: loot/shop/steal).
## Scope
- In: Event definitions + emit points in game glue listening to sim events
- In: Encounter/puzzle id conventions in content
- Out: Analysis (e34-analysis-scripts)
## Notes
- Emit from game layer listening to the sim event bus — never call telemetry from src/sim.
- Abandon = left encounter/puzzle volume for > 60 s without resolution (configurable).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the testbed with a scripted fight replay ending in player death, when run, then exactly one `death` event is recorded with cause, killer id and 2 m-bucketed position.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player leaves an encounter volume for 61 s unresolved, when evaluated, then `encounter_abandon` is emitted once; returning at 59 s emits nothing.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a puzzle solved via an alternative solution path, when emitted, then `puzzle_solve.solutionPath` identifies that path id.
- AC-4 [unit] Given telemetry disabled, when sim events fire, then emitters short-circuit without allocation-heavy work (≤ 0.01 ms per event measured).

title: Add opt-in telemetry consent, privacy notice and data controls
description:
## Why
Privacy-first: players must knowingly opt in, see exactly what is recorded, and delete it anytime.
## What
As a player, I want to choose whether gameplay statistics are recorded, see what is recorded and delete it so that I stay in control.
Off by default. First-launch (or playtest-mode) prompt explains local-first recording; settings toggle; "View my data" (event counts by type + sample), "Export", "Delete all". `docs/privacy.md` published with the site.
## Scope
- In: Consent prompt, settings controls, privacy doc
- Out: Upload consent (separate, e34-opt-in-upload)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a fresh profile, when the game starts, then telemetry is off until the player explicitly opts in.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given telemetry on with stored events, when "Delete all" is confirmed, then the store is empty and the counts show 0.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the player opts out after opting in, when playing further, then no new events are stored.
- AC-4 [manual] Given docs/privacy.md, when reviewed, then it lists every event type and field recorded and states nothing leaves the device without a separate explicit action.

title: Define local-first telemetry event schema, store and export
description:
## Why
Measuring deaths, abandonments and spell usage guides design — but this is a free game and players' privacy comes first.
## What
Add `src/game/telemetry`: a zod-typed event catalogue (`{type, v, sessionId (random per session), tick, simTimeMs, area, payload}`), a typed `emit()` API, a bounded local ring buffer in IndexedDB (max 50k events / 20 MB, oldest dropped), and export to NDJSON (gzip). No network code in this item. Events are only recorded if telemetry is enabled (e34-consent) except a small in-memory buffer used for bug reports.
## Scope
- In: Event catalogue, emitter, IndexedDB store, export, clear-all
- In: Schema rule: no free-text string fields except enumerated ids (enforced by schema test)
- Out: Consent UI (e34-consent)
- Out: Specific gameplay events (e34-gameplay-events)
- Out: Any upload (e34-opt-in-upload)
## Notes
- Session id is random, not derived from device; no user id, no IP, no fingerprinting data (UA only as coarse browser family + version).

**Integration note:** Moved to m2 — e04-skeleton-fun-validation (m2) consumes it.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an event missing a required payload field, when emitted, then it is dropped and a dev-only warning logged (never throws into gameplay).
- AC-2 [unit] Given the ring buffer at capacity, when a new event is stored, then the oldest is evicted and count stays at the cap.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the event catalogue, when a schema-lint test inspects it, then no event has an unconstrained free-text string field.
- AC-4 [integration] Given 1,000 stored events, when exported, then the NDJSON file has 1,000 valid lines that re-parse against the schema.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given telemetry disabled (default), when playing for 2 minutes, then nothing is written to the telemetry IndexedDB store and zero network requests carry telemetry.

title: Preview dialogue graphs and edit quest/world state in-game
description:
## Why
Branching quests with multiple resolutions are untestable by playing through every path manually.
## What
As a narrative designer, I want a dialogue previewer and a quest/world-fact editor so that I can test any branch instantly.
Dialogue previewer runs a dialogue graph standalone with editable condition inputs (disposition, facts, inventory). Quest panel lists quests, states, objectives; set state/fact via recorded debug commands. Graph lint: unreachable nodes, dead ends without exit.
## Scope
- In: Previewer panel, quest/fact panel, graph lint in content:check
- Out: Runtimes (e22-dialogue-runtime, e23-quest-runtime, e27-world-state-store)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a dialogue id, when opened in the previewer with disposition=friendly, then only nodes whose conditions pass are selectable.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a dialogue graph with an unreachable node, when linted, then content:check reports the node id.
- AC-3 [integration] Given `quest set <id> <state>`, when executed, then dependent world facts update and the change is recorded in the replay.

title: Create a creature arena to spawn and pit creatures
description:
## Why
Creatures are creatures, not target dummies; their behaviours and relationships need a place to be observed.
## What
As a designer, I want an arena where I can spawn any creature with chosen disposition/faction and watch interactions so that I can tune behaviours.
Scene `sandbox-creatures`, commands `spawn <creature> --faction --disposition`, `ai freeze/unfreeze`, `faction set`.
## Scope
- In: Arena scene, commands
- Out: AI implementation (mw-e11/mw-e12)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the arena, when `spawn goblin-grunt --disposition hostile` and `spawn wolf --disposition neutral` run, then both spawn with those dispositions visible in the inspector.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `ai freeze`, when ticks advance, then frozen creatures' AI systems do not update while physics still does.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature id with invalid disposition, when spawned, then validation fails with allowed values listed.

title: Create a spell sandbox scene with live parameter tuning
description:
## Why
Magic must feel magical; designers need a playground to cast every spell against every material and creature.
## What
As a designer, I want a sandbox with material stations (water, oil, wood, rope, metal) and dummies where I can cast any spell and tweak its parameters live so that I can find surprising combinations.
Scene `sandbox-spells`, console `learnall`, `cast <spellId>`, parameter panel bound to hot-reloadable spell data.
## Scope
- In: Sandbox scene, commands, parameter panel
- Out: Spell content (mw-e08)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given `?scene=sandbox-spells` and `learnall`, when opened, then every spell in content is castable from a list.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given a spell's radius changed in the panel, when cast again, then the new radius applies without reload.
- AC-3 [content] Given the sandbox scene, when validated, then it contains at least one entity for every property tag defined in e03-world-properties.

title: Visualize light levels, element propagation and trigger volumes
description:
## Why
The systemic world (fire, water, light, triggers) is invisible data until visualized; debugging emergent interactions depends on it.
## What
As a designer, I want heatmap overlays for light level, temperature/fire, wetness/electricity and trigger volume outlines so that I can see why systemic interactions do or do not happen.
Grid-sampled overlays from sim queries; property-tag filter ("show all flammable").
## Scope
- In: Light field heatmap, element overlays, trigger volume wireframes, property filter
- Out: The systems themselves (mw-e03)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the light overlay in a room with one torch, when shown, then sampled values decrease with distance from the torch.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the property filter `flammable`, when enabled, then exactly the entities with that tag are highlighted.
- AC-3 [integration] Given overlays on vs off, when the same replay runs, then state hashes are identical.

title: Visualize perception cones, alert states and noise events
description:
## Why
Stealth that feels fair requires designers to see exactly what creatures perceive and why.
## What
As a designer, I want overlays for sight cones, hearing radii, current alert state, last-known-position markers, search paths and noise events so that I can tune stealth encounters.
Overlay toggles per category; reads sim data only (no sim changes).
## Scope
- In: Overlay renderer for AI/perception data, toggles via console
- Out: AI logic (mw-e11)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a guard in the testbed with the overlay on, when the player is in the sight cone, then the cone renders and the guard's alert label changes as the state progresses.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given a noise event, when emitted, then an expanding ring shows its propagated radius for 1 s.
- AC-3 [integration] Given overlays toggled on vs off, when the same replay runs, then sim state hashes are identical (overlay is read-only).

title: Capture a reproducible bug report with one keypress
description:
## Why
Emergent systems create hard-to-reproduce bugs; a deterministic replay of the last minutes turns "it happened once" into a failing test.
## What
As a developer or playtester, I want to press F9-dev (configurable) to save a bug bundle so that the exact situation can be replayed.
The game continuously keeps a rolling buffer: a save snapshot every 60 s plus input commands since. Capture writes `bug-<timestamp>.mwbug` (snapshot + inputs + build SHA + content hash + settings + recent console/errors + screenshot + optional note). `?bug=<file>` or drag-drop loads and replays it; `pnpm bug:test <file>` converts it into a golden replay test.
## Scope
- In: Rolling buffer, bundle format (zod), loader, conversion to test
- Out: Telemetry export bundles (e34-playtest-export) — reuse format pieces
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given 3 minutes of play then capture, when the bundle is replayed on a fresh load of the same build, then the final state hash equals the captured final hash.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a bundle from a different build SHA, when loaded, then the user is warned that replay may diverge and divergence is reported at the first checkpoint mismatch.
- AC-3 [perf] Given the rolling buffer active, when measured in the testbed, then added cost is ≤ 0.2 ms per frame and memory ≤ 20 MB.
- AC-4 [integration] Given `pnpm bug:test`, when run on a bundle, then a replay test file is generated that passes.

title: Hot-reload content JSON into the running game
description:
## Why
Tuning spells and creatures by editing JSON and seeing the change in under a second is the core of fast content iteration.
## What
As a designer, I want edits to content files to apply to the running game without restart so that tuning is instant.
Vite HMR for `content/**` → re-validate the changed file → swap catalogue entry → notify systems (`content.on("changed", id)`) which refresh live instances where safe (e.g. spell damage, creature speed); invalid edits keep the old version and show an overlay error.
## Scope
- In: HMR handler, catalogue swap, change notifications, error overlay
- Out: Production (dev only)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the dev server and testbed running, when a testprop JSON field is edited, then the change is visible in-game within 1 s without page reload.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given an edit introducing a schema error, when saved, then an overlay shows the error with file and path and the game keeps running on the previous valid data.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a hot-swapped entry, when the content hash is recomputed, then it changes and the replay recorder marks the recording as content-modified.

title: Scaffold new content entries with a test stub via CLI
description:
## Why
Every content entry must have a test (contract §3); scaffolding makes the right thing the easy thing.
## What
`pnpm new <type> <id>` creates `content/<type>/<id>.json` from a per-type template (valid defaults) and a test stub `test/content/<type>/<id>.test.ts` that exercises the entry via `describeContent`; refuses duplicate ids; validates id format (kebab-case).
## Scope
- In: CLI, per-type templates registered alongside schemas
- Out: GUI editors (not planned for MVP)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given `pnpm new testprop lantern`, when run, then the JSON and test stub are created, `pnpm content:check` passes and the new test runs green.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an id that already exists, when run, then it exits non-zero without overwriting.
- AC-3 [unit] Given id `Big Lantern`, when run, then it rejects with a kebab-case suggestion `big-lantern`.

title: Add `pnpm content:check` validator with cross-reference report
description:
## Why
Designers need fast, readable validation of all content before committing; CI needs the same check.
## What
CLI wrapping the content pipeline: validates all content types, cross-references (loot tables → items, spawns → creatures, dialogue → quests), orphan detection (defined but never referenced), string-table key existence; human-readable output with file:line, `--json` for CI annotations; runs in CI job `content`.
## Scope
- In: CLI, CI job, GitHub annotation formatter
- Out: Schemas themselves (owned by respective epics)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given all committed content, when `pnpm content:check` runs, then it exits 0 in ≤ 10 s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a loot table referencing a missing item, when checked, then it exits non-zero printing the file, JSON path and missing id.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an item defined but never referenced by any loot table, shop or placement, when checked with `--orphans`, then it is listed as a warning (not an error).
- AC-4 [integration] Given `--json`, when run in CI with an error, then a GitHub annotation appears on the offending file.

title: Inspect and edit entity components live
description:
## Why
Systemic bugs ("why didn't the rope burn?") are solved by seeing the properties involved.
## What
As a developer, I want to click an entity and see/edit its components live so that I can debug systemic interactions.
Pick via raycast (or list/search), panel showing components with schema-driven editors (number, bool, enum, vector), edits applied through a `debug.setComponent` sim command (recorded), highlight selected entity.
## Scope
- In: Picker, inspector panel, edit command
- Out: World overlays (e33-world-overlays)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the testbed, when a crate is clicked in inspect mode, then its components (e.g. Position, Physics) are listed with current values updating live.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an edit setting a numeric field to a string, when applied, then schema validation rejects it and the sim is unchanged.
- AC-3 [integration] Given an edit to `flammable=true`, when recorded and replayed, then the replay reproduces the edited state.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the selected entity is destroyed, when the next frame renders, then the panel shows "entity destroyed" instead of throwing.

title: Pause, slow-motion and frame-step the simulation
description:
## Why
Tuning parry windows and debugging propagation needs time slowed or stepped one tick at a time.
## What
As a developer, I want to pause, change timescale (0.1×–4×) and step single ticks so that I can inspect fast interactions.
Implemented in the game loop (sim steps at fixed dt; timescale changes how many steps per real second), so determinism is preserved.
## Scope
- In: Loop timescale, pause, step; console commands and hotkeys (dev)
- Out: Replay scrubbing (possible follow-up)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given timescale 0.5, when 1 real second passes at 60 Hz, then 30 sim steps occur.
- AC-2 [unit] Given paused, when "step" is invoked 3 times, then exactly 3 ticks advance.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a session played at mixed timescales and recorded, when replayed at 1×, then the final state hash matches.

title: Run and record a full perf pass on reference and low-tier machines
description:
## Why
Absolute frame-time budgets cannot run on GPU-less CI; a documented manual pass before playtests closes the loop.
## What
Write `docs/perf/runbook.md` (machine prep, browser versions, `pnpm perf:ref` steps) and execute it on the reference machine and a low-tier machine across Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari; commit results to `perf/results/`; file beads for any budget misses.
## Scope
- In: Runbook doc, committed results, beads for misses
- Out: Fixes (separate beads)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the runbook, when executed on the reference machine in all 4 browsers, then results files are committed with browser/OS versions.
- AC-2 [perf] Given the results, when compared to the baseline, then every budget passes or has a filed bead with owner and priority.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the low-tier machine run, when complete, then Low preset results are recorded for `perf-baseline` and `perf-combat`.

title: Add combat stress scene with 12 creatures and heavy VFX
description:
## Why
The worst case — a chaotic fight with spells flying — is what players remember; budgets must be measured there.
## What
Scene `perf-combat` in the greybox kit: 12 active creatures in combat AI, 4 simultaneous spell effects, 30 physics props, fire propagation active, 8 dynamic lights. Scripted deterministic camera path and input replay so measurements are repeatable. Added to both perf modes.
## Scope
- In: Scene data, scripted replay, perf-budgets.json entries
- Out: Creature content (mw-e13)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given `perf-combat` on the reference machine (High), when measured over 1,800 frames, then p95 frame time ≤ 16.7 ms.
- AC-2 [perf] Given `perf-combat` on Low at 1080p on the low-tier class machine, when measured, then worst-case frames stay ≥ 30 fps (p99 ≤ 33.3 ms).
- AC-3 [unit] Given the scripted replay, when run twice, then sim state hashes match (repeatable measurement).

title: Detect memory leaks across repeated scene loads
description:
## Why
Area transitions and reloads after death repeat hundreds of times per session; leaks compound into crashes.
## What
Playwright test (Chromium, CDP heap) loads/unloads testbed scenes and save/load cycles 20 times, forcing GC, and asserts heap growth and GPU resource counts stay bounded.
## Scope
- In: Leak test spec, renderer resource counters
- Out: Fixing specific leaks (bug beads)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given 20 scene load/unload cycles, when heap is sampled after forced GC, then growth from cycle 2 to cycle 20 ≤ 5%.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given 20 save/load cycles, when renderer geometry/texture counts are read, then they return to the cycle-2 value (±2).
- AC-3 [integration] Given a deliberately leaking fixture, when the test runs, then it fails (test proves it can detect leaks).

title: Show a dev perf HUD with frame graph, draw calls and heap
description:
## Why
Developers need to see performance cost while building content, not after CI complains.
## What
As a developer, I want an overlay showing fps, frame-time graph (last 240 frames), sim tick ms, draw calls, triangles, textures/geometries count and JS heap so that I can spot regressions immediately.
Toggle via debug console or F3; dev builds only.
## Scope
- In: Overlay, renderer stats adapter
- Out: Automated budgets (e32-perf-budgets)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a dev build, when F3 is pressed, then the HUD shows fps, frame-time graph, sim ms, draw calls and heap values that update each frame.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a production build, when F3 is pressed, then nothing happens and HUD code is absent from the bundle.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `performance.memory` is unavailable (Firefox/Safari), when the HUD renders, then heap shows "n/a" without errors.

title: Eliminate frame hitches from GC, shader compilation and long tasks
description:
## Why
Stable frame pacing matters more than average fps for combat feel (parry timing).
## What
Detect and fix hitch sources: shader/pipeline pre-warm during loading, object pooling for projectiles/particles/events on hot paths, long-task detection in dev overlay, allocation audit of the sim tick (target near-zero allocations per tick).
## Scope
- In: Shader pre-warm, pools, allocation test for sim tick
- Out: Perf HUD (e32-perf-hud)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the combat stress scene for 60 s on the reference machine, when measured, then frames > 33 ms number ≤ 3 and none > 50 ms after warm-up.
- AC-2 [unit] Given 1,000 steady-state sim ticks, when heap allocations are measured in Node (`--expose-gc` heap delta), then growth ≤ 64 KB.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the first cast of each VFX type after loading, when measured, then no frame exceeds 33 ms (pre-warm effective).

title: Cache hashed assets for warm reload ≤ 3 s
description:
## Why
Warm reload ≤ 3 s keeps the death/retry and playtest loops snappy.
## What
Immutable caching for content-hashed assets (Pages headers are limited, so add a service worker with cache-first for hashed URLs and network-first for index.html); versioned cache names with cleanup of old versions on activate; opt-out via `?nosw`.
## Scope
- In: Service worker (Workbox or hand-rolled), update flow ("new version available — reload")
- Out: Offline play guarantee (nice side effect, not a goal)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given a previously loaded build, when the page is reloaded, then load to playable ≤ 3 s on the reference machine.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given a new deployment, when the page loads, then the old cache version is deleted after activation and a "new version available" prompt appears.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given `?nosw`, when loaded, then no service worker is registered and existing ones are unregistered.

title: Stream and compress assets with a progress-reporting loader
description:
## Why
Load to playable ≤ 10 s requires compressed assets and loading only what the current area needs.
## What
Asset manifest generated at build (id → hashed URL, size, area tags); area-based preloading with priority; texture compression (KTX2/Basis), mesh compression (meshopt or Draco per ADR), audio as Opus/AAC with fallback; loading screen showing real progress; failed-fetch retry with backoff.
## Scope
- In: Manifest build step, loader with priorities/retries, compression tooling scripts
- In: Loading screen progress
- Out: Service-worker/HTTP caching (e32-asset-caching)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given a cold load at 50 Mbps throttling in CI mode, when Briar-Glen-equivalent testbed area loads, then playable ≤ 10 s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a fetch failing twice then succeeding, when loading, then the loader retries with backoff and completes; after 3 failures it surfaces a retry UI.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the manifest, when an asset id is missing, then a typed error names the id at build time (build fails).
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the loading screen, when assets load, then the progress bar increases monotonically from 0 to 100%.

title: Implement Low/High graphics presets and dynamic resolution
description:
## Why
The baseline defines two presets; they must actually hit 60 fps on their target hardware.
## What
As a player, I want Low/High presets plus individual toggles and optional dynamic resolution so that the game runs smoothly on my machine.
Preset controls render scale, shadow resolution/cascades, max dynamic lights, post-processing, particle density, LOD bias, draw distance. Dynamic resolution adjusts render scale between 50–100% to hold a frame-time target, with hysteresis.
## Scope
- In: Preset table, settings UI section, dynamic resolution controller (pure logic unit-tested)
- Out: Asset LODs creation (art epics)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given frame times consistently 20 ms with target 16.7 ms, when the controller updates, then render scale steps down by ≤ 10% per second and never below 50%.
- AC-2 [unit] Given frame times oscillating around target ±0.5 ms, when the controller runs, then scale changes at most once per 2 s (hysteresis).
- AC-3 [perf] Given the combat stress scene on Low at 1080p on an Iris Xe / base M1 class machine, when measured, then p50 ≥ 60 fps and p95 frame time ≤ 33.3 ms.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given a preset switch at runtime, when applied, then it takes effect within 1 s without reload or console errors.

title: Detect GPU/browser capabilities and pick a safe default preset
description:
## Why
First impressions matter: a low-end laptop should start on Low, and unsupported browsers need a clear message.
## What
On boot detect WebGL2 (and WebGPU if the ADR uses it), WASM + SIMD, max texture size, `deviceMemory`, `hardwareConcurrency`, renderer string (where exposed); choose default preset (High/Low) on first launch; show an unsupported screen listing what is missing; log capabilities to local telemetry.
## Scope
- In: Capability probe, preset heuristic table, unsupported screen
- Out: Dynamic resolution at runtime (e32-quality-presets)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given capabilities {deviceMemory: 4, renderer contains "Intel"}, when the heuristic runs, then Low is chosen; given an Apple M1 Pro renderer string, then High.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given WebGL2 unavailable (init-script override), when loaded, then the unsupported screen names WebGL2 and links to browser help.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the renderer string is masked/unavailable, when the heuristic runs, then it falls back to deviceMemory/cores and never throws.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player has already chosen a preset, when the game boots again, then detection does not override it.

title: Run smoke suite on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in CI
description:
## Why
Target browsers are current Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari; engine-specific breakage must be caught before players see it.
## What
Playwright projects for chromium, firefox, webkit running the boot + testbed smoke specs in CI (chromium required per-PR; firefox/webkit required on main and nightly, optional per-PR label `full-matrix`). Known-difference allowlist per browser with bead references.
## Scope
- In: Playwright project matrix, CI job(s), docs of manual Edge/Safari checks
- Out: Mobile browsers (mw-e36)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the smoke suite, when run on chromium, firefox and webkit, then the testbed boots with zero console errors on all three.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a nightly run failing on webkit only, when complete, then a GitHub issue is opened/updated with the failing spec and trace artifact.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a known-difference allowlist entry without a bead id, when validated, then CI fails.

title: Enforce JS bundle and asset size budgets per PR
description:
## Why
Initial download ≤ 50 MB and load ≤ 10 s are easiest to protect byte by byte at PR time.
## What
size-limit (or custom script) over `dist/`: initial JS ≤ 1.5 MB gz, total initial payload ≤ 50 MB, per-asset caps by type (texture ≤ 4 MB, audio loop ≤ 3 MB). PR comment/job summary shows delta vs main; dev tools must not appear in the production bundle.
## Scope
- In: Size budget config + check job
- In: Assertion that `src/tools/**` modules are absent from prod chunks
- Out: Asset compression pipeline (e32-asset-loading)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a PR increasing initial JS beyond 1.5 MB gz, when CI runs, then the size check fails showing the delta.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a production build, when chunk contents are inspected, then no module from `src/tools/` is present.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a single texture of 6 MB added, when checked, then it fails naming the file and the 4 MB cap.

title: Benchmark sim tick cost in CI with regression alerts
description:
## Why
The sim runs every tick regardless of GPU; its cost is measurable headlessly and must stay well inside the frame budget.
## What
`vitest bench` suites for representative sim loads (500 entities with propagation, 30 AI agents perceiving, 200 physics props) with a budget: mean tick ≤ 4 ms in Node on CI hardware. CI compares against main baseline artifact and fails on > 25% regression.
## Scope
- In: Bench suites, baseline artifact, comparison script
- Out: Frame-time budgets (e32-perf-budgets)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the "full-load" bench, when run in CI, then mean tick ≤ 4 ms and p99 ≤ 8 ms.
- AC-2 [unit] Given baseline 2.0 ms and PR 2.6 ms, when compared, then the check fails (30% > 25%); at 2.4 ms it passes.
- AC-3 [unit] Given no baseline available, when compared, then it records a new baseline and passes with a warning.

title: Audit MVP against Game Accessibility Guidelines basic tier
description:
## Why
Individual features do not guarantee an accessible whole; an audit before external playtests catches gaps.
## What
Walk through every GAG "basic" guideline (motor, cognitive, vision, hearing, speech, general) against the MVP build; record pass/fail/N-A with evidence in `docs/accessibility/audit-<date>.md`; file beads for each failure.
## Scope
- In: Audit doc, beads for findings
- Out: Fixing findings (separate beads)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the MVP build, when every GAG basic guideline is assessed, then the audit doc records a status and evidence for each.
- AC-2 [manual] Given any failing guideline, when the audit completes, then a bead exists for it with priority and a link from the audit doc.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the audit, when complete, then zero failures are left without a decision (fix, defer with reason, or N/A).

title: Make every menu keyboard- and gamepad-operable with visible focus
description:
## Why
Menus that require a mouse block keyboard-only and gamepad players, and screen readers need labelled controls.
## What
As a player, I want to navigate all menus with keyboard or gamepad and see where focus is so that I never need a mouse.
Shared focus manager (spatial navigation), visible focus ring meeting 3:1 contrast, Esc/B back, ARIA labels/roles on DOM menus, axe-core checks in Playwright.
## Scope
- In: Focus manager, gamepad UI navigation, ARIA roles
- In: Playwright axe scan of each menu screen
- Out: In-game HUD screen reader support (post-MVP)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given each menu screen, when traversed with Tab/arrow keys only, then every interactive element is reachable and focus is always visible.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given each menu screen, when axe-core runs, then there are zero serious or critical violations.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given an emulated gamepad, when D-pad/A/B are used, then the same navigation works and B always returns to the previous screen.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given a modal dialog open, when Tab reaches its last control, then focus wraps inside the modal (focus trap).

title: Provide difficulty presets and granular assists read by the sim
description:
## Why
Souls-like weight should not mean exclusion; granular assists let players keep the fantasy while tuning the challenge.
## What
As a player, I want difficulty presets and individual assists so that combat and stealth challenge suit me.
A sim-side `DifficultyConfig` (injected, part of save metadata): damage taken multiplier, parry/dodge timing window multiplier, enemy detection speed multiplier, stealth last-known-position search duration, puzzle hint availability, fall damage on/off. Presets Story/Adventurer/Veteran map to values; custom allowed. Changing mid-game allowed and recorded in local telemetry.
## Scope
- In: DifficultyConfig schema + injection into World
- In: Settings UI section
- In: Sim helper `difficulty.scale("damageTaken", x)` for systems to use
- Out: Systems applying the multipliers (each combat/stealth bead reads the config)
## Notes
- Related: e04 and e09 systems must read these multipliers; integration pass should add ACs there.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given preset Story, when resolved, then damageTaken=0.5, parryWindow=1.5, detectionSpeed=0.6 per the documented table.
- AC-2 [unit] Given damageTaken multiplier 0.5, when a 20-damage hit is scaled, then 10 damage results (integer rounding rule documented and tested).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a config value outside allowed bounds (e.g. parryWindow 10), when injected, then it is rejected by schema validation.
- AC-4 [unit] Given difficulty changed mid-session, when saved and reloaded, then the new config is restored and the change event was emitted once.
- AC-5 [integration] Given two replays identical except difficulty preset, when run, then state hashes differ (config is an input) and each replays deterministically.

title: Add per-bus volume sliders and mono audio
description:
## Why
Players must balance music against gameplay-critical sound; single-sided hearing requires mono.
## What
As a player, I want master/music/SFX/UI/ambience volume sliders and a mono toggle so that I can hear what matters.
Sliders map to audio engine buses (perceptual/log curve); mono downmix; mute when tab unfocused (optional).
## Scope
- In: Settings wired to e28 bus API
- Out: Mixer implementation (e28-audio-engine)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given music slider at 0, when the music bus gain is read, then it is 0 (silent) and SFX unaffected.
- AC-2 [unit] Given slider value 50%, when mapped, then gain follows the documented perceptual curve (≈ −10 dB ±1).
- AC-3 [integration] Given mono enabled, when a sound positioned hard left plays, then both output channels carry equal signal.

title: Ensure no gameplay information relies on colour alone
description:
## Why
Stealth awareness states, damage types and puzzle cues must be readable by colour-blind players (~8% of men).
## What
As a player, I want gameplay cues distinguishable without colour so that colour-blindness does not block me.
Audit and fix HUD/indicators to pair colour with shape/icon/pattern (alert states, element types, interactables), plus optional palette presets (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia) for UI indicator colours.
## Scope
- In: UI indicator palette tokens + presets
- In: Design rule in docs/art/style-bible.md cross-reference
- Out: Full-screen colour filters (not planned; they degrade art)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given each awareness state indicator (Unaware→Combat), when rendered, then each has a distinct icon/shape independent of colour.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given each palette preset, when the HUD test page renders all indicators, then adjacent indicator colours differ by a contrast ratio ≥ 3:1 under simulated deficiency.
- AC-3 [manual] Given a colour-blind tester or simulator run through the testbed, when playing a stealth encounter, then all state changes are identified correctly.

title: Add motion comfort and photosensitivity safeguards
description:
## Why
Spectacular magic (constitution: magic should feel magical) must not trigger motion sickness or photosensitive seizures.
## What
As a player, I want to reduce camera shake, motion blur, head bob and flashes so that the game is comfortable and safe.
Settings: camera shake 0–100%, motion blur off, reduce flashing (caps full-screen luminance change frequency to ≤ 3 flashes/s and limits intensity), reduce screen effects (vignette/chromatic aberration). Honour `prefers-reduced-motion` as initial default.
## Scope
- In: Settings + a global "flash limiter" utility VFX must route through
- In: Default from prefers-reduced-motion
- Out: VFX system (e29-vfx-framework)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given reduce-flashing on, when VFX request 10 full-screen flashes within 1 s, then the limiter lets at most 3 through with intensity capped.
- AC-2 [unit] Given camera shake at 0%, when an impact requests shake, then camera offset remains zero.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulated on first launch, when settings initialise, then shake defaults to 0% and reduce-flashing to on.
- AC-4 [manual] Given the spell/VFX showcase with reduce-flashing on, when reviewed against the Harding test guidance, then no sequence exceeds the flash threshold.

title: Add camera sensitivity, invert, FOV and auto-centre options
description:
## Why
Camera discomfort drives players away from third-person action games; control over it is basic comfort.
## What
As a player, I want to adjust camera sensitivity, inversion, FOV, distance and auto-centering so that the camera feels right to me.
Settings: mouse and stick sensitivity (separate X/Y), invert X/Y, FOV 60–100°, camera distance, auto-recentre on/off, lock-on switch sensitivity.
## Scope
- In: Settings wired to camera parameters via subscriptions
- Out: Camera implementation (e02-camera)
- Out: Shake/motion (e31-motion-comfort)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given invert Y enabled, when mouse moves up by 100 px, then camera pitch changes in the opposite direction to the default.
- AC-2 [unit] Given FOV set to 120 via storage tampering, when loaded, then it clamps to 100.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given sensitivity changed in the options menu, when returning to play, then the new sensitivity applies without reload.

title: Caption gameplay-critical sounds with direction indicators
description:
## Why
Stealth and combat depend on sound (footsteps, alerts, creature cues); deaf and hard-of-hearing players need that information visually.
## What
As a player, I want captions for important sounds with direction so that I can react to threats I cannot hear.
Sound events tagged `caption` (content data: text key, priority) display as short captions with an on-screen direction arrow relative to the camera; stacking/merging rules; size/background from text settings; toggle on/off.
## Scope
- In: Caption event pipeline from audio/sim noise events
- In: Direction indicator
- In: Content field `caption` on sound definitions
- Out: Audio engine (e28-audio-engine)
- Out: Noise event model (e09-sound-propagation)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a captioned noise event 90° to the player's right, when displayed, then the indicator points right (±15°).
- AC-2 [unit] Given 5 identical "footsteps" events within 2 s, when displayed, then they merge into one caption with a refreshed timer rather than 5 lines.
- AC-3 [unit] Given more than 4 simultaneous captions, when displayed, then the lowest-priority captions are dropped first.
- AC-4 [content] Given every sound definition flagged gameplay-critical, when validated, then it has a caption text key that exists in the strings table.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given captions enabled in the testbed, when a scripted guard alert sound plays, then its caption appears within 100 ms.

title: Scale UI text 80–200% with readable defaults
description:
## Why
Books are central to the sorcerer fantasy and dialogue is text-only; unreadable text excludes players.
## What
As a player, I want to scale UI and book/dialogue text so that I can read comfortably at my screen distance.
Global UI scale and separate text size (80–200%), minimum default body size 18 px at 1080p, optional dyslexia-friendly font toggle, text background opacity for subtitles/dialogue.
## Scope
- In: CSS variable-driven scaling (or engine UI equivalent)
- In: Layout reflow at 200% without clipping
- Out: Captions content (e31-captions)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given text size 200%, when the dialogue, book reader and inventory screens are opened at 1280×720, then no text is clipped (Playwright overflow check on text nodes).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a stored value of 350%, when loaded, then it is clamped to 200%.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the dyslexia-friendly font toggled, when menus render, then the font family changes without reload.
- AC-4 [manual] Given default settings at 1080p on the reference machine, when a tester reads dialogue from 70 cm, then it is legible (body text ≥ 18 px).

title: Offer hold vs toggle for sprint, crouch, block and aim
description:
## Why
Sustained key holds are a common motor-accessibility barrier; stealth and knight play involve long holds.
## What
As a player, I want to choose hold or toggle for sustained actions so that I do not need to keep keys pressed.
Per-action setting for sprint, crouch/sneak, block, aim/draw; toggle mode auto-releases on context change (e.g. entering dialogue).
## Scope
- In: Setting + input-layer adapter that converts toggle into a held state
- Out: Action definitions (e02-input-actions)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given crouch in toggle mode, when the key is pressed and released once, then the crouch command stays active until pressed again.
- AC-2 [unit] Given block toggled on, when dialogue opens, then block is released and does not resume after dialogue.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the setting changed mid-hold, when applied, then the action state resets to released without getting stuck.

title: Let players remap keyboard, mouse and gamepad bindings
description:
## Why
Remapping is the single most-requested accessibility feature and a baseline expectation for PC action games.
## What
As a player, I want to rebind every action for keyboard/mouse and gamepad so that controls fit my hands and hardware.
Bindings screen lists actions from the action map with primary/secondary bindings per device; "press a key" capture with Esc to cancel; conflict detection with swap/replace prompt; reset per action and all; bindings persisted in settings.
## Scope
- In: Bindings UI over e02-input-actions API
- In: Conflict detection within the same context (e.g. exploration vs menu)
- Out: The action map itself (e02-input-actions)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given "Dodge" bound to Space, when rebound to Shift, then pressing Shift in the testbed triggers dodge and Space no longer does.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a new binding that conflicts with another action in the same context, when applied, then the user is prompted to swap or cancel and no silent duplicate exists.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an attempt to unbind the last binding for a required action (Pause/Menu), when applied, then it is refused with an explanation.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given capture mode, when Esc is pressed, then capture cancels without binding Esc.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given remapped bindings, when the page reloads, then bindings persist.

title: Recover from corrupt saves using backups and clear messaging
description:
## Why
Nothing kills goodwill faster than a lost 10-hour save; recovery must be automatic and honest.
## What
As a player, I want the game to fall back to a backup when a save is damaged so that I never lose everything.
On `SaveCorruptError`/migration failure: try the slot's backup blob, then the next most recent save; show what was restored and its age; offer to export the corrupt file for a bug report.
## Scope
- In: Recovery chain, messaging, corrupt-file export
- Out: General export/import (e30-export-import)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a slot whose primary blob fails checksum and whose backup is valid, when loaded, then the backup loads and the UI states "restored backup from <time>".
- AC-2 [integration] Given primary and backup both corrupt, when loaded, then the next most recent valid save across slots is offered.
- AC-3 [integration] Given all saves corrupt, when loading, then the player can start a new game and export the corrupt files; the game does not crash.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a migration that throws, when loading, then it is treated like corruption (recovery chain) and the error is logged to local telemetry.

title: Write CONTRIBUTING.md covering worktrees, beads, DoD and ADRs
description:
## Why
Humans and agents both contribute; one short guide prevents process drift (wrong branch, missing Closes lines, unsigned commits).
## What
Document: worktree-per-branch flow, bead lifecycle (claim → PR with Closes lines → close after merge), commit sign-off (DCO), squash-merge, DoD, coverage layers and how to request an exclusion, determinism rules for src/sim, ADR process (docs/adr), CHANGELOG convention, how to regenerate backlog.html locally. Add a DCO check job if sign-off is required.
## Scope
- In: CONTRIBUTING.md, link from README and AGENTS.md
- In: DCO check (GitHub DCO app or action) as a required check
- Out: Code of conduct / licence choice (separate decision if needed)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given a new contributor following only CONTRIBUTING.md, when they make a trivial change, then they produce a PR with a Closes line, signed-off commit and green CI without further guidance.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a PR with an unsigned commit, when CI runs, then the DCO check fails.
- AC-3 [integration] Given markdown link checking, when CI runs on docs changes, then CONTRIBUTING.md has no broken relative links.

title: Create CHANGELOG.md and a check for user-facing changes
description:
## Why
DoD item 8: players and testers need to know what changed between playtest builds.
## What
Add `CHANGELOG.md` (Keep a Changelog format, `Unreleased` section). Add a lightweight CI check: if a PR touches `src/{game,ui,render,audio,sim,content}/**` and has neither a CHANGELOG diff nor the `no-changelog` label, fail with guidance.
## Scope
- In: CHANGELOG.md
- In: changelog check job/script
- Out: Release tagging automation (later, if needed)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a PR modifying `src/sim/foo.ts` without touching CHANGELOG.md or labelling `no-changelog`, when CI runs, then the changelog check fails.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a PR touching only `docs/**` or `.github/**`, when CI runs, then the check passes without a CHANGELOG entry.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a CHANGELOG with no `## [Unreleased]` heading, when the check parses it, then it fails.

title: Track object ownership and record thefts as world facts
description:
## Why
"Treasures stolen" must persist, and a thief's actions should have consequences (shopkeepers notice missing stock) — without a full crime system in this epic.
## What
As a thief, I want stolen goods to be tracked as stolen so that fences, witnesses and owners can react later.

Owner tag property on items/containers/areas (owner faction or NPC id); taking an owned item without permission sets a stolen flag on the item instance and a theft fact (owner, item, location, witnessed=unknown until AI resolves). Returning or buying clears it.
## Scope
- In: Ownership property on items/containers, permission predicate
- In: Stolen item flag + theft facts; clearing rules
- In: Event for witness resolution by AI
- Out: Witness detection and crime reactions — see mw-e11 / mw-e10
- Out: Fences and prices — see e20-shop-system
## Notes
Related: e17-inventory-core stores item instance flags.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an item owned by NPC Mirela and no permission, when the player takes it, then the item instance is flagged stolen and a theft fact with owner Mirela is recorded.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player buys the item or is gifted it, when transferred, then no stolen flag is set.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a stolen item returned into its owner container, when placed, then the stolen flag clears and theft fact resolves to returned.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unowned item (owner none), when taken, then no theft fact is recorded (edge).
- AC-5 [integration] Given a theft then save/reload, when inspected, then the stolen flag and theft fact persist.

title: Spawn fact-gated entity variants so the world reacts to choices
description:
## Why
Helping the miller should put him back in his mill; befriending the minotaur should change the labyrinth. The world visibly reacting is what makes actions feel meaningful.
## What
As a designer, I want to mark level entities as present/absent or swapped based on world conditions so that the world changes after player choices without scripting.

Level entities may declare spawnIf/despawnIf conditions (e27-fact-queries) and variant groups (exactly one variant active, chosen by first matching condition). Evaluated on level load and on condition change when not in player view (no pop-in within camera frustum unless flagged).
## Scope
- In: spawnIf/despawnIf + variant groups in level schema
- In: Evaluation on load + deferred out-of-view swaps
- In: Interaction with deltas (a despawned entity keeps its delta)
- Out: NPC schedules — see mw-e22 / mw-e14
## Notes
Example: boarded-up door variant appears after "cellar.sealed_by_guard"; the thief can still break the boards (they are breakable).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an entity with spawnIf(fact(miller.rescued)), when the fact becomes true while the entity location is out of view, then it spawns; if in view, it waits until out of view.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a variant group of three with conditions, when multiple conditions match, then the first listed wins deterministically.
- AC-3 [content] Given a variant group where no variant has a default/fallback, when validated, then a warning lists the uncovered case.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a despawned entity with deltas, when it respawns later, then its deltas are re-applied (edge).
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox slice, when a fact flips, then the corresponding variant is active after save/reload.

title: Apply permanent, rest-reset and transient persistence policies
description:
## Why
Not everything should persist forever: fires burn out, ice melts, respawning herbs regrow, enemy camps may restock. Policies keep the world believable and saves small.
## What
As a designer, I want to choose whether a change is permanent, resets on rest/time, or is transient so that the world feels alive without undoing player achievements.

Policies per fact/component: permanent; resetAfter(ticks) or onRest; transient (never saved: wetness, temperature, active fires by default); decaysTo(value) on reload (burning → burnt). Declared in registry/component metadata.
## Scope
- In: Policy evaluation on save capture and on load/rest
- In: Rest event hook (from inn/campfire — owner elsewhere)
- In: Defaults: element transients not saved; burning resolves to burnt on reload
- Out: Offscreen time simulation — see e27-offscreen-catchup
- Out: Resting UI — see mw-e17 / mw-e24
## Notes
Resolving "burning at save time" to burnt on reload avoids saving the element field while keeping outcome consistency (the fire would have finished anyway).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a fact with policy resetAfter(72000 ticks), when 72000 ticks pass (loaded or not), then it returns to its default.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an entity burning at save time with policy decaysTo(burnt), when loaded, then it is in burnt state and not burning.
- AC-3 [unit] Given wetness (transient), when saved and reloaded, then wetness is 0.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a looted chest with permanent policy, when the player rests 10 times, then it stays looted.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a fact declared both transient and with a reset timer (invalid combination), when the registry validates, then it fails (edge).

title: Inspect, edit and diff world state from the debug console
description:
## Why
Testing a late-game branch should not require replaying the game. Developer tooling pillar.
## What
Debug console commands: facts.list [prefix], facts.get/set, deltas.list [level], state.diff <saveA> <saveB>, state.snapshot/restore (in-memory), plus a panel view.
## Scope
- In: Console commands and panel
- In: Diff output grouped by facts and per-level deltas
- Out: Save slot management — see e30-save-serialization
## Notes
Dev builds only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the console, when facts.set quest.x.stage 3 is executed, then the fact is set and dependent conditions re-evaluate.
- AC-2 [integration] Given two saves differing by one looted chest, when state.diff runs, then the output lists exactly that delta.
- AC-3 [integration] Given facts.set with an undeclared key, when executed, then the console reports the error without throwing (edge).

title: Query world facts with a shared condition API for all systems
description:
## Why
Quests, dialogue, puzzles, shops and level variants all need "if the minotaur was befriended and the cellar is open". One predicate language avoids four inconsistent ones.
## What
As a designer, I want to write conditions like all(fact(minotaur.befriended), not(fact(cellar.sealed))) in any content file so that every system gates on world state identically.

JSON predicate AST: fact eq/neq/gt/gte/lt/lte/has, template matches (count(entity:*.looted in level mine) ≥ 3), all/any/not, compiled with dependency lists for change-driven re-evaluation.
## Scope
- In: Predicate AST schema, compiler, dependency extraction, explain()
- In: Subscription API: onConditionChanged(cond, cb)
- Out: Puzzle-specific live-property predicates — see e15-goal-conditions (extends this)
## Notes
Related: e22-dialogue-runtime and e23-quest-runtime should consume this rather than inventing their own (integration pass).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given condition all(fact(a)=true, fact(b)≥3), when a=true and b=2, then false; when b becomes 3, then onConditionChanged fires true exactly once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given count(entity:mine/*.looted) ≥ 3, when three matching facts are true, then it evaluates true.
- AC-3 [content] Given a condition referencing an undeclared fact, when validated, then it fails (via registry).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a deeply nested condition (depth 64), when compiled, then it compiles without stack overflow; depth > 64 is rejected with a clear error (edge).

title: Build greybox reference puzzles for statues, darkness and sound
description:
## Why
Completes the six constitution puzzle archetypes, exercising statues, darkness navigation and sound following.
## What
As a designer, I want three more reference puzzles so that all six constitution examples are proven.

(4) Watchers: rotate statues so all face the altar — push/rotate, pull remotely via levitation, or knock one over (breakable) to satisfy "no statue faces the door". (5) Dark crossing: navigate a pit room where light reveals safe tiles — torches, light spell, relighting braziers, or following the drafts in the smoke. (6) Chimes: reproduce a chime order heard behind a wall — or shoot the bells in order from a balcony, or find the order written in a book.
## Scope
- In: 3 puzzle files + greybox rooms + replays for each declared solution
- Out: Final placement — see mw-e26
## Notes
Watchers deliberately includes a destructive solution (breaking a statue) — confirm softlock policy covers it.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 3 puzzle files, when validated, then each passes with ≥ 2 distinct solutions.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each declared solution replay, when run in CI, then the puzzle reaches solved.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the Watchers puzzle, when a statue is destroyed, then the puzzle remains solvable (validator) and no softlock is reported (edge).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the git diff, when inspected, then no files under src/ change.

title: Build greybox reference puzzles for light, freezing and weight
description:
## Why
The kit is only proven when real puzzles are built with zero code. These cover the first three constitution examples.
## What
As a designer, I want three reference puzzles in greybox so that the kit is proven and future designers have templates.

(1) Sunbeam: redirect light via mirrors to a sensor — also solvable by igniting a brazier near the sensor or a light spell. (2) Frozen channel: cross a water channel — freeze it, float crates, levitate across or climb the ceiling beams. (3) Scales: two plates must hold equal weight — crates, bodies, an ice block, or standing on one yourself while levitating a crate on the other.
## Scope
- In: 3 puzzle files + greybox rooms + scenario replays for each declared solution
- In: Each ≥ 2 validated solutions (target 3–4)
- Out: Final dungeon placement and art — see mw-e26
## Notes
Zero new TypeScript permitted; any engine gap discovered becomes a bead in e03/e15.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 3 puzzle files, when validated, then each passes schema and the solvability validator with ≥ 2 distinct solutions.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each declared solution, when its replay runs in CI, then the puzzle reaches solved.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the git diff of this item, when inspected by CI script, then no files under src/ are changed (data-only proof).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the scales puzzle, when the player removes weight after solving, then the puzzle stays solved (one-shot) and the door stays open (edge).
- AC-5 [manual] Given 3 playtesters, when each attempts the puzzles, then at least 2 distinct solutions are observed per puzzle across testers.

title: Report and enforce per-class solution coverage for puzzles in CI
description:
## Why
"Problems support multiple solutions" and "Classes change possibilities" must be measurable across the MVP.
## What
A report (docs/design/puzzle-coverage.md, regenerated in CI) listing each puzzle × {knight, archer, sorcerer, thief, any} with validated solvability, minimum capability sets and step counts. CI rule: every mvp puzzle ≥ 2 validated distinct solutions and solvable by at least 3 of 4 classes at MVP capability levels.
## Scope
- In: Class capability profiles at MVP progression milestones (data)
- In: Report generator + CI gate + PR diff summary
- Out: Encounter-level route audits — see mw-e16
## Notes
Related: mw-e16 class-specific solutions will reuse the class capability profiles; e19-progression-core supplies capability ids.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given all puzzles, when the audit runs, then the report lists every puzzle with per-class solvable yes/no/inconclusive.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an mvp puzzle solvable by only 2 classes, when CI runs, then the gate fails naming the puzzle and missing classes.
- AC-3 [unit] Given two declared solutions that reduce to the same capability set and step list, when counted, then they count as 1 distinct solution (edge).

title: Detect puzzle softlocks and recover with diegetic resets
description:
## Why
Failure creates stories, not dead saves. Burning the only crate or dropping the key object into a chasm must not permanently block progress (or must be a deliberate, alternate-route design).
## What
As a player, I want puzzles to recover when I destroy or lose a key object so that experimenting never bricks my save.

Validator side: search for reachable irreversible states from which the goal is unreachable and require a declared recovery policy. Runtime side: recovery policies — respawn source (crate chute drops a new crate after N s), reset lever (restore mechanism states), reversible-only flag, or alternate route declared. Resets are diegetic and persisted.
## Scope
- In: Softlock search extension to the solver (irreversible transitions: burn, break, fall out of bounds, melt)
- In: Runtime policies: respawner, reset lever/volume, out-of-bounds return
- In: Reset fact + telemetry event
- Out: Save rollback — out of scope; recovery is in-world
## Notes
Objects falling out of the world are returned to their spawner via an out-of-bounds trigger (property-based: any entity with puzzleCritical=true).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a weighted-plate puzzle whose only crate is flammable, when the solver explores burning it, then it reports a softlock unless a recovery policy exists.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a respawner policy of 10 s, when the critical crate is destroyed, then a replacement spawns at the chute after 10 s and emits puzzleRecovered.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a puzzleCritical object falls below the kill plane, when resolved, then it returns to its spawn point within 1 tick without breaking.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a reset lever, when pulled, then all mechanism states in the puzzle return to authored defaults and the puzzle state returns to in-progress (unless already solved).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a respawner whose chute is blocked by an object, when respawning, then it retries each 2 s and never spawns overlapping geometry (edge).

title: Prove declared puzzle solutions reachable with a headless solver
description:
## Why
Multiple solutions must be verified, not hoped for. A headless solver catches broken puzzles before playtests do.
## What
As a designer, I want to run a validator that proves each declared solution works for its capability set so that I know my puzzle is solvable before anyone plays it.

Two layers: (1) abstract search — a BFS/A* over an abstracted puzzle state (mechanism states, object cells, element states) with actions derived from the capability set (push, rotate, ignite, freeze, levitate, shoot, climb), proving the goal reachable within a step bound; (2) concrete confirmation — each declared step list is executed in the headless sim with scripted actions to confirm the goal. Reports unreachable solutions, minimum steps, and shortcut solutions found with fewer capabilities.
## Scope
- In: Abstract state extraction from puzzle + level data
- In: Capability → action generators; bounded search with memoisation
- In: Headless concrete execution of declared step lists via e00-replay-harness
- In: CLI: pnpm puzzle:validate [id] + CI job
- Out: Softlock detection — see e15-softlock-guard
- Out: Class coverage report — see e15-solution-audit
## Notes
Abstraction must be conservative; when the abstract solver says unreachable but the concrete run succeeds, report an abstraction gap. Time-box per puzzle 10 s in CI.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a brazier puzzle with a declared solution requiring spell.fire, when validated, then the solver finds a path and reports minimum step count.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a puzzle whose only declared solution needs a crate that the level does not contain, when validated, then it reports the solution unreachable with the missing requirement.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a puzzle solvable with an empty capability set although tagged class-specific, when validated, then it reports a shortcut solution (informational warning).
- AC-4 [integration] Given each declared step list, when executed in the headless sim, then the goal becomes true; failures show the step index where it diverged.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a state space exceeding the search bound, when validated, then it stops at the bound within 10 s and reports inconclusive rather than hanging (edge).
- AC-6 [integration] Given CI, when any mvp puzzle has an unreachable declared solution, then the job fails.

title: Support ordered, timed and sound-clue puzzle mechanisms
description:
## Why
"Following sounds" and "interpreting books" are named puzzle types; ordered/timed mechanisms generalise bell towers, rune floors and race-the-door puzzles.
## What
As a player, I want to hear chimes behind a wall and replay their order on bells so that listening and observation are puzzle skills.

Prefab-level wiring using e03 logic nodes: sound-clue emitters (play a sequence of positional cues on trigger), sequence validators with tolerance, timed windows (open door for N seconds after plate), and book-clue binding (a readable item text references puzzle ids for hint attribution).
## Scope
- In: Sound clue emitter component (cue list, spacing, positional audio via e28)
- In: Sequence + timed window prefab compositions
- In: Readable clue binding for attribution
- Out: Book reading UI — see mw-e17 / mw-e07
## Notes
Accessibility: every sound clue has a subtitle/visual equivalent (E31) — e.g. subtitle "[high chime, left]".
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a sound clue emitter with cues [low, high, mid], when triggered, then three cue events fire in order at the configured spacing (1.0 s).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a sequence validator expecting [low, high, mid], when the player strikes bells low, high, mid, then success fires; any wrong bell resets and fires a failure cue.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a timed door of 8 s, when the plate is released and the player passes at 8.1 s, then the door is closed.
- AC-4 [unit] Given subtitles enabled, when a clue cue fires, then a subtitle event with its direction label is emitted (edge: accessibility).

title: Ship reusable puzzle prefabs built only from world components
description:
## Why
Fast content creation: designers compose from a kit rather than asking engineers for "a mirror that turns".
## What
As a designer, I want a palette of puzzle prefabs so that I can assemble puzzles in minutes.

Prefabs (data only, composed from e03 components): rotatable statue (facing sensor), rotatable mirror, lens stand, weighted crate set (5/10/20/40 kg), brazier (flammable + receiver), water basin with valve and drain, counterweight lift, sliding block (grid pushable), bell, crystal receiver, beam sensor, scale plate pair, timed door, rune tile (sequence input).
## Scope
- In: 15 prefabs + per-prefab tests exercising their property behaviour
- In: Prefab catalogue docs generated from data
- Out: Final models/art — see mw-e37 asset beads
## Notes
Rule: a prefab may not introduce a new TypeScript component. If one is needed, it goes to e03 first as a general property/component.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given each prefab, when validated, then it references only existing e03 components and passes schema.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the rotatable statue prefab facing north, when rotated 4 steps, then its facing sensor emits the facing value east/south/west/north in order.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the basin prefab with valve opened, when simulated, then water level drops and a submerged plate at its bottom becomes reachable.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a prefab instance with a required override missing (e.g. mirror without step angle), when loaded, then default values apply or validation fails if no default exists (edge).
- AC-5 [content] Given the prefab directory, when the docs generator runs, then docs/design/puzzle-prefabs.md lists all prefabs with their properties and outputs.

title: Run data-defined puzzles composed from reusable world objects
description:
## Why
Designers can construct systemic puzzles from reusable world objects instead of custom-coding every puzzle (E15 outcome).
## What
As a designer, I want to drop a puzzle file next to a level and have it tracked, solved, rewarded and persisted so that I never write TypeScript for a puzzle.

Puzzle runtime: loads puzzle definitions for the active level, binds entity refs, tracks lifecycle (dormant → discovered → in-progress → solved/failed), evaluates goal conditions, fires outputs (signals, world facts, rewards), detects which declared solution path was used where possible (by capability usage trail), and persists state via e27.
## Scope
- In: Lifecycle state machine and discovery triggers (volume enter / first interaction)
- In: Outputs: signal emit, fact set, reward hook, one-shot vs repeatable
- In: Solution attribution from stimulus/capability trail
- In: Designer guide docs/design/puzzles.md
- Out: Prefab pieces — see e15-prefab-pieces
- Out: Validation tooling — see e15-solvability-validator
## Notes
Unanticipated solutions are welcome: if the goal becomes true via an undeclared route, attribution records "undeclared" and emits a telemetry event — valuable designer feedback.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a puzzle in dormant state, when the player enters its discovery volume, then it becomes discovered and emits puzzleDiscovered.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an in-progress puzzle, when its goal becomes true, then it becomes solved, emits configured signals and sets its solved fact exactly once.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a solved one-shot puzzle, when its goal later becomes false (e.g. brazier extinguished), then it remains solved and outputs are not re-fired.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the goal was reached using capabilities not matching any declared solution, when solved, then attribution = undeclared and a puzzleSolvedUndeclared event fires (edge).
- AC-5 [integration] Given a solved puzzle, when saved and reloaded, then it is still solved and its outputs (door open) are restored without re-firing rewards.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the greybox brazier puzzle, when the bot lights all braziers with a torch in one replay and a fire stimulus from range in another, then both replays solve it.

title: Express puzzle goals as conditions over live properties and facts
description:
## Why
Puzzle goals must describe outcomes ("all braziers lit", "a beam reaches the sensor", "≥ 40 kg on the plate") rather than steps, so any method that achieves the outcome counts.
## What
As a designer, I want to write goals like all(entities tagged brazier-3, burning) so that any way of lighting them solves the puzzle.

A small, deterministic condition language: property predicates on entity refs or tag sets (all/any/count ≥ n), signal state, world facts (via e27 queries), spatial predicates (entity inside volume), boolean combinators, and sustained-for duration. Compiled once to a closure; evaluated each tick only when dependencies change.
## Scope
- In: Grammar/JSON AST + compiler + dependency tracking
- In: Predicates: property, signal, fact, inVolume, sustained(seconds)
- In: Human-readable explain() for debug and hints
- Out: Fact store — see e27-world-state-store
## Notes
Shares the fact predicate primitives from e27-fact-queries rather than duplicating them.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given goal all(tag:brazier, burning), when 2 of 3 braziers burn, then it is false; when the third ignites by any source, then it becomes true on that tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given goal sustained(inVolume(any weight≥40, plateZone), 3s), when weight is held for 2.9 s then removed, then it stays false.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a goal whose dependencies did not change this tick, when the runtime ticks, then the goal is not re-evaluated (dependency tracking).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a malformed goal AST (unknown predicate), when compiled, then compilation fails with a path to the node (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given any goal, when explain() is called, then it returns a readable string listing each sub-condition and its current truth value.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: mw-e15.1 puzzles embed conditionSchema as goal and register it in CONDITION_USAGES (pointer /goal), so new predicate kinds are accepted in puzzle goals automatically. When predicates name entity ids, add a puzzle check that each goal entity is listed in the puzzle's entities (puzzle-checks.ts already checks entities against the scene's spawns). Example to convert: src/content/data/puzzle/testbed-room-lever.json reads the fact testbed.room-lever.thrown as a stand-in for the lever's live state.

title: Define the puzzle data schema with goals, solutions and policies
description:
## Why
Puzzles are data, not code (contract §1). A schema is the contract between designers, the runtime and the validator.
## What
A zod schema for content/puzzles/*.json: id, region, entity refs (by level entity id), goal condition (expression over live properties and world facts), declared solutions (name, required capability set, abstract step list for the validator), reset policy, hint ladder, tags (mvp, class focus), and rewards/fact outputs.
## Scope
- In: Schema + example puzzle + schema tests
- In: Cross-reference validation against level entity ids
- Out: Runtime evaluation — see e15-puzzle-kit
- Out: Goal expression language — see e15-goal-conditions
## Notes
Capability sets reference e19 capability ids (e.g. spell.frost, arrow.rope, climb.rough). Related: e19-progression-core defines capability ids.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the example puzzle file, when validated, then it passes and every field is documented.
- AC-2 [content] Given a puzzle referencing an entity id absent from its level, when validated, then validation fails naming the id and level.
- AC-3 [content] Given a puzzle tagged mvp with fewer than 2 declared solutions, when validated, then validation fails (edge).
- AC-4 [content] Given a solution requiring an unknown capability id, when validated, then validation fails with the id.

title: Budget element, physics and light simulation cost per tick
description:
## Why
Systemic worlds die by a thousand cuts in the browser. The element sim must stay within a fixed slice of the frame on the reference and low-preset machines.
## What
Stress scenes (large fire spread, flooded room freezing, gas explosion, 200 physics bodies) with perf assertions wired into e32. Add adaptive degradation: when budget exceeded, reduce far-chunk update rate deterministically (sim-rate LOD keyed by distance, not by wall time, to keep determinism).
## Scope
- In: 4 stress scenes + perf tests
- In: Deterministic distance-based update LOD for field chunks
- Out: Global frame budget — see e32-perf-budgets
## Notes
LOD must not depend on measured frame time (non-deterministic); only on player distance and active counts.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the fire-spread stress scene (2,000 active cells), when simulated on the reference machine, then element step ≤ 2.0 ms per tick p95.
- AC-2 [perf] Given the same scene on the low-preset profile, when simulated, then element step ≤ 3.5 ms per tick p95.
- AC-3 [unit] Given field chunks > 40 m from the player, when LOD applies, then they update every 4th tick and results are deterministic across runs.
- AC-4 [perf] Given the gas explosion scene (worst case), when simulated, then no single tick exceeds 8 ms (edge: spike).

title: Show properties, element fields and light levels in a debug overlay
description:
## Why
Designers and developers cannot tune invisible fields. Developer tooling is a technical pillar.
## What
Debug overlay (via e33 debug console) toggling: property inspector on the focused entity (with live edit), temperature/moisture/gas/charge heatmaps, light level grid, signal-graph wire view with live states, stimulus log timeline. Console commands to spawn stimuli (stim heat 500 r=2 at cursor).
## Scope
- In: Overlay layers + inspector panel + console commands
- In: Read-only in production builds (stripped)
- Out: Puzzle inspector — see e15-puzzle-inspector
## Notes
Overlay reads sim state through the public query API only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the overlay toggled to temperature, when a heat stimulus is spawned, then the heatmap shows the hot region within 1 frame.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the inspector on an entity, when wetness is edited to 1.0, then the sim reflects it next tick and propertyChanged fires.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a production build, when scanned, then overlay code is absent (edge).
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the overlay is toggled through all layers, then no console errors occur.

title: Show burning, wet, frozen and charged states through VFX and audio
description:
## Why
Systems the player cannot read are systems the player cannot exploit. Wet, frozen, charged and burning must be legible at a glance.
## What
As a player, I want to see and hear that something is soaked, frozen or crackling with charge so that I can plan combos.

A presentation bridge subscribing to propertyChanged and element events: drives material parameters (wet darkening, frost overlay, char), VFX hooks (fire, steam, sparks, smoke volumes, beams) via e29 and audio cues (crackle loops, sizzle, freeze crack, zap) via e28. Placeholder grey-box visuals are acceptable; final art via separate beads.
## Scope
- In: Event → material/VFX/audio mapping table in data
- In: Pooling and LOD for element VFX; field-visualisation for gas/smoke
- In: Playwright smoke + perf checks
- Out: Final VFX art — see mw-e29 asset beads
- Out: Final SFX — see mw-e38 asset beads
## Notes
Mapping is data-driven by property/state, not entity type: any burning entity gets fire VFX sized to its bounds.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the mapping table, when an entity gains burning=true, then exactly one fire VFX handle is requested sized to its bounds and released when burning=false.
- AC-2 [unit] Given 200 entities ignite in one tick, when bridged, then VFX requests beyond the pool cap (64) are LOD-culled by distance deterministically (edge).
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the chaos room, when the fire and freeze scenarios run in the browser, then VFX nodes appear (scene probe) and there are no console errors.
