- AC-4 [perf] Given 40 burning entities and a smoke cloud in view, when rendering on the reference machine (High), then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms.
- AC-5 [manual] Given a playtest, when testers are shown 6 objects in different states, then ≥ 80% correctly identify wet, frozen, burning and charged without UI text.

title: Replay a library of emergent combo scenarios in a greybox chaos room
description:
## Why
We need living proof that "Wait… I can do that?" moments emerge from properties, and a regression net so they keep emerging as rules change.
## What
As a designer, I want a catalogue of emergent combos, each a replayable greybox scenario, so that I can see and protect the game's surprising interactions.

A chaos-room greybox level plus ≥ 12 scenario files, each with setup, input log and asserted outcome expressed via properties/facts. Initial catalogue: oil puddle ignition chain; burn rope → dropped chandelier; freeze river → walk across; soak enemies + charge in puddle; frozen actor shattered by blunt hit; levitated crate weighs 0 on plate; wedge portcullis with crate; gust extinguishes candles but not brazier; smoke blocks sight line; burning haystack ejects hider; focused beam ignites web barrier; ice block on pressure plate melts → plate releases (timer puzzle for free).
## Scope
- In: Chaos room level, scenario schema, runner integrated with e00-replay-harness
- In: 12+ scenarios with property-based outcome assertions
- In: Catalogue doc docs/design/emergence-catalogue.md generated from scenario metadata
- Out: Randomised coverage — see e03-interaction-matrix
## Notes
Scenario outcomes are phrased as properties ("some entity with flammable ends burnt"), never "the rope entity". New combos discovered in playtests get added here.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given each scenario, when replayed in CI, then the asserted property outcome holds and the final state hash matches its golden.
- AC-2 [content] Given the scenario directory, when validated, then there are ≥ 12 scenarios and each has setup, inputs, outcome and a player-facing description.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a rule change breaks a scenario, when CI runs, then the failure names the scenario and its outcome description.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the ice-on-plate scenario, when simulated, then the plate deactivates only after the ice melts below the weight threshold (edge: time-based emergent state).
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the chaos room in the browser, when the Playwright bot runs the rope/chandelier scenario, then it completes with no console errors.

title: Property-test all element × property combinations in a matrix harness
description:
## Why
Emergence is only a feature if it is safe: combinations nobody designed must not crash, loop forever or break invariants. Property-based testing is how we cover a combinatorial space we cannot enumerate by hand.
## What
As a developer, I want a generator-driven harness that throws random entities (random property sets) and random stimulus sequences into a sandbox world so that invariants hold for every element × property combination.

Uses fast-check to generate property bags and stimulus programs; runs N ticks headless; checks invariants: determinism (double-run hash), termination (fields return to ambient after sources stop), conservation (heat/gas/water within tolerance), no NaN/Infinity, state consistency (frozen ⇒ not burning; burnt ⇒ fuel 0), no type-pair logic reachable. Emits a matrix report (element × property → observed transitions) committed as docs/design/interaction-matrix.md.
## Scope
- In: fast-check arbitraries for property bags, materials and stimulus programs
- In: Invariant library and shrinking-friendly failure output (seed + minimal case)
- In: Matrix report generator; CI job with fixed seed budget ≤ 60 s + nightly long run
- Out: Handcrafted scenario replays — see e03-emergence-scenarios
## Notes
Every failing case found becomes a named regression test. Matrix report diff in PRs makes emergent behaviour changes visible to designers ("this PR makes wet wood no longer conduct").
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 500 generated worlds × 300 ticks with a fixed seed, when run in CI, then all invariants hold and the job completes in ≤ 60 s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a deliberately injected bug (burning allowed while frozen), when the harness runs, then it fails and prints a shrunk minimal reproduction with seed.
- AC-3 [unit] Given every pair of (element ∈ heat,cold,water,charge,force,gas,light) × (property ∈ schema), when the matrix report is generated, then every cell is populated with observed transitions or "no effect".
- AC-4 [integration] Given a PR that changes an element rule, when CI runs, then the regenerated matrix report is diffed and the diff is attached to the job summary.
- AC-5 [unit] Given extreme values (temperature 1e6, weight 0, radius 0), when generated, then no NaN/Infinity appears in any property or field cell (edge).

title: Emit noise events from world interactions with material loudness
description:
## Why
Breaking glass, slamming doors, falling crates, bells and splashes must be audible to AI and audio through one consistent event, not per-system hacks.
## What
World systems (impacts, breaks, doors, mechanisms, splashes, fire crackle, explosions) emit NoiseEvent{pos, loudness, kind, source} via the event bus, with loudness computed from impact energy × material loudness (data).
## Scope
- In: NoiseEvent type + emission from e03 systems
- In: Material loudness data, energy→loudness curve
- Out: Propagation, occlusion and perception — see e09-sound-propagation, e11-perception
- Out: Audio playback — see e28-audio-engine
## Notes
Related: e09-sound-propagation consumes these; keep the event schema stable and documented in docs/design/noise-events.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a crate impact of 200 J on stone, when resolved, then a NoiseEvent is emitted with loudness from the documented curve and the impact source.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a door slam vs a slow close, when compared, then slam loudness ≥ 3× slow close loudness.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 50 micro-impacts per second from a settling pile below the min energy threshold, when resolved, then no noise events are emitted (edge: spam suppression).

title: Apply world properties and elements to creatures and the player
description:
## Why
Enemies are part of the same world: a soaked goblin conducts lightning, a burning spider flees, a knight in iron armor is conductive, a frozen skeleton shatters. No per-creature element scripts.
## What
As a sorcerer, I want creatures to be wet, burning, frozen or charged by the same rules as objects so that combining spells on enemies is intuitive.

Actors carry the same property components (with actor-specific resistances from e12 creature data and equipment): wetness, temperature, burning, frozen (slow → immobilised), charge, conductive (from armor), weight (for plates/carry). Element rules emit actor-facing events (onFire, frozenSolid, shocked, soaked) that combat/AI respond to. Actors spread fire to what they touch.
## Scope
- In: Property components on actors with resistance modifiers from creature/equipment data
- In: Status thresholds and events; movement speed modifier hooks
- In: Burning actors ignite flammables they touch; wet actors extinguish
- Out: Damage values and poise — see e04-damage-model
- Out: AI panic/flee — see mw-e11
- Out: Creature data schema — see e12-creature-schema
## Notes
Frozen-solid actors become temporary physics objects with fragile=true (the shatter combo) — pushing one off a ledge should work.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any actor with wetness ≥ 0.5, when a charge stimulus hits it, then shock intensity is multiplied by the conductive-wet factor from data.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a burning actor moving through flammable grass cells, when ticks run, then grass cells along its path ignite.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an actor accumulating cold beyond its frozen threshold, when resolved, then it becomes frozen solid (immobile, fragile) for the data duration and emits frozenSolid.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an actor with fire immunity (resistance 1.0), when exposed to heat, then burning never becomes true but it can still ignite things it touches if its own burning is data-forced (e.g. fire elemental) (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a player equips iron armor, when conductive is queried, then it returns true; unequipping restores the base value.
notes: From mw-e03.1 (PR #41): creature.properties (mw-e12.1, PR #40) is currently a string-tag list; switch it to embed worldPropertiesSchema (src/content/world-properties.ts) when actors join the property system.

title: Hide in wardrobes, barrels and haystacks and search containers
description:
## Why
Hiding places are a named stealth factor; containers hold loot, bodies and secrets. They must also be systemic (a burning haystack evicts you; a searched wardrobe is found).
## What
As a thief, I want to slip into a wardrobe or haystack and stash bodies in chests so that I can break line of sight and cover my tracks.

Hideable component (capacity, concealment 0..1, exit points, noise on enter/exit, peek allowed) and container component (inventory, lockable via e03 lock, capacity by weight, holds bodies if large). Actors inside are removed from sight queries except by search; containers that burn/break eject contents and occupants.
## Scope
- In: Enter/exit hide verbs via interaction, peek camera hook, occupancy
- In: Container inventory binding to e17, open/search/loot affordances
- In: Break/burn/submerge ejects occupants and spills contents
- Out: AI searching hiding spots — see mw-e11 (uses the occupancy query)
- Out: Loot tables — see e18-loot-tables
## Notes
Hay is flammable; hiding in a haystack next to a torch-wielding guard is a story. Occupancy query: isOccupied(entity) for AI search, respecting "last seen near" logic on their side.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a hideable with capacity 1, when the player enters, then the player is flagged hidden with the container concealment value and a second actor cannot enter.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a hidden player, when the hideable ignites or breaks, then the player is ejected to the nearest free exit point on that tick and takes heat exposure if burning.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a container holding items, when it breaks, then all items spawn as world pickups around it.
- AC-4 [unit] Given all exit points are blocked, when the player tries to exit, then exit is refused and the prompt shows "Blocked" (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a container with capacity 60 kg, when a 70 kg body is stashed, then it is refused.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the save system, when saving with an item and a body inside a chest, then after reload both are still inside (via e27).

title: Mark climbable surfaces and ledges from properties and geometry
description:
## Why
Climbing routes must be authorable quickly and change systemically (burn ivy, freeze a wall, prop a ladder).
## What
As a designer, I want to tag surfaces as climbable and have ledges auto-detected so that I can create alternate routes quickly.

Climbable property on colliders with grade (ladder, rope, ivy, rough, sheer=no), plus an offline/at-load ledge extraction pass over greybox geometry producing ledge segments (with overrides to disable/enable). Property changes at runtime (ivy burned, surface frozen → slippery) update climbability.
## Scope
- In: Climbable grade property + capability requirement data
- In: Ledge extraction pass with per-edge override markup, ledge query API
- In: Runtime invalidation on property change
- Out: Player climbing movement — see e02-climb-surfaces, e02-ledge-mantle
## Notes
Ivy uses material ivy (flammable) — burning removes the climbable property via burnt-state data. Frozen surfaces set a slippery flag that blocks climbing unless the actor has ice tools (future).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a greybox box of height 1.5 m, when ledge extraction runs, then ledge segments are produced along its top edges and none along vertical edges.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an edge override disable, when extraction runs, then no ledge is produced there.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an ivy surface that burns out, when the burnt state applies, then its climbable grade becomes none and ledge/climb queries reflect it on the next tick.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a surface becomes frozen, when queried, then climbable returns slippery and climb attach is refused (edge).
- AC-5 [content] Given a level file with a climbable grade not in the enum, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Trigger distant mechanisms with projectiles, impacts and force
description:
## Why
"The archer might shoot a distant mechanism." Bullseye switches, bells, hanging counterweights and crystal switches must respond to any impact source, so thrown rocks and spells work too.
## What
As an archer, I want to shoot a target on a far wall to lower a bridge so that precision opens routes others must work around.

Impact-switch component: activates when an impact/stimulus meets its filter (min energy, damage type set, element set, hit zone). Variants: bullseye (pierce, small hit zone), bell (any impact, emits loud noise), crystal (charge/light), counterweight (release via rope support).
## Scope
- In: Impact switch with filters and hit-zone geometry
- In: Variants as prefabs; bell as noise-emitting distraction tool
- In: Outputs to signal system
- Out: Arrow projectile — see e05-bow-core
## Notes
A sorcerer's Mage Hand pressing the button, a thief's thrown dagger, a knight's thrown shield — all valid if the filter permits. Designers restrict filters only deliberately.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a bullseye filtered to pierce with min energy 20 J, when a 25 J pierce impact hits inside the hit zone, then it activates; the same impact 5 cm outside the zone does not.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a bell switch filtered to any impact, when a thrown object at ≥ 5 J hits it, then it activates and emits a noise event with loudness 1.0.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a crystal switch filtered to charge, when a heat stimulus hits it, then it does not activate; a charge stimulus does.
- AC-4 [unit] Given multiple hits in one tick on a momentary switch, when resolved, then exactly one activation event fires (edge).

title: Activate pressure plates by total weight of anything resting on them
description:
## Why
"Weighing pressure plates" is a named puzzle pattern. Plates must count any weight — crates, bodies, ice blocks, summoned skeletons — so solutions multiply.
## What
As a player, I want a plate to trigger when enough weight rests on it so that I can use a crate, a body, a frozen block or myself.

Plate component: min/max weight window, hysteresis, momentary vs latching, arming delay; weight = sum of weight properties of bodies and actors in contact (including carried items).
## Scope
- In: Plate weight summation from contacts incl. actors and their carried/equipped weight
- In: Windowed thresholds (too heavy also fails), hysteresis, latching, delay
- In: Trap variant: hidden plate outputs to trap signals
- Out: Trap effects — see mw-e10
## Notes
Weight window enables "exactly 40 kg" scale puzzles. Levitated objects (gravity scale 0) weigh nothing on a plate — emergent sorcerer trick.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a plate with min 40 kg, when a 25 kg crate and a 20 kg barrel rest on it, then it activates; removing the barrel deactivates it after hysteresis.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a plate with window 40–60 kg, when 70 kg rests on it, then it does not activate (too heavy).
- AC-3 [unit] Given an actor carrying a 10 kg object stands on a plate, when summed, then weight includes actor + carried weight.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an object under gravity-scale 0 (levitated) hovers touching the plate, when summed, then it contributes 0 kg (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a latching plate, when weight is removed after activation, then it stays active until reset by a signal.

title: Redirect light beams with mirrors and lenses onto receivers
description:
## Why
"Redirecting light" is the first puzzle example in the constitution; beams should also interact with properties (burn through webs, blind creatures, melt ice).
## What
As a player, I want to angle mirrors so that a sunbeam reaches a sealed door's sensor.

Beam emitters (sunlight shaft, crystal, spell) cast deterministic segmented rays in sim; surfaces with reflective bounce, transparent pass (with tint), opaque stop; lens focus multiplies intensity; beams apply a continuous light stimulus (and heat when focused) where they end; light receivers emit signals when intensity ≥ threshold for a dwell time.
## Scope
- In: Beam tracing with max bounces (default 8), reflection, transmission, stop
- In: Light receiver component with threshold + dwell + optional colour filter
- In: Focused beams apply heat stimulus
- Out: Rotating mirrors — see e02-push-pull (rotate affordance)
- Out: Beam VFX — see e03-state-feedback-bridge / e29-vfx-framework
## Notes
Frozen water/ice is transparent; a player or creature standing in the beam blocks it (actors are opaque) — enabling "stand here to break the beam" solutions.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a beam hitting a reflective surface at 30°, when traced, then it reflects at 30° about the surface normal within 0.01°.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a beam reaching a receiver with threshold 0.5 for dwell 1.0 s, when intensity is 0.6 for 1.0 s, then it emits activated; interrupted at 0.9 s, it does not.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a beam passing through a lens, when it hits a flammable entity, then heat stimulus is applied and the entity ignites per fire rules.
- AC-4 [unit] Given two mirrors facing each other creating a loop, when traced, then tracing stops at max bounces without hanging (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given an actor steps into the beam path, when traced, then the beam terminates at the actor and downstream receivers deactivate.

title: Extinguish and relight torches, candles and braziers systemically
description:
## Why
"Extinguishing lights" is a named thief verb; relighting a brazier is a named puzzle pattern. Both must work via properties so a water arrow, a gust, a hand pinch or rain all work.
## What
As a thief, I want to snuff torches by hand, with a water arrow, or with a gust so that I can carve a path through darkness.

Light source prefabs (candle, torch, wall sconce, brazier, lantern, fireplace) = flammable fuel + light emitter tied to burning. Extinguish via wetness, force above windResistance, smother interaction (hand, requires reach), or fuel exhaustion. Relight via heat. Enemies noticing lights out is AI's job but a lightChanged event with attribution is emitted.
## Scope
- In: Light source prefabs, snuff interaction (silent, 1.0 s), wind/force extinguish thresholds
- In: lightChanged event with source attribution
- In: Unlit-at-start and infinite-fuel flags for designers
- Out: Guard relighting behaviour — see mw-e11
- Out: Water arrows — see mw-e05
## Notes
Lanterns carried by guards are the same prefab attached to an actor — freeze or soak one and the guard walks in darkness.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any lit light source, when its wetness rises ≥ 0.5 from any water stimulus, then it extinguishes and the local light level drops accordingly.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a candle (windResistance low) and a brazier (high), when the same force stimulus hits both, then the candle extinguishes and the brazier does not.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a player uses snuff on a torch, when completed, then it extinguishes and emits a noise event of loudness ≤ 0.05.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unlit torch, when any heat stimulus exceeds its ignition point, then it relights and emits lightChanged with the heat source as attribution.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a soaked torch (wetness 1.0), when heat is applied, then it does not relight until dried below 0.5 (edge).

title: Support hanging objects on ropes that burn, cut or snap
description:
## Why
Shooting the rope that holds a chandelier onto enemies, burning a rope bridge behind you, or cutting a hanging cage free are classic emergent moments.
## What
As an archer, I want to shoot or burn a rope so that whatever it holds falls — chandeliers, cages, drawbridges, counterweights, bridges.

Rope/chain support entities connect an anchor to a supported body; they have material properties (rope: flammable, slash/pierce-weak; chain: not). When hp reaches 0 or burnt, the support releases, the supported object becomes dynamic (falling damage via impact) and any linked mechanism receives a signal. Rope bridges are chains of planks supported by ropes.
## Scope
- In: Support constraint entity with hp/resistances and load
- In: Release → dynamic body + signal output
- In: Rope bridge prefab (planks + two support ropes)
- Out: Climbable ropes — see e02-climb-surfaces (a rope can be both climbable and a support)
## Notes
Overload: a support snaps if load weight exceeds its rating — putting a heavy crate on a rotten rope bridge snaps it (failure creates stories).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any support with flammable material, when it burns out, then it releases and the supported body becomes dynamic on that tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a rope support with pierce resistance 0.3, when hit by pierce damage ≥ its hp/0.7, then it releases; a chain support with pierce immunity does not.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a released support linked to a mechanism, when released, then the mechanism receives a signal exactly once.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a rope bridge rated for 150 kg, when total load exceeds 150 kg, then the weakest rope snaps and planks fall (edge/failure).
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox chandelier room, when a pierce stimulus hits the rope, then the chandelier falls and impact damage events fire for actors beneath it.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: From mw-e04.19: when a hanging object is let go (rope burnt, cut or snapped), clear its `suspended` property with the cutter as the setProperty source — installEnvironmentDamage blames that source for whatever the object crushes (tests/integration/environment-damage.test.ts has a stand-in drop rule to replace).

title: Let external forces hold, levitate and fling liftable objects
description:
## Why
Mage Hand, Telekinesis, Gravity Well and "throwing creatures / catching projectiles" all need one world-side API for being held and moved at a distance.
## What
As a sorcerer, I want to lift a crate onto a balcony, pull a lever from across a chasm or yank a shield from a goblin so that magic manipulates the world itself.

A holdable-at-distance API: external holders attach a spring-damper constraint to any body with liftable=true (or actors with a liftable tier), limited by holder strength vs. weight, with gravity scale overrides (float), point attractors (Gravity Well), and release with velocity. Interactables (levers) can be actuated remotely if flagged remoteActuatable.
## Scope
- In: Remote hold constraint, strength vs weight check, break-hold on obstruction or overload
- In: Gravity scale override zones and point attractors
- In: Remote actuation of interactables with remoteActuatable
- Out: The spells themselves — see e06-spell-pipeline / mw-e08
- Out: Player hand-carry — see e02-carry-throw
## Notes
Standing on a levitated platform should work (it is just a moving body; controller handles moving-platform carry). Catching projectiles: arrows are liftable light bodies.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a liftable 30 kg object and a holder strength of 50, when held, then it tracks the target point with settling time ≤ 0.5 s; given 80 kg, the hold fails with reason overweight.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a held object blocked by a wall for > 1.0 s with the target far behind it, when resolved, then the hold breaks and the object drops (edge).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a point attractor of strength S, when loose liftable objects are within radius, then each accelerates toward the point proportional to S/mass and non-liftable objects are unaffected.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a remoteActuatable lever within the holder range, when remote actuation is applied, then the lever toggles exactly as if interacted with; a lever without the flag does not.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a held object released with velocity v, when released, then its initial velocity equals v within 1%.

title: Conduct electrical charge through conductive and wet objects
description:
## Why
Storm magic becomes spectacular when lightning arcs through a puddle into three goblins standing in it, or powers an old mechanism — pure property combos.
## What
As a sorcerer, I want lightning to spread through water and metal so that I can electrify puddles, armored knights or arcane conduits.

Charge stimuli add charge to entities/cells; charge flows along connected conductive networks (conductive property or wetness ≥ 0.5, or water volumes) with per-hop falloff within one tick; charge above thresholds deals shock (actors), ignites flammables at high intensity, and powers "charge receiver" mechanisms (arcane conduits, old dwarven lifts).
## Scope
- In: Connectivity graph build from contacts/overlaps, cached and invalidated on movement/wetness change
- In: Charge distribution with falloff, discharge, shock event, ignition at threshold
- In: Charge receiver component feeding the signal system
- Out: Storm spells — see mw-e08
- Out: Damage numbers — see e04-damage-model
## Notes
Network flood fill capped (e.g. 256 nodes) with deterministic BFS by entity id. A knight in metal armor is conductive via actor properties (e03-actor-properties).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a water volume containing three actors, when a charge stimulus hits the water, then all three receive a shock event with intensity reduced by the documented falloff per hop.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a chain of conductive entities touching, when charge enters one end, then charge reaches the far end in the same tick; with a non-conductive gap, it does not cross.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a dry wooden entity next to a charged metal entity, when resolved, then the wood receives no charge; once wetness ≥ 0.5 it conducts.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a charge receiver in a charged network, when charge ≥ its activation threshold, then it emits an activated signal; below threshold it does not.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a conductive network larger than the node cap, when charge floods, then propagation stops at the cap deterministically and logs a warning (edge).

title: Freeze water and wet objects into ice and melt them with heat
description:
## Why
"Magic can freeze water." Frozen rivers as bridges, frozen doors that shatter, ice surfaces for sliding enemies are signature "Wait… I can do that?" moments.
## What
As a sorcerer, I want cold to freeze water and wet things so that I can make bridges, jam mechanisms and shatter frozen objects.

Cold stimuli lower temperature; water volume cells and wet entities below freezePoint become frozen: water volume surface becomes a walkable ice solid (thickness grows with exposure), wet entities gain frozen (immobilised mechanisms, brittle → fragile multiplier), creatures slowed/frozen via actor properties. Heat melts; ice slabs are physics objects that float and can be broken.
## Scope
- In: Freezing/melting rules with latent time, ice thickness per cell
- In: Frozen water surface colliders generated/removed deterministically
- In: Frozen modifiers: mechanisms jam, fragility ×3, friction → ice
- Out: Player sliding/walking on ice — see e02-water-ice-traversal
- Out: Frost spells — see mw-e08
## Notes
Jammed mechanisms: any mechanism entity with frozen=true refuses to move (e.g. freeze a portcullis winch to stop it closing). Ice collider changes must notify physics to wake bodies resting on it.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a water volume cell at the surface receiving cold until temperature ≤ freezePoint, when resolved, then an ice collider with thickness ≥ 0.1 m exists at that cell and thickness grows with continued cold up to 0.5 m.
- AC-2 [unit] Given any wet entity (wetness ≥ 0.3) cooled below freezePoint, when resolved, then frozen=true and its fragility threshold is divided by 3.
- AC-3 [unit] Given any mechanism entity with frozen=true, when a signal tries to move it, then it does not move and emits a jammed event until thawed.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an ice surface with an object resting on it, when heat melts it, then the collider is removed and the object falls/floats into the water volume on the same tick.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a dry entity (wetness 0) cooled far below freezing, when resolved, then it becomes cold but not frozen (edge: freezing requires water).
- AC-6 [integration] Given the greybox river, when a cold stimulus is swept across it, then the bot can walk across the resulting ice and a replay reproduces the same hashes.

title: Simulate water volumes, splashes, wetness and drying
description:
## Why
Water extinguishes fire, conducts electricity, freezes into bridges and makes creatures vulnerable — it is the most combinatorial element after fire.
## What
As a player, I want water to soak things and put out flames so that dousing a torch or soaking a goblin before a lightning spell just works.

Water volumes (lakes, basins, puddles) with level and drain/fill rates; water stimuli (splash, rain, spell) raise entity wetness and cell moisture; wetness decays by heat and time; entities submerged in a volume become fully wet; puddles spawn from spilled liquid; liquid types (water, oil) share the volume model with different properties (oil floats, flammable).
## Scope
- In: Water volume entity (level, fill/drain), submersion checks, puddle spawning from spills
- In: Wetness gain/decay rules; rain zone stimulus
- In: Liquid types: water, oil (flammable, slippery)
- Out: Freezing — see e03-freeze-melt
- Out: Fluid dynamics / flowing rivers simulation — out of scope (volumes are level-based)
## Notes
Basins with drains/valves are puzzle pieces (see e15-prefab-pieces). Oil on water floats and can burn on the surface — emergent, not scripted.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any entity fully inside a water volume, when a tick runs, then its wetness becomes 1.0.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a wet entity (1.0) at 20°C ambient and no heat source, when time passes, then wetness decays to ≤ 0.1 within the documented drying time; near a burning entity it dries at least 3× faster.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a basin with a drain opened, when ticks run, then level decreases at the drain rate and entities previously submerged emerge when level falls below them.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an oil liquid spilled onto a water volume, when resolved, then an oil layer sits on the surface and igniting it burns the surface layer only.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a water stimulus onto a non-absorbent material (iron), when resolved, then wetness rises but caps at the material absorbency max (edge).

title: Push and pull heavy objects such as crates and statues
description:
## Why
Manipulating statues and moving objects are explicit puzzle examples (Puzzle constitution); knights should shove what others can only drag.
## What
As a player, I want to grab a heavy crate and push or pull it so that I can reach high ledges or weigh down pressure plates.

Objects with pushable=true enter a grab state; movement speed scales with weight vs. actor strength (data), restricted to the object axes if the object declares them (grid statues, rails). Pushing across frozen surfaces is easier (friction from properties).
## Scope
- In: Grab/release, push/pull speed curve by weight and surface friction
- In: Axis/rail-constrained pushables and grid-snapped pushables (for puzzles)
- In: Rotate-in-place affordance for rotatable statues/mirrors
- Out: Puzzle-specific prefabs — see e15-prefab-pieces
## Notes
Speed = base × clamp(strength / (weight × friction), 0, 1); knight strength higher. Friction from world properties (ice ~0.05).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 120 kg crate on stone and a strength profile of 150, when pushed, then movement speed equals the documented formula within 1%.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same crate on a frozen surface, when pushed, then speed is higher than on stone and the crate continues sliding 1.0 m ± 0.2 after release.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a grid-snapped statue, when a push is released mid-cell, then it completes to the next cell centre.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a pushable blocked by a wall or another object, when pushed, then neither the player nor the object moves and no penetration occurs (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a rotatable mirror, when rotate is used, then it turns by its configured step (15°) and emits a rotation-changed event.

title: Pick up, carry, drop and throw liftable objects
description:
## Why
Throwing a bottle to distract a guard, stacking crates to reach a window, or carrying a body out of sight are core systemic verbs.
## What
As a thief, I want to pick up a bottle and throw it so that the noise draws the guard away.

Any entity with liftable and weight ≤ the actor carry limit can be picked up via interaction, held in front (collides), dropped, placed precisely, or thrown with a charge (0.2–1.0 s → 4–14 m/s). Thrown objects are physics objects: they deal impact via e03, break if fragile, and emit noise events. Bodies (unconscious/dead actors) are carriable with slow movement.
## Scope
- In: Carry limit per class (data), carry pose, drop/place/throw
- In: Throw arc preview line (UI hint)
- In: Carrying bodies (heavy carry: 50% speed, no jump)
- Out: Telekinesis lifting — see e03-liftable-levitation (magic uses the same object side)
- Out: Distraction AI response — see mw-e11
## Notes
A thrown burning object remains burning; a thrown oil flask shatters and spills oil (fragile + contents). No special cases — all via properties.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a liftable object weighing 8 kg and a carry limit of 25 kg, when Interact is used, then the object is held; given 40 kg, then the affordance is unavailable with reason "Too heavy".
- AC-2 [unit] Given a held object and throw charged for 1.0 s, when released, then it leaves at 14 m/s ± 0.1 along the aim direction.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a thrown fragile object, when it impacts above its break threshold, then it breaks via e03-breakables and a noise event with the break loudness is emitted.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a held object is set on fire (burning property), when still held after 2.0 s, then the actor takes heat exposure and auto-drops it (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a held object would clip into a wall, when carried, then it is pushed back and never penetrates geometry by > 2 cm.
- AC-6 [unit] Given the player carries a body, when moving, then speed is 50% and jump is disabled.

title: Lock on to and cycle between targets with camera framing
description:
## Why
Knight and archer combat need reliable targeting; poor lock-on makes intrinsically fun combat frustrating.
## What
As a knight, I want to lock onto an enemy and circle-strafe around it so that I can focus on timing and positioning.

Target selection in sim (targetable component, distance ≤ 20 m, within 60° of camera forward, LOS), cycling left/right by screen angle, strafing movement relative to target, lock break on distance > 25 m or LOS lost for > 1.0 s, and camera framing of player + target.
## Scope
- In: Targetable component with lock point(s) and priority
- In: Selection, cycle, break rules; strafe mode in controller
- In: Camera framing lerp that keeps both in view
- Out: Weak-point targeting on bows — see e05-bow-core
- Out: Soft aim assist for spells — see e06-spell-pipeline
## Notes
Targetables can be creatures, but also shootable mechanisms and interactables flagged lockable (lets archers lock onto a distant bell).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given three targetables within the cone, when lock is pressed, then the one nearest the camera forward axis (weighted by distance) is selected, deterministically.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a lock on target A, when cycle-right is pressed, then the next target clockwise in screen angle is selected; with no other targets, lock stays on A.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a locked target moves behind a wall, when 1.0 s elapses without LOS, then the lock breaks; if LOS returns at 0.8 s, the lock persists (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a locked target dies, when resolved, then the lock auto-switches to the next valid target within 10 m or releases.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a lock-on, when move=(1,0), then the player strafes around the target maintaining distance within 5% per second.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox arena with 3 dummies, when the bot locks and cycles, then the HUD lock marker moves across all three and no console errors occur.
notes: 2026-09-29 from mw-e02.9: the gamepad default layout leaves cycleTarget unbound on the pad (RS click is lockOn). Add a right-stick flick to cycle targets while locked on, or bind a pad button, and update docs/design/controls.md.

title: Apply knockback, launches and fall damage to the player controller
description:
## Why
Gust, Thunderclap, explosions, trolls and collapsing floors must move the player through one impulse API; failure (being blasted off a ledge) creates stories.
## What
As a player, I want explosions and heavy blows to physically throw me so that the world feels powerful and dangerous.

The controller accepts impulses from any source (force stimulus from e03, attacks from e04), transitions to a ragdoll-free "launched" airborne state with reduced air control, and computes fall damage from impact speed via data thresholds. Self-cast impulses (a sorcerer using Gust on themselves) are allowed — "too useful" is permitted.
## Scope
- In: Impulse API (vector, source, stagger flag), launched state, recovery
- In: Fall damage curve (safe ≤ 8 m/s impact, lethal ≥ 20 m/s) as data
- In: Landing into water or soft materials (hay, snow) reduces damage via material property
- Out: Stagger/poise — see e04-damage-model
## Notes
Soft landing uses a material property (impactAbsorb) so hay carts and snowdrifts work automatically.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an impulse of 10 m/s horizontal + 5 m/s up, when applied to a grounded player, then the player enters launched state and follows the ballistic arc within 1% error.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an impact speed of 7 m/s, when landing, then no damage event fires; at 14 m/s a damage event matching the data curve fires.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a landing surface with impactAbsorb=0.8 (hay), when landing at 14 m/s, then damage is reduced by 80%.
- AC-4 [unit] Given two impulses in the same tick, when resolved, then they sum and the result is order-independent (deterministic).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a launched player hits a wall mid-flight, when resolved, then horizontal velocity is removed and wall-impact damage uses the same curve (edge).

title: Wade and swim in water and slide on frozen surfaces
description:
## Why
"Magic can freeze water … open traversal opportunities." Freezing a lake to walk across it must emerge from properties, not a scripted bridge.
## What
As a sorcerer, I want to freeze a river and walk across it so that magic opens new routes.

Water volumes (from e03) drive wading (depth 0.5–1.2 m, speed reduction), swimming (> 1.2 m; no weapons, limited breath), and diving. Frozen water becomes a walkable solid with low friction (ice sliding, reduced accel). Melting ice drops the player back into water.
## Scope
- In: Wade/swim/dive states, breath meter (20 s default), drowning damage hook
- In: Low-friction movement on any surface with frozen state or friction < 0.2
- In: Transitions when water freezes/melts under the player
- Out: Water/freezing simulation — see e03-water-wetness, e03-freeze-melt
- Out: Drowning damage numbers — see e04-damage-model
## Notes
Swimming makes the player wet (sets wet property on the actor), which matters for fire and electricity.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given water depth 0.9 m, when moving, then the player wades at 60% run speed and footstep events report material water.
- AC-2 [unit] Given depth 1.5 m, when entered, then the player swims, breath depletes over 20 s underwater, and damage events fire each 1 s after depletion.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a water volume transitions to frozen while the player swims on the surface, when resolved, then the player is placed on top of the ice rather than embedded in it (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a frozen surface, when the player stops input at run speed, then they slide ≥ 2.0 m before stopping (vs ≤ 0.5 m on stone).
- AC-5 [unit] Given the player stands on ice that melts, when the tick runs, then the player drops into the water volume and state becomes wading/swimming.
- AC-6 [unit] Given the player exits a water volume, when checked, then the actor wet property is set to 1.0 and decays per e03 drying rules.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: From mw-e04.19: fall damage takes a LiquidDepthReader (installEnvironmentDamage option liquidDepth, default noLiquid). When water volumes exist, pass one that reports liquid depth over the landing feet so ≥1.5 m deep water cancels fall damage in play (AC-2 of e04.19 is tested with a stub reader).

title: Climb ladders, ivy, ropes and rough walls marked climbable
description:
## Why
Climbing is a core thief verb and an alternate-route generator; burning the ivy or freezing the wall should change it (systemic).
## What
As a thief, I want to climb any surface the world marks as climbable so that I can find routes others cannot.

Climb state attaches the player to a climbable surface (ladder, rope, ivy, rough stone), moves in surface space, transitions to ledge mantle at the top, and detaches on jump-off. Climbability comes only from world properties (climbable grade + capability requirement), so fire removing ivy or ice making walls slippery works automatically.
## Scope
- In: Climb attach/detach, surface-space movement (0.8 m/s default), corner transitions ≤ 45°
- In: Ropes (vertical, swaying anchor) and ladders (all classes), grade-gated walls (thief capability)
- In: Stamina hook (value from progression) and fall on stamina exhaustion
- Out: Climbing claws/tools — see mw-e10
- Out: Rope arrows — see mw-e05 (they spawn a climbable rope entity)
## Notes
Rope arrows, vines spell, and a knight propping a ladder all work by spawning entities with the climbable property — no special cases.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a surface with climbable=ladder, when any class presses toward it, then they attach and climb at 1.2 m/s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a surface with climbable=rough and requiresCapability=climb.rough, when a class without it approaches, then no attach occurs; with it, attach succeeds.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a climbing player whose ivy surface loses the climbable property (e.g. burned away), when the next tick runs, then the player detaches and falls (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a runtime-spawned rope entity with climbable=rope, when approached, then the player can climb it exactly like an authored rope.
- AC-5 [unit] Given stamina reaches 0 while climbing, when the tick runs, then the player slips and falls.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox climbing wall, when the bot climbs to the top and mantles, then it reaches the upper platform with no console errors.

title: Mantle onto and grab ledges detected from world geometry
description:
## Why
Classes change possibilities: "the thief might climb through a window". Verticality is also a stealth factor. Every class needs baseline mantling; thieves go further.
## What
As a player, I want to jump at a ledge and pull myself up so that I can reach windows, crates and balconies.

Ledge detection uses forward + down shape casts against surfaces with the ledge/climbable markup, validates headroom and standing space, and performs: auto-mantle (≤ 1.0 m), mantle (≤ 1.6 m, all classes), ledge grab/hang with shimmy and pull-up (≤ 2.2 m reach, capability-gated), and drop-down to hang from an edge.
## Scope
- In: Ledge query + validation (headroom, surface angle ≤ 20°, clearance)
- In: Mantle, ledge hang, shimmy, pull-up, drop, jump-back states
- In: Capability gates (e.g. ledge hang may require climbing capability per class data)
- Out: Free climbing walls — see e02-climb-surfaces
- Out: Surface markup authoring — see e03-climbable-surfaces
## Notes
Mantle is deterministic and uses sim-driven motion curves, not root motion. Heavy encumbrance may block pull-up (data).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 1.4 m crate edge ahead and jump pressed while moving forward, when resolved, then the player mantles onto the top in 0.6 s ± 0.05 and ends grounded on it.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a ledge with 1.0 m headroom above it, when mantle is attempted, then it is rejected unless crouched mantle fits (capsule check) (edge).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a player hanging from a ledge, when moving sideways, then they shimmy at 1.0 m/s and stop at ledge ends or gaps > 0.3 m.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a class without ledge-hang capability, when jumping at a 2.0 m ledge, then no grab occurs and the player falls normally.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a ledge surface that becomes frozen or burning (via e03 properties), when hanging, then the player is forced to drop after the configured grace time (1.0 s).
- AC-6 [integration] Given the greybox traversal course, when the golden mantle replay runs, then state hashes match.

title: Emit footstep events tagged with surface material and gait
description:
## Why
Surfaces matter to stealth (Thief constitution) and footsteps are a key audio feedback channel (E28).
## What
As a thief, I want gravel to be louder than carpet and wet stone to sound different so that I choose my path deliberately.

The sim emits footstep events at stride intervals carrying position, foot, surface material (from world properties of the ground collider), wetness/frozen state, gait and loudness = profile noise × material loudness.
## Scope
- In: Stride-distance based footstep cadence per gait
- In: Ground material lookup via e03-world-properties (including wet, frozen, burning states)
- In: Event consumed by audio and stealth (via event bus)
- Out: Sound propagation/perception — see e09-sound-propagation
- Out: Footstep SFX assets — see mw-e38
## Notes
Material loudness examples (data): carpet 0.3, wood 0.7, stone 0.8, gravel 1.2, shallow water 1.3, ice 0.9. Loudness is data, not code.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a player walking 10 m at walk speed, when footsteps are counted, then the count equals floor(10 / strideLength) ± 1.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the ground collider has material gravel, when a step lands, then event.material = gravel and loudness = profileNoise × 1.2.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a stone floor with wet=0.8, when stepping, then the event carries wet=true and loudness uses the wet-stone modifier.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player is airborne or standing still, when ticks elapse, then no footstep events are emitted (edge).

title: Enforce input latency and controller cost budgets in the perf suite
description:
## Why
"Responsive" must be a number. The contract requires numeric feel targets and perf budgets on the reference machine.
## What
Add Playwright perf tests measuring input-to-motion latency (synthetic key event timestamp → first rendered frame where the player transform changed) and controller + camera CPU cost per tick; wire into e32 budgets.
## Scope
- In: Latency probe hook in dev builds only
- In: Budgets: input-to-motion ≤ 100 ms p95 (target ≤ 50 ms), controller sim ≤ 0.3 ms/tick p95, camera ≤ 0.2 ms/frame p95
- Out: General frame-time budgets — see e32-perf-budgets
## Notes
Latency probe must be stripped from production bundles (check bundle for the probe symbol).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the greybox testbed on the reference machine (High), when 50 synthetic move key presses are measured, then input-to-motion latency is ≤ 100 ms at p95.
- AC-2 [perf] Given 60 s of scripted traversal, when profiled, then controller sim cost ≤ 0.3 ms per tick p95 and camera ≤ 0.2 ms per frame p95.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a production build, when the bundle is scanned, then the latency probe symbol is absent.
- AC-4 [perf] Given a simulated 30 fps render (low preset worst case), when measured, then input-to-motion latency is ≤ 133 ms p95 (edge).

title: VFX stress scene, quality tiers and auto-degrade
description:
## Why
Spectacle must never break frame pacing on the target hardware (hardware baseline).

## What
A combat stress scene: 12 creatures, 4 simultaneous spells, fire spreading over 10 objects, 2 destructions. Budgets added to the e32 suite. Quality tiers per preset, plus auto-degrade: when frame time exceeds budget for 2 s, halve emission rates, then disable distortion, then reduce decal cap; recover after 10 s under budget.

## Scope
- In: Stress scene, budget assertions, auto-degrade controller
- Out: Global perf suite (e32-perf-budgets)

## Notes
Cites contract baseline: High 60 fps reference machine at 1440p-equivalent; Low 60 fps at 1080p, 30 fps floor in worst-case combat on Iris Xe / base M1 class.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the stress scene on the reference machine (High), when measured for 60 s, then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms.
- AC-2 [perf] Given the stress scene on the Low preset on a base-M1-class device, when measured, then frame rate never drops below 30 fps.
- AC-3 [unit] Given frame time over budget for 2 s, when the controller evaluates, then emission rates halve; after 10 s under budget, they restore.
- AC-4 [unit] Given frame time spikes shorter than 2 s, when evaluated, then no degradation occurs.

title: World-space awareness indicators and optional noise ripples
description:
## Why
Stealth must be readable: players need to see who is suspicious and how noisy they were, without an all-knowing eye icon.

## What
As a thief, I want to see how aware each creature is and, optionally, how far my noise carried so that I can make informed stealth decisions.
World-space awareness indicator above creatures reflecting e11 alert states (Unaware hidden → Suspicious fill → Investigating → Searching → Alerted → Combat), shape-coded as well as colour-coded for colour-blind players; optional last-known-position ghost marker (assist); optional noise ripple visualisation from e09 noise events (assist, off by default); extinguish puff when lights go out.

## Scope
- In: Indicators, assist visuals, colour-blind-safe shapes
- Out: Alert-state logic (e11-alert-states)
- Out: Player visibility meter HUD (stealth group)

## Notes
Related: coordinate with the stealth group's HUD so indicators and meters share a visual language.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a creature entering Suspicious with suspicion 0.4, when rendered, then its indicator shows the Suspicious shape filled 40%.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a creature in Unaware state, when rendered, then no indicator is visible.
- AC-3 [unit] Given colour-blind simulation (deuteranopia filter), when states are compared, then every state remains distinguishable by shape alone.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the noise ripple assist off (default), when a noise event occurs, then no ripple renders.

title: Arrow VFX: trails, payload bursts, stuck and broken arrows
description:
## Why
Trick arrows need readable visuals — a splash, an unfurling rope, a rattle ring — so players understand what each did.

## What
As an archer, I want each arrow type to show clearly what it did so that trick arrows are readable.
Arrow trail (brighter for focused shots), flame on fire-arrow shafts, water burst + wet decal, rope unfurl ribbon, subtle ring pulse for noise arrows, dust for blunt impacts, deflect sparks, stuck-arrow wobble on impact, broken-arrow mesh swap when not retrievable.

## Scope
- In: Effects and cue rules for arrow events
- Out: Arrow models (asset group)

## Notes
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a water arrow impact, when processed, then the burst spawns and a wet decal appears matching the 1.5 m radius.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an arrow that sticks intact, when it impacts, then it wobbles for 400 ms; a broken one shows the broken mesh.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a deflected arrow, when processed, then deflect sparks spawn at the contact point.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a focused shot, when its trail spawns, then the focused trail variant is used.

title: Spell VFX slots and templates for the spell pipeline
description:
## Why
Every spell should look spectacular from day one by composing templates, before bespoke art (Magic should feel magical).

## What
As a designer, I want to give a spell cast, projectile, impact, area and beam visuals by choosing templates and tints so that new spells look good without custom VFX code.
Standard slots consumed by the VFX layer: `castWindup`, `castRelease`, `projectile` (head + trail), `impact`, `area` (ring/volume sized to spell radius), `beam` (start/end sockets, width), `sustainOnTarget`, `summon`/`dissolve`. Templates for each with tint/scale params. Interface documented in docs/vfx/spell-hooks.md for the magic group.

## Scope
- In: Slot definitions, templates, docs, a demo spell in the testbed
- Out: Spell data and effects logic (e06-spell-pipeline)
- Out: Signature spell art (sorcerer/asset groups)

## Notes
Related: e06-spell-pipeline should depend on this item for visuals; not expressed here to avoid blocking VFX on the magic group.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given a spell VFX block using templates only, when validated, then it passes and resolves every slot to an effect.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an area spell with radius 4 m, when it resolves, then the area template renders a ring 4 m in radius.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a beam spell, when its caster moves, then the beam start follows the cast socket every frame.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a spell VFX block missing an optional slot, when cast, then that slot is skipped without error.

title: Destruction VFX: fracture chunks, dust and crack stages
description:
## Why
Smashing a wall has to look as good as it feels; crack stages make breakable things readable (Zelda-like readability).

## What
As a knight, I want smashed walls and crates to burst convincingly and cracked walls to look weak so that I know what I can break.
On `ObjectBroken`: pre-fractured chunk meshes when available, otherwise procedural box chunks for greybox; dust cloud; cosmetic debris render-only (cap 200 pieces, fade after 8 s) — gameplay rubble remains sim physics from e03. Crack stage visuals (0/1/2) for `breakable` objects so weak walls read as weak before any hit.

## Scope
- In: Chunk spawner, dust, cosmetic debris cap/fade, crack stage materials
- Out: Break rules (e04-smash-breakables)
- Out: Fractured art assets (asset group)

## Notes
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a weak wall broken, when processed, then chunks and a dust cloud spawn and cosmetic debris count stays ≤ 200.
- AC-2 [integration] Given crack stage 1 in sim, when rendered, then the stage-1 crack material is applied.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 250 cosmetic debris requests, when processed, then the oldest 50 are removed.
- AC-4 [perf] Given 3 simultaneous wall breaks, when measured, then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms on the reference machine (High).

title: Visuals derived from element states: burning, wet, frozen, shock
description:
## Why
Systemic visuals mean any object that catches fire looks on fire without per-object authoring — the visual half of the property engine.

## What
As a player, I want anything burning, wet, frozen or electrified to look it so that I can read the world's state at a glance.
The VFX layer observes e03 element states on any entity: `burning` → flame emitter scaled to bounds + smoke; `wet` → darkened material + drips; `frozen` → frost shader + ice crust; `electrified` → arcs; transitions (e.g. burning→wet) → steam puff; gas volumes → tinted fog. Pure presentation — states come from the sim.

## Scope
- In: State observers, bounds-scaled emitters, material parameter blending, transition effects
- Out: Element rules (e03-element-propagation)
- Out: Light emission from fire (e03-light-field)

## Notes
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given any entity gaining `burning`, when observed, then a flame emitter sized to its bounds attaches within one frame; losing `burning` stops it.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an entity transitioning from `burning` to `wet`, when observed, then a steam puff spawns once.
- AC-3 [integration] Given 30 burning objects, when the budget is exceeded, then farthest flames drop to a low LOD before any are culled.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an entity with both `wet` and `frozen`, when material params resolve, then frozen takes precedence per the documented order.
- AC-5 [manual] Given a greybox room with mixed element states, when three playtesters are asked what state each object is in, then they identify ≥ 90% correctly.

title: Magical material library: dissolve, glow, distortion, runes
description:
## Why
"Magic should feel magical." A shared shader library gives spells, summons and deaths a consistent, spectacular look.

## What
As a designer, I want a library of magical materials so that spells, summons and deaths share a spectacular, consistent look.
Reusable materials/shaders: dissolve (death, summon, illusion fade), fresnel glow, heat-haze/distortion (High only; Low falls back to none), rune decal projection, emissive pulse, soft particles with depth fade. Parameterised for tint and intensity. Creature death uses dissolve by default (skeletons collapse then dissolve).

## Scope
- In: Shader/material set, parameters, Low-preset fallbacks, creature death dissolve
- Out: Spell-specific art (sorcerer/asset groups)

## Notes
Renderer-specific; covered by Playwright screenshot sanity + perf.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a material test scene, when each shader renders, then screenshot sanity checks pass and no shader compile errors are logged in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the Low preset, when distortion is requested, then it is skipped and no distortion pass runs.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a creature `Died` event, when processed, then the dissolve runs over 1.2 s and the render entity is removed afterwards.
- AC-4 [perf] Given 6 simultaneous distortion effects on High, when measured, then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms on the reference machine.

title: Weapon swing trails and charge build-up glow
description:
## Why
Trails make arcs and reach readable — useful for learning timing — and add spectacle to heavy blows.

## What
As a knight, I want to see the arc of my swings and my charge building so that reach and timing are readable.
Ribbon trails from weapon sockets rendered only during active frames (from sim phase), tinted by dominant damage type; charge build-up glow stepping at 33/66/100% charge with a burst on `ChargeReady`; faint trails on focused arrows. Socket samples smoothed with Catmull-Rom; max 8 concurrent trails.

## Scope
- In: Trail renderer, phase binding, tint mapping, charge glow
- Out: Weapon models (art)

## Notes
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a light attack, when it runs, then the trail is visible only on frames whose sim tick lies in the active window.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a fire-damage weapon, when swung, then the trail uses the fire tint from data.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 9 trail requests, when processed, then the oldest trail is released and 8 remain.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a charged heavy reaching full charge, when `ChargeReady` fires, then the burst effect spawns at the weapon socket.

title: Camera shake, damage vignette and low-health effects
description:
## Why
Screen feedback sells impact and danger, but must respect motion sensitivity and photosensitivity.

## What
As a player, I want the camera to react to big impacts and the screen to warn me when I am hurt so that danger is felt — and I want to turn it down if it bothers me.
Trauma-based shake (trauma 0–1, offset ∝ trauma², decay 1.5/s; light hit 0.15, heavy 0.3, guard break 0.5, explosions distance-scaled). Shake scale slider 0–100% and reduce-motion toggle via e31-settings-framework. Damage vignette for 300 ms scaled by % health lost; desaturation below 25% health. No full-screen flash more than 3 times per second (WCAG 2.3.1).

## Scope
- In: Shake model, vignette, low-health grade, settings hooks, flash limiter
- Out: Camera rig itself (e02-camera)
- Out: Hit-stop timing (e04-hit-stop)

## Notes
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given trauma 0.3 added, when 200 ms pass with no new trauma, then trauma is 0.0 (0.3 − 1.5 × 0.2).
- AC-2 [unit] Given shake scale 0% or reduce-motion on, when trauma is added, then camera offset is exactly 0.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 5 flash requests within 1 s, when processed, then at most 3 full-screen flashes render.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a hit removing 40% of health, when processed, then vignette intensity is 0.4 of max and fades by 300 ms.
- AC-5 [manual] Given A/B shake settings, when three playtesters fight for 3 minutes, then none report nausea at the default and all rate impact ≥ 4/5.

title: Impact VFX by material: sparks, splinters, bone dust, parry flash
description:
## Why
Visible impacts confirm hits instantly and give combat its crunch; the stylised, gore-free look fits the warmer tone.

## What
As a knight, I want every hit to burst with a material-appropriate effect so that I can see what connected and how hard.
Effects: metal sparks, wood splinters, bone chips/dust, stylised ichor puff (no gore), stone chips; block sparks/wood chips; parry flash (radial star + brief bloom boost, never culled); guard-break shatter ring; critical/riposte burst. Enemy hit flash (emissive white 80 ms). Oriented to hit normal, scaled by damage tier.

## Scope
- In: Effect definitions, cue rules, hit flash material param
- Out: Final textures (asset group)
- Out: Screen shake (e29-screen-feedback)

## Notes
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a sword hitting a metal-armored target, when `DamageApplied` fires, then the metal-sparks effect spawns at the contact point oriented to the hit normal.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a parry at the particle cap, when it fires, then the parry flash still spawns (priority highest) and lower-priority particles are culled.
- AC-3 [integration] Given any damaged creature, when hit, then its emissive flash lasts 80 ms ± one frame.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a material pair with no specific rule, when resolved, then a generic impact puff spawns (never nothing).
- AC-5 [manual] Given the sandbox, when three playtesters fight, then each can say which hits were blocked versus clean from visuals alone.

title: Audio performance and download budgets
description:
## Why
Audio must fit the hardware baseline: ≤ 50 MB initial download and steady 60 fps.

## What
Budgets added to the e32 perf suite: decoded audio memory ≤ 96 MB; main-thread audio work ≤ 0.5 ms/frame p95; voices ≤ 48 High / 24 Low; audio share of initial download ≤ 12 MB (music streamed); format strategy (Opus in WebM/Ogg with AAC fallback for Safari).

## Scope
- In: Budget assertions, format pipeline, lazy-load per area
- Out: Global perf suite (e32-perf-budgets)

## Notes
Cites the contract hardware baseline; no new targets invented beyond audio shares.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the combat stress scene, when profiled on the reference machine, then main-thread audio work ≤ 0.5 ms per frame p95.
- AC-2 [perf] Given a cold load of the vertical slice, when measured, then audio bytes before playable ≤ 12 MB.
- AC-3 [perf] Given a 20-minute scripted session, when measured, then decoded audio memory never exceeds 96 MB.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given Safari (WebKit), when sounds load, then the AAC fallback is selected and plays without errors.

title: Directional sound captions for important cues
description:
## Why
Deaf and hard-of-hearing players need footsteps behind them and attack telegraphs as much as anyone (E31 accessibility).

## What
As a player, I want captions for important sounds with a direction hint so that I do not miss audio-only information.
Cue-sheet rules may flag `caption: <stringId>`; captions show text such as "[Footsteps, behind left]" with a direction arrow relative to the camera, only for sources within 20 m, de-duplicated per source for 2 s, max 4 visible. Toggle and text size via e31-settings-framework.

## Scope
- In: Caption flag in cue data, caption UI, direction computation, settings
- Out: Dialogue subtitles (dialogue group)

## Notes
Initial flagged cues: footsteps (creatures), creature telegraphs, alert barks, noise-arrow rattle, door open/close, breaking objects.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a flagged cue from a source 135° to the camera's left-rear, when captioned, then the direction label is "behind left".
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same source triggering 5 times in 1 s, when captioned, then only one caption shows.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a flagged source 25 m away, when it plays, then no caption appears.
- AC-4 [unit] Given 6 simultaneous captions, when rendered, then the 4 highest-priority show.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given captions enabled in settings, when a creature telegraph plays in the sandbox, then the caption appears within 100 ms.

title: Ambient beds and randomised positional one-shots
description:
## Why
Dripping caves and rustling forests make exploration rewarding even when nothing is fighting you (The world rewards curiosity).

## What
As a player, I want each place to have its own living soundscape so that quiet exploration is atmospheric.
Per-zone ambient bed loops (2 s crossfade) plus randomised positional one-shots (drips, wind gusts, distant birds, creaks) with min/max interval and spawn radius, defined in zone data and placed via e03-triggers.

## Scope
- In: Ambience zone data, bed crossfades, one-shot scheduler
- Out: Ambience assets (asset group)

## Notes

**Integration note:** Promoted to P1 — the MVP ambience beds (town, wilds, dungeon, river, harbour) are P1 and play through this runtime.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a one-shot with interval 4–9 s, when 10 minutes elapse, then every gap falls within [4, 9] s.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the listener crossing between two ambience zones, when processed, then beds crossfade over 2 s with no gap in loudness greater than 3 dB.
- AC-3 [unit] Given one-shot spawn radius 10–25 m, when spawned, then each position lies within that annulus around the listener.

title: Adaptive music controller with layered stems and stingers
description:
## Why
Music that swells into combat and relaxes afterwards carries mood without despair (tone: warmer souls-like).

## What
As a player, I want the music to follow the tension of the moment so that exploration, stealth and combat each feel distinct.
A music controller playing location tracks as synchronised stems (explore, tension, stealth, combat), cross-fading layers on bar boundaries using BPM metadata (within 2 bars). Combat layer enters on alert state Combat and exits 8 s after no hostile remains in Combat. Stinger hook events (from e28-creature-audio-hooks) play one-shots quantised to the next beat. Music streams via media elements to protect the initial download budget.

## Scope
- In: Stem sync, bar-quantised crossfades, state bindings, stingers, streaming
- Out: Music composition in Suno (asset group, e38)

## Notes
Placeholder stems: simple generated drones/pulses at 90 BPM until Suno tracks integrate.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 90 BPM track and a layer change requested mid-bar, when processed, then the crossfade starts on the next bar boundary (≤ 2.67 s).
- AC-2 [integration] Given combat ends, when 8 s pass with no creature in Combat state, then the combat layer fades out; if combat resumes at 6 s, then it does not.
- AC-3 [integration] Given all four stems playing, when measured after 5 minutes, then stem drift is ≤ 10 ms.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a music track fails to load, when the controller starts, then it continues silently and logs once without affecting sfx.

title: Mix snapshots and ducking for combat, stealth and menus
description:
## Why
The mix should focus attention: a parry should cut through the music, and a pause menu should feel like a breath.

## What
As a player, I want the mix to shift with the situation so that important sounds cut through when they matter.
Snapshots (explore, stealth, combat, menu, paused) define bus gains and filters (paused = low-pass 800 Hz on sfx/ambience). Transitions ramp 250–1500 ms. Ducking: music and ambience duck −6 dB for 400 ms on parry/critical; sfx ducks −4 dB under UI stingers. Snapshot selection follows game state (alert state via e11-alert-states, pause menu).

## Scope
- In: Snapshot data, transition ramps, ducking rules, state bindings
- Out: Adaptive music layers (e28-adaptive-music)

## Notes
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the explore snapshot, when the game enters Combat alert state, then bus gains ramp to combat values over the configured duration.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a parry event, when processed, then music and ambience are −6 dB for 400 ms and restore with a 200 ms ramp.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the pause menu opens, when the snapshot applies, then sfx/ambience are low-passed at 800 Hz and restore on close.
- AC-4 [unit] Given two overlapping duck requests, when processed, then attenuation takes the deepest value, not the sum.

title: Creature audio slots and audible attack telegraphs
description:
## Why
Creatures feel alive through sound, and an audible telegraph before a big attack is key to Zelda-like readability.

## What
As a player, I want creatures to sound distinct and warn me audibly before big attacks so that I can react without staring at them.
Creature schema audio slots: idle loop, footstep set, alert bark, attack telegraph, hurt, poise break, death. Telegraph cues play on `TelegraphStarted` and must start ≥ 250 ms before active frames; unblockable moves use a distinct high-priority telegraph. Alert-state transitions (Suspicious, Alerted, Combat) expose hook events for stingers.

## Scope
- In: Schema audio slots, telegraph cue playback, alert-state hook events
- Out: Creature sound creation (asset group)
- Out: Alert-state logic (e11-alert-states)

## Notes
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given creature data, when validated, then every creature declares all required audio slots (placeholder ids allowed).
- AC-2 [integration] Given a skeleton starting an unblockable move, when `TelegraphStarted` fires, then the unblockable telegraph cue plays ≥ 250 ms before the move's first active tick.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a creature transitioning Suspicious→Alerted, when the event fires, then the alert bark plays at its position and a `MusicStinger` hook event is emitted.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature dies while its idle loop plays, when `Died` is processed, then the loop stops within 200 ms and the death cue plays.

title: Bow audio: draw creak, release, flyby and payload cues
description:
## Why
A creaking draw and a sharp release make the bow feel tense and powerful (Archery epic outcome: bows feel excellent).

## What
As an archer, I want the bow to creak as I draw and arrows to whistle past so that shots feel tense and physical.
Draw creak loop whose playbackRate (0.9→1.1) and gain follow draw fraction; focused-release chime; release twang by draw strength; arrow flyby when passing within 3 m of the listener (pitch bend simulating doppler); impacts reuse the combat material matrix; ricochet; trick payload cues (ignite, splash, rope unfurl, rattle); pickup cue on retrieval.

## Scope
- In: Continuous draw loop control, flyby detection, cue rules for bow events
- Out: Final bow SFX (asset group)

## Notes
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given draw fraction 0.5, when the creak loop updates, then playbackRate is 1.0 and gain is the 50% curve value.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an arrow passing 2 m from the listener, when its closest approach occurs, then one flyby cue plays; at 4 m, then none.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a focused release event, when processed, then the chime plays in the same frame as the release twang.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the draw is cancelled, when processed, then the creak loop fades out within 100 ms and no release twang plays.

title: Surface-aware footsteps modulated by stance and armor
description:
## Why
Footsteps ground the character in the world and teach players how loud they are — the audible face of the stealth system.

## What
As a player, I want footsteps that change with the surface, my stance and my armor so that I can hear where and how I am moving.
Foot plant events from animation, with a stride-distance fallback (every 0.7 m walking, 1.1 m running). Surface from the ground collider material tag (stone, wood, dirt, grass, shallow-water, metal, rug, gravel). Crouch −10 dB, sprint +3 dB; armor layer (chain jingle / plate clank) by e04-armor-weight class; landing sounds scale with fall height. Creatures use the same system with their own sets.

## Scope
- In: Foot plant bridge, surface lookup, stance/armor modulation, landings, creature reuse
- Out: Sim noise emission for stealth (e09-sound-propagation) — audio reads the same surface table but never emits sim noise

## Notes
Shared read-only surface table keeps audible loudness consistent with stealth noise values.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player walking from stone onto wood, when the next foot plant occurs, then a wood footstep variant plays.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a crouched player, when a footstep cue resolves, then its volume is 10 dB below the standing value.
- AC-3 [unit] Given no animation foot plant events (fallback mode), when the player walks 3.5 m, then exactly 5 footsteps play.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unknown surface tag, when resolved, then the stone set plays and a dev warning names the tag once.
- AC-5 [integration] Given plate armor, when walking, then each footstep also plays the plate layer.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: Placeholder footstep sets now exist (mw-e28.2): sfx-foot-{stone,wood,dirt,grass,gravel,water-shallow}-{sneak,walk,run} (4 variants each) and sfx-foot-land-{light,heavy} on the footsteps bus, loudness-ordered per audio bible 7.3. No footstep cue sheet/cue event yet: LocomotionEvents is not in src/content/cue-events.ts, so this bead should add the cue event binding + a footsteps cue sheet; they will be audible in the testbed through the cue bridge wired in main.ts.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: Implemented without mw-e02.11: the cue lookups read the surface from the collider the character stands on (CharacterController.groundBody -> bound entity -> material.footstepSurface), read-only in presentation. When mw-e02.11 puts the material on the footstep event, the LocomotionEvents reader can prefer it. Armour layer rules exist but are silent in-game until mw-e04.16 (follow-up mw-e28.18).

title: Per-bus volume settings, tab-hidden mute and mono option
description:
## Why
Players must control their mix; accessibility options such as mono downmix matter for hearing-impaired players (E31).

## What
As a player, I want volume sliders per category and audio accessibility options so that I can hear the game the way I need.
Sliders for master, music, sfx, ambience, ui (0–100 mapped to a perceptual −60..0 dB curve, 0 = mute); mute when tab hidden (default on); mono downmix; "night mode" dynamic range compressor. Persisted through e31-settings-framework, applied with a 50 ms ramp (no clicks).

## Scope
- In: Bus gain control, settings entries, persistence, ramps, mono and compressor options
- Out: Mix snapshots/ducking (e28-mix-snapshots)
- Out: Sound captions (e28-sound-captions)

## Notes
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given sfx slider set to 50, when applied, then the sfx bus gain equals the curve value for 50 and ramps over 50 ms.
- AC-2 [unit] Given slider 0, when applied, then the bus gain is exactly 0.
- AC-3 [integration] Given tab-hidden mute on, when `visibilitychange` reports hidden, then master ramps to 0; on visible, it restores the previous value.
- AC-4 [integration] Given settings changed and the page reloaded, when the audio engine boots, then saved bus volumes are applied before the first sound plays.
- AC-5 [unit] Given mono downmix on, when a hard-left panned source plays, then both output channels carry equal signal.

title: Combat impact audio matrix: hits, blocks, parries, whiffs
description:
## Why
Sound carries half of combat weight; a parry must ring out and a heavy blow must thud (Combat is intrinsically fun).

## What
As a knight, I want every hit, block and parry to sound distinct so that I can read the fight by ear.
Impact matrix: attacker material (blade, blunt-wood, blunt-metal, claw, bone, arrow) × target material (flesh, bone, metal armor, wood shield, metal shield, stone, wood) → cue. Distinct high-priority cues for block, parry (never stolen), guard break, riposte, wall recoil; whooshes by weapon class and light/heavy; stamina-rejected wheeze; charge-ready. Impact cues start on the first hit-stop frame; volume tier by light/heavy/critical.

## Scope
- In: Cue sheet rules, material tags on moves/hurtboxes, parry priority, hit-stop sync
- Out: Final SFX (asset group)
- Out: Creature vocals (e28-creature-audio-hooks)

## Notes
Uses placeholders from e28-placeholder-sounds until final assets integrate.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a sword hitting a skeleton (bone), when `DamageApplied` fires, then the blade×bone cue plays at the victim position.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a successful parry during a 48-voice saturation test, when it fires, then the parry cue plays (not stolen) and a lower-priority voice is dropped.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a heavy hit with 5-tick hit-stop, when it lands, then the impact cue starts within the first frozen frame (≤ 17 ms after the event).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a material pair without a specific rule, when resolved, then the attacker-material generic cue plays (no silence).
- AC-5 [manual] Given the sandbox, when three playtesters close their eyes during a dummy fight, then each can distinguish block, parry and clean hit by sound alone.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: Parry: no sim event until mw-e04.12, so no parry rule yet; AC-2 moves to mw-e28.16. AC-5 (manual listening) is mw-e28.17. Wall recoil / charge-ready need sim events: mw-e28.19. Blocks, guard breaks, whiffs (DodgedHit), whooshes (ActionPhaseChanged + move presentation.audioCue) and the slash/blunt/pierce x material matrix are in.

title: Greybox archery range for tuning and e2e tests
description:
## Why
Draw timing, drop and trick arrows need a fast, repeatable test space just as melee has the combat sandbox.

## What
As a developer, I want an archery range scene so that I can tune ballistics and verify trick arrows quickly.
Static targets at 10/20/40/60 m, targets on rails at 2/4/6 m/s, a 6 m elevated platform, an overhead wooden beam (rope anchor), a brazier, a `shootable` bell wired to a door, a `cuttable` rope holding a crate, a pool of water. Stats overlay: hit %, flight time, impact speed, focused-shot rate.

## Scope
- In: Scene, fixtures, stats overlay, deterministic seed
- Out: Final art for the range (none planned)

## Notes
Lives alongside the combat sandbox under /dev/archery.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the range loaded in Chromium, when it boots, then all fixtures exist, no console errors occur and the overlay reads 0 shots.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the rail targets, when 10 s elapse, then their positions match the deterministic schedule within 0.01 m.
