1. **Default for bulk props, environments, modular architecture and most characters: CC0 low-poly kits** (KayKit + Quaternius as the primary families, Kenney for gaps). They are already chunky/bevelled, use gradient/palette atlases that we recolour with `tex-palette-master-01`, and carry zero licence risk. Mixing kit families is the main consistency risk — mitigated by one shared stylized material and palette remap.
2. **Animations: CC0 first** (KayKit character animations, Quaternius Universal Animation Library) retargeted to one humanoid skeleton. **Mixamo only as fallback**: its terms allow use in games but restrict redistributing raw animation files, and our repo is public — only commit animations baked into our own .glb, never raw FBX, and record the decision in the ADR.
3. **Hero/unique assets (minotaur, bespoke NPCs such as the bookseller, unique props): Meshy** is the named candidate (owner preference), contested by **Tripo** in the bake-off. Flow: approved GPT reference sheet → image-to-3D → remesh/retopo to budget (≤ 20 k tris minotaur, 4–7 k key NPC) → auto-rig → export glTF → gltf-transform (meshopt + KTX2) → renderer.
4. **No DCC at all:** the owner never opens Blender. Everything is API + gltf-transform CLI (simplify/weld/compress/pivot/scale fixes) scripted by Claude; if a model needs manual DCC fixes to be usable, that counts against it in scoring.
5. **Workflow (style bible §17.2):** concept → OWNER GATE (flat image) → API image-to-3D → remesh/retopo → rig/animate via API → glb → validator → turntable preview → OWNER GATE (turntable) → commit + CREDITS + approvals.

**Meshy facts (owner-verified, Sept 2026):** Web app — Free = 100 credits/mo, outputs **CC BY 4.0** (attribution in `assets/CREDITS.md` + in-game credits — acceptable for this free game); Pro = $20/mo ($240/yr), 1,000 credits/mo, private licence; image-to-3D 25 (Meshy 7) / 20 (Meshy 6), text-to-3D 20 (Meshy 6 only), AI texturing 10, remesh/rigging/animation free in-app. **API (what Claude uses): prepaid API credits** — image-to-3D 30 (2K textures), remesh 5, rigging 5, animation 3 per action ⇒ ≈ 46 credits for one hero with 2 actions. Confirm output licence for API-generated assets in the ADR.
**Tripo facts (Aug–Sep 2026, official pricing page blocked — medium confidence, re-verify):** Web — Free 200–300 credits/mo, **CC BY 4.0**, ~15 downloads/mo cap; Pro $19.90/mo with ~3,000 credits. **API: $0.01/credit** — image-to-3D 20–30, smart low-poly retopo 30, auto-rig 25, animation retarget 10 each ⇒ ≈ 95–105 credits (≈ $1) per hero with 2 actions.

**Bake-off scoring rubric (each 1–5, weighted):** topology & tri count after reduction to budget (×3), texture fidelity vs style bible palette/painted look (×3), rig quality — deformation at shoulders/hips/knees in walk + attack (×2), time-to-glTF in our renderer incl. automated fixes (×2), API ergonomics for an unattended client — task submit/poll/download, errors, rate limits (×2), licence clarity for a public repo (×1), cost for the MVP hero set (×1). Same input image, same target budget.
Owner prerequisites: API keys in env (`MESHY_API_KEY`, `TRIPO_API_KEY`) and a small prepaid credit top-up for each provider; keys never logged or committed.
**Decision output:** one image-to-3D provider, at most one paid month / one prepaid credit purchase sized for the MVP hero set, with rationale and evidence files. Feeds `e37-3d-gen-api-client`.
Related: e39-story-bible (minotaur design intent).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the owner-approved GPT minotaur concept (approval recorded), when Claude runs it through the Meshy API image-to-3D → remesh to ≤ 20 k triangles → rigging → one animation → glb download → KTX2/meshopt compression → import into the renderer test scene, then the model renders animated (idle + one attack) with no console errors, and elapsed time and credits used are logged in the ADR.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the SAME concept image, when run through the equivalent Tripo API pipeline (image-to-3D → smart low-poly retopo → auto-rig → retarget → glb → import), then its results are scored with the same rubric and both scorecards appear side by side in the ADR with turntable renders under `spikes/3d-pipeline/`, and the owner picks a winner at a recorded turntable gate.
- AC-3 [manual] Given one KayKit or Quaternius character and one prop set, when recoloured with the palette texture and rendered with the draft stylized material next to the minotaur, then the ADR records whether kit and generated assets read as one style (with screenshot).
- AC-4 [content] Given every spike output kept in the repo, when inspected, then each has an `assets/CREDITS.md` row (tool, model, tier, date, CC BY 4.0 attribution text where applicable) and is flagged `placeholder: yes`.
- AC-5 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it names exactly one image-to-3D provider, at most one paid month / credit purchase (with timing and size), the animation source (provider API vs CC0 library vs Mixamo with redistribution caveat), and confirms no step requires owner DCC work.
- AC-6 [manual] Edge: given an image-to-3D result that cannot reach the tri budget without visible collapse, a rig that breaks at the shoulders, or an API task that fails/times out, when scored, then the ADR documents the fallback (retry policy, CC0 kit recolour, or simplified hero concept) rather than accepting an over-budget asset.

title: Placeholder asset kit: CC0 stand-ins at correct scale and naming
description:
## Why
Gameplay is never blocked by final art (contract §5). Placeholders with the final naming, scale and pivots make integration a file swap later.

## What
Assemble a placeholder kit from CC0 packs: one humanoid for each class (colour-coded by class accent), skeleton, goblin, wolf, spider, minotaur stand-in (scaled humanoid/ogre), and props for every Legibility cue (door, lever, chest, climbable ledge, flammable rope/barrel, breakable crate, weak wall, pushable block, lockable door), each named with its final asset id and placed under `assets/kits/` + `assets/source/`.

## Scope
- In: CC0 selection and download, unmodified kits in `assets/kits/<kit>/` with licence files
- In: Scale (1 unit = 1 m), pivot at base centre, forward = +Z (or engine convention)
- In: CREDITS rows flagged `placeholder: yes`
- In: Kit catalogue page listing asset id → placeholder file
- Out: Greybox level geometry kit (owned by `e00-greybox-testbed`)
- Out: Final assets (per-asset beads)

## Notes
Candidate sources: KayKit Adventurers/Skeletons/Dungeon, Quaternius Ultimate Monsters/Modular Dungeon, Kenney. Keep total kit ≤ 15 MB built.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the kit catalogue, when validated, then every placeholder has a final-format asset id, a CREDITS row with CC0-1.0 and `placeholder: yes`.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the kit showcase scene loads, then all placeholders render at correct relative scale (humanoid 1.7–1.9 m, minotaur stand-in 2.6–3.2 m) and screenshot sanity passes.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the built kit, when measured, then total runtime size ≤ 15 MB and every asset passes the validator budgets.
- AC-4 [manual] Given each Legibility cue prop, when viewed at 20 m on the Low preset, then the cue (cracks, pale ledge, straw/rope, brass keyhole) is identifiable by a second person.
- AC-5 [integration] Edge: given a placeholder swapped for a file with a different pivot or scale, when the validator runs, then it flags the pivot/scale deviation beyond 5 %.

title: Review and finalize image prompt templates
description:
## Why
Every per-asset prompt bead copies a template; errors or gaps in templates multiply across the whole asset set.

## What
Review the 14 image templates in `assets/prompts/_templates/` (concept-art, character-reference-sheet, creature-reference-sheet, environment-concept, tileable-texture, prop-sheet, ui-element, item-icon, spell-icon, npc-portrait, book-cover-and-page, vfx-flipbook-texture, skybox-backdrop, key-art-title-screen) and `assets/prompts/README.md` against the signed-off style bible; fill one example per template category that has a first real asset (anchor assets for series: item icon, spell frame, portrait, UI panel).

## Scope
- In: Template edits to match the signed-off bible
- In: One worked example each for item-icon, spell-icon, npc-portrait and ui-element (these become the series anchors)
- In: README workflow review
- Out: Music/SFX templates (see `e38-prompt-templates`)
- Out: Per-asset prompt beads (later wave)

## Notes
Templates carry `{{GPT_STYLE_PREAMBLE}}` placeholders — the validator (`e37-asset-validator`) can check filled prompt files contain the verbatim preamble text.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given every file in `assets/prompts/_templates/` for image categories, when inspected, then each contains the contract §6 fields: asset id, consuming bead(s), filled prompt with preamble placeholder, output spec, consistency checklist, iteration log and provenance table.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the 4 worked examples, when Claude generates them via `e37-image-gen-runner`, then each passes its own consistency checklist, is approved by the owner (recorded in `assets/approvals.json`) and is committed as the series anchor with a CREDITS row.
- AC-3 [content] Given a filled prompt file, when the validator checks it, then it fails if the preamble text differs from style bible §14 by any character.
- AC-4 [manual] Edge: given a template whose instructions produced a failed generation twice (e.g. flipbook grid misalignment), when reviewed, then the template intro documents the workaround used.

title: Image generation runner wrapping codex exec with Images API fallback
description:
## Why
Claude generates all 2D images; the owner only approves. A reliable, logged runner turns a filled prompt file into a versioned candidate image with provenance, so image "generate" tasks are Claude-run rather than needs-human.

## What
As a developer, I want `pnpm assets:gen-image <prompt-file>` to run the OpenAI Codex CLI non-interactively (`codex exec`, signed in with the owner's ChatGPT subscription, built-in gpt-image tool), pick up the new image from `~/.codex/generated_images/`, and copy it to `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` with `vN.json` recording prompt file path + hash, tool, model, date and attempt count. On usage-limit errors: exponential backoff with jitter and resumable batch queue. Fallback: OpenAI Images API when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set and subscription generation is unavailable/rate-limited beyond a threshold.

## Scope
- In: Runner in `src/tools/assets/image-gen/` with the codex process and HTTP behind injectable interfaces
- In: Prompt-file parsing (extract filled prompt block; verify verbatim preamble before spending a generation)
- In: Batch mode over a list of prompt files with a max-per-session cap
- In: Versioning vN, never overwriting
- Out: Approval recording (see `e37-asset-approval-log`)
- Out: Post-processing/compression (see `e37-model-import-pipeline`)

## Notes
Owner requirement: **100 % coverage** with the codex process mocked (spawn stub emitting stdout/exit codes; fake generated_images dir). Risk: ChatGPT subscription image usage limits — generate in planned batches, not bursts; the runner must stop cleanly and report remaining queue. `OPENAI_API_KEY` read from env only, never logged (redact in error output). Transparent backgrounds: request in prompt; validate alpha channel for categories that need it.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a filled prompt file for `icon-item-lockpick-iron-01` and a mocked codex run that writes one PNG to the generated-images dir, when the runner executes, then `assets/_incoming/icon-item-lockpick-iron-01/v1.png` and `v1.json` (prompt hash, tool "codex-gpt-image", model, ISO date) exist; a second run produces v2 without touching v1.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a prompt file whose preamble differs from the style bible, when the runner starts, then it refuses before invoking codex and reports the first differing position.
- AC-3 [unit] Given codex exits with a usage-limit error twice then succeeds, when run, then the runner retries with exponential backoff (injected clock) and succeeds on attempt 3, recording attempts: 3.
- AC-4 [unit] Given usage-limit errors persist past the threshold and `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set, when run, then the runner falls back to the mocked Images API and records tool "openai-images-api"; without the key it stops and reports the remaining batch queue.
- AC-5 [unit] Edge: given codex exits 0 but produces no new image (or a non-PNG), when run, then the attempt is marked failed with a clear message and no empty version folder is left behind.
- AC-6 [unit] Given any error path, when logs are captured, then no API key or auth token value appears in output (redaction test).
- AC-7 [unit] Given the runner module, when coverage runs, then all four metrics are 100 %.

title: Record owner approval gates and block unapproved assets in CI
description:
## Why
Claude generates the assets; the owner's taste is exercised only at approval gates (flat image, 3D turntable, music take, SFX batch). Those decisions must be durable and machine-checked, or unapproved generations will slip into the game.

## What
As the owner, I want every approval I give recorded with the exact file version so that nothing I have not approved can ship. Add `assets/approvals.json` (zod schema): entries of `{ assetId, gate: "image"|"turntable"|"music-take"|"sfx-batch", version, sha256, decision: "approved"|"rejected", approver, date, note }`; a small CLI (`pnpm assets:approve <asset-id> <gate> <version> [--reject --note]`) that hashes the candidate and appends the record; and a validator rule: any non-placeholder runtime asset must have `approved` records for every gate its category requires, matching the committed source file hash.

## Scope
- In: Schema + CLI in `src/tools/assets/approvals/`
- In: Required gates per category as data (images: image; 3D: image + turntable; music: music-take; SFX: sfx-batch)
- In: Validator rule wired into `assets:validate`
- Out: The preview UIs themselves (turntable: see `e37-turntable-preview`)
- Out: Licence checks (see `e37-asset-validator`)

## Notes
100 % coverage (same rule as the validator). The approver field is a name/handle only — no emails or secrets.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a final 3D asset with an approved `image` record but no `turntable` record, when validated, then validation fails naming the missing gate.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an approval record whose sha256 does not match the committed source file (file changed after approval), when validated, then validation fails with "approval stale" and both hashes.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `pnpm assets:approve model-creature-minotaur-01 turntable v3`, when run, then a schema-valid record with the file sha256 and ISO date is appended and the file is otherwise unchanged.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a placeholder asset (`placeholder: yes` in CREDITS), when validated, then no approval is required.
- AC-5 [unit] Edge: given a rejected record followed by an approved record for a later version, when validated, then only the approved version's hash is accepted; a malformed approvals.json fails with a parse error location.
- AC-6 [unit] Given the approvals module, when coverage runs, then all four metrics are 100 %.

title: Asset validator: naming, budgets and licence entries in CI
description:
## Why
A solo developer cannot manually police hundreds of assets. Budgets and licences must be enforced by machine or they will drift — and a licence mistake in a public repo is expensive to undo.

## What
As a developer, I want `pnpm assets:validate` to check every asset against the bibles so that CI rejects misnamed, over-budget or unlicensed assets. Checks: asset-id naming regex and category prefix; source/runtime folder mirroring; `assets/CREDITS.md` row exists with an allowed licence and required fields; glTF budgets (triangles, materials, bones, texture sizes by asset class per style bible §13.2); texture power-of-two + KTX2 for runtime; filled prompt files contain the verbatim preamble; placeholder flags reported.

## Scope
- In: Validator module in `src/tools/assets/` with pure functions (parsing CREDITS table, naming, budget rules as data)
- In: glTF inspection via a glTF parsing library (no renderer)
- In: CI job + JSON/markdown report
- In: Budget table as a data file shared with docs
- Out: Audio-specific checks (see `e38-audio-validator`, which extends this)
- Out: Import/compression (see `e37-model-import-pipeline`)

## Notes
Owner requirement: **100 % tested** (lines/branches/functions/statements) even though `src/tools` normally needs ≥ 90 % — add the path to the 100 % group in coverage config. Budget classes are inferred from the asset-id prefix (`model-char-*`, `model-creature-*`, `model-prop-*`) with an override in a sidecar JSON.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given asset ids `model-creature-minotaur-01` and `Model_Minotaur`, when validated, then the first passes and the second fails with a message naming the naming rule.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a runtime asset with no matching `assets/CREDITS.md` row, or a row whose licence is `CC-BY-NC-4.0`, when validated, then validation fails listing the asset id and reason.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a glTF fixture for a standard creature with 7 000 triangles, 2 materials or a 2048² texture, when validated against the creature budget (≤ 6 k tris, 1 material, ≤ 512²), then each violation is reported separately with actual vs limit.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a filled prompt file whose preamble differs from style bible §14 by one character, when validated, then it fails and shows the first differing position.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the CI pipeline, when a PR adds an invalid asset, then the `assets:validate` job fails and uploads a markdown report artifact.
- AC-6 [unit] Edge: given a malformed CREDITS table row (missing columns) or a corrupt .glb, when validated, then the validator reports a parse error for that file and continues validating the rest instead of crashing.
- AC-7 [unit] Given the validator source, when coverage runs, then lines, branches, functions and statements are all 100 %.

title: Review and sign off the visual style bible and GPT style preamble
description:
## Why
Consistency across hundreds of generated assets is only possible if it is defined once, up-front (contract §6). The draft exists; the owner must own the look before any prompt bead is written.

## What
The owner reads the draft `docs/art/style-bible.md`; Claude test-runs the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE on 4 sample prompts (one concept, one icon, one tileable, one portrait) via `codex exec` and the owner judges them; the owner adjusts palette/pillars/budgets where they disagree, and marks the bible signed-off (version + date in the header).

## Scope
- In: Owner review of every section; edits to the draft
- In: Preamble smoke test: 4 Claude-generated samples (ad-hoc `codex exec` if `e37-image-gen-runner` is not ready) committed under `assets/source/concept/` as style probes with CREDITS rows
- In: Sign-off header
- Out: Prompt templates (see `e37-prompt-templates`)
- Out: Story/lore names (owned by `e39-story-bible`; placeholders in the bible are updated when it lands)

## Notes
Draft written by the art-direction planning pass. Key decisions to confirm: 60/30/10 palette ratio, warm-key/cool-fill rule, Legibility Language table (§7), budgets (§13) vs `e32-perf-budgets`, fonts (all OFL). Related: e39-story-bible (minotaur heart-chamber and NPC names are placeholders).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the draft style bible, when the owner completes review, then the header shows `Status: SIGNED OFF vX.Y — <date>` and all open questions are resolved or filed as beads.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE pasted verbatim, when 4 sample prompts (concept, item icon, tileable, portrait) are generated, then at least 3 of 4 match the palette/lighting checklist on the first or second attempt; failures lead to a preamble revision recorded in the bible changelog.
- AC-3 [content] Given the 4 style probe images committed, when the asset validator (or a manual check before it exists) runs, then each has an `assets/CREDITS.md` row with tool, model version, tier and date.
- AC-4 [manual] Given the budgets in §13, when compared with `e32-perf-budgets`, then any mismatch is reconciled so both documents cite the same numbers.
- AC-5 [manual] Edge: given a preamble sample that produces text/letters or photorealism in 2 consecutive attempts, when reviewed, then the preamble negative clause is strengthened and re-tested before sign-off.

title: E40 — Wendmouth Harbor
description:
## Outcome
Wendmouth, the rowdy harbour town at the mouth of the River Wend, is an optional-but-rewarding MVP level where shenanigans ensue: sneakiness is richly rewarded (customs house, bonded warehouse, manifests, rooftops, rigging, crowds, the Undertow), every other class gets hijinks (brawls, arm-wrestling, duels, the Gull Shoot, the Regatta, freezing the harbour pool), and everyone can equip themselves better than in Briar Glen (the Tidemarket and the Undertow). The Crate for Mr. S— heist, the Tidefair and Contraband Pages play out here.

## Scope
- In: harbour grey-box; Stone Wharf and the gated Silver Quay; Customs House and book confiscation; Bonded Warehouse and bay nine; the Drowned Gull; Tidemarket and Undertow stock data (Tereza Maelo, Nell Gannet, the foreign book cart); rooftop/net-loft route; the Gilded Tern; breakwater, sea-door and tides; crowds and dockhand disguises; human opposition (harbour watch, Low Tide Company, Tern crew); a small contest framework and the Tidefair events; heist placement; class routes; secrets/rumours; art, lighting/audio, perf/playtest.
- Out: new creature types (none — the roster stays at 10); flowing-water or ship simulation (water is standing volumes; barge travel is a narrated ride in e25-barge-travel); quest graphs and dialogue (e39-harbor-*, e39-dialogue-harbor-*); shop/bookshop/crime/disguise runtimes (E20/E21/E22/E10); final assets (E37/E38).
- Constraint: Wendmouth is optional; no main-quest step requires it.

## Exit criteria
- Every bible §3.6 place exists, is reachable by barge and towpath, and hosts at least one interaction.
- The Crate for Mr. S— is solvable by all six routes; every quest-mandatory harbour obstacle passes the E16 audit with >= 3 classes.
- Every class can buy or earn >= 2 items not sold in Briar Glen.
- Market day and the Tidefair brawl meet the hardware-baseline budgets on both presets.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the six heist route replays, when run in CI, then each sets its crate outcome fact.
- EC-2 [manual] Given 5 testers, when they spend 30 minutes in Wendmouth, then >= 4 report a hijink or heist moment unprompted.

title: E26 — First Dungeon
description:
## Outcome
One exceptional multi-route dungeon network — the Deepworks mine, Bellwater Priory and the Knot labyrinth (Outer Ring, Ossuary Galleries, Chapel of Echoes, the Fold, Horn's Hall, Sounding Shaft, the Cradle) — combining combat, stealth, the six MVP puzzles, creatures and secrets, ending in the Sounding Shaft climb and the ringing of the Vesper Bell, with level states for all four endings.

## Scope
- In: dungeon layout doc; grey-box blockout per area; encounters and systemic objects; the six MVP puzzles placed from e15 references; rune navigation; shortcuts and loops; Fold respawn point; set pieces (sour bell, Horn's Hall, Cradle, climb, Vespers); ending level variants; class routes; secrets/lore; art/lighting/audio/perf/playtest passes.
- Out: creature behaviour (E13), social logic (E14), quest graphs and text (E39), puzzle framework (E15), final assets (E37/E38).

## Exit criteria
- The dungeon is completable end to end by each class via at least two distinct macro-routes.
- All six MVP puzzles pass the solvability validator in their final placement.
- Each dungeon area meets perf budgets on both presets.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 [e2e] Given a save at the mine gate, when each class's critical-path replay runs, then it reaches "Vespers rung".
- EC-2 [integration] Given the placed puzzles, when e15-solution-audit runs, then all six pass with >= 2 solutions and >= 3 classes.

title: E25 — Wilderness Region
description:
## Outcome
The Briarwood, Mooring's Watch, the River Wend and the Deepworks' exterior approach form an interconnected wilderness around Briar Glen: the Sleepers' Path, the Standing Horn, the wolf den, the woodcutter's hut, the millpond and drowned lane, the watchtower with its signal mirror and supply tunnel, and the boarded mine gate, plus the river (Briar Glen Quay and the Stone Stair, the Millweir sluice walk, the Weeping Adit into the lower mine, the towpath and Kestrel Lock, and barge travel to Wendmouth) — with loops and shortcuts unlocked by abilities.

## Scope
- In: Briarwood, Mooring's Watch and River Wend blockout; barge travel service (narrated ride / fast travel — no flowing-water sim; e03 rules apply to standing water); encounters, set pieces, the mine-gate "getting in" obstacle, shortcuts, secrets, class routes, art/lighting/audio/perf passes.
- Decision: the Deepworks INTERIOR lives in E26 (First Dungeon), because the bible and constitution treat mine → priory → Knot as one dungeon network with shared encounter, puzzle and shortcut logic. E25 owns everything outside the mine gate, the watchtower supply tunnel up to the collapse, the Weeping Adit up to its emergence and the Stone Stair slipway; E26 owns everything inside the mine.
- Out: Deepworks interior, Bellwater Priory and the Knot (E26); town (E24); Wendmouth (E40); creature data (E13).

## Exit criteria
- Every wilderness location in bible §3.5 exists and is reachable from town with the starting kit.
- At least three shortcuts in the region are unlockable and persist.
- Wilderness meets perf budgets with full foliage on both presets.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the connectivity graph, when validated, then every E25 node is reachable from town with base capabilities of every class.
- EC-2 [perf] Given the densest Briarwood view, when measured, then both preset budgets from the hardware baseline hold.

title: E16 — Class-Specific Solutions
description:
## Outcome
Every mandatory obstacle in the MVP has deliberate routes for knight, archer, sorcerer and thief (at least three of four, target four), documented in a route matrix, declared as data, proved by replays and enforced by a CI audit.

## Scope
- In: route-matrix document; obstacle registry data; CI audit reusing e15-solution-audit class capability profiles and e19-capability-registry ids; route replays; gap-closing authoring passes; per-class playtest.
- Out: the capabilities themselves (E04/E05/E08/E10); puzzle-level audits (e15-solution-audit); per-area first-pass routes (the class-route items in E24/E25/E26).

## Exit criteria
- CI fails if any mandatory obstacle has fewer than 3 validated class routes.
- Each class completes the MVP critical path in a playtest using its own fantasy.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the obstacle registry, when the route audit runs, then every mandatory obstacle reports >= 3 validated class routes.
- EC-2 [manual] Given one playtester per class, when they finish the MVP, then each reports >= 3 moments where their class opened a route others could not.

title: E24 — Briar Glen
description:
## Outcome
Briar Glen is a dense, lived-in settlement: every named building from the story bible exists and is enterable, merchants and the Lamplit Stacks have authored stock, named NPCs keep day/night schedules, rumours point at real places, rooftops and secrets reward thieves and the curious, and the first-night sleepwalk plays out through its streets.

## Scope
- In: world map/connectivity doc; day/night content on the e27-world-clock; town blockout; the Sleeping Ox, Lamplit Stacks, Forge, Fletchery & Simples, Bakery, Watch House and jail, Vane House, schoolhouse, Glen Well → cistern, cemetery; rooftop/thief routes; NPC placement and schedules; merchant stock; rumour and secret placement; first-night staging; class routes; art-dress, lighting/audio and perf passes.
- Out: dialogue text (E39); quest graphs (E39); shop/bookshop/dialogue runtimes (E20/E21/E22); the priory end of the cistern (E26); final assets (E37/E38).

## Exit criteria
- All bible §3.5 town locations exist, are reachable and have at least one interaction.
- Town hits the hardware-baseline perf budgets with the full NPC population.
- Every town rumour resolves to a fact produced by placed content.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 [e2e] Given a new game, when the town tour replay visits every named building, then each interior loads and its key interactable responds.
- EC-2 [perf] Given Market Green at midday with the full schedule population, when measured, then High preset p95 frame time <= 16.7 ms on the reference machine.

title: E14 — Social Creatures
description:
## Outcome
The Rootcellar goblins (Mother Kettleback, Snig), Clatter the skeleton who remembers, Brother Horn and Mortimer the book mimic can be talked to, fed, gifted, calmed, befriended and helped — not only fought — using e22 dialogue/disposition/gifts and e12 dispositions/affordances, with outcomes persisted as world facts.

## Scope
- In: humming the Vesper hymn as a player verb; creature-side social behaviour, affordances, disposition rules, gift preferences, befriend/help state machines, follower/ally behaviour where required; scenario tests for every social path.
- Out: dialogue text (e39-dialogue-*); quest graphs (e39-main-quest-data, e39-side-quests-*); dialogue/disposition runtimes (E22/E12); combat move sets (E13).

## Exit criteria
- Every social path in bible §4.2, §5.9–5.11 and §6.1 is reachable in an automated scenario and sets the documented facts.
- No social creature path dead-ends: failure always lands in a new state.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the social scenario suite, when run in CI, then every declared path reaches its outcome fact.
- EC-2 [manual] Given a playtest, when testers meet Horn, then >= 2 of 5 discover a non-combat resolution unprompted.

title: E13 — Bestiary
description:
## Outcome
The ten MVP creature types from the story bible (the Forgotten, Rootcellar Goblins, Brother Horn, Loom Spiders, Briar Wolves, Hushlings, Tallow Ooze, Mimics, Hollow Sentinels, the Sleepless Abbot) exist as data on e12-creature-schema with behaviours, property-driven vulnerabilities, readable telegraphed attacks and at least one avoid/trick option each. Horn and the Abbot have authored boss encounters.

## Scope
- In: creature data, move sets, vulnerabilities via world properties, factions, song-intensity modulation, boss encounter logic, readability/avoidability CI audit, tuning.
- Out: creature framework/AI runtime (E11/E12); dialogue and non-combat relationships (E14/E39); level placement (E24–E26); creature models and audio (E37/E38).

## Exit criteria
- Every MVP creature validates, spawns in the creature arena and has an automated test per declared vulnerability and avoid option.
- Every creature attack passes the readability rule (windup >= 300 ms; unblockable/grab >= 500 ms with distinct cue).
- The Forgotten skeleton ships in m1.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the bestiary audit, when CI runs, then all ten creature types pass readability and avoidability checks.
- EC-2 [manual] Given an internal playtest, when players meet each creature, then each creature is described by >= 3 of 5 testers by a behaviour, not only by its damage.

title: E22 — NPC & Dialogue System
description:
## Outcome
Characters support conversations with conditions and effects, disposition, meaningful choices, class-specific options, persuasion (Divinity: Original Sin 2 style), rumors that lead to places, and lightweight state tracking. Text only for MVP (no voice), with subtitle/text-size accessibility hooks. Dialogue is authored as validated data, never bespoke code.
## Scope
- In: Shared condition/effect DSL, dialogue authoring format + schema, dialogue runtime (anchor), disposition, class/capability-gated options, deterministic persuasion checks, rumors, gifts/bribes, NPC conversation hookup, dialogue UI with accessibility, ambient barks/subtitles, dialogue validator, preview/debug tooling
- Out: Specific Briar Glen NPCs and their dialogue (world-content group)
- Out: Social creature behaviours beyond dialogue (mw-e14)
- Out: Voice acting (not in MVP)
## Exit criteria
- A grey-box NPC conversation exercises conditions, effects, disposition changes, a class-gated option and a persuasion check end-to-end.
- Dialogue validator guarantees every node is reachable, every non-terminal node has an exit, and all references resolve; CI runs it on all dialogue content.
- Dialogue UI respects text-size, background opacity and reading-speed settings.
- Dialogue runtime and DSL at 100% coverage.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 A grey-box NPC conversation exercises conditions, effects, disposition changes, a class-gated option and a persuasion check end-to-end.
- EC-2 Dialogue validator guarantees every node is reachable, every non-terminal node has an exit, and all references resolve; CI runs it on all dialogue content.
- EC-3 Dialogue UI respects text-size, background opacity and reading-speed settings.
- EC-4 Dialogue runtime and DSL at 100% coverage.

title: E23 — Quest Framework
description:
## Outcome
Quests support branching objectives and multiple resolutions (including non-combat) authored as data without bespoke scripting. Quest state lives in the world-state store and persists; failure transitions continue the story instead of dead-ending it. Players track progress in an in-character journal.
## Scope
- In: Quest authoring format + schema, quest runtime (anchor), objective trackers bound to sim events, failure-continues-story transitions, quest validator (every quest resolvable), journal UI, optional wayfinding hints, debug/simulation tools, reference fixture quest, authoring guide
- Out: Specific Briar Glen quests and the main story (world-content / narrative groups, e39-story-bible)
- Out: Cutscene system (not planned for MVP)
## Exit criteria
- A reference grey-box quest can be resolved via at least three distinct resolutions (combat, stealth, dialogue) and a failure path, each covered by an automated e2e test.
- Quest validator proves every authored quest has at least one reachable resolution and every failure state has a continuation.
- Quest state round-trips through save/load mid-objective with no loss.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 A reference grey-box quest can be resolved via at least three distinct resolutions (combat, stealth, dialogue) and a failure path, each covered by an automated e2e test.
- EC-2 Quest validator proves every authored quest has at least one reachable resolution and every failure state has a continuation.
- EC-3 Quest state round-trips through save/load mid-objective with no loss.

title: E20 — Economy & Shops
description:
## Outcome
Gold has meaningful uses and merchants have identities, inventories and specialties (Quest for Glory merchants with personality; Elder Scrolls living shops). Players can buy, sell, haggle and steal, and prices respond to disposition, specialty and stolen goods.
## Scope
- In: Economy design doc (income vs sinks), merchant schema + validator, pure price model, buy/sell transactions (anchor), restock/rotation, fences and stolen goods, shoplifting consequences, haggling, services as gold sinks, merchant barks, shop UI, economy balance tool
- Out: Bookshop-specific inventory rules (e21-bookshop-system builds on this epic)
- Out: Specific merchants and inventories for Briar Glen (world-content group)
- Out: Real-money anything (free game)
## Exit criteria
- A grey-box merchant supports buy, sell, haggle and theft with persistent stock and gold.
- Prices are a pure deterministic function of item value, merchant, disposition, specialty and stolen state, covered 100% by unit tests.
- Economy balance tool reports total obtainable gold vs total meaningful sinks for the MVP region and CI fails if ratio leaves the band set in the design doc.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 A grey-box merchant supports buy, sell, haggle and theft with persistent stock and gold.
- EC-2 Prices are a pure deterministic function of item value, merchant, disposition, specialty and stolen state, covered 100% by unit tests.
- EC-3 Economy balance tool reports total obtainable gold vs total meaningful sinks for the MVP region and CI fails if ratio leaves the band set in the design doc.

title: E19 — Progression
description:
## Outcome
Character advancement primarily unlocks capabilities (verbs), specialization and new play styles — never Firebolt I → II (+12%). The player picks a class at the start; each class earns new verbs through its own fiction: books (sorcerer), techniques from trainers (knight), arrows and trick-shot techniques (archer), tools and tricks (thief). Supporting stats are minimal and subordinate.
## Scope
- In: Progression model ADR (incl. XP yes/no and respec policy), capability registry, progression core, class definitions as data, class selection, minimal supporting stats, per-class unlock channels, deed-based unlocks, capabilities screen + unlock feedback, respec implementation per ADR
- Out: Individual spells (mw-e08), spell learning mechanics (e07-spellbook-learning — we integrate with it)
- Out: Combat move implementation (mw-e04, mw-e05) and thief tool mechanics (mw-e10) — this epic only grants/gates the verbs
- Out: Specific trainer NPCs (world-content group)
## Exit criteria
- All four classes are defined purely in data and selectable at new game.
- Every class has at least one in-fiction unlock channel working end-to-end in grey-box (book, trainer, arrow schematic, tool).
- No progression data entry is a pure numeric increase of an existing capability unless flagged `supporting: true`; the content validator enforces this.
- Capabilities persist through save/load and are queryable by dialogue, quests, puzzles and interaction prompts.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 All four classes are defined purely in data and selectable at new game.
- EC-2 Every class has at least one in-fiction unlock channel working end-to-end in grey-box (book, trainer, arrow schematic, tool).
- EC-3 No progression data entry is a pure numeric increase of an existing capability unless flagged `supporting: true`; the content validator enforces this.
- EC-4 Capabilities persist through save/load and are queryable by dialogue, quests, puzzles and interaction prompts.

title: E10 — Thief Toolkit
description:
## Outcome
Lockpicking, pickpocketing, thrown distractions, extinguishing lights, climbing, hiding bodies, disguises, silent movement, takedowns, traps and escape tools produce a complete thief fantasy built on shared world systems (properties, light, sound, AI perception).

## Scope
- In: thief tool item data, distractions, light extinguishing, takedowns (lethal/non-lethal), body carry/hide, lockpicking (spike + in-world implementation), pickpocketing/planting, climbing + ropes, disguises, trap placement and disarming, smoke/flash escapes, silent-movement capability unlocks, lean/peek, environmental takedowns, grey-box thief vault challenge.
- Out: stealth simulation core (mw-e09), AI (mw-e11), progression UI (E19), loot/shop placement (E18/E20), final art/animation.

## Exit criteria
- Thief vault challenge solvable by ≥ 3 scripted routes plus one failure-and-escape route.
- Every thief verb interacts through properties, not item-specific scripts.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the thief vault challenge, when each scripted route runs, then all complete deterministically.
- EC-2 [unit] Given thief rule modules, when coverage runs, then `src/sim` coverage is 100%.
- EC-3 [manual] Given 3 playtesters, when completing an undetected infiltration, then ≥ 2 rate it at least as satisfying as a hard fight (≥ 4/5).

title: E09 — Systemic Stealth
description:
## Outcome
Visibility, lighting, sound, suspicion, searching, last-known-position and hiding work as coherent, deterministic systems. Stealth is not crouching + an eye icon: players read light exposure, noise and each enemy’s awareness, and failure escalates into new situations rather than a reload.

## Scope
- In: visibility model (light, stance, motion, distance, contrast), multi-point LOS with partial cover, sound propagation through rooms/doors/walls/floors, surface acoustics and footsteps, verticality rules, hiding places, anomaly detection, stealth HUD and directional awareness indicators, LKP ghost, text barks/stingers, zone alarm escalation, stealth tuning data, stealth grey-box course, deterministic infiltration scenario suite, assists.
- Out: thief verbs (mw-e10), AI state machine and behaviours (mw-e11), creature data (mw-e12), final art/audio (E37/E38 asset beads), crime/bounty systems.

## Exit criteria
- Stealth rules in `src/sim` at 100% coverage.
- ≥ 10 infiltration replay scenarios green and deterministic.
- Stealth grey-box course playable end-to-end in the browser.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the infiltration scenario suite, when run in CI, then all scenarios pass with identical state-hash sequences across two runs.
- EC-2 [unit] Given coverage reports, when CI runs, then stealth modules in `src/sim` report 100% lines/branches/functions/statements.
- EC-3 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box course, when a scripted player completes it undetected and once detected-then-escaped, then both runs finish without errors.
- EC-4 [manual] Given 5 playtesters, when asked why they were detected, then ≥ 4 of 5 can name the cause (light, noise, anomaly).

title: E39 — Story & Narrative
description:
## Outcome
The MVP adventure "The Labyrinth Beneath Briar Glen" is a coherent, reactive story: the town, the Briarwood, the River Wend, Mooring's Watch, the Deepworks, Bellwater Priory, the Knot and the optional harbour town of Wendmouth are populated with memorable characters, class-flavoured dialogue, multi-resolution quests, rumours that lead somewhere, and books/item text that carry the lore. The minotaur twist lands, failure bends the story instead of ending it, and every class experiences the key beats differently.

## Scope
- In: story bible sign-off and title decision; all MVP dialogue, quest, rumour, book, spellbook-flavour, item/creature description, intro and ending text as schema-validated data in `src/content`; class-specific variants; failure-state narrative; a narrative lint pass; a playtest comprehension check.
- Out: dialogue/quest runtimes (E22/E23), bookshop rules (E21), spell mechanics (E06/E08), creature behaviour (E12/E13/E14), voice acting (none in MVP), art/audio (E37/E38).

## Exit criteria
- Story bible signed off by the owner; title decided.
- Main quest completable to all four headline endings with data only (no bespoke scripting).
- Every principal NPC has dialogue with class-variant lines; 5 core side quests and 3 Wendmouth side quests each have ≥ 2 resolutions.
- The main quest is completable without ever visiting Wendmouth.
- Narrative lint is green in CI; playtesters can explain the twist unprompted.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 EC-1 Story bible signed off and title decision recorded in docs/decisions.
- AC-2 EC-2 All narrative content files validate against dialogue/quest/content schemas in CI.
- AC-3 EC-3 Main quest reaches each of the 4 headline endings in automated quest-graph tests.
- AC-4 EC-4 Narrative lint (names, canon facts, dangling IDs) passes with zero errors.
- AC-5 EC-5 ≥ 4 of 5 playtesters explain the minotaur twist and the bell solution in their own words.

title: E21 — Bookshops
description:
## Outcome
Magical bookshops are exciting progression and exploration destinations. A data-authored bookshop definition combines regional stock pools, school specialties, deterministic rotation, rare one-off books, secret back-room stock, stolen and forbidden books, book-specific pricing and a bookseller identity that hooks into dialogue and rumours. Any settlement's bookshop can be authored purely as data.

## Scope
- In: bookshop system rules on top of the generic shop system, stock rules, pricing, legality, bookseller identity hooks, bookshop browsing UI, authoring template + validator, persistence of stock state.
- Out: the Briar Glen bookshop, its NPC, dialogue and book selection (world-content group, E24), generic buy/sell (mw-e20), book items themselves (mw-e07).

## Exit criteria
- A fixture bookshop authored only in data exhibits regional, rotating, rare, secret, stolen and forbidden stock in the greybox testbed.
- 100% coverage on bookshop stock and pricing rules (economy rule per contract §3).
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 Every E21 child bead closed or explicitly deferred.
- EC-2 The bookshop authoring template validates and a fixture shop passes all bookshop content tests.
- EC-3 Same seed + same in-game date always yields identical stock (determinism test).

title: E08 — Spell Catalogue
description:
## Outcome
An MVP library of ~20 spells across Fire, Frost, Storm, Arcane, Illusion, Alteration, Conjuration, Necromancy, Nature, Light, Shadow, Gravity and Time, emphasising qualitatively different effects: ignition, freezing, force, telekinesis, teleportation, decoys, restraint, summoning, gravity, transformation, light, darkness, water and time. Every spell interacts with the world only through properties and stimuli, and ridiculous combinations are encouraged.

## Scope
- In: spell content files, per-spell automated tests (effects + world interactions), placeholder VFX/SFX cue ids, book item for each spell, school conventions doc, combination test suite.
- Out: engine/runtime (mw-e06), learning (mw-e07), final VFX/SFX assets (asset prompt beads under E28/E29/E37/E38), placement of books in the world (E24–E26).

## Exit criteria
- 19 P1 spells shipped (P2 spells optional for MVP).
- Every spell has unit tests for its effects and integration tests for at least two property-based world interactions.
- Spell combination suite green; "too useful" spells are documented as intentionally allowed.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 Every E08 P1 child closed.
- EC-2 Content test: every spell file references a school, a book item, a VFX cue and an SFX cue, and has a matching test file.
- EC-3 Combination suite covers every pair of stimulus types emitted by catalogue spells.

title: E07 — Spellbook & Magical Learning
description:
## Outcome
Spells are discovered through books, shops, exploration, quests, secrets and experimentation rather than appearing on level-up. Books are inventory items with language, condition, comprehension difficulty and legality; reading and study teach spells; damaged, untranslated and forbidden books create side-goals; experimentation with the world reveals new verbs. Progression unlocks new verbs (Firebolt → Flame Jet → Fire Wall), never +% tiers.

## Scope
- In: book item schema, reading and study, comprehension, damaged/untranslated/forbidden books, experimentation insights, verb-chain progression, grimoire + reader UI, book acquisition hooks, persistence.
- Out: book shops and pricing (mw-e21), spell definitions (mw-e08), generic inventory (mw-e17), world placement of specific books (world-content epics E24–E26).

## Exit criteria
- A sorcerer can find a book, read it, study it and cast the taught spell, all in the greybox testbed.
- At least one spell in the catalogue is reachable only via experimentation, and one only via a verb-chain unlock.
- 100% coverage on learning rules and book schema.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 Every E07 child bead closed or explicitly deferred.
- EC-2 Content validator rejects any progression step whose only difference from its predecessor is numeric.
- EC-3 Playwright e2e: pick up book → read → study → spell appears in grimoire and hotbar → cast succeeds.

title: E06 — Magic Framework
description:
## Outcome
A data-driven spell architecture where every spell is a content file composed of a delivery (self, projectile, AoE, beam, touch, summon point) and a list of effect operations (damage, world-property stimulus, force, status, summon, transform, displace). Spells never script pairwise interactions: they emit world stimuli (heat, cold, force, light, moisture, charge, life, decay, sound) into the systemic engine (E03), which resolves outcomes through object properties. Casting has a mana resource, cast times, channeling, interruption and botched casts that create new situations.

## Scope
- In: spell schema + validators (src/content), deterministic spell runtime (src/sim), mana, cast lifecycle, delivery types, effect ops, statuses, summons, transformations, displacement, miscasts, light/noise emission, spell hotbar/selection UI, aiming, VFX/SFX cue binding with placeholder visuals, save state, debug tooling, NPC casting. Telemetry emission is left to E34 (Related: spell_cast/spell_miscast/spell_combo events).
- Out: individual spells (mw-e08), learning spells from books (mw-e07), bookshops (mw-e21), final VFX art (mw-e29), final SFX (mw-e28/e38).

## Exit criteria
- A new spell with qualitatively new behaviour can be added as data only (no src/sim change) whenever it uses existing effect ops.
- src/sim/magic and src/content/spells at 100% coverage; replay tests hash-identical for spell-heavy recordings.
- A sorcerer can cast, aim, run out of mana, be interrupted and botch a cast in the greybox testbed.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 Every E06 child bead closed or explicitly deferred.
- EC-2 A fixture spell composed only of existing ops loads and runs with zero code changes (content test).
- EC-3 grep of src/sim/magic contains no spell-id or object-id specific branches (lint rule or test).
- EC-4 Sorcerer core loop (select, aim, cast, interrupt, miscast) demonstrated in the greybox testbed via Playwright e2e.

title: E34 — Telemetry & Playtesting
description:
## Outcome
Privacy-first, local-first, opt-in measurement of deaths, abandoned encounters, spell usage, puzzle completion and other signals that complements — never replaces — direct observation of players.
## Scope
- In: Event schema + local store + export
- In: Consent/opt-in, gameplay events, error capture, in-game feedback, playtest bundle export, analysis scripts, optional opt-in upload
- Out: Third-party analytics SDKs, fingerprinting, ads (never)
- Out: Running the playtests (mw-e35)
## Exit criteria
- With default settings the game makes zero telemetry network requests (automated e2e).
- A playtester can export one bundle file and an analysis script turns N bundles into a death heatmap + spell/puzzle report.
- No event contains free-text PII fields; schema tests enforce it.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 With default settings the game makes zero telemetry network requests (automated e2e).
- EC-2 A playtester can export one bundle file and an analysis script turns N bundles into a death heatmap + spell/puzzle report.
- EC-3 No event contains free-text PII fields; schema tests enforce it.

title: E35 — MVP Fun Validation
description:
## Outcome
External players demonstrate that combat, magic, stealth and exploration are intrinsically enjoyable, measured against fun hypotheses written before testing.
## Scope
- In: Fun hypotheses, playtest protocol, tester recruitment, playtest build channel
- In: Internal greybox and class-fantasy playtests, external rounds, triage, go/no-go decision
- Out: Telemetry tooling (mw-e34)
- Out: Mobile (mw-e36)
## Exit criteria
- Two external rounds with ≥ 8 players each completed and reported.
- Go/no-go decision recorded against the pre-registered hypotheses.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 Two external rounds with ≥ 8 players each completed and reported.
- EC-2 Go/no-go decision recorded against the pre-registered hypotheses.

title: E33 — Developer/Content Tools
description:
## Outcome
Developers and designers can create, tune and debug spells, creatures, loot, encounters, dialogue and puzzles in minutes, with visual insight into the systemic simulation and one-keypress bug capture.
## Scope
- In: Debug console + cheats, entity inspector, time controls, overlays (AI, world systems), sandboxes (spells, creatures), content validator/scaffolder/hot reload, dialogue/quest/loot tooling, replay bug capture
- Out: Full level editor (use external DCC/greybox kit)
- Out: Player-facing modding
## Exit criteria
- Adding a new spell/creature/item from scaffold to in-game test takes ≤ 10 minutes without restarting the dev server.
- All dev tools are stripped from production builds (bundle check).
- A captured bug report replays deterministically on another machine.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 Adding a new spell/creature/item from scaffold to in-game test takes ≤ 10 minutes without restarting the dev server.
- EC-2 All dev tools are stripped from production builds (bundle check).
- EC-3 A captured bug report replays deterministically on another machine.

title: E32 — Performance & Browser Compatibility
description:
## Outcome
Stable frame pacing and fast loading on the hardware baseline across current desktop Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, protected by automated budgets so regressions are caught in PRs rather than playtests.
## Scope
- In: Perf budget suite, bundle/sim-tick budgets, browser matrix, capability detection, quality presets + dynamic resolution, asset loading/caching, context-loss recovery, memory-leak tests, reference-machine runbook
- Out: Mobile performance profiles (mw-e36)
- Out: Engine selection (e00-engine-decision)
## Exit criteria
- High preset holds 60 fps (p95 frame time ≤ 16.7 ms) in the combat stress scene on the reference machine.
- Initial load to playable ≤ 10 s at 50 Mbps, warm reload ≤ 3 s, initial download ≤ 50 MB, JS heap ≤ 1.5 GB.
- Smoke suite green on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in CI.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 High preset holds 60 fps (p95 frame time ≤ 16.7 ms) in the combat stress scene on the reference machine.
- EC-2 Initial load to playable ≤ 10 s at 50 Mbps, warm reload ≤ 3 s, initial download ≤ 50 MB, JS heap ≤ 1.5 GB.
- EC-3 Smoke suite green on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in CI.

title: E31 — Accessibility & Settings
description:
## Outcome
Players can tailor controls, text, camera, audio, visuals and difficulty so the game is comfortable and playable for a broad audience, meeting the basic tier of the Game Accessibility Guidelines.
## Scope
- In: Settings framework and options UI
- In: Remapping, hold/toggle, text scaling, captions for gameplay-critical sounds, camera and motion comfort, colour-blind support, difficulty assists, menu keyboard/gamepad navigation
- In: Accessibility audit
- Out: Graphics quality presets implementation (see e32-quality-presets)
- Out: Voice/TTS narration (no voice in MVP)
## Exit criteria
- Every setting persists across reloads and applies without restarting the game.
- All menus are fully operable by keyboard only and by gamepad only (automated e2e).
- Accessibility audit against GAG basic tier has no open P1 findings.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 Every setting persists across reloads and applies without restarting the game.
- EC-2 All menus are fully operable by keyboard only and by gamepad only (automated e2e).
- EC-3 Accessibility audit against GAG basic tier has no open P1 findings.

title: E15 — Puzzle Framework
description:
## Outcome
Designers compose systemic puzzles from reusable world objects and data — not custom code. A puzzle is a data file naming world entities, a goal condition over live properties and world facts, declared solutions per capability set, and reset/hint policies. Tooling proves each declared solution is reachable, detects softlocks, and reports which classes can solve each puzzle, so "several solutions" is verified rather than hoped for.
## Scope
- In: Zod puzzle schema, goal-condition language over properties + world facts, puzzle runtime (e15-puzzle-kit)
- In: Prefab puzzle pieces built purely from e03 components (statues, mirrors, braziers, basins, counterweights…)
- In: Ordered/timed/sound-clue mechanisms, softlock guards and diegetic resets, escalating diegetic hints
- In: Headless solvability validator, multi-solution class-coverage audit in CI, puzzle inspector tool
- In: Reference greybox puzzles covering the constitution examples, puzzle telemetry events
- Out: Final dungeon puzzle content — see mw-e26 / mw-e24 (they author puzzles with this kit)
- Out: Underlying element/mechanism simulation — see mw-e03
- Out: Separate minigames (lockpicking UI) — see mw-e10
## Exit criteria
- A designer can author a new two-solution puzzle using only data + prefabs, with zero new TypeScript, and it passes the solvability validator.
- CI fails if any puzzle tagged mvp has fewer than 2 validated solutions or any reachable softlock without a recovery policy.
- Six reference greybox puzzles (light redirect, freezing water, weighted plates, statues, darkness navigation, sound following) are replay-tested end to end.
- Puzzle runtime and validator logic in src/sim/src/tools meet coverage policy (100% / ≥ 90%).
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 A designer can author a new two-solution puzzle using only data + prefabs, with zero new TypeScript, and it passes the solvability validator.
- EC-2 CI fails if any puzzle tagged mvp has fewer than 2 validated solutions or any reachable softlock without a recovery policy.
- EC-3 Six reference greybox puzzles (light redirect, freezing water, weighted plates, statues, darkness navigation, sound following) are replay-tested end to end.
- EC-4 Puzzle runtime and validator logic in src/sim/src/tools meet coverage policy (100% / ≥ 90%).

title: E29 — VFX & Magical Spectacle
description:
## Outcome
Magic, impacts, destruction, stealth feedback and environmental effects establish the game's visual identity, derived from sim events and world properties, within the particle and frame budgets.

## Scope
- In: VFX framework and budget manager, cue sheets, placeholders, hit sparks, screen feedback, weapon trails, spectacle shader library, elemental state visuals, destruction, spell VFX slots/templates, arrow effects, stealth indicators, decals, ambient effects, perf/auto-degrade.
- Out: final textures/flipbooks (asset group via e37 prompt beads), spell logic (e06), stealth HUD meters (stealth group).

## Exit criteria
- Element states and breakables are visualised automatically from properties.
- VFX stress scene meets the hardware baseline on High and Low.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 VFX stress scene p95 ≤ 16.7 ms on the reference machine (High) and ≥ 30 fps on Low-class hardware.
- EC-2 Any spell can be visualised with templates only (demonstrated in the testbed).
- EC-3 VFX on/off replays produce identical sim hashes.

title: E28 — Audio & Combat Feedback
description:
## Outcome
Weapons, spells, footsteps, creatures and environments have satisfying positional audio and feedback, driven by data from sim events, within the browser and performance baseline.

## Scope
- In: Web Audio engine, cue sheets, placeholder pack, combat/bow audio rules, footsteps, creature audio slots, mixer settings, snapshots/ducking, occlusion, reverb zones, ambience, adaptive music controller, sound captions, audio perf budgets.
- Out: creating final SFX/music (art/audio group via e38 prompt beads), stealth noise simulation (e09-sound-propagation), dialogue subtitles (dialogue group).

## Exit criteria
- Every gameplay event with feedback value has a cue rule; placeholder report shows the remaining gaps.
- Audio never influences sim determinism (verified by audio-on/off replay hash tests).
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 src/audio ≥ 90% coverage; audio on/off replays produce identical sim hashes.
- EC-2 Audio perf budgets are green in the e32 suite.
- EC-3 Sound captions cover all creature telegraphs and alert barks.

title: E05 — Archery
description:
## Outcome
Bows feel excellent; arrows have physical presence (gravity, drag, sticking, retrieval), weak points and elevation matter, and trick arrows (fire, water, rope, noise, blunt) solve problems through world properties rather than scripted pairings.

## Scope
- In: arrow schema, ballistics, draw/aim/release, focused release, sway, weak points, elevation, moving targets, retrieval, trick arrows, shootable/cuttable mechanisms, archery range, archer mobility.
- Out: arrow crafting/economy (e17/e20), creature reactions to noise (stealth group), final bow/arrow art/audio (asset group).

## Exit criteria
- Every trick arrow's effect is expressed via world-property emissions and validated by property-based tests.
- The archer can reach a high ledge, open a distant gate and douse a light in the greybox testbed.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 Ballistics and bow rules in src/sim reach 100% coverage with deterministic replays.
- EC-2 An extended arrow can be added as data only (demonstrated by e05-trick-arrows-extended or a test fixture).
- EC-3 Median playtest rating for "the bow feels satisfying" ≥ 4/5.

title: E38 — Audio Direction & Asset Pipeline
description:
## Outcome
The Vesper Bell sounds like one world — acoustic dark-folk music (hurdy-gurdy, nyckelharpa, low strings, wordless choir) that adapts to exploration, stealth, tension and combat, and tactile SFX whose loudness and character match the stealth/sound simulation — produced with Suno and a decided SFX source through a validated, licence-tracked pipeline.

## Scope
- In: audio bible (`docs/audio/audio-bible.md`) with Suno and SFX preambles; music + SFX prompt templates; SFX tool decision; audio import pipeline (resample, encode Opus + AAC, loop metadata); audio validator (LUFS, true peak, loop seams, naming, licence); placeholder audio kit; Suno adaptive-family feasibility spike; music state mapping data; audio style target; mix review gate.
- Out: the Web Audio engine, buses and occlusion (`e28-audio-engine`); sound propagation rules (`e09-sound-propagation`); per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads (later wave); voice acting (not in MVP).

## Exit criteria
- Audio bible signed off by the owner.
- Every runtime audio file passes the validator in CI.
- One location has a complete adaptive family (explore/stealth/tension/combat + stingers) transitioning on bar lines in-game.
- Mix review passes at m3.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 `docs/audio/audio-bible.md` is marked signed-off with a date and version.
- EC-2 The audio validator runs in CI and fails on loudness, loop-seam, naming or licence violations.
- EC-3 A location music family transitions between explore, tension and combat on bar boundaries with no audible clicks in a recorded playtest.
- EC-4 All shipping music was generated on a tier whose terms permit free public distribution, as recorded in `assets/CREDITS.md`.

title: E37 — Art Direction & Asset Pipeline
description:
## Outcome
The Vesper Bell has one coherent, readable, performant visual identity — a hand-painted, chunky low-poly storybook world — produced by a solo developer with GPT image generation, CC0 kits and one image-to-3D tool, and every art asset flows through a validated, licence-tracked pipeline from prompt to runtime.

## Scope
- In: style bible (`docs/art/style-bible.md`) and GPT style preamble; image prompt templates; 3D sourcing decision (CC0 kits + image-to-3D bake-off); model/texture import pipeline (glTF, meshopt, KTX2, atlases); asset validator (naming, budgets, licences); placeholder asset kit; animation retargeting pipeline; shared stylized material; gameplay Legibility Language kit; style-target diorama; style consistency gate; CREDITS/licence audit.
- Out: per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads (created by a later planning wave per contract §6); VFX system itself (`e29-vfx-framework`); perf budget suite (`e32-perf-budgets`); level building (E24–E26).

## Exit criteria
- Style bible signed off by the owner and referenced by every prompt file.
- Style-target diorama renders within High/Low budgets and passes the consistency review.
- Every runtime art asset passes the validator (naming, budgets, CREDITS entry, allowed licence) in CI.
- Licence audit clean at m3.
acceptance_criteria:
- EC-1 `docs/art/style-bible.md` is marked signed-off with a date and version.
- EC-2 The asset validator runs in CI and fails on any art asset with a naming, budget or licence violation.
- EC-3 The style-target diorama holds 60 fps on the reference machine (High) and the Low preset target on an Iris Xe-class device.
- EC-4 `assets/CREDITS.md` audit at m3 finds zero unlicensed or placeholder-flagged shipping assets.

title: Bake one navmesh per agent size class (small, humanoid, large)
description:
## Why
Briar Wolves (0.4 m) and Brother Horn are wider than the humanoid radius (0.35 m) every scene is baked for (mw-e11.4, ADR-0006), so they can clip corners and squeeze through gaps they should not fit; goblins (0.3 m) path more conservatively than they need to.

## What
Bake each navigated scene for a small set of agent size classes (e.g. 0.3 / 0.35 / 0.6 m radius, matching heights) and pick the navmesh by a creature's NavAgent radius at query time.

## Scope
- In: bake settings per size class in the navmesh data or a sibling file, query-time selection, pnpm nav:check coverage
- Out: crowd simulation

## Notes
Related: src/sim/nav/bake.ts, src/tools/navmesh/bake.ts, ADR-0006 consequence 'One agent size per navmesh'.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 0.6 m gap, when a 0.35 m agent and a 0.8 m-radius agent request a path through it, then only the smaller one's path uses the gap.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the testbed, when the bake runs for every size class, then all navmeshes are produced in <= 10 s and content validation passes.

title: Reconcile controller stance×gait visibility with the stealth tuning
description:
## Why

Two tables now describe how visible movement is: the controller's stealth.profiles[stance][gait].visibility (mw-e02.10, published on MovementProfile) and the stealth tuning's stance × motion bands (mw-e09.2), which the visibility model uses. The shipped values agree today (stance × motion reproduces the controller table) but can drift.

## What

Pick one source: drop visibility from the controller profiles (MovementProfile.visibility derived from the stealth tuning) or document why both exist. Move the AI stand-in senses onto the visibility model.

## Scope

• In: Remove or derive the duplicate, update the stand-in senses, docs
• Out: New tuning values (mw-e09.6)
acceptance_criteria:
• AC-1 [unit] Given the shipped content, when a movement profile and the visibility model are computed for every stance × gait, then they read from one table.
• AC-2 [content] Given the controller file, when validated, then no second visibility table exists (or a check pins them equal).

title: Supply equipment brightness, cloak and disguise to the visibility profile
description:
## Why

The visibility model (mw-e09.2) has a profile term (equipment brightness × cloak × disguise), and selfVisibilityOf reads a stealth.visibilityProfile component, but nothing writes it: items have no brightness and there is no cloak or disguise flag, so every character reads neutral.

## What

Add an optional item stealth field (brightness 0–2, conceals: cloak) and have equipment derive each actor's VisibilityProfileComponent (product of worn brightness, cloaked when a concealing item is worn); disguise from the disguise system when it exists.

## Scope

• In: Item schema field, equipment-derived profile, register the component in the game world
• Out: Disguise gameplay (its own bead)
acceptance_criteria:
• AC-1 [unit] Given polished plate (brightness 1.3) equipped, when the profile is derived, then brightness is 1.3 and self-visibility rises by that factor.
• AC-2 [unit] Given a cloak equipped, when derived, then cloaked is true and the tuning's cloak modifier applies.
• AC-3 [content] Given an item brightness outside 0–2, when validated, then loading fails.

title: Thrown liquid containers shatter and spill a property-carrying puddle
description:
## Why
mw-e17.6 shipped thrown oil flasks that land whole and burn where they lie. The bead's intent (a thrown flask shatters and leaves a flammable puddle) needs breakables that spill their liquid contents.

## What
Fragile containers break on impact above a threshold and spawn a puddle entity inheriting the container's liquid worldProperties (flammable, wet, conductive...), with a data-driven radius. Purely property-based — no flask-specific code.

## Notes
Follow-up from PR #154 (mw-e17.6).
acceptance_criteria:
AC-1 [unit] A fragile container with liquid properties breaking emits a puddle spawn carrying exactly those properties.
AC-2 [integration] In the greybox testbed a thrown oil flask shatters, leaves a puddle, and igniting it burns the area via e03 propagation.

title: Reconcile breakable profiles with the unused toughness and bashable world properties
description:
## Why
PR #138 (mw-e03.11) added a breakable profile type with its own fragile threshold and resistances, but the existing world properties `toughness` (single-hit threshold per kind) and `bashable` remain unused. Two ways to express the same thing breaks the single property-based model (contract §2).

## What
Either derive breakable thresholds from `toughness`/`bashable` or remove those properties; also decide whether physics impacts should wear down structural hp (today they only test fragility) and whether break loudness belongs on the material rather than the profile.
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [unit] Given a content entity, when it declares breakability, then exactly one property path determines its break thresholds and the validator rejects the other.

title: Flaky bench recurred: light-field p95 over 0.5 ms on CI
description: mw-64w was closed but the light-field AC-6 benchmark failed again on 2026-10-02 in PR #131's unit job (p95 0.517 ms vs 0.5 ms limit); it passed on rerun. Investigate whether the CI gate needs the same looser-CI/strict-local split used for line-of-sight (owner decision 2026-09-29), or whether the bench has noise that can be reduced. Related: mw-64w.
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [perf] Given 20 consecutive CI runs, when the light-field bench runs, then it never fails spuriously, while a real 2x regression still fails it.

title: Run the element rules (fire) in the game world so burning hazards hurt in play
description:
## Why
mw-e04.34 wired the environmental damage rules into the game world (src/main.ts, the testbed and the replay world via startTestbedCombat), including the burning-hazard rule. But the game world does not run the element or fire rules, so nothing ever has burning=true in play, and the hazard damage (and the frame-data World column's 'hazard') can't happen outside tests.

## What
Install the element rules (fire/heat) and their systems in installGamePhysics or the game wiring, after stimulusSystem. Add a way to light something in the testbed (a lit brazier prop, or a console heat stimulus), so a burning prop hurts the knight standing in it.

Discovered from mw-e04.34.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the testbed with a burning prop, when the player stands within its reach, then they take fire damage in 250 ms pulses.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the testbed, when the player stands in a fire, then the frame-data HUD shows hazard damage.

comments.author: Dave Tashner
comments.text: Found in mw-e17.6: scene props (e.g. the testbed loose crate) get no temperature property, so contact heat and the element field never warm them and they cannot ignite in the game world. World items now spawn with the 20 C default temperature (mw-e17.6); props likely need the same when fire runs in the game.

title: Creatures name their own lock-on targetable profile in data
description:
## Why

Spawned creatures are lock-on targets (mw-e12.4), but their lock points are derived from their nav agent height (chest 60 %, head 90 %, base 25 %) because the creature schema has no way to name a targetable profile, though src/content/types/targetable.ts says creatures will. A spider's weak point or a wraith's head should be data, not a formula.

## What

Add an optional targetable ref to CreatureDef; the spawner uses it when present and keeps the derived profile as the default.

## Scope

- In: schema field, docs regen, spawner use, fixture untouched (default).
- Out: bow weak-point targeting (e05).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature naming a targetable profile, when spawned in a world with lock-on, then its Targetable points equal the profile's.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature naming none, then its points are the derived chest/head/base profile.

title: Playtest: parry window is learnable against the sandbox metronome
description:
## Why

mw-e04.12 AC-8 is a manual playtest the agent cannot run: parrying must feel learnable (Knight fantasy: mastery).

## What

As the owner, I want three playtesters to practise parrying the combat sandbox attacker dummy (?scene=combat-sandbox, 2 s metronome, parry on 3 / LB, F3 frame data shows the window, the Parried stun and 'riposte ready') so that the 10-tick window and the placeholder riposte tuning are validated.

Also judge these placeholder decisions from mw-e04.12: (1) parry bound to ability 3 (LB / 3) while block holds LT / right click; (2) a successful parry still plays out its 30 ticks before the knight can riposte (no early exit); (3) the riposte's 8/4/24 frames, 2.0 m thrust and critical-tier hit-stop (src/content/data/move/sword-riposte.json).

## Scope

- In: playtest, tuning notes back into move data
- Out: creature attacks through the executor are not yet tagged parryable (they route through hit volumes in mw-e04.20)
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [manual] Given the sandbox attacker dummy with a 2 s metronome, when three playtesters practise for 5 minutes, then each lands >= 5 parries and rates the window 'learnable' >= 4/5 (carried over from mw-e04.12 AC-8).

title: Creature projectile attacks fly as ballistic arrows and meet level geometry
description:
## Why

Creature projectiles (mw-e12.5) fly in straight lines and pass through walls (the executor says level geometry does not stop them yet), while arrows (mw-e05.2) arc, collide with the level and use region-tagged hurtboxes. Two projectile models drift apart; a skeleton archer's arrow should behave like the player's.

## What

Route projectile attacks through the arrow system: the attack's projectile data names an arrow content id (or a drag-free projectile body), `runActive` looses it with `fireArrow` (shooter = attacker), and hits go through the hurtbox query and CollisionWorld like any arrow. Keep AttackProjectileLaunched/AttackHit for AI and cues. Retire the straight-line `projectileSystem` once no content uses it.

## Scope

- In: executor projectile launch via fireArrow, attack schema field, migration of shipped projectile attacks, tests.
- Out: creature bow animation, AI aiming with lead.

Discovered from mw-e05.2.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature projectile attack at a target behind a wall, when fired, then the projectile stops at the wall and deals no damage.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a projectile attack at a target in range, when it hits, then AttackHit is emitted with the damage results of the struck hurtbox's region.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the creature attack replays, when re-recorded, then only content hashes change or the change is explained.

title: Block dodges, attacks and blocks while mantling or hanging from a ledge
description:
## Why

A dodge, swing or raised shield started while the player mantles or hangs (mw-e02.12) plays its action timeline (i-frames, hitboxes, stamina) while the ledge hook holds the character in place: a free i-frame exploit and a pose that makes no sense.

## What

As a player, I want combat buttons to do nothing while my hands are on a ledge, so that traversal and combat never overlap.

## Scope

- In: dodge input, light attack and block are refused while CharacterState.traversal is mantle or hang (and later climb)
- Out: attacks from a hang (a future thief move)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a player hanging from a ledge, when dodge, attack or block is pressed, then no move starts and stamina is unchanged.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a player mid-mantle, when dodge is pressed, then no dodge starts; once the mantle ends a new press dodges as usual.

title: Reconcile spell noise-op loudness (metres) with the NoiseEvent loudness scale
description: The spell schema's noise op documents loudness as a hearing radius in metres (fixture-bolt uses 15), while the arrow noise payload (mw-e05.1) and mw-e05.11 use loudness 70 on the NoiseEvent scale that mw-e03.25 will define. Once mw-e03.25 fixes the NoiseEvent loudness unit, align the spell noise op description/values and the arrow noise payload to it (and regenerate content docs/schemas).

title: Wall recoil and charge-ready combat cues
description:
## Why

mw-e28.4 lists distinct cues for a swing recoiling off a wall and a charged attack reaching full charge; the sim emits neither event yet, so the placeholder ids sfx-knight-wall-recoil-clang and sfx-knight-charge-ready are unused.

## What

Once the sim emits a wall-recoil event (mw-e04.15) and a charge-full event (mw-e04.13), add them to the cue-event table and bind combat cue rules.

## Scope

- In: cue events and rules
- Out: the sim events themselves
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a charged heavy held to full charge, when it becomes ready, then sfx-knight-charge-ready plays at the knight.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a sword swing that hits a wall, when it recoils, then sfx-knight-wall-recoil-clang plays at the contact.

title: Feed armour weight class into the footstep armour layer
description:
## Why

The footsteps cue sheet (mw-e28.6) plays sfx-armor-plate-layer / sfx-armor-chain-layer on each step when the cue lookups know a character's armour class, but nothing supplies it until armour weight exists, so the layer is silent in the testbed.

## What

Pass armorOf (attachGameAudio option) from the e04.16 armour weight class so the knight in plate clanks as it walks; add the leather layer placeholder.

## Scope

- In: armorOf wiring in main.ts, leather placeholder
- Out: final armour SFX (mw-e38.24 to mw-e38.27)
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [integration] Given the player in plate armour in the testbed, when walking, then each footstep also plays sfx-armor-plate-layer.

title: Playtest: hear block, parry and clean hit apart with eyes closed
description:
## Why

mw-e28.4 AC-5 is a manual listening test and cannot be claimed by automated tests.

## What

In the combat sandbox, three playtesters close their eyes during a dummy fight and name block, parry and clean hit by sound alone. Record the result in the bead.

## Scope

- In: the listening session and its notes
- Out: sound changes (file beads for any)
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [manual] Given the sandbox, when three playtesters close their eyes during a dummy fight, then each can distinguish block, parry and clean hit by sound alone (mw-e28.4 AC-5).

title: Blind A/B playtest: hit-stop on vs off for impact (mw-e04.11 AC-5)
description: mw-e04.11 AC-5 [manual]: given A/B builds with hit-stop on vs off, three playtesters try both blind; at least two of three prefer hit-stop on for impact. Hit-stop off = set every tier to 0 in src/content/data/hit-stop/hit-stop.json. Also a chance to tune the PLACEHOLDER tick values.

title: Let solved puzzles grant item and loot rewards
description:
## Why

mw-e15.1 puzzle outputs can only write facts (solvedFact, set). Rewards such as an item or a loot table on solve have no field yet because items are not content.
