## What

As a designer, I want to declare a puzzle's item or loot reward in its file so that solving it grants the reward exactly once without a quest wrapper.

## Scope

- In: outputs.rewards referencing item/loot content ids, checked at load; runtime grant once on solve
- Out: item schema (mw-e17.2), puzzle runtime (mw-e15.3)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given a puzzle reward naming an unknown item id, when validated, then validation fails naming the id.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a one-shot puzzle with an item reward, when solved, saved and reloaded, then the item was granted exactly once.

title: Check interaction affordance capability requirements against the capability registry
description:
## Why

Scene affordances (src/content/types/interaction.ts) declare requires: [{ capability }] as a plain kebab content id, while puzzles (mw-e15.1) name capabilities by registry id (spell.mage-hand) checked against src/content/data/capability/. Two spellings of the same idea means a gated lever can name a capability nothing grants.

## What

As a designer, I want affordance capability requirements to use the capability id format and be checked against the registry at load so that a typo fails in CI rather than greying out a prompt forever.

## Scope

- In: interaction requirement uses capabilityId; load check against the capability registry with file and pointer
- Out: the runtime capability registry (mw-e19.2)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given a scene spawn whose affordance requires an undeclared capability id, when validated, then validation fails naming the id, file and pointer.
- AC-2 [content] Given an affordance requirement that is not in capability id format, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Ledges on movable props and runtime-spawned geometry
description:
## Why

mw-e03.22 extracts ledges once at scene load from static greybox parts. Movable props (physics-object crates from testprops with bodies) and runtime-spawned geometry (propped ladders, debug-console spawns) have no ledges, so a player cannot mantle a pushed crate.

## What

Ledges for physics-object boxes derived from their current pose (top edges of upright boxes), refreshed as they move/sleep, exposed through the same LedgeIndex query (LedgeHit) as scene ledges.

## Notes

Build on src/sim/climb/ledges.ts (extractLedges, LedgeIndex). Only upright boxes need ledges; tilted ones can be skipped.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 1.4 m physics crate at rest, when ledges are queried near its top, then its four top edges are returned with its entity.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the crate is pushed 2 m, when queried on the next tick, then the ledges follow its new pose.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the crate is tipped over past 20°, when queried, then it has no ledges (edge).

title: Remove a level piece's static colliders when fire or damage destroys it
description:
## Why

Fire burnout destroys an entity whose material burns away (ivy, straw, cloth). When that entity is a scene kit piece (e.g. a placement with material ivy, now possible via scene placement properties from mw-e03.22), its bound static colliders stay in the physics world (bindCollider: 'the collider stays when the entity goes; its owner removes it'), leaving invisible solid geometry. Climb/ledge queries already treat the piece as gone.

## What

When a piece entity with PhysicsColliderComponent is destroyed during play, remove its colliders from the physics sink (and keep unloadScene from double-removing them).

## Notes

Discovered while implementing mw-e03.22.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a scene piece of material ivy that burns out, when the burnout applies, then its colliders are removed from the physics world by the end of the tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given such a scene is then unloaded, when unloadScene runs, then no collider is removed twice and no error is thrown.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the piece is destroyed, then line-of-sight, light occluder statics and ledge queries no longer see it.

title: Wire environmental damage and character impulses into the game world
description:
## Why
mw-e02.15 / mw-e04.19 shipped the sim rules (applyCharacterImpulse, installCharacterImpulses, installEnvironmentDamage with src/content/data/environment-damage/default.json) but the game world (src/game, testbed player) installs no damage model yet, so none of it runs in play. Also: characters have no spatial.placement, so only contact-shaped force stimuli reach them; area Gusts/explosions need character placements kept in step with the controller.

## What
When the player/creatures get a damage model in the game world, install installCharacterImpulses + installEnvironmentDamage (capsule from controller tuning, surface = physicsSurface) and keep characters' placements synced so shaped stimuli reach them.

Discovered from mw-e02.15 / mw-e04.19.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the testbed with the player, when a sphere force stimulus goes off next to them, then the player is launched.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the testbed, when the player drops off a ledge higher than 4 m-equivalent, then fall damage shows on the HUD.

title: Creatures standing in fire catch fire per creature burning rules
description:
## Why
mw-e04.19 says fire volumes deal 8 fire/s *and apply burning per creature rules*. The hazard damage shipped (src/sim/combat/environment, 8 fire/s in 250 ms pulses through the damage model), but creatures have no burning status yet: fire rules (mw-e03.5) only ignite world objects with flammable/temperature properties.

## What
Give creatures a burning state (duration, damage over time, extinguished by water/rolling) applied when a creature is hit by a hazard whose property is burning, respecting fire immunity (resistance 0 never ignites).

Discovered from mw-e04.19.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature with fire resistance 1 in a fire volume, when a pulse lands, then it gains the burning state per its creature data.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature with fire resistance 0, when it stands in fire, then it never gains burning.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a burning creature entering water, then burning ends.

title: Make the room training dummy a lock-on target
description:
## Why
mw-e04.6 added a combat training dummy (with Health) in the testbed room while mw-e02.16 added lock-on with three separate targetable dummies in the arena. Locking on to the one you can actually hit is the knight's core loop.

## What
As a knight, I want to lock on to the room training dummy so that I can practise strafing and attack timing on it.

## Scope
- In: give the `training-dummy` spawn a `targetable` profile, locate it by its combat transform (it may be knocked back), pass zeroHealth so its death hands the lock on.
- Out: lock-on rules (src/sim/targeting).

## Notes
src/game/combat (TRAINING_DUMMY, readDummyTransform); TestbedLockOn.locate in src/game/player/testbed-player.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the testbed, when the player presses lock on facing the room dummy, then the lock targets it and the marker sits on it.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a lock on the room dummy, when its health reaches 0, then the lock releases (no other target within 10 m).

title: e2e/vfx.spec.ts times out under load
description: Several agents report e2e/vfx.spec.ts timing out in full local Chromium e2e runs on a loaded machine (passes alone; CI e2e-smoke green so far). Find the slow step (likely waiting on frame counts/particle totals) and make the spec deterministic and cheap rather than raising the timeout.

title: Playtest the knight light chain for weight (mw-e04.6 AC-8)
description:
## Why
mw-e04.6 AC-8 is a manual playtest (three testers, median ≥ 4/5 for 'swings feel heavy and committed', none say floaty) that needs the combat sandbox (mw-e04.9).
## What
Run the 5-minute sandbox session and record ratings.
## Scope
- In: the playtest and its notes
## Notes
Also review the defaults chosen in mw-e04.6: planted during attacks, facing locked through recovery, chain memory forgotten on interrupt, training dummy 200 hp.
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [manual] Given a 5-minute sandbox session, when three playtesters use the chain, then the median rating for 'swings feel heavy and committed' is ≥ 4/5 and none describe attacks as floaty.

title: Owner feel review of lock-on tuning
description:
## Why
mw-e02.16 shipped lock-on with documented default numbers the bead did not specify (distance weighting, priority weight, turn rate, flick thresholds, camera framing). Feel is the owner's call.

## What
As a designer, I want the lock-on feel reviewed in the testbed arena so that the defaults are confirmed or retuned.

## Scope
- In: src/content/data/lock-on/player.json values (distanceWeight 0.5, priorityWeight 0.25, turnRate 720°/s, stick flick 0.7/0.3, mouse flick 40/5 counts, framing 0.2 s / 0.5 / −10°).
- Out: rule changes (new beads).

## Notes
Open the testbed, walk into the arena, lock on (Q / RS click), cycle (Tab, mouse swipe, RS flick), strafe with A/D.
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [manual] Given the testbed arena with three dummies, when the owner locks, cycles and strafes with keyboard+mouse and with a pad, then each tuning value is confirmed or a new value is recorded in the content file.

title: Spawn debug-console props as physics objects
description:
## Why

The debug console's `spawn` (mw-e33.1) creates test props as plain scene-spawn entities: they are drawn but do not fall, stack or collide. Since mw-e03.39, scene props with a `body` are physics objects, so console-spawned props should behave the same way when testing physics, stacking and fire.

## What

As a developer, I want `spawn testprop-crate 3` to drop three physical crates so that I can test physics interactions without editing a scene.
Spawners for props with a `body` give the entity its material properties and make it a physics object (`addPhysicsObject`) through the debug command system. Material properties added during a tick are deferred, so the body is added once they are live (e.g. on the tick after the spawn); the renderer binds these props with `readPhysicsObjectTransform`.

## Scope

- In: Physics-object spawning for props with a body, render binding for them
- Out: Spawning creatures (mw-e12.4)

## Notes

- Keep it deterministic and recorded: everything happens inside `World.step` from the recorded spawn command.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given spawn testprop-crate 3 above the floor, when the sim runs, then the 3 crates are physics objects with wood properties and the crate's mass, and fall to rest on the floor.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a recorded session with a physics spawn, when replayed, then every checkpoint hash matches.

title: Owner review: dodge feel defaults and controls
description:
## Why
mw-e04.8 shipped numbers and controls the bead did not fix; they are documented defaults awaiting the owner's call.

## What
Review and confirm or change: backstep travel 1.2 m (backstep.json); roll attack 10/4/20 ticks, 14 stamina, 16 slash, 12 poise (roll-attack.json); keyboard dodge on R (F stays the remap example; Ctrl/Alt trip browser shortcuts); pad dodge on B with crouch moved to D-pad Down and ability 3 on LB only; a swing dodged once cannot hit the dodger later in the same active window; a dodge and an attack pressed on the same tick start the attack; the roll moves only on its 13 active ticks and stands still in recovery.

## Scope
- In: decisions, data edits, docs/design/controls.md
- Out: new mechanics
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [manual] Given the list in the description, when the owner has reviewed it, then each item is confirmed or changed in content data/bindings with the decision noted in the move notes or controls doc.

title: Flaky bench: light-field AC-6 p95 just over 0.5 ms budget on CI
description: tests/bench/light-field.bench.ts > AC-6 (64 dynamic emitters, 500 samples/tick, p95 <= 0.5 ms) failed the unit job on PR #91 (run 36639965025) with p95 0.50294 ms; unrelated change (test-only). Budget has no headroom on shared CI runners; investigate optimising the light query or measuring more robustly (e.g. median of runs) rather than silently raising the budget.

title: Move the debug console overlay onto the UI component kit
description:
## Why

The debug console (mw-e33.1) shipped with its own minimal, inline-styled DOM because the HUD/menu component kit (mw-e00.23) was still being built. Tools should share one UI kit so focus handling, theming and the UI test harness apply to them too.

## What

As a developer, I want the debug console built on the UI component kit so that it looks and behaves like the rest of the in-game UI and is testable with the same harness.
Replace the hand-built overlay in src/tools/console/view.ts with kit components (panel, log list, text input); keep the command registry, history and key behaviour unchanged.

## Scope

- In: Console overlay on the kit, focus capture through the kit's focus/input-context API
- Out: New console commands; entity inspector (mw-e33.3)

## Notes

- Existing e2e (e2e/debug-console.spec.ts) must keep passing unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the console open, when inspected, then it is composed of kit components and takes keyboard focus through the kit's input-context API (player does not move while it is open).
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the existing debug-console e2e suite, when run, then it passes unchanged.
close_reason: Superseded: the console was built on the UI kit (mw-e00.23) within mw-e33.1, PR #98

title: Let light pass partially through foliage, cloth and glass
description:
## Why

Shadows under a hedge or behind a curtain should be dimmer, not pitch black or fully lit. Line of sight (mw-e09.1) already treats partial cover as transmittance; the light field (mw-e03.15) only knows opaque blockers.

## What

As a thief, I want foliage and cloth to cast soft shadows so that partial cover hides me partly.

Light paths through transparent (glass, water, ice) and partial-cover entities are attenuated by a transmittance factor, using the same occlusion vocabulary as line of sight (opaque | transparent | partial:<factor>), instead of only opaque entities blocking fully.

## Scope

- In: transmittance for dynamic light occluders; sharing the occlusion factor source with mw-e09.1
- Out: coloured light and caustics (render only)

## Notes

Follow-up from mw-e03.15. Keep the sampling budget (AC-6 of mw-e03.15).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a partial:0.5 bush between an emitter and a sample, when sampled, then the emitter's contribution is halved.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a transparent pane between an emitter and a sample, when sampled, then the contribution is unchanged.
- AC-3 [perf] Given the mw-e03.15 light benchmark, when partial occluders are added, then it stays within budget.

title: Flaky timeout: fire.test.ts AC-5 (water extinguishes burning object) under coverage load
description: src/sim/elements/fire.test.ts > drying and extinguishing > AC-5 hit the default 5 s test timeout in CI (PR #85 unit job, first attempt) and locally under pnpm test:coverage on a loaded machine; it passes alone in ~0.6 s for the whole file. tests/toolchain/scaffold.test.ts AC-4 then fails as a consequence (coverage files not written). Find the slow part (likely a long field simulation) and make it cheaper or give it an explicit timeout.

title: Derive collider sight occlusion from world properties (opaque/transparent + partial factor)
description:
## Why
mw-e09.1 gives line of sight its own per-collider Occlusion (opaque | transparent | partial:<factor>) supplied through LineOfSight's occlusionOf callback; unregistered colliders are opaque. The world-property vocabulary (v2, mw-e03.31) has opaque/transparent flags but no partial-cover factor, and colliders do not yet map to entities.

## What
Map physics colliders to their entities and derive occlusionOf from world properties: opaque -> opaque, transparent -> transparent, neither -> partial with a factor (add a sightTransmittance-style property or material default). Level geometry without properties stays opaque.

## Notes
Adding a property is a schema change: bump WORLD_PROPERTIES_VERSION.

title: Fade the player and near occluders when the orbit camera is pulled in close
description:
## Why

When collision pulls the orbit camera (mw-e02.4) in tight, for example behind a pillar in the testbed corridor or with the player backed against a wall, the placeholder capsule can fill half the screen and hide the path ahead. mw-e02.4 scoped a transparency fade of occluders near the camera, but it shipped without one.

## What

As a player, I want the character and anything right in front of the camera to fade out when the camera is squeezed in close, so that I can still see where I am going.

## Scope

- In: Fade the player's body by camera distance, and fade scene pieces that the camera's near sphere or the camera-to-player line passes through, with a smooth fade in and out.
- Out: Camera placement and collision (done in mw-e02.4).

## Notes

src/game/camera/orbit-camera.ts already publishes boom length and ideal distance each frame. The fade is presentation only and never touches the sim.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the boom pulled in below the fade start distance, when a frame is drawn, then the player's opacity falls monotonically with distance and is fully opaque at or beyond it.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a scene piece between the camera and the player, when a frame is drawn, then that piece fades out within 0.2 s and fades back in once it is clear.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the testbed corridor, when the bot walks past the pillars, then there are no console errors and the frame time stays within the perf budget.

title: Verify Rapier deterministic state hashes match on x86 in CI
description:
## Why
ADR-0001 checks Rapier determinism only across browsers on one Apple Silicon machine. Cross-architecture equality (x86 vs arm64) is untested, and saves and replays depend on it.
## What
Add a CI job that runs spikes/determinism (node-run) on ubuntu x86_64 and compares the final hash with the committed arm64 hash.
## Scope
- In: CI job, expected-hash file
- Out: production physics wiring
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [integration] Given the committed 600-step script, when run on an x86_64 CI runner, then the final hash equals the arm64 hash recorded in ADR-0001, or the job fails with both hashes printed.

title: Attribute fire spread to whoever started it (instigator chains through fire)
description:
Follow-up from mw-e03.5 (PR #68). Fire rules currently write property changes with source null: a fire lit by the player's torch and spread through three crates carries no attribution, so quests, crime and AI blame (mw-e04.19, mw-e11) cannot tell who burned the barn. Record the heat source that ignited an entity (e.g. the attributed stimulus that raised its temperature, or the burning entity whose flames reached it) in a snapshotted component, and pass it as the source of ignition/burn/burnout property writes and fire events.

AC-1 [unit] Given a player heat stimulus that ignites crate A whose flames ignite crate B, when both burn, then fireIgnited for B and B's burning propertyChanged carry the player as source.
AC-2 [unit] Given the attribution state, when the world is snapshotted and restored mid-fire, then attribution survives and replays hash identically.

title: Creature projectiles collide with level geometry
description: The mw-e12.5 projectile executor flies straight and only tests living hurtboxes (placement + health); walls and props do not stop it. Once the physics layer (e03.10) exposes sim-side raycasts/sweeps, stop projectiles at geometry and emit an impact event.

title: Test trigger volumes for element presence in element-field cells
description:
## Why

mw-e03.21 filters volumes by element presence on entities (fire = burning, water = wetness > 0, ice = frozen, charge = charge > 0). A room flooding with gas or a patch of burning oil on the floor lives in the element grid (mw-e03.4), not on entities, so a volume cannot see it yet.

## What

As a designer, I want a trigger volume filter that tests element-field cells inside the volume (fire, gas, water, charge above a threshold) so that burning oil or seeping gas can trip a mechanism.

## Scope

- In: a field-presence predicate for volume nodes (element + min concentration), content schema + sim evaluation
- Out: the element grid itself — see mw-e03.4

## Notes

Reuse shapeBounds to find the cells; keep evaluation order canonical.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a volume filtered to gas ≥ 0.3, when gas cells above that concentration overlap it, then active is true; below it, false.
- AC-2 [content] Given a field predicate naming an unknown element, when validated, then validation fails naming the element.

title: Wire canvas thumbnail capture into saves and verify it in a browser
description:
## Why
mw-e30.4 added captureCanvasThumbnail (src/render/thumbnail.ts, coverage-excluded) and the SaveSlots captureThumbnail seam, but no renderer exists yet (mw-e00.13), so the capture is never exercised in a real browser.

## What
Once the renderer exists, pass () => captureCanvasThumbnail(canvas) to SaveSlots saves (pause-menu save, autosave, quicksave), make sure the WebGL canvas is captured right after a render (or preserveDrawingBuffer), and add a Playwright check that a saved slot shows a non-placeholder WebP/PNG thumbnail within 256x144 and 64 KiB in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1 [e2e] Given a manual save from the running game, when the slot list is read, then the slot has a captured thumbnail (not the placeholder) in each of Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.

title: Reintroduce trig into the core replay scenario now that simMath is portable
description:
## Why

The core golden replay (src/sim/replay/scenarios/core.ts) deliberately avoids simMath transcendentals because Node's Math.sin/cos differed between macOS arm64 and Linux x64. mw-e00.28 made simMath bit-identical on every platform, so the golden can again cover trig-driven motion, the most likely source of future cross-platform drift.

## What

Feed at least one moving entity's velocity from simMath.sin/cos (and ideally atan2) in the core scenario, update the scenario's header comment, and re-bless the golden with pnpm replay:rebless.

## Scope

- In: core scenario, its golden, its comment
- Out: simMath itself
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the core scenario with a trig-driven velocity, when replayed in CI on Linux x64, then every checkpoint hash matches the golden recorded on macOS arm64.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the re-blessed golden, when simMath.sin is perturbed by 1 ULP in a test, then the replay reports a divergence.

title: Lint direct Math transcendental calls in src/sim (use simMath)
description:
## Why

src/sim/math.ts (simMath) is the single place the sim touches Math.sin/cos/tan/atan2/exp/log/pow/hypot, whose results are only guaranteed identical within the same engine build. If a future cross-engine determinism need arises, one file changes. Nothing stops code calling Math.sin directly today.

## What

Extend eslint/layers.js so src/sim (except src/sim/math.ts) cannot use Math transcendental functions directly; the message points to simMath. Add lint fixtures proving it.

## Scope

- In: eslint rule + fixtures + test update
- Out: a cross-engine deterministic math library
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given src/sim code calling Math.sin, when linted, then it errors naming simMath.
- AC-2 [unit] Given src/sim/math.ts calling Math.sin, when linted, then no error.
- AC-3 [unit] Given src/game calling Math.sin, when linted, then no error.

title: Dependabot: ignore @types/node and TypeScript majors
description:
## Why

Dependabot proposed @types/node 24 -> 26 (PR #26), but the repo pins Node 24, so its types must stay 24.x. TypeScript 7 majors would also break lint until typescript-eslint supports them.

## What

Add ignore rules for major updates of @types/node and typescript to .github/dependabot.yml, each with a comment saying when to lift it.

## Scope

- In: .github/dependabot.yml
- Out: upgrading Node or TypeScript
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [manual] Given the dependabot config, when Dependabot runs, then it does not propose @types/node or typescript major updates.

title: Probe the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE on four sample images
description:
## Why

The style bible was signed off (mw-e37.1) before its GPT STYLE PREAMBLE was tested. Four contrasting samples show whether the preamble holds the palette, lighting and no-text rules before prompt beads start producing hundreds of assets.

## What

Claude runs the preamble (style bible §14, verbatim) on four sample prompts via codex exec, using the image runner (mw-e37.4) if it's ready or ad hoc if not: one concept (Wendmouth's Stone Wharf, to also test the stone-harbour canon), one item icon, one tileable, one portrait. The owner judges them against the palette/lighting checklist. Commit them under assets/source/concept/ as style probes with CREDITS rows (placeholder: yes). Revise the preamble if needed and log the revision in the style bible change log (§18).

## Scope

- In: 4 probes, owner review, CREDITS rows, preamble revisions
- Out: prompt templates, real assets
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the preamble pasted verbatim, when the 4 samples are generated, then at least 3 of 4 match the palette/lighting checklist on the first or second attempt; otherwise the preamble is revised, logged in §18 and re-tested.
- AC-2 [content] Given the 4 committed probes, when checked, then each has an assets/CREDITS.md row with tool, model version, tier and date.
- AC-3 [manual] Edge: given a sample with text/letters or photorealism in 2 consecutive attempts, when reviewed, then the negative clause is strengthened and re-tested.

title: Probe the SFX PREAMBLE on a footstep, a spell cast and a UI click
description:
## Why

The audio bible was signed off (mw-e38.1) before its SFX PREAMBLE was tested. Three contrasting sounds show whether the preamble produces the tactile, heavy, true palette of audio bible §7 before the SFX batches start.

## What

Using the ElevenLabs client (mw-e38.7), generate a stone footstep, an Ember spell cast and a UI click from the audio bible §8 preamble. Run them through the loudness and naming rules (§5, §6), commit them as placeholders with CREDITS rows, and put them up for owner approval. Revise the preamble if they miss.

## Scope

- In: 3 probe sounds, placeholder CREDITS rows, preamble revisions
- Out: the SFX batches themselves
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the three probe sounds, when the owner reviews them, then they are approved as matching §7, or the preamble is revised and re-probed.
- AC-2 [content] Given the committed probes, when validated, then each has a CREDITS row flagged placeholder: yes and meets the §5 loudness targets.

title: Probe the SUNO STYLE PREAMBLE on two explore tracks
description:
## Why

The audio bible was signed off (mw-e38.1) before its preamble was tested on location music. The approved main theme shows the preamble can produce an instrumental take, but a town cue and a labyrinth cue stress different parts of it (warmth vs cavernous dread).

## What

Claude writes two probe prompts from audio bible §4.1: Briar Glen explore and labyrinth (the Knot) explore. The owner auditions takes in Suno and downloads only a take worth keeping (download cap: see Suno plan notes). Record any vocals-despite-Instrumental failure pattern in audio bible §4 and revise the preamble or exclusions if needed.

## Scope

- In: 2 prompts, owner audition, bible §4 notes if anything fails
- Out: final location music (the per-location e38 music beads)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the two probe prompts, when generated in Suno, then the kept takes contain no intelligible vocals and use only the listed instrumentation; otherwise the preamble or exclusions are revised and re-tested.
- AC-2 [manual] Given a take with vocals despite the Instrumental toggle, when reviewed, then it is rejected and the failure pattern is recorded in audio bible §4.
close_reason: Completed in PR #21: owner kept both probe takes (Suno v6, Pro)

title: Sync backlog and asset plans with the stone-trade canon
description:
## Why

Story bible v0.3 (mw-e39.26) made glenstone the valley's original export and Wendmouth a monumental stone harbour: the Ore Wharf is now the Stone Wharf, the Ore Stair the Stone Stair, ore barges are stone barges, and the Deepworks is a glenstone mine with silver galleries. About 28 beads, plan/world.json, plan/assets-harbor.json, plan/world-asset-needs.md and plan/id-map.json still use the old terms, including 'stilted tarred warehouses' in the harbour art briefs.

## What

Update bead descriptions and plan files to the new canon. Decide whether to rename keys and asset ids (e40-ore-wharf, env-wendmouth-ore-wharf-tidefair-01 and friends) or keep them as stable ids with updated titles and descriptions. Refresh harbour asset briefs so art prompts ask for monumental glenstone quays, breakwater, warehouses and Customs House (style bible §2.2 Wendmouth row).

## Scope

- In: bd descriptions, plan/*.json, plan/*.md, id-map if keys change
- Out: story and style bible text (done in mw-e39.26)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] No bead or plan file describes Ore Wharf, Ore Stair, ore barges or stilted warehouses except as ids deliberately kept stable.
- AC-2 [content] node scripts/load-plan.mjs --check passes after the edits.

title: Opt-in main theme player on the landing page
description:
## Why

The owner wants the title main theme (music-title-main-theme, Suno take in assets/_incoming/music/) playable on thevesperbell.com.

## What

Encode web copies (Opus/Ogg 112 kbps primary, AAC/M4A 160 kbps fallback per audio bible §5.2) into site/audio/, and add a play/pause toggle in the hero. Off by default: no autoplay, preload=none, so nothing downloads until the visitor opts in. Record provenance (prompt file + CREDITS.md) and the owner's approval for website use.

## Scope

- In: site/index.html toggle, site/audio/*, assets/prompts/music/music-title-main-theme.md, CREDITS.md row
- Out: in-game music integration (mw-e38.104), adaptive music
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given a fresh visit, when the page loads, then no audio plays and no audio file is requested.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the visitor clicks the theme toggle, then the theme plays (looping) and the toggle shows a pause state; clicking again pauses.
- AC-3 [manual] Given a browser without Ogg Opus support (Safari), when toggled on, then the M4A fallback plays.

title: Serve the site and backlog from thevesperbell.com
description:
## Why
The owner bought thevesperbell.com. The backlog (and later the playable build) should live at the game's own domain instead of davetashner.github.io/thevesperbell.

## What
As the owner, I want thevesperbell.com to serve the GitHub Pages site so that the backlog and future builds have a memorable, stable address.

## Scope
- In: DNS records at the registrar (owner), GitHub Pages custom domain setting, HTTPS enforcement, updating links in CLAUDE.md and docs
- Out: the game landing page design (later), email on the domain

## Notes
Apex needs A/AAAA records to GitHub Pages IPs (or ALIAS/ANAME); www needs a CNAME to davetashner.github.io. Verify the domain in GitHub account settings to prevent takeover.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given DNS records set at the registrar, when GitHub Pages checks the custom domain, then the check passes and HTTPS is enforced.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given a merge to main, when the Pages workflow finishes, then https://thevesperbell.com/backlog.html serves the latest backlog.
- AC-3 [content] Given the domain is live, when docs are read, then CLAUDE.md and the backlog contract link to thevesperbell.com.
- AC-4 [manual] Edge: given the domain is verified in GitHub account settings, when another account tries to claim it for Pages, then GitHub refuses.
notes: 2026-09-27 owner decision: host on AWS account 205074708100 instead of GitHub Pages. Route 53 hosted zone created: Z1026384SYV7U6UO2WXU; nameservers ns-1454.awsdns-53.org, ns-150.awsdns-18.com, ns-834.awsdns-40.net, ns-1885.awsdns-43.co.uk (owner sets these as Custom DNS at Namecheap). Planned stack: private S3 bucket + CloudFront (OAC) + ACM cert in us-east-1 (DNS-validated) for apex and www, Route 53 alias records, deploy from GitHub Actions via OIDC role (no long-lived keys).

title: Add harbour gulls that steal shiny things and rats that give you away
description:
## Why
Ambient life with systemic hooks: gulls with criminal records and rats that squeal at the worst moment.

## What
As a player, I want gulls that snatch unattended shiny items and rats that scatter from light so that the harbour feels alive and mischievous.
Gulls: ambient agents that grab unattended items tagged shiny and fly to rooftop hoards (followable, lootable). Wharf rats: flee light, emit a startle noise event when a sneaking player passes within 1.5 m.

## Scope
- In: Two ambient agent definitions (not creature types), hoard containers, startle noise rule
- Out: Creature roster (stays at 10 types)

## Notes
Not counted as creature types (bible §8).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given an unattended shiny item on the wharf, when a gull reaches it, then it is carried to the nearest hoard container.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a sneaking player passes within 1.5 m of a rat, when evaluated, then a startle noise event is emitted that nearby watchers can hear.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a gull carrying a quest item, when it lands, then the item is placed in a reachable hoard (edge: quest items never lost).

title: Let dockhand disguises fool the watch and warehouse crews
description:
## Why
A dockhand disguise from the Undertow is the classic heist entry.

## What
As a thief, I want a dockhand disguise that lets me walk into restricted wharf areas so that I can case the warehouse in daylight.
Disguise data for the dockhand faction look: accepted by harbour watch and warehouse crew until suspicious behaviour (running, climbing, entering bay nine, picking locks in view) exposes it.

## Scope
- In: Disguise definition, restricted-area rules, exposure behaviours for harbour factions
- Out: Disguise system (e10-disguises)

## Notes
Related: e40-crate-heist lists the disguise as one heist entry when this lands.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the disguise worn, when the player walks through the warehouse yard by day, then the watchman stays Unaware.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the disguised player climbs in view, when perceived, then the disguise is exposed and crime.disguise.exposed fires.
- AC-3 [integration] Given Nell's crew sees the disguise, when perceived, then they recognise it and do not report (edge: faction-specific).

title: Stage Tereza Maelo's first-blood duel
description:
## Why
A retired duellist looking for a reason not to be: a knight's signature Wendmouth moment.

## What
As a knight, I want to accept Tereza's first-blood duel so that winning unlocks her under-the-counter stock and her respect.
Duel mode: non-lethal, first clean hit landed wins; Tereza uses a fast parry-heavy sabre move set (readability rules apply); dirty tricks count as a loss of honour (fact).

## Scope
- In: Duel encounter state, Tereza combat moves as creature data, outcome facts
- Out: Stall stock (e40-tidemarket)

## Notes
Any class may duel; knights receive the challenge unprompted.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given Tereza's move data, when validated, then every move passes the readability rule.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player lands the first clean hit, when resolved, then tereza.duelWon is set and combat ends immediately with no further damage.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player uses a thrown distraction or poison during the duel, when detected, then tereza.dishonoured is set and the stock stays hidden (edge).

title: Stage the Tidefair Regatta rowing race on the harbour pool
description:
## Why
The sorcerer's hijinks: "no magic" is a rule nobody enforces until Cray walks by.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to win a rowing race by gusting my sail or freezing a rival's oars so that magic creates comedy.
Boats are kinematic course-followers on the standing-water pool (no flow sim): speed from a rowing input rhythm, plus force stimuli on the sail (any impulse), minus frozen oars (frozen property halts a boat for 3 s). Cheat rule: magic observed by Cray disqualifies.

## Scope
- In: Boat kinematic course entity, rowing input, stimulus responses, contest definition
- Out: Boat physics or flowing water (not planned)

## Notes
True extra: cut first if schedule slips.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a force impulse applied to the player's sail, when evaluated, then boat speed rises by the impulse-derived boost for its duration.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a rival's oars frozen by any cold stimulus, when evaluated, then that boat halts for 3 s.
- AC-3 [integration] Given Cray perceives a cast during the race, when detected, then the player is disqualified and fact cray.regattaCheat is set (edge).

title: Place dungeon secrets, notes, horn-coins and lore books
description:
## Why
Lore is offered, not lectured; the dungeon should reward every detour.

## What
As a curious player, I want hidden rooms, notes and relics so that I piece together the history myself.
Place 6–8 "friend below" notes, horn-coins (tiny ox asleep on the back), Hornfolk inscription fragments (sorcerer route), Mooring-era items, damaged spellbook pages, the Ox Beneath the Hill last page, 12–20 treasures per the e18 guide, and one book mimic trap per area.

## Scope
- In: Placements, discovery rules, facts
- Out: Text (e39-books-lore, e39-dialogue-abbot)

## Notes
Three sources that disagree for each big fact (bible §7.1).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the dungeon scenes, when audited, then every "friend below" note id from e39 is placed exactly once.
- AC-2 [content] Given the big facts (Long Vespers, the minotaur), when audited, then each has >= 3 placed sources (book, object, person).
- AC-3 [integration] Given a secret room opened, when saved and reloaded, then it stays open (edge).

title: Place wilderness and river secrets, lore caches and treasure
description:
## Why
The world rewards curiosity: a hollow tree, a drowned cart, a goblin stash.

## What
As a curious player, I want hidden things in the Briarwood and the tower so that detours pay.
Placement: Tansy's hair ribbon on the mine rail, the keeper's log pages, a goblin stash in a hollow oak, a drowned cart in the lane, a Juniper snare cache, a spellbook page in the woodcutter's hut, Mags' split-plank horn-coin at the quay, the Kestrel Lock toll board, a lost cargo crate in the lock chamber, and 8–12 small treasures.

## Scope
- In: Placements, discovery rules, facts
- Out: Text (e39-books-lore, e39-item-creature-text)

## Notes
Use e18 treasure density guidance.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the wilderness scenes, when audited, then every "interesting-looking" landmark tag has >= 1 placed discovery.
- AC-2 [integration] Given Tansy's ribbon picked up, when inspected, then its item text matches e39 text ids.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a cache looted, when saved and reloaded, then it remains empty (edge).

title: Place the Standing Horn menhir and its readable inscription
description:
## Why
Statues speak through posture; the menhir teaches the Hornfolk visual language early.

## What
As a player, I want a Hornfolk stone with hands over its ears so that I start to understand the people who built the Knot.
Clearing with the menhir (hands over ears), an inscription band readable in part by any class and fully by a sorcerer holding Hornfolk fragments (reveals the first rule of the Knot), a hidden horn-coin under a root, and a quiet spot where the song is audible at night (hint of what is below).

## Scope
- In: Menhir placement, inscription readable with conditions, hidden coin, night audio emitter
- Out: Inscription text (e39-books-lore)

## Notes
Resolves rumour 12.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a sorcerer with the Hornfolk fragment item, when reading, then the full inscription shows and lore.knot.rule1 is set.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a non-sorcerer, when reading, then a partial translation shows and no fact is set (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player reaches the clearing, when entered, then rumour 12 resolves.

title: Place Briar Glen's secrets, lore books and hidden treasure
description:
## Why
Interesting-looking places should usually contain something interesting; every bookshelf has a book.

## What
As a curious player, I want secrets in town — stashes, notes, books — so that exploring town pays off.
Placement: every bookshelf gets a book, Dot's stamped trinket in the cellar, Hale's dusty boots (Captain's Boots clue), the Pell family Bible, the "friend below" note under the player's door, a thief stash on the Forge roof, a chimney cache, and 6–10 small treasures per the e18 treasure guide.

## Scope
- In: Lore/treasure placements, discovery rules, fact ids
- Out: Text (e39-books-lore)
- Out: Loot tables design (e18-treasure-design-guide)

## Notes
Density target from e18-treasure-design-guide.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the town scenes, when audited, then every bookshelf entity has >= 1 book placed.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player morning 1, when they leave the room, then the "friend below" note is at the door and readable.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a hidden stash taken, when saved and reloaded, then it stays empty (edge).

title: Place the rumour set on sources and wire targets to real facts
description:
## Why
"NPC rumors can lead somewhere." Each of the twelve rumours must point at something placed.

## What
As a player, I want rumours from Dot, townsfolk and goblins to lead to real places so that talking becomes exploring.
Bind e39 rumour data to sources (Dot, townsfolk tags, goblins) and ensure each rumour's resolvesWhen fact is produced by placed content (well echo, Mooring armour, stamped trinkets, cracked bell, ledger, restricted shelf, Hale's boots, millpond lantern, the Fold, Clatter, the Standing Horn).

## Scope
- In: Source bindings, fact producers placed where missing, validation run
- Out: Rumour text (e39-rumor-set)
- Out: Rumour runtime (e22-rumors)

## Notes
Rumours 10–11 come from goblins (E26 camp).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the rumour set, when validated, then all 12 rumours have >= 1 source and a produced resolvesWhen fact (no warnings).
- AC-2 [integration] Given rumour 4 heard and the cistern entered, when evaluated, then it resolves as Investigated.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the false rumour 3 (goblins took them), when the Framed in Brass proof is found, then it resolves with a "false" journal note (edge).

title: Build the lychgate cemetery and the empty schoolhouse
description:
## Why
Quiet places carry the story: Vesperine graves and a teacher's empty desk.

## What
As a player, I want to find lore in the cemetery and schoolhouse so that the town's history and its missing people feel real.
Cemetery: lychgate, Vesperine graves with epitaphs (Hornfolk ear-covering motif on the oldest), Mooring family plot, a fresh unmarked grave (false alarm, humour beat). Schoolhouse: Mina Coles' desk, the skipping rhyme on the slate, Tansy's reading corner, a torn page from The Ox Beneath the Hill.

## Scope
- In: Two small scenes/areas, readable epitaphs and slate, lore item placements
- Out: Text content (e39-books-lore)

## Notes
The torn last page links to Tansy's copy of the book (lore payoff).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given both areas, when validated, then every readable references an existing text id.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player reads the slate rhyme, when complete, then fact lore.rhyme.read is set (used by Mirela dialogue).
- AC-3 [integration] Given night, when the player enters the cemetery, then no hostile creature spawns there (tone rule: the lights are on in town, edge).

title: Author the Stacks' restricted shelf and forbidden back room
description:
## Why
Some books are expensive, forbidden, hidden or stolen; Mirela's curtain and back room are where the sorcerer's best finds live.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a restricted shelf that opens when Mirela trusts me and a back room holding a book she will never sell so that trust and theft both matter.
Restricted shelf (Mirror Self, Gravity Well and other restricted schools — writ or Trusted disposition), back room with Nine Sleeps on a locked lectern (never for sale; readable; stealable, teaching Lull), Court-seal markings, and Mirela's reaction facts.

## Scope
- In: Secret/restricted stock data, back-room scene dressing, Nine Sleeps placement, reaction facts
- Out: Public stock (e24-lamplit-stacks)
- Out: Forbidden-book side effects (e07-forbidden-books)

## Notes
Legality per story bible §3.3. Rumour 7 resolves on first restricted-shelf reveal.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given disposition below Trusted and no writ, when viewing the restricted shelf, then its stock is hidden; at Trusted it appears and rumour 7 resolves.
- AC-2 [integration] Given Nine Sleeps, when the player attempts to buy it, then it is not for sale; when stolen, then theft is recorded and Mirela reacts on the next visit (edge).
- AC-3 [content] Given the secret stock data, when pnpm validate:bookshops runs, then every restricted book carries the restricted legality tag and no forbidden book is purchasable.

title: Add Mortimer, the tame book mimic who guards the rare shelf
description:
## Why
Mortimer makes the bookshop memorable and makes shoplifting a story rather than a menu.

## What
As a player, I want Mirela's tame mimic to bite shoplifters and be won over with paper so that the bookshop has a guardian with personality.
npc-mortimer: stationary mimic on the rare shelf; detects witnessed theft from the shop (e27-ownership-theft) within 6 m and bites (non-lethal); sets mirela.banned for 1 in-game day; bringing biscuits to Mirela lifts it early; can be fed paper for a treat (Mortimer's tooth rare drop if provoked).

## Scope
- In: Creature data, theft-detect-and-bite rule, ban fact with timeout, feed rule
- Out: Bookshop stock (e24-lamplit-stacks)
- Out: Snig-meets-Mortimer beat (e39-side-quests-town)

## Notes
Mortimer never leaves his shelf; theft from other shelves out of his view is not detected by him.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player takes an owned book within Mortimer's view, when theft is recorded, then Mortimer bites for non-lethal damage and mirela.banned is set.
- AC-2 [unit] Given mirela.banned set at day 3 08:00, when world time reaches day 4 08:00, then the ban clears.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a theft outside Mortimer's view, when recorded, then Mortimer does not react (edge).

title: Bring Snig to life: pocket-picking, reading lessons and vouching
description:
## Why
Snig is the game's comic heart and the goblin who wants to read.

## What
As a player, I want Snig to steal from me, follow me and vouch for me so that he becomes a recurring ally.
npc-snig: attempts to pickpocket the player (thief can notice and allow — snig.trusted); Bookshop Burglar outcomes as facts (jailed, lessons, scared of the reading one); follower mode in town and mine; vouch flag used by Horn befriend; fear of Mortimer (flees if within 5 m).

## Scope
- In: Creature data, pickpocket-the-player behaviour, follower mode, outcome facts
- Out: Bookshop Burglar quest graph (e39-side-quests-town)

## Notes
If jailed, the thief can bust him out through the jail drain (e24-watch-house-jail).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given Snig adjacent and the player idle, when his pickpocket attempt succeeds, then one low-value item moves to his inventory and the thief class receives a notice prompt.
- AC-2 [integration] Given snig.lessons is set, when Horn's befriend conditions are evaluated, then the vouch option is available.
- AC-3 [integration] Given Mortimer within 5 m of Snig, when evaluated, then Snig flees and follower mode pauses until distance > 10 m (edge).

title: Add optional quest wayfinding hints as an accessibility setting
description:
## Why
Default play favours discovery (no waypoints), but some players need help navigating; an opt-in hint respects both.
## What
As a player who gets lost, I want to enable subtle hints toward my pinned objective so that I can keep playing without a guide.

Objectives may author `hintTarget` (entity/area). Setting "Quest hints": Off (default) / Subtle (compass nudge when facing direction) / Clear (on-screen marker). Hints never reveal hidden/secret objectives.
## Scope
- In: Hint target data, three-level setting, compass nudge + marker rendering hook
- Out: Full world map (not planned for MVP)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: compass nudge glyph, objective marker icon.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given setting Off, when a pinned objective has a hintTarget, then no hint renders.
- AC-2 [integration] Given setting Clear, when the target is on-screen, then a marker renders at its projected position; off-screen, an edge arrow renders.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a hidden objective with a hintTarget, when any setting is active, then no hint renders for it.

title: Add quest debug commands and "why is this stuck" explainer
description:
## Why
Diagnosing stuck quests must be fast for designers and playtest bug reports.
## What
Debug console: `quest.list`, `quest.start <id>`, `quest.objective <id> <obj> complete`, `quest.resolve <id> <res>`, `quest.why <id>` (prints each resolution/objective condition with describe() and current truth values). CLI `pnpm quest:sim <id> --script path` to run a quest against scripted fact/item changes headlessly.
## Scope
- In: Console commands, explainer, headless quest simulator
- Out: Visual quest editor (post-MVP)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an active quest with an unmet resolution condition, when `quest.why` runs, then output lists that condition as false with its describe() text.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `quest.resolve q1 bogus`, when executed, then the console lists valid resolution ids and changes nothing.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a scripted sim of the reference quest stealth path, when run headlessly, then it ends with resolution `stealth`.

title: Add dialogue preview runner and debug console commands
description:
## Why
Fast content creation (constitution §10): writers need to play a conversation in seconds with any state.
## What
CLI `pnpm dialogue:play <id> --class thief --fact x=true --item y` running the real runtime in the terminal; `pnpm dialogue:graph <id>` exporting Mermaid for docs/review. Debug console: `dlg.start <id>`, `disp.set <npc> <n>`, `fact.set`, `rumor.list`.
## Scope
- In: Terminal runner, Mermaid export, console commands
- Out: A visual dialogue editor (post-MVP)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a fixture dialogue and `--class thief`, when run with scripted choice input, then the transcript matches the snapshot including the thief option.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `dialogue:graph`, when run on a fixture, then the output is valid Mermaid containing every node id.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `disp.set unknown-npc 50`, when executed, then the console reports an unknown NPC and changes nothing.

title: Show ambient NPC barks as accessible positional subtitles
description:
## Why
Overheard lines make the world feel alive and deliver rumors and stealth feedback; without voice they must be readable subtitles.
## What
As a player, I want to read what nearby characters say (guards muttering, merchants calling out) with speaker names and direction so that I overhear the world.

Bark runtime: condition-filtered lines triggered by events (alert state changes, proximity, time), priority + cooldown + anti-repetition. Subtitle display: speaker name, direction indicator for off-screen speakers, max 3 concurrent, respects text size, background opacity and "show speaker names" settings; can be toggled.
## Scope
- In: Bark schema + selector, subtitle HUD, settings hooks
- Out: Merchant bark content (e20-merchant-barks)
- Out: AI state bark triggers wiring (mw-e11 emits events)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: subtitle background plate, off-screen direction chevron.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 5 barks triggered in the same second, when displayed, then at most 3 are visible, ordered by priority.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a bark line used once with cooldown 30 s, when triggered again at 10 s, then a different line or no line is chosen.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a speaker behind the camera, when a bark shows, then a direction indicator points toward the speaker.
- AC-4 [integration] Given subtitles disabled for barks in settings, when a bark triggers, then nothing is shown but the bark event is still emitted for telemetry/tests.

title: Add economy balance report and CI gate
description:
## Why
Balance drifts as content grows; a CI gate keeps gold meaningful without playtesting every change.
## What
CLI `pnpm content:economy-report`: sums expected obtainable gold (loot report + quest rewards + sellable items at average buy rates) vs total cost of meaningful sinks (books, techniques, tools, services) for the MVP region; fails CI if the ratio leaves the band in docs/design/economy.md. Outputs markdown report artifact.
## Scope
- In: Report CLI, CI step, markdown output
- Out: Loot distribution details (e18-treasure-audit-tool, reused)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given fixture content with known totals, when the report runs, then the computed ratio matches the analytic value.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a ratio outside the configured band, when run in CI mode, then the process exits non-zero naming the direction (too rich/too poor).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a quest with a gold reward effect, when the report runs, then it is included in obtainable gold.

title: Add data-driven merchant barks for shop events
description:
## Why
Merchants with personality (QfG5) react to what you do — browsing forever, haggling badly, offering them their own candlestick.
## What
Bark sets keyed by shop event (`greet`, `browseLong`, `buyExpensive`, `sellJunk`, `haggleWin`, `haggleFail`, `stolenRecognized`, `banned`, `farewell`) with condition filters and anti-repetition (no same line twice within 5 uses). Uses e22 bark system for display.
## Scope
- In: Bark set schema for shop events, selection logic, 1 grey-box bark set
- Out: Actual merchant writing (world-content group)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a bark set with 3 greet lines, when greet fires 3 times, then 3 distinct lines are chosen before any repeats.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a `browseLong` threshold of 60 s in the shop UI, when exceeded, then exactly one browseLong bark is emitted.
- AC-3 [content] Given a bark set missing the `greet` event, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Add haggling with class options and disposition risk
description:
## Why
QfG-style merchant banter and DOS2 persuasion make trading a social encounter rather than a spreadsheet.
## What
As a player, I want to haggle a price using my class's strengths (knight's reputation, thief's bluff, sorcerer's impressive trick, archer's trade in pelts) so that talking well saves gold.

Haggle is a short dialogue sub-flow: choose an approach, deterministic check (disposition + class/capability modifiers + merchant personality), success grants a haggle modifier (bounded by the economy doc), failure worsens price or disposition; limited to 2 attempts per item per day.
## Scope
- In: Haggle flow via dialogue runtime, deterministic check formula, attempt limits, personality modifiers
- Out: General persuasion checks (e22-persuasion-checks is reused)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a greedy merchant and a thief bluff approach with modifiers summing above threshold, when haggling, then the price improves by the data-defined amount and never beyond the doc cap.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a failed haggle, when resolved, then disposition drops per personality data and the next haggle on that item has a penalty.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 2 attempts already made on an item today, when a third is requested, then the option is unavailable with the merchant's refusal line.
- AC-4 [unit] Given identical state, when the same haggle is attempted twice from the same save, then the outcome is identical (no hidden randomness).

title: Allow stealing shop stock with witness-based consequences
description:
## Why
Shops are prime thief targets; lifting an item from a counter while the merchant is distracted is a classic thief moment.
## What
As a thief, I want to steal displayed wares or from the merchant's stock when unobserved so that distractions and timing pay off.

Shop display items are world items owned by the merchant; taking them uses e18 ownership + witness checks. Witnessed shoplifting: merchant disposition drop, prices up, possible ban (`merchant.banned` fact) and guard alert. Stolen shop stock decrements merchant stock.
## Scope
- In: Display items bound to merchant stock, consequences ladder (warning → price hike → ban), ban lifting via fine/quest effect
- Out: Pickpocketing the merchant (mw-e10)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an unwitnessed theft of a displayed item, when taken, then merchant stock decrements and the instance is stolen with owner = merchant.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a first witnessed theft, when detected, then the consequence ladder moves to "warning" and disposition drops per data.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a banned merchant, when the player opens the shop, then trade is refused with a ban dialogue line until a `fine.paid` effect lifts the ban.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the greybox shop with a merchant facing away, when the thief takes a displayed item, then no crime event fires; facing toward, then one fires.

title: Implement respec/loadout policy decided in the progression ADR
description:
## Why
Experimentation is a pillar; if any capability choices are exclusive, players need a fair way to change them.
## What
As a player, I want to adjust my loadout of prepared capabilities (per ADR) so that I can experiment without restarting.

Implements whatever the ADR chose: expected default is loadout slots (e.g. prepared spells / equipped techniques) swappable at rest points, with no destructive respec because learned capabilities are additive.
## Scope
- In: Loadout slots per ADR, swap rules, rest-point integration, save section
- Out: Anything the ADR rejects
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a loadout of N slots full, when a new capability is slotted at a rest point, then the displaced one returns to the known pool (never lost).
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player is not at a rest point, when a swap is requested, then it fails with reason `not-at-rest` if the ADR requires rest.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a slotted capability later revoked (e.g. source item lost), when revoked, then its slot empties and an event is emitted.
close_reason: Won't do: superseded by ADR-0004 (owner decision 2026-10-02) — capabilities are additive, no respec and no loadout slots

title: Unlock capabilities from notable deeds via data-driven rules
description:
## Why
Some verbs are best earned by doing something memorable (befriending the minotaur, surviving a fall into the mine), rewarding curiosity instead of repetition.
## What
As a player, I want remarkable actions to teach me something so that the world itself trains me.

Deed rules: `{when: event/fact conditions, grants: capability, once: true, message}` evaluated on world-state changes. Explicitly not repetition counters (anti-grind): validator rejects deed rules whose condition is a count > 3 of the same event unless flagged.
## Scope
- In: Deed rule schema, evaluator on world-state/event bus, validator anti-grind rule, notification event
- Out: Specific deeds (world-content group)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a deed rule on fact `minotaur.befriended`, when the fact becomes true, then the capability is learned with channel `deed` exactly once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the fact toggles false then true again, when evaluated, then the deed does not grant twice.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a deed rule requiring 20 kills of the same creature type without `allowRepetition`, when validated, then validation fails citing the anti-grind rule.

title: Build treasure audit and loot distribution report tool
description:
## Why
Designers need to see what a region yields before playtesting it, and to catch gold inflation or missing books.
## What
CLI `pnpm content:loot-report [region]`: enumerates placements, containers and creature drops; simulates each table N times (seeded) and outputs expected gold, item counts by category, unique artifact locations, and per-class availability of progression items (books, tools, schematics). Debug console command `loot.roll <table> [n]`.
## Scope
- In: CLI report (markdown + JSON), console command
- Out: Economy balance CI gate (e20-economy-balance-tool)
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a fixture region with 2 containers and known tables, when the report runs with seed 1 and N=1000, then expected gold equals the analytic expectation within ±1%.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a region where a class-gated progression item has no source, when the report runs, then it lists that item under "Unobtainable".
- AC-3 [unit] Given `loot.roll unknown-table`, when executed in the console, then it reports an error and suggests close matches.

title: Environmental takedowns: drop, push and douse via world properties
description:
## Why
The progression ladder ends at environmental takedowns; the world itself becomes the thief’s weapon, and it must be systemic.

## What
As a thief, I want to drop a chandelier, cut a hanging load or push a crate from a ledge onto an enemy so that the world does my work. Any object with `suspended` property released (cut rope, shot chain, lever) falls under physics; impact damage = f(mass, fall height) via the damage model. Deaths/knockouts caused by environment are tagged `accident` so witnesses raise lower suspicion (Suspicious/Investigating instead of Alerted) unless they perceived the player causing it.

## Scope
- In: Falling-object damage rule by mass/height
- In: Accident attribution + AI response weights
- Out: Specific set-pieces (E26 content)
- Out: Rope cutting by arrows (E05, works via property)

## Notes
Property-based: never "chandelier" in rules.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any object tagged `suspended` with mass 80 kg released from 5 m onto a creature, when impact resolves, then damage equals the documented mass×height curve.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature killed by a falling object with no witness perceiving the player within 3 s, when attributed, then the event is tagged `accident`.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a witness to an `accident`, when evaluated, then it enters Investigating (not Alerted).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a witness perceived the player releasing the object, when evaluated, then it enters Alerted with the player LKP.

title: Lean around corners and peek through keyholes
description:
## Why
Information is the thief’s currency; peeking lets players scout routines before committing.

## What
As a thief, I want to lean around corners and peek through keyholes so that I can scout without exposing myself. Lean shifts camera and exposes only the head sample point to LOS (reduced visibility). Keyhole peek on doors with a `keyhole` flag gives a narrow view of the next room with the player fully hidden from that room.

## Scope
- In: Lean input + camera offset + LOS sample override
- In: Keyhole peek interaction
- Out: Camera system (e02-camera)

## Notes
During lean, only the head sample point counts for LOS (1 of 4).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player leaning, when LOS is queried by an observer, then only the head sample point is considered.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a door without a keyhole, when interaction options are built, then peek is not offered.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a keyhole peek, when active, then the camera renders from the keyhole position and visibility to observers in the other room is 0.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player is attacked while peeking, when damage applies, then peek ends immediately.

title: Silent movement unlocks: soft steps, muffled gear, shadow dash
description:
## Why
Anti-grind rule: progression unlocks verbs, not +12%. Silent movement should grow into new capabilities.

## What
As a thief, I want to unlock ways to move more silently so that I can take bolder routes. Capability unlocks via the progression model: `soft-step` (sneak gait ignores creaky-board creaks and gravel offset), `muffled-gear` (equipment noise halved while sneaking), `shadow-dash` (short burst of sneak-speed movement at walk noise while in light ≤ 0.2). Each is a data-defined modifier applied to the footstep/visibility rules.

## Scope
- In: Three capability modifiers as data + rule hooks
- Out: Progression UI and unlock sources (E19)

## Notes
Modifiers alter inputs to e09-footstep-noise and e09-visibility-model only; rules stay pure.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given `soft-step` unlocked, when sneaking on `wood-creaky`, then no creak event is ever emitted over 1,000 seeded steps.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `muffled-gear` and equipment noise +10 dB, when sneaking, then the footstep includes +5 dB equipment noise.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `shadow-dash` in light 0.5, when activated, then it is refused because light exceeds 0.2.
- AC-4 [unit] Given no unlocks, when evaluated, then footstep results equal the base rule exactly.

title: Place traps: noisemakers, tripwires and caltrops
description:
## Why
Traps let the thief shape the battlefield ahead of time — dirty tricks and disengagement are the thief combat fantasy.

## What
As a thief, I want to place traps so that I can lure, slow or warn about enemies. Place trap items on valid surfaces with a placement preview: noisemaker (timed or triggered noise event), tripwire (trigger volume between two anchors → alarm noise for player, or trip/stagger), caltrops (slow + damage zone, noise when stepped). Traps are world objects with properties (flammable tripwire burns, etc.), perceivable by AI (visibility check); perceiving an armed trap makes AI avoid it and become Suspicious.

## Scope
- In: Placement preview + validity, trap objects, trigger logic via e03-triggers
- In: AI avoidance of perceived traps (nav cost)
- Out: World/dungeon traps and disarming (e10-trap-disarm)
- Out: Trap art (placeholders)

## Notes
Creatures can trigger player traps; the player can too (friendly fire).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a caltrops item and a flat valid surface, when placed, then a slow zone (×0.5 speed) with damage 2/s exists at the location.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a placement on a slope > 30° or in water, when previewed, then placement is invalid with reason.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a tripwire between two anchors, when any creature crosses it, then its trigger fires once and it becomes spent.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a guard perceives an armed caltrops zone, when pathing, then its path avoids the zone if an alternative exists and it enters Suspicious.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a tripwire tagged `flammable` in a fire volume, when 1 s passes, then it burns and is removed without triggering.

title: Disguises that fool factions until behaviour gives you away
description:
## Why
Disguises are a later thief verb in the progression ladder and create social infiltration moments.

## What
As a thief, I want to wear a faction’s uniform so that I can walk among guards if I behave. Equipping a `disguise:<faction>` item makes that faction’s members treat the player as `disguised` instead of intruder: sight stimuli accumulate a separate suspicion meter driven by proximity (< 3 m), suspicious behaviour (running, crouching, climbing, being in restricted zones, being seen committing crimes, carrying bodies), and observer traits (officers and dogs see through faster; `sees-through-disguise` flag). Suspicion full → disguise blown for that zone (remembered).

## Scope
- In: Disguise state, per-observer suspicion rules, restricted zone data, blown-state memory
- Out: Dialogue with disguised player (E22)
- Out: Uniform art (placeholder recolour)

## Notes
Suspicion rules are tuning data; restricted zones are level regions.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player wears a disguise of faction A and walks at normal speed 8 m from an A guard in a public zone, when 30 s pass, then the guard remains Unaware.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same player sprints within 3 m, when evaluated, then disguise suspicion accumulates at the running rate and the guard enters Suspicious within 3 s.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an observer flagged `sees-through-disguise`, when it perceives the player, then the disguise is ignored.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the disguise is blown in zone Z, when the player re-enters Z still disguised, then Z’s guards treat the player as an intruder.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a faction B guard, when perceiving the player in faction A disguise, then normal intruder rules apply.

title: Playtest and tune stealth feel on the grey-box course
description:
## Why
A perfectly executed infiltration should feel as satisfying as a hard fight; only playtesting confirms that.

## What
Run 5 playtest sessions on the stealth course and first dungeon grey-box, record telemetry (detections, causes, time in each state, restarts), adjust tuning data, document changes in `docs/design/stealth-tuning-log.md`.

## Scope
- In: Sessions, telemetry capture, tuning edits, log
- Out: New mechanics (file new beads)

## Notes
Tuning changes that alter scenario baselines must update them in the same PR with rationale.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given 5 sessions, when players complete the course, then ≥ 4 of 5 rate stealth ≥ 4/5 for “I understood why I was seen”.
- AC-2 [integration] Given telemetry events for alert transitions, when exported, then each includes cause, state, and time-in-state fields.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the tuning log, when reviewed, then each change lists the metric that motivated it.

title: Stealth accessibility assists: slower detection, stronger cues
description:
## Why
Stealth must be approachable for players with different reaction speeds, hearing or vision without removing its systemic nature.

## What
As a player, I want stealth assist options so that I can enjoy infiltration at my own pace. Options: detection speed (50–150%), show indicators for unperceived agents, visual captions for noise events (“Footsteps — left”), stronger visibility gem contrast, extended hiding stagger window. Applied via the whitelisted stealth/AI tuning overrides.

## Scope
- In: Settings entries, override application, captions for noise events
- Out: Global accessibility framework (E31)

## Notes
Assists alter tuning inputs only; rules stay identical so scenario tests still hold at 100%.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given detection speed 50%, when a constant stimulus accumulates, then time to Suspicious doubles versus 100%.
- AC-2 [integration] Given noise captions on, when a 40 dB noise is perceived by the player from the left, then a caption with direction `left` appears within 100 ms.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an assist value outside the allowed range in settings storage, when loaded, then it clamps to the nearest bound.
- AC-4 [integration] Given all assists off, when the infiltration suite runs, then baselines are unchanged.

title: Show a last-known-position ghost where enemies think you are
description:
## Why
Showing where guards believe you are turns last-known position into a tool — the player can see the gap between belief and reality and exploit it.

## What
As a thief, I want to see a faint silhouette where the enemies last saw me so that I can plan to double back or set up an ambush. When at least one hunting agent (Searching/Alerted) holds a player LKP and the player is out of its perception, render a translucent silhouette at the LKP in the stance last observed. Disappears when all agents lose the memory or re-acquire. Toggleable.

## Scope
- In: Ghost model from aggregated agent memories
- In: Placeholder translucent capsule silhouette
- In: Settings toggle
- Out: Accurate player mesh silhouette (asset integration later)

## Notes
Aggregate: show the most recent LKP among hunting agents; if two diverge by > 10 m, show both.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given one Searching agent with an LKP and no perception of the player, when the ghost model is built, then one ghost at that LKP is returned.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the agent re-acquires the player, when the model is built, then no ghost is returned.
- AC-3 [unit] Given two hunting agents with LKPs 15 m apart, when built, then two ghosts are returned; if 5 m apart, one.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box course, when the player breaks LOS from an Alerted guard, then a ghost appears at the break point within 250 ms.

title: Write the creature authoring guide with a worked example
description:
## Why
The world-content group will author the bestiary in parallel; a single guide keeps creatures consistent and systemic.

## What
A designer guide `docs/content/creatures.md`: every schema section explained, how senses/fears/needs/personality affect AI, property-based vulnerability rules, a worked example built from fixtures (not a real bestiary creature), checklist for a new creature (data, smoke test, placeholder asset ids, prompt bead).

## Scope
- In: Guide + checklist + links to generated schema reference
- Out: Bestiary entries (E13)

## Notes
Link from docs/backlog-contract.md is out of scope for this bead; content group will reference the guide.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the guide, when its worked-example JSON is extracted by a doc test, then it validates against `CreatureDef`.
- AC-2 [manual] Given a designer unfamiliar with the code, when following the checklist, then they can add a new creature that passes the smoke harness in ≤ 30 min.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the generated schema reference, when a schema field is added without documentation, then the doc-coverage check fails.

title: Creature needs (hunger, sleep, fatigue) with behaviour hooks
description:
## Why
A hungry beast that can be lured with meat or a guard who dozes at 3am turns creatures into systems the player can read and exploit.

## What
As a thief, I want creatures to eat, sleep and tire so that I can time or engineer my approach. Needs (hunger, sleep, fatigue, plus extensible custom needs) rise over sim time at data-defined rates; satisfiers are world objects tagged with properties (`edible:meat`, `bed`) or schedule windows. Crossing thresholds emits intents (`SeekFood`, `Sleep`) the behaviour runtime may choose. Sleeping creatures use a reduced sense profile.

## Scope
- In: Need decay/satisfaction model
- In: Property-based satisfier discovery via perception
- In: Sleep modifies senses (e.g. sight off, hearing −20 dB)
- Out: Day/night world clock (owned by world/time systems — Related: world clock)
- Out: Poisoned bait (e10 / alchemy post-MVP)

## Notes
Needs must be cheap: update at 1 Hz, not per tick. Related: a world time-of-day clock is needed for schedule windows; if none exists use sim time with a configurable day length.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given hunger rate 10/min and threshold 70, when 7 sim minutes pass from 0, then a `SeekFood` intent is emitted exactly once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a hungry creature that perceives any object tagged `edible:meat` within 15 m, when it chooses `SeekFood`, then its target is the nearest perceived edible object.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a sleeping creature, when a 30 dB noise occurs 5 m away and its awake threshold is 25 dB with sleep penalty 20 dB, then it does not wake; a 50 dB noise wakes it into Suspicious.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an edible object that is removed while a creature walks to it, when it arrives, then the intent fails gracefully and the creature returns to its routine within 3 s.
- AC-5 [unit] Given 200 creatures with needs, when 1 sim hour elapses, then needs update 3,600 times per creature (1 Hz) and never per tick.

title: Personality traits that weight AI decisions per individual
description:
## Why
Personalities make creatures memorable: a lazy guard who gives up searching early, a curious goblin who investigates every noise.

## What
Trait vector (bravery, curiosity, aggression, diligence, sociability, greed) 0–1 per creature, def default plus seeded per-spawn jitter within a declared range. Traits are exposed as inputs to the behaviour runtime (utility weights or BT conditions) and to tuning curves (e.g. diligence scales search duration).

## Scope
- In: Schema, deterministic jitter, accessor API
- In: Documented list of which AI behaviours read which trait
- Out: Dialogue personality/voice (E22)
- Out: Named-character authored personalities (E13/E14 content)

## Notes
Jitter must come from the seeded sim RNG keyed by entity id so replays match.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a def with curiosity 0.5 ± 0.2, when 1,000 spawns are sampled with a fixed seed, then all values lie within 0.3–0.7 and the sequence is identical across runs.
- AC-2 [unit] Given diligence 1.0 vs 0.0 with base search duration 60 s and diligence scale 0.5–1.5, then search durations are 90 s and 30 s respectively.
- AC-3 [content] Given a trait outside 0–1, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature with no personality section, when resolved, then all traits default to 0.5 with zero jitter.

title: Write item and creature description text
description:
## Why
Lore lives in item text (Dark Souls) and creatures are characters, not target dummies; descriptions should imply history and hint at non-combat options.

## What
As a player, I want item and creature descriptions that hint at stories and weaknesses so that reading them helps me play. 1–3 sentence descriptions for every MVP key item, quest item, notable equipment and consumable; descriptions for Wendmouth imports (foreign weapons/armour, exotic arrows, Undertow thief tools) and the harbour's human factions (Low Tide Company, harbour watch, Tern crew); bestiary/inspect text for all 10 creature types in bible §8 (Wendmouth adds none), each hinting at at least one non-lethal or systemic option (fear of light, sound sensitivity, flammability, feeding).

## Scope
- In: desc-* fields for items and creatures
- In: bestiary entries with unlock tiers (seen / studied)
- Out: creature stats/behaviour (Related: E12/E13)
- Out: loot placement (Related: E18)

## Notes
Voice examples in bible §7.4. Avoid numbers in flavour text; mechanics belong in tooltips.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given item and creature data, when validated, then every MVP item and each of the 10 creature types has a description of 1–3 sentences.
- AC-2 [content] Given each creature entry, when reviewed against bible §8, then it hints at ≥ 1 non-combat or systemic interaction.
- AC-3 [unit] Given all flavour text, when scanned, then it contains no digits (numbers belong in tooltips).
- AC-4 [unit] Edge: given a creature at "seen" tier, when its bestiary entry is shown, then only the seen-tier text is returned and studied-tier hints stay hidden.

title: Write spellbook titles, authors and flavour texts
description:
## Why
For the sorcerer, books are progression; each spellbook should feel like a found object with a voice, not a stat card.

## What
