As a sorcerer, I want each spellbook to have a title, an author and a human detail so that buying or finding one feels special. Flavour for every MVP spell (~15–20), following bible §7.3 house style, plus Lantern Court seal status (licensed/restricted/forbidden), and damaged-copy variant text for books that teach misfiring versions.

## Scope
- In: flavour fields on spellbook item data (title, author, blurb, seal status, damaged variant)
- In: Nine Sleeps ch. 1 (Lull) forbidden flavour
- Out: spell mechanics and the spell catalogue (Related: E08 spell catalogue)
- Out: learning mechanics (e07-spellbook-learning)

## Notes
School legality per bible §3.3. Keep each blurb ≤ 80 words and include one concrete, human or funny detail.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the spellbook data, when validated, then every spell in the MVP catalogue has exactly one spellbook with title, author, blurb and seal status.
- AC-2 [unit] Given each spellbook, when its seal status is compared with its school, then it matches the legality table in bible §3.3.
- AC-3 [unit] Given each blurb, when measured, then it is ≤ 80 words.
- AC-4 [content] Edge: given a book with a damaged variant, when validated, then the damaged text differs from the intact text and names the misfire flavour.
- AC-5 [manual] Given a read-through, when the narrative designer reviews all blurbs, then none reads as a numeric stat description.

title: Write in-game books, notes and inscriptions
description:
## Why
"Bookshelves can contain books." Lore should come from contradicting voices in objects and texts, Souls- and Elder Scrolls-style, and the bookshop must feel stocked.

## What
As a player, I want to find short, readable books and notes that reveal the world in pieces so that curiosity is rewarded. Full texts for the bible §7.2 books (Vesperine Hours, Traveller's Account, On the Silence of Goblins, The Ox Beneath the Hill, Keeper's Log, Abbot's Letters, Nine Sleeps lore pages, Deepworks Ledger), 8–12 additional short books for the Lamplit Stacks and shelves, notes (Hale's list, Duggan's instructions, sleepwalker scrawls), and statue/wall inscriptions.

## Scope
- In: book-* data files with title, author, text, location(s)
- In: note-* and inscription-* data
- In: ≥ 3 independent sources for each major fact (Long Vespers, Horn, the bell)
- Out: spellbook teaching texts (e39-spellbook-flavor)
- Out: bookshop stock rules (e21-bookshop-system)

## Notes
Length 100–300 words per book (readable in under a minute); the Vesper hymn text must be identical everywhere it appears.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given all book, note and inscription files, when validated, then they pass and each has ≥ 1 placement location from the glossary.
- AC-2 [unit] Given each book text, when measured, then word count is between 40 and 400.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the Vesper hymn, when every occurrence is compared, then all occurrences are byte-identical.
- AC-4 [content] Given the lore map in the file header, when checked, then the Long Vespers, Horn's role and the bell each have ≥ 3 independent sources (book, object, person).
- AC-5 [content] Edge: given the damaged-book convention, when a book is flagged damaged, then its text includes the missing/illegible markers the UI renders.

title: Write the rumour set with sources, truth values and targets
description:
## Why
The constitution promises that NPC rumours lead somewhere; rumours are the town's map of secrets.

## What
As a player, I want rumours that are true, half-true or false and point at real places so that listening pays off. Encodes town/wilderness rumours 1–12 in bible §6.2 (plus up to 6 more; harbour rumours 13–18 live in e39-harbor-rumors-texts) with source NPC(s), truth value, target location/secret, unlock conditions, and follow-up lines when the player confirms or debunks one with Dot.

## Scope
- In: src/content/rumors data
- In: truth value (true | half | false) and target reference per rumour
- In: Dot trade-back lines for confirmed/debunked rumours
- Out: rumour UI/journal (E22)
- Out: Dot's general dialogue (e39-dialogue-town-core)

## Notes
Every target must resolve to a glossary location, quest or fact. Goblin rumours are only available after goblin standing ≥ wary.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the rumour data, when validated, then there are 12–18 rumours and each has a source, truth value and target that resolves to an existing ID.
- AC-2 [unit] Given goblins.standing = hostile, when rumour availability is evaluated, then no goblin-sourced rumour is offered.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player has visited a rumour's target, when Dot is spoken to, then the confirm/debunk follow-up line is available once.
- AC-4 [content] Given the set, when counted, then at least 2 rumours are false or half-true and each false rumour has a debunk path.
- AC-5 [unit] Edge: given all rumours are already known, when Dot offers to trade, then a fallback line plays and no coin is taken.

title: Script The Watch Still Stands, Framed in Brass, Name on the Bones
description:
## Why
These quests carry class-specific solutions (knight relieves the Sentinels, archer rings the cord), Vane's exposure and the game's most emotional thread (Clatter remembering).

## What
As a player, I want wilderness and dungeon side quests with class-flavoured solutions so that exploring off the main path changes the story. The Watch Still Stands (watchword / knight formal relief / archer bell cord / sorcerer dispel / thief stealth / smash). Framed in Brass (free Duggan by force, trade the kettle, persuade, take the kit; combine with ledger — and optionally Quell's foundry invoice from Wendmouth — to expose Vane). The Name on the Bones (psalter, pear tree, sister's letter; sorcerer memory-read risk; join or rest).

## Scope
- In: quest-watch-still-stands, quest-framed-in-brass, quest-name-on-the-bones data
- In: facts: sentinels.relieved, duggan.freed, vane.exposed, clatter.memories, clatter.restored, clatter.choice
- Out: Sentinel/goblin AI (E11/E13)
- Out: pear tree bloom VFX (E29)

## Notes
A failed sorcerer memory-read permanently removes one memory piece option but must still allow completion via the remaining pieces plus an alternate (bible §6.1).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the three quest files, when validated, then they pass and each has ≥ 3 resolutions.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player class is knight, when The Watch Still Stands is evaluated at the Sentinels, then the formal-relief resolution is available; given other classes, it is not.
- AC-3 [unit] Given vane.ledger.obtained and duggan.freed, when Framed in Brass completes, then vane.exposed can be set.
- AC-4 [unit] Edge: given a failed memory-read, when The Name on the Bones is re-evaluated, then it remains completable and clatter.memories max is reduced by exactly 1.
- AC-5 [unit] Given clatter.restored, when the join/rest choice is made, then clatter.choice is set and the main quest Cradle/Climb variants read it.

title: Script side quests The Bookshop Burglar and The Captain's Boots
description:
## Why
Town side quests make Briar Glen dense and reward talking to people; both feed the main quest (Snig vouches for you; Hale backs your testimony).

## What
As a player, I want small town mysteries with several honest solutions so that my class and choices matter even in town. The Bookshop Burglar: stake out, track to the well, find Snig; resolutions turn in / broker lessons / sell the book / Mortimer scare. The Captain's Boots: follow Hale at night; resolutions wakeful tea / wrong draught / tie down / bell on door / follow route; then tell the town or keep the secret.

## Scope
- In: quest-bookshop-burglar and quest-captains-boots data
- In: world-state facts they set (snig.lessons, hale.secret.kept, route.briarwood.revealed)
- Out: NPC dialogue text (e39-dialogue-town-core, e39-dialogue-labyrinth-folk)

## Notes
Picking the sleep draught instead of wakeful tea must create a story (Hale walks into the Deepworks and must be retrieved), not a fail state. Bible §6.1.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given both quest files, when validated by the quest validator, then they pass and each has ≥ 3 resolutions.
- AC-2 [unit] Given each Bookshop Burglar resolution, when completed, then the documented goblin-standing and snig facts are set.
- AC-3 [unit] Edge: given the player gives Hale the sleep draught, when night falls, then the "Hale walks in" branch starts and the quest remains completable.
- AC-4 [unit] Given The Captain's Boots completes with the secret kept, when Act III testimony is evaluated, then Hale backs the player.
- AC-5 [manual] Given a playtest, when each quest is completed with two different solutions, then both feel intentional and neither is flagged as a "failure" by the tester.

title: Handle stolen and forbidden books in bookshop trade
description:
## Why
Some books are stolen or forbidden (constitution §4) — trading them should carry risk and create thief/sorcerer crossover.

## What
As a sorcerer or thief, I want booksellers to react to stolen and forbidden books — refusing, fencing at a discount, or selling forbidden stock under the counter — so that illicit books have a market with consequences.
Bookseller profile flags: buysStolen, sellsForbidden, reportsContraband. Selling a book stolen from this very shop triggers recognition. Forbidden stock is only shown when no lawful witnesses are nearby.

## Scope
- In: stolen-owner tracking in trade, bookseller legality flags, witness check for forbidden sales, recognition consequence
- Out: guard response behaviour (E11)
- Out: forbidden reading consequences (e07-forbidden-books)

## Notes
Stolen flag comes from the E17/E10 ownership model — Related: thief group stealing/ownership bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a bookseller with buysStolen=false, when offered a stolen book, then the sale is refused with reason "stolen".
- AC-2 [unit] Given buysStolen=true, when buying a stolen book, then price is the fence rate (default 50% of normal sell-back).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player tries to sell a book stolen from this same shop, when offered, then the bookseller recognises it: disposition drops and a world fact "caught_selling_back" is recorded.
- AC-4 [integration] Given sellsForbidden=true and a lawful NPC within perception range, when the shop opens, then forbidden stock is hidden until the witness leaves.
- AC-5 [integration] Given reportsContraband=true, when the player sells a forbidden book, then a ContrabandReported event fires.

title: Reveal secret back-room stock through dialogue, trust or discovery
description:
## Why
Secret inventory rewards curiosity and relationships — the "do you have anything… special?" moment.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want some bookshops to have hidden stock unlocked by a password, high disposition, a quest, or physically finding the back room so that secrets exist even in shops.
Secret pool gated by unlock method; can be accessed by a thief breaking in (stolen goods flagged on removal).

## Scope
- In: secret pool unlock via dialogue action/disposition/world fact, physical back-room container hook
- Out: dialogue content and passwords (world-content group)

## Notes
Taking from the back room without buying marks books stolen (e21-stolen-forbidden-stock).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a dialogue action unlockSecretStock, when executed, then the secret pool becomes purchasable for this shop.
- AC-2 [unit] Given disposition below the threshold and no other unlock, when the shop opens, then secret items are not listed.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player takes a secret-stock book from the back-room container without buying, when removed, then the book is flagged stolen with owner = the shop.
- AC-4 [unit] Given secret stock unlocked, when saved and reloaded, then it remains unlocked.

title: Add Stasis: freeze one object or creature in time
description:
## Why
Time magic creates novel puzzle and combat verbs: hold a falling gate, stop a swinging blade, pause an enemy.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to lock a single target in time for 5 s so that I can freeze moving traps, suspend falling objects or stop an attacker mid-swing.
Stasis status: zero velocity, immune to damage and forces, mechanisms paused; stored impulses from hits apply on release (capped).

## Scope
- In: Stasis spell
- In: stasis status with stored impulse
- In: spell JSON + book item JSON, unit tests for effects, integration tests for world interactions, placeholder cue ids
- Out: final VFX/SFX/icon/book cover (asset prompt beads)
- Out: world placement of the book (E24–E26)

## Notes
School: Time. Placeholder cues: vfx-spell-stasis-{lock,release}, sfx-spell-stasis-{lock,release}. Icon: icon-spell-stasis. Book cover: ui-book-cover-stasis.
TOO USEFUL — INTENTIONALLY ALLOWED (constitution §4). Do not nerf this spell to prevent sequence breaks or cheese; encounters and puzzles must tolerate it. Balance only via mana/cast time/cooldown, never by adding pairwise exceptions.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell data file, when validated and loaded, then it has a school, book item, vfxCue and sfxCue and casts in the headless sim.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a moving mechanism (swinging blade, falling portcullis), when stasis is applied, then it halts for 5 s and resumes its prior motion afterwards.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a creature in stasis struck by forces totalling 300 N·s, when stasis ends, then the stored impulse (capped at 200 N·s) applies at once.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature in stasis, when damage is applied, then health is unchanged during stasis.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a creature tagged boss or immune-time, when targeted, then duration is reduced to 1 s.

title: Add Snuff: extinguish all light sources in a radius
description:
## Why
Shadow magic that serves stealth: the sorcerer can create darkness like the thief extinguishing lights.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to snuff every flame and magical light within 6 m so that I can plunge a room into darkness and use it to hide or disorient.
AoE that removes lit state from light-source objects and ends light ops; smothers small fires (not large blazes); quiet cast.

## Scope
- In: Snuff spell
- In: spell JSON + book item JSON, unit tests for effects, integration tests for world interactions, placeholder cue ids
- Out: final VFX/SFX/icon/book cover (asset prompt beads)
- Out: world placement of the book (E24–E26)

## Notes
School: Shadow. Placeholder cues: vfx-spell-snuff-pulse, sfx-spell-snuff-hush. Icon: icon-spell-snuff. Book cover: ui-book-cover-snuff.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell data file, when validated and loaded, then it has a school, book item, vfxCue and sfxCue and casts in the headless sim.
- AC-2 [integration] Given 5 lit candles and 1 torch within 6 m, when Snuff is cast, then all become unlit and the light field drops accordingly.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a burning object larger than the small-fire threshold, when Snuff is cast, then it remains burning.
- AC-4 [integration] Given guards in the darkened room, when they evaluate visibility of the player, then the reduced light level lowers the player's visibility score.
- AC-5 [unit] Given Snuff noise loudness, when cast, then emitted loudness is ≤ 20 (quiet).

title: Add Arcane Sight: reveal hidden mechanisms and magical properties
description:
## Why
Magic "can reveal secrets" — a sorcerer-flavoured alternative to the thief finding hidden passages.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a 15 s self buff that outlines objects tagged hidden, magical or trapped within 12 m so that I discover secret doors, traps and enchanted items.
Revealed status applied to matching entities; revealed traps become visible to the player only.

## Scope
- In: Arcane Sight spell
- In: revealed status rendering hook (placeholder outline)
- In: spell JSON + book item JSON, unit tests for effects, integration tests for world interactions, placeholder cue ids
- Out: final VFX/SFX/icon/book cover (asset prompt beads)
- Out: world placement of the book (E24–E26)

## Notes
School: Arcane. Placeholder cues: vfx-spell-arcane-sight-overlay, sfx-spell-arcane-sight-cast. Icon: icon-spell-arcane-sight. Book cover: ui-book-cover-arcane-sight.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell data file, when validated and loaded, then it has a school, book item, vfxCue and sfxCue and casts in the headless sim.
- AC-2 [integration] Given any object tagged hidden within 12 m, when Arcane Sight is active, then it gains revealed for the duration.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a trap tagged trapped behind a wall with no line of sight, when active, then it is revealed (sight through walls up to 12 m).
- AC-4 [integration] Given a hidden object at 13 m, when active, then it is not revealed until the player comes within 12 m.
- AC-5 [unit] Given Arcane Sight ends, when duration expires, then all revealed statuses it applied are removed.

title: Add Fire Wall: a persistent line of flame that blocks and burns
description:
## Why
Third step of the fire chain: area denial as a new verb — split a fight, block a corridor, burn a bridge.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to draw a 6 m line of fire on the ground that lasts 8 s so that I can block paths and ignite what crosses it.
Persistent line volume with heat stimulus; creatures with fear-of-fire disposition refuse to cross; it emits strong light.

## Scope
- In: Fire Wall spell
- In: chain link Flame Jet → Fire Wall
- In: spell JSON + book item JSON, unit tests for effects, integration tests for world interactions, placeholder cue ids
- Out: final VFX/SFX/icon/book cover (asset prompt beads)
- Out: world placement of the book (E24–E26)

## Notes
School: Fire. Placeholder cues: vfx-spell-fire-wall-{spawn,loop,end}, sfx-spell-fire-wall-{spawn,loop}. Icon: icon-spell-fire-wall. Book cover: ui-book-cover-fire-wall.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell data file, when validated and loaded, then it has a school, book item, vfxCue and sfxCue and casts in the headless sim.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a Fire Wall placed across a corridor, when a creature whose disposition includes fears-fire paths to the player, then it routes around or waits rather than crossing.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a wooden floor tagged flammable under the wall, when the wall persists 8 s, then the floor ignites and continues burning after the wall ends.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a moisture stimulus (rain, Wellspring) applied to the wall, when resolved, then wall segments inside the moisture area are extinguished.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a placement line crossing a wall, when cast, then the fire line is clipped at the geometry.

title: Translate books written in unknown languages
description:
## Why
Untranslated books create quests and reasons to talk to scholars and find lexicons — curiosity rewarded.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want books in unknown languages to be unreadable until I obtain a lexicon or a translation so that decoding knowledge feels earned.
Languages are data; the player knows languages via lexicon items or NPC translation service (dialogue action); partially known languages show garbled text proportional to knowledge.

## Scope
- In: language registry, known-language state, lexicon items, translate action hook for dialogue, garbled text renderer data
- Out: NPC translator dialogue content (E22/E24)

## Notes
Garbling is deterministic per book + knowledge level so the same text appears on re-read.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a book in "Old Tessic" and no knowledge, when read, then study is disabled with reason "language" and pages render garbled.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player acquires the Old Tessic lexicon item, when reading, then the book is studyable.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 50% language knowledge, when rendering page text, then the same deterministic ~50% of words are garbled on every read.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a dialogue action "translate book X", when executed, then the book gains a translated flag and is studyable regardless of language knowledge.

title: Restore damaged books by finding their missing pages
description:
## Why
Damaged books turn a spell into an exploration hook: the rest of the pages are somewhere in the monastery.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a damaged book to teach a partial version of its spell and point me towards missing pages so that finding pages completes it.
Missing pages are separate page items (loot) linked by bookId; a damaged book teaches nothing, lore-only, or an unstable variant as configured; combining pages restores the book.

## Scope
- In: page items, combine action, partial-teach behaviour, restoration event
- Out: placement of pages in the world (E24–E26 content)

## Notes
Missing page text may hint at location (Related: world-content group authors hints).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a damaged book missing pages 3 and 7 configured partialTeach=unstable, when studied, then the spell is learned with comprehension capped at 0.5.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player holds both missing page items, when combining, then the book becomes intact, the page items are consumed and the comprehension cap lifts.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player holds only page 3, when combining, then the book remains damaged with only page 7 missing.
- AC-4 [content] Given a page item referencing a book that is not damaged, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Add magic debug commands and stimulus visualisation
description:
## Why
Fast content creation needs designers to grant spells, ignore mana and see stimuli while testing combinations.

## What
Debug console commands: spell.grant <id|all>, spell.infiniteMana, spell.noCooldown, spell.forceMiscast <table>, spell.reload (hot-reload spell JSON); overlay drawing active stimulus volumes, beams and summon lifetimes.

## Scope
- In: console commands, hot reload of spell content in dev builds, debug overlay
- Out: general console (e33-debug-console)

## Notes
Hot reload re-validates; invalid file keeps the previous version and prints errors.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the debug console, when "spell.grant all" runs, then every catalogue spell is known and assignable.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a spell file edited with an invalid value, when hot-reloaded, then the previous definition remains active and the validation error is printed.
- AC-3 [integration] Given spell.infiniteMana on, when casting 100 spells, then mana never decreases.

title: Let creatures and NPCs cast catalogue spells through the same pipeline
description:
## Why
Enemy mages should obey the same rules as the player so that interrupts, miscasts and world interactions apply to them too.

## What
As a designer, I want creature definitions to list spells with usage hints so that goblin shamans and liches cast via the standard pipeline.
Exposes a cast-request API for AI; creature mana optional; AI can be interrupted and miscast.

## Scope
- In: creature schema extension for spells (via E12 hooks), AI cast API, tests
- Out: AI decision-making about when to cast (E11 — Related: combat behaviours)

## Notes
Player-learnable spells dropped as books by enemy casters is handled in e07-book-acquisition-hooks.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature with a fixture projectile spell, when AI requests a cast at a target, then the pipeline processes it identically to a player cast (same events).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature caster hit hard during wind-up, when poise breaks, then its cast is interrupted.
- AC-3 [content] Given a creature referencing an unknown spell id, when validated, then validation fails.

title: Simulate loot tables and report drop distributions
description:
## Why
Exploration should produce interesting discoveries; designers need to see actual distributions, not guess from weights.
## What
CLI `pnpm loot:sim <tableId> --rolls 10000 --seed 1` prints item frequencies, expected gold, and flags items with 0 drops or duplicates of "unique" items; also available as console command.
## Scope
- In: CLI + console command using sim loot roller with seeded RNG
- Out: Loot runtime (e18-loot-tables)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a table with weights 1:3, when 10,000 rolls simulate with seed 1, then frequencies are 25% ± 1.5% and 75% ± 1.5% and the output is identical across runs.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a unique item that can drop twice in one roll, when simulated, then it is flagged.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an unknown table id, when run, then it exits non-zero listing close matches.

title: Add named teleport bookmarks and dev state snapshots
description:
## Why
Reaching the room you are working on in seconds, in the right world state, removes most iteration friction.
## What
As a developer, I want named bookmarks and instant dev snapshots so that I can jump to a place and state repeatedly.
Bookmarks as content (`content/dev/bookmarks.json`) + console `tp <name>`; `snap save <name>` / `snap load <name>` store full save envelopes in a dev IndexedDB store; URL `?snap=<name>` boots into a snapshot.
## Scope
- In: Bookmarks, snapshot commands, URL param
- Out: Player save slots (e30-save-slots)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given bookmark `arena-center`, when `tp arena-center` runs, then the player is placed there next tick.
- AC-2 [integration] Given `snap save a` then changes then `snap load a`, when compared, then the state hash equals the snapshot's.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a snapshot from an older save schema, when loaded, then save migrations apply; if they fail, a clear error is shown.

title: Recover gracefully from WebGL/GPU context loss
description:
## Why
GPU resets happen (driver updates, sleep/wake); losing a session to a black screen is avoidable.
## What
Handle `webglcontextlost`/`restored` (or WebGPU device lost): pause sim, show overlay, rebuild GPU resources from the asset cache on restore, resume; if restore fails within 10 s, autosave (if safe) and offer reload.
## Scope
- In: Context-loss handler, resource rebuild path
- Out: Save logic (e30-autosave)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given `WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext()` then `restoreContext()`, when triggered in the testbed, then rendering resumes within 5 s with the same sim state hash as before loss.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the context is never restored, when 10 s pass, then an autosave is attempted and a reload prompt appears.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given loss during loading, when restored, then loading completes without duplicate resources or errors.

title: Add gamepad deadzone, sensitivity curve and vibration settings
description:
## Why
Gamepad is second-class but supported; stick drift and vibration sensitivity vary by player and hardware.
## What
As a player, I want to tune stick deadzones, response curves and vibration so that my gamepad feels accurate.
Inner/outer deadzone per stick, response curve (linear/exponential), vibration intensity 0–100% (where Gamepad haptics are supported).
## Scope
- In: Settings + input-layer processing
- Out: Gamepad action mapping (e02-input-actions)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given inner deadzone 0.15, when stick magnitude is 0.1, then output is 0; at 1.0 output is 1.0 (rescaled).
- AC-2 [unit] Given vibration 0%, when a haptic request is made, then no vibration API call occurs.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a browser without `vibrationActuator`, when haptics are requested, then no error is thrown.

title: Export and import save files
description:
## Why
Browser storage can be cleared; players and playtesters need a way to back up and share saves.
## What
As a player, I want to export a save to a file and import it later so that clearing browser data does not erase my adventure.
Export produces `the-vesper-bell-<slot>-<date>.vbsave` (JSON envelope, gzip). Import validates envelope, checksum and version, then runs migrations and places it into a chosen slot.
## Scope
- In: Export/import in settings/load menu
- In: Validation errors shown in plain language
- Out: Cloud sync
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given an exported save, when imported into a fresh profile, then loading it yields the same sim state hash.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a file that is not a save (random JSON or PNG), when imported, then a clear "not a save from The Vesper Bell" error is shown and no slot changes.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a save from an older schema version, when imported, then migrations run and it loads.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a save file larger than 20 MB, when imported, then it is rejected before parsing.

title: Prevent two open tabs from clobbering each other's saves
description:
## Why
Browser games are easily opened twice; concurrent writers silently overwrite progress.
## What
Use the Web Locks API (fallback: BroadcastChannel heartbeat) to elect a single "active" tab. A second tab shows "Game already open in another tab" with a "Play here instead" option that asks the first tab to release (it autosaves and pauses).
## Scope
- In: Lock acquisition, takeover protocol, fallback
- Out: Cross-device sync (not planned)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the game open in tab A, when opened in tab B, then B shows the already-open message and makes no writes.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given B chooses "Play here instead", when A receives the request, then A autosaves, pauses with a notice, and B loads that autosave.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given tab A crashes (closed abruptly), when tab B retries, then it acquires the lock within 5 s.

title: Add quicksave and quickload actions
description:
## Why
Experimentation-heavy play (constitution: "too useful" spells) benefits from instant save-scumming for players who want it.
## What
As a player, I want quicksave/quickload keys so that I can try risky ideas instantly.
Quicksave writes the single quicksave slot (subject to the same safety vetoes as autosave, except combat is allowed); quickload asks for confirmation if unsaved progress > 60 s.
## Scope
- In: Quicksave/quickload actions registered in the action map
- In: Confirmation prompt
- Out: Default key bindings list (e02-input-actions)
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given quicksave during combat, when triggered, then the save succeeds (combat not vetoed for quicksave) but mid-air/dialogue still vetoes with a HUD message.
- AC-2 [integration] Given no quicksave exists, when quickload is pressed, then a "no quicksave" toast appears and nothing else changes.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given progress of 90 s since the last save, when quickload is pressed, then a confirmation dialog appears before loading.

title: Budget world-state save size and serialization time
description:
## Why
Browser saves live in IndexedDB and autosave during play; large or slow saves cause hitches and quota errors.
## What
Stress fixture with 10,000 facts + 5,000 deltas across 6 levels; perf tests for serialize/deserialize time and compressed size; autosave must not hitch the main thread (serialize off the sim tick via snapshot + worker compression).
## Scope
- In: Stress fixture, perf tests, snapshot-then-compress in a worker
- Out: IndexedDB quota handling — see e30-save-serialization
## Notes
Budgets from epic exit criteria.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the stress fixture, when serialized on the reference machine, then snapshot time on the main thread ≤ 50 ms and compressed size ≤ 1 MB.
- AC-2 [perf] Given autosave during 60 s of play, when measured, then no frame exceeds 33 ms due to save work.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a snapshot taken while the sim continues ticking, when compressed in the worker, then the saved state equals the state at snapshot tick (edge: no tearing).

title: Resolve elapsed time for unloaded levels when the player returns
description:
## Why
Leaving a freezing spell on a river and returning a day later should find it melted; a fire should have burned out. Cheap catch-up rules preserve consistency without simulating unloaded levels.
## What
As a player, I want time to have passed in places I left so that the world feels continuous.

On level load, compute elapsed sim time since last visit and apply analytic catch-up rules per component (ice melts after X, fires resolve to burnt, doors on timers close, puzzle respawners complete, reset policies apply) instead of simulating.
## Scope
- In: Last-visited tick per level, catch-up rule registry per component
- In: Deterministic ordered application
- Out: NPC off-screen schedules — see mw-e22
## Notes
Catch-up rules are pure functions (state, elapsed) → state, 100% unit-tested.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given ice created with melt time 10 min and a return after 30 min, when the level loads, then the ice is gone and water volume restored.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a return after 1 min, when loaded, then the ice remains with proportionally reduced thickness.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a timed door open when left, when returning after its timer, then it is closed.
- AC-4 [unit] Given elapsed time is negative or zero (clock anomaly / immediate re-entry), when loaded, then no catch-up applies and no error occurs (edge).

title: Emit puzzle discovery, attempt, solve and abandon telemetry events
description:
## Why
E34 wants puzzle completion signals; undeclared solutions are gold for designers.
## What
Emit e34 telemetry events: puzzleDiscovered, puzzleAttemptFailed, puzzleHintShown{tier}, puzzleSolved{solutionId|undeclared, durationS, class}, puzzleAbandoned (left region > 10 min unsolved after discovery).
## Scope
- In: Event schema entries + emission from runtime
- Out: Dashboards/export — see e34-telemetry-events
## Notes
Local-first; no network by default.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a puzzle solved via an undeclared route, when solved, then puzzleSolved carries solutionId=undeclared and the capability trail.
- AC-2 [unit] Given discovery then leaving the region for 10 min unsolved, when the tick runs, then puzzleAbandoned fires once.
- AC-3 [unit] Given telemetry disabled, when events occur, then nothing is recorded (edge).

title: Inspect puzzle goals, wiring and solver results in an in-game tool
description:
## Why
Designers iterate fastest when they can see why a puzzle is not solving (developer tooling pillar).
## What
Debug panel listing puzzles in the level with lifecycle state, live goal explain() tree, wiring graph highlight, attribution trail, and buttons to reset, force-solve, and run the solver for the current capability set.
## Scope
- In: Panel in e33 debug console; goal tree view; reset/force-solve/solve commands
- Out: Standalone level editor — out of scope
## Notes
Force-solve must set facts exactly as a real solve would (for save testing).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a level with a puzzle, when the inspector opens, then it lists the puzzle with current state and goal explain tree.
- AC-2 [integration] Given force-solve, when executed, then the solved fact and outputs match a real solve (compared via fact store diff).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the solver button on a puzzle whose search is inconclusive, when run, then the panel shows inconclusive without freezing the game for > 100 ms (runs in a worker) (edge).

title: Offer escalating diegetic hints when players are stuck on puzzles
description:
## Why
Puzzles should create "aha", not abandonment. Hints must be in-world (companion remarks, glinting clues) to preserve discovery.
## What
As a player, I want subtle in-world nudges after I have been stuck a while so that I stay engaged without being handed the answer.

Hint ladder per puzzle (data): tiers triggered by time-in-puzzle and failed attempts, each tier a hint action (player bark text, highlight pulse on a relevant object, NPC rumour unlock fact). Hints are class-aware (choose a tier text relevant to current capabilities). Disable-able in settings.
## Scope
- In: Hint ladder runtime + data, class-aware selection, settings toggle
- In: Attempt counting from puzzle failure pulses
- Out: Hint UI styling — see mw-e31
## Notes
Default thresholds: tier1 at 3 min or 3 failed attempts, tier2 at 6 min, tier3 at 10 min.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a puzzle in progress for 3 min, when the tick runs, then tier-1 hint fires once and not again for that tier.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a sorcerer with spell.frost, when a tier with class variants fires, then the frost-relevant text is chosen.
- AC-3 [unit] Given hints disabled in settings, when thresholds pass, then no hint fires (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a puzzle solved at 2:59, when time passes, then no hint fires.

title: Float and sink objects in liquid volumes by density
description:
## Why
Floating crates as stepping stones, sinking a heavy chest to trip a submerged plate, or ice slabs drifting are cheap emergent traversal once density is a property.
## What
As a player, I want wooden objects to float and iron to sink so that I can improvise rafts and stepping stones.

Buoyancy force from submerged volume × liquid density vs. object density, with drag; objects adjust to the liquid level; wet/soaked materials may change density (data).
## Scope
- In: Buoyancy + drag forces for bodies in liquid volumes
- In: Standing on floating bodies (moving platform)
- In: Density changes from waterlogging (data)
- Out: Currents / flowing rivers — out of scope for MVP
## Notes
Ice (density 0.92) floats automatically once frozen slabs break free.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an object with density 0.6 in water (1.0), when settled, then 60% ± 5% of its volume is submerged.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an iron object (density 7.8), when placed in water, then it sinks to the bottom and can rest on a submerged pressure plate.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a floating crate with a 20 kg load exceeding its buoyancy reserve, when loaded, then it sinks (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given the water level drops (drain), when resolved, then floating objects descend with the surface and settle on the floor.

title: Spread gas, smoke and steam clouds that react to fire and wind
description:
## Why
Gust clearing poisonous gas, igniting swamp gas, smoke blocking sight lines for a thief escape — gas turns rooms into systemic spaces.
## What
As a thief, I want smoke to block vision and flammable gas to explode when lit so that I can escape or set traps.

Gas types in the element field (smoke: blocks vision; steam: obscures, scalds lightly; poison: damages actors; flammable/marsh gas: ignites with flash + force stimulus when concentration ≥ threshold). Gas diffuses, rises/sinks by type, is blocked by walls/doors, vents through openings, and is pushed by force stimuli (Gust).
## Scope
- In: Gas species data (buoyancy, diffusion, decay, effects)
- In: Ignition of flammable gas → explosion stimulus
- In: Visibility occlusion query for stealth/AI (density along a ray)
- Out: AI reaction to smoke — see mw-e11
- Out: Gas VFX — see e29-vfx-framework
## Notes
Closed doors block gas (door entities are field blockers) — opening a door lets smoke pour out.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given flammable gas at concentration ≥ threshold in a cell and a heat source ≥ ignition, when resolved, then the gas is consumed and a force + heat stimulus is applied with radius scaled by the consumed volume.
- AC-2 [unit] Given smoke between an observer and a target, when densityAlongRay is queried, then it returns the integrated density and exceeds the vision-block threshold for a 2 m thick cloud.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a closed door separating two rooms, when gas fills room A, then room B stays at 0 until the door opens, after which concentration equalises over time.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a force stimulus through a gas cloud, when applied, then gas is displaced along the force direction by the documented amount.
- AC-5 [unit] Given gas in a fully sealed room with no decay source, when simulated for 30 minutes, then total gas mass is conserved and no cell exceeds max concentration (edge).

title: Run a controller feel review and retune against reference games
description:
## Why
Automated tests keep the controller correct; only humans can tell if it feels excellent. Numeric targets need validating against the tone references (Souls weight, Zelda responsiveness).
## What
Time-boxed (1 day) playtest of the greybox traversal course with 3+ testers, comparing jump arc, acceleration, camera lag and mantle timing against reference feel notes. Output: tuning changes committed to controller data and a short findings doc.
## Scope
- In: Playtest script, questionnaire, tuning deltas
- In: docs/design/controller-feel.md with before/after values
- Out: Combat feel — see mw-e04
## Notes
Time-box: 1 day. Record sessions (e34 telemetry optional).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given 3 testers on the traversal course, when surveyed, then median "controls feel responsive" score is ≥ 4/5.
- AC-2 [content] Given the review, when finished, then all tuning changes are committed to controller data and golden replays are re-blessed with diffs attached.
- AC-3 [manual] Given any tester reports a specific frustration (e.g. missed mantle), when reviewed, then it is either fixed or filed as a bead with a failing test.

title: Ambient environment VFX: dust motes, embers, fireflies, fog
description:
## Why
Light shafts full of dust and torches spitting embers give Briar Glen and the Labyrinth their mood (visual identity).

## What
As a player, I want places to feel alive with dust, embers, fireflies and fog so that exploring is atmospheric.
Ambient effects placed via level data or derived from properties: dust motes in light shafts, torch embers and flicker (auto on `burning` light sources), fireflies (forest night), falling leaves, height fog / fog volumes, water drips and ripples. Environment effects are limited to ≤ 25% of the particle budget.

## Scope
- In: Ambient effect set, placement data, budget share
- Out: Level dressing (location epics)

## Notes
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given ambient effects requesting 40% of the particle cap, when evaluated, then they are throttled to 25%.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a torch with `burning`, when loaded, then the ember effect attaches without per-torch authoring.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given an environment test scene in Chromium, when loaded, then all ambient effects render with no console errors.
- AC-4 [perf] Given the forest test scene at night, when measured, then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms on the reference machine (High).

title: Projected decals: scorch, frost, wet, arrow holes, cracks
description:
## Why
Decals leave evidence of what happened — scorch after fire, wet stone after a splash — making the world feel reactive.

## What
As a player, I want surfaces to show scorch, frost, wetness and arrow holes so that the world visibly remembers what happened.
Projected decals with a cap of 128 (High) / 48 (Low), FIFO fade-out. Wet decals match the sim `wet` duration exactly so visuals never lie about state; scorch remains after `burning` ends; frost while `frozen`; arrow holes when arrows are pulled; crack decals for crack stages.

## Scope
- In: Decal projector, cap/fade, state-synced lifetimes
- Out: Decal textures (asset group)

## Notes
Rule: a decal never conveys a gameplay state unless that state exists in the sim.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 129 decals on High, when the 129th spawns, then the oldest fades out over 1 s.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a surface becoming `wet` in sim for 20 s, when rendered, then the wet decal appears and is gone within one frame of the sim state clearing.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a burning object that is extinguished, when processed, then a scorch decal remains.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the Low preset, when decals spawn, then the cap is 48.

title: Reverb zones per space: caves, halls, interiors, forest
description:
## Why
Acoustic space sells the dungeon: a sword clang should echo in the labyrinth and die in the forest.

## What
As a player, I want each space to sound like its size and material so that caves, halls and forests feel different.
Convolution reverb sends per zone type (cave, stone hall, wooden interior, forest, open field) using impulse-response assets; zone chosen via e03-triggers volumes; 1 s crossfade across boundaries; Low preset uses a single shared convolver with fewer IRs.

## Scope
- In: Reverb send buses, zone volumes, crossfade, Low-preset fallback, placeholder IRs
- Out: Recorded/generated IR assets (asset group)

## Notes
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the listener entering a cave trigger volume, when processed, then the cave send ramps to its target over 1 s while the previous zone fades.
- AC-2 [unit] Given overlapping zones, when resolved, then the zone with the highest declared priority wins.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the Low preset, when zones switch, then at most one ConvolverNode exists.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a missing IR asset, when the zone activates, then the dry signal plays unaffected and a warning is logged.

title: Audio occlusion through walls and doors
description:
## Why
Hearing a muffled fight behind a door is atmosphere and information; it should match how creatures hear (the stealth model) conceptually.

## What
As a player, I want sounds behind walls and doors to be muffled so that I can judge where things are and whether a door is open.
For the top 16 priority sources within 30 m, raycast listener↔source at 10 Hz (staggered). Occluded: low-pass 22 kHz→900 Hz and −8 dB; closed door on the path: −12 dB and 600 Hz; open door: unoccluded path. 150 ms smoothing. Door states from e03-doors-locks-switches; acoustic values shared with the stealth group's door constants.

## Scope
- In: Ray scheduling, filter/gain mapping, door state lookup, smoothing
- Out: Sim noise occlusion for creatures (e09-sound-propagation)
- Out: Full path-finding propagation (post-MVP)

## Notes
Budget: ≤ 16 rays per 100 ms.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a source behind a solid wall, when occlusion updates, then its low-pass cutoff settles at 900 Hz and gain at −8 dB within 150 ms.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a source behind a closed door that then opens, when occlusion updates, then filtering clears within 150 ms.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 40 eligible sources, when scheduled, then only the 16 highest-priority are raycast and no more than 16 rays run per 100 ms.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the listener inside a collider (camera clipping), when raycasting, then the result is treated as unoccluded (no false muffling).

title: Archer mobility: quickstep while drawn and aerial shots
description:
## Why
The archer's fantasy is precision **and** movement; they should reposition without losing a draw.

## What
As an archer, I want to sidestep while holding a draw and shoot mid-jump so that I can stay mobile under pressure.
Quickstep: 12-tick sidestep with i-frames ticks 2–7, 15 stamina, retains up to 60% of current draw. Aerial shot: firing while airborne is allowed with +1.0° additional spread; draw progress continues in the air.

## Scope
- In: Quickstep move, draw retention, aerial shot spread
- Out: Knight roll (e04-dodge-iframes)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given full draw, when quickstep executes, then draw fraction after it is 0.6 and i-frames cover ticks 2–7.
- AC-2 [unit] Given 40% draw, when quickstep executes, then draw fraction remains 0.4 (retention caps at 60%, never increases).
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player airborne, when an arrow is released, then its spread includes +1.0°.
- AC-4 [manual] Given the range with rail targets, when three playtesters use quickstep, then median rating for "I feel mobile as an archer" is ≥ 4/5.

title: Moving-target payoffs: leg stumbles, wing downs, lead assist
description:
## Why
Hitting a running target should be hard and rewarding (Archer fantasy: moving targets).

## What
As an archer, I want well-led shots on moving creatures to trip or ground them so that tracking a target is worth mastering.
A `limb` (leg) hit on a creature moving > 3 m/s causes a stumble (60-tick knockdown for bipeds; quadrupeds slowed 50% for 3 s). A `wing` region hit on a flying creature grounds it for 4 s. Optional lead-indicator assist (off by default): shows the intercept point for the lock-on target from its velocity and arrow flight time (3-iteration solver).

## Scope
- In: Moving-limb stumble rule, wing grounding, lead solver + indicator assist
- Out: Flying locomotion (e12)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a biped moving at 4 m/s, when a leg region is hit, then it is knocked down for 60 ticks; moving at 2 m/s, then normal hit reactions apply.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a flying creature, when its wing region is hit, then it is grounded for 240 ticks.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a target moving at a constant 5 m/s at 30 m, when the lead solver runs, then its predicted intercept is within 0.3 m of the simulated arrow impact.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the lead assist disabled (default), when locked on, then no indicator renders.

title: Elevation grants archery damage and range advantage
description:
## Why
High ground should matter to an archer: climbing a tower should change the fight (Archer fantasy: elevation).

## What
As an archer, I want shooting from above to hit harder and reach farther so that seeking high ground is a real tactic.
Range gain is natural from ballistics. Additionally: shooter at ≥ 3 m above target → +15% damage; ≥ 6 m → +25% (data-tunable). Implemented as an attacker-stage modifier in the damage pipeline tagged `elevation`.

## Scope
- In: Elevation modifier, thresholds in data
- Out: AI reaction to unreachable attackers (e11)

## Notes
Related: AI group should give melee creatures a behaviour for unreachable archers (seek path, throw rocks, take cover).
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a shooter 4 m above the target, when a 20-pierce arrow hits, then 23 damage applies and the hit is tagged `elevation`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a shooter 2.9 m above, when an arrow hits, then no elevation bonus applies.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a 30%-draw shot from 10 m height versus ground level, when simulated, then horizontal range increases by ≥ 20%.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a shooter below the target, when an arrow hits, then no bonus or penalty applies.

title: Combat assist settings: wider parry, extra i-frames, stamina
description:
## Why
Accessibility: more players should reach the joy of a parry without removing the skill ceiling for others.

## What
As a player, I want optional combat assists so that timing-heavy combat is accessible to me.
Options via e31-settings-framework: parry window ×1.0/×1.5/×2.0 (extends the end tick), i-frames +0/+3/+6 ticks, stamina costs ×1.0/×0.75, extended creature telegraph cue (+10 ticks warning). Values are injected into the sim at session start and recorded in the replay header for determinism.

## Scope
- In: Assist options, sim injection, replay header recording, settings UI entries
- Out: Difficulty levels / enemy damage scaling (later if needed)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given parry assist ×2.0, when parry is pressed on tick 0, then hits on ticks 4–23 are parried (window 20 ticks).
- AC-2 [unit] Given i-frame assist +3, when a medium-load roll executes, then i-frames cover ticks 2–17.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a replay recorded with assists on, when replayed on a machine with assists off, then the header values are used and hashes match.
- AC-4 [unit] Given assists changed mid-session, when applied, then they take effect at the next safe point (no action in progress) and an `AssistsChanged` event is logged.

title: Select CC0 kit pieces for cemetery and schoolhouse props (7 models)
description:

Lychgate, Vesperine headstones with a small bell mark (two variants), the Mooring family plot, school desks, the slate board (rhyme rendered by the game font) and a stack of children's books.

- `model-prop-headstone-vesperine-02`
- `model-prop-mooring-plot-01`
- `model-prop-school-desk-01`
- `model-prop-slate-board-01`
- `model-prop-books-children-01`

## Scope

title: Texture atlas and palette-remap build step for prop sets
description:
## Why
Draw-call budgets (≤ 150 on Low) require one material per prop set; kits from different families only look like one world after palette remapping.

## What
As a developer, I want prop sets declared in a data file to be packed into one atlas with UVs rewritten, and kit gradient textures remapped to `tex-palette-master-01`, so that each set uses one material. Supports palette-atlas (KayKit-style) and painted-texture atlases, padding/bleed for mips, High/Low sizes.

## Scope
- In: Set definition data (`assets/sets/*.json`)
- In: Atlas packer with UV rewrite in glTF
- In: Palette remap table (kit colour → palette token)
- In: Integration with `assets:build`
- Out: Tileable textures (not atlased)
- Out: Character atlases (authored per character)

## Notes
Mip bleed: ≥ 8 px padding at 2048² so Low (1024²) mips do not bleed.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a set of 12 props with 12 materials, when atlased, then output meshes reference exactly 1 material and render pixel-identical within ΔE ≤ 3 against the unatlased screenshot at LOD0.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a palette remap table, when applied to a kit gradient texture, then every mapped source colour is replaced by its palette token hex and unmapped colours are reported.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the atlas at Low size, when mip level 2 is inspected, then no island samples a neighbour island (bleed check passes).
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given a set whose islands cannot fit in the maximum atlas size, when packed, then the build fails with the set id and the required size instead of shrinking texel density silently.

title: Remove finished spike prototypes from main once their runtimes land
description:
## Why
Spike prototypes sit outside every quality gate on purpose (spikes/README.md). Left on main they rot, confuse search results and invite imports into game code. Depth before breadth applies to the repo too: one maintained implementation beats two.

## What
As a developer, I want finished spikes moved off main so that the only AI and engine code I find is the maintained code in src/. Tag the current spikes on an archive ref (`archive/spikes-2026`), delete `spikes/engine-*`, `spikes/determinism`, `spikes/bench`, `spikes/shared` (ADR-0001, mw-e00.13) and `spikes/ai-architecture` (ADR-0005, mw-e11.1) from main, and update the ADRs' evidence links to point at the archive ref so the evidence stays reproducible.

## Scope
- In: Archive tag/branch, deletion, ADR link updates, the spikes ignore entries in eslint.config.js and .prettierignore (keep them if spikes/ stays as the home for future spikes)
- Out: Future spikes (they follow the same pattern and get their own removal)

## Notes
Do it after mw-e11.2 has its own tests for the patrol → investigate → return scenario, so the spike is no longer the only executable evidence for ADR-0005.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the archive ref, when checked out, then the ADR-0001 and ADR-0005 spike commands in each spike README still run.
- AC-2 [unit] Given main after the change, when `git ls-files spikes/` runs, then it lists only spikes/README.md (or nothing).
- AC-3 [manual] Given ADR-0001 and ADR-0005, when their evidence links are followed, then every link resolves on the archive ref.
- AC-4 [unit] Given main after the change, when pnpm lint, typecheck, test:coverage and build run, then they pass with no coverage change.

title: FakeCollisionWorld: an airborne capsule pushing into a wall sticks at the wall's square top edge
description:
## Why

Found while testing mw-e02.12: in the in-memory collision world, a falling capsule held against a wall whose top edge is within the capsule's height hangs in mid-air (velocity 0, not grounded) forever. The fake's square-edge Minkowski approximation reports the wall's top face (normal +y) for a diagonal down-and-in sweep beside the edge, and the controller's slide then cancels the fall. Rapier rounds edges, so the game is unaffected, but unit tests and goldens on the fake can hit it.

## What

As a developer, I want the fake to behave like Rapier at wall top edges, so that controller tests never pin a test-double artifact.

## Scope

- In: fix the fake's contact choice at edges (prefer the face the core is beside), plus a contract test run against both worlds
- Out: changes to the Rapier port
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [unit] Given a capsule falling while pushing into a 2 m wall, beside its top edge, when stepped, then it slides down and lands, in both the fake and the Rapier collision world (contract suite).

title: Heavy encumbrance blocks the pull-up from a ledge hang
description:
## Why

mw-e02.12 notes that heavy encumbrance may block pull-up (data). Mantling and hangs shipped without it because the sim has no carried weight yet.

## What

As a player carrying too much, I want pulling up from a hang to fail (with a cue), so that weight matters on climbs.

## Scope

- In: an encumbrance threshold in the controller's ledge tuning (content); the ledge hook refuses the pull-up above it
- Out: the inventory and weight model itself
acceptance_criteria: - AC-1 [unit] Given a hanging player above the pull-up weight threshold, when jump is pressed, then the player keeps hanging; below it, the pull-up runs.

title: Hit-stop freezes knockback travel and creature-executor attacks too
description: mw-e04.11 freezes the action timeline, its hitbox sweeps and hit-reaction clocks. Not yet frozen: a knocked-back/launched victim keeps flying via the character controller during the freeze, and attacks run by the creature attack executor (src/sim/combat/attacks) have their own clock and ignore hit-stop. Decide whether they should follow local time (isHitStopped) and implement.

title: Debug teleport moves physics-object props
description: The debug console's tp/teleport command (src/sim/debug/system.ts teleport) moves a placed object by rewriting its SceneTransform. Since mw-e33.16, console-spawned and scene props with a body are physics objects whose pose lives in the physics port and physics.object, so teleporting one changes nothing visible. Teleport should move the body (and wake it at rest) through the physics port inside the recorded command's tick. Discovered while doing mw-e33.16.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a physics-object prop, when the debug tp command teleports it, then its physics body is moved to the target pose (and woken) within the recorded command's tick, and physics.object reflects the new pose.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same command log replayed twice, then the resulting state hashes match (deterministic).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a non-physics placement, tp still rewrites its SceneTransform as before.

title: Give NPC interactors their own interact input
description: From PR #100: interaction system applies the Interact button to every interactor entity by default. Fine while only the player interacts; future NPC interactors must supply input via the system's input option.

title: Add InteractPrompt widget to the UI component gallery
description: From PR #100: InteractPrompt is not in src/ui/gallery.ts, so gallery axe and text-scale checks don't cover it. Add it.

title: Interpolate the lock point for moving targets in the lock marker and framing
description:
## Why
The lock-on marker and camera framing (mw-e02.16) read the locked target's lock point from the sim's ViewAnchor as of the last tick. Training dummies stand still, but a moving creature would make the marker step at 60 Hz instead of gliding with the interpolated render.

## What
As a player, I want the lock ring to stay glued to a moving target so that locked combat reads cleanly at any refresh rate.

## Scope
- In: interpolate the target's lock point with RenderSync alpha (or read the drawn transform) for the HUD marker and LockFraming.
- Out: lock-on rules (src/sim/targeting).

## Notes
src/game/player/testbed-player.ts lockTarget(); src/game/player/lock-marker.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a target moving at 5 m/s and a 144 Hz display, when frames are drawn between ticks, then the marker position follows the interpolated lock point (error ≤ 1 px at 1080p).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a stationary target, when frames are drawn, then the marker writes no DOM changes (idle HUD stays free).

title: Add Somnomancy to the constitution's list of magic schools
description: Owner decided 2026-09-29 to keep Somnomancy (story bible: forbidden dream magic, spell Lull) as a spell school; spell schema (PR #88) already includes it. Add it to CONSTITUTION.md line listing potential schools so docs agree.

title: Label discriminated-union variants in generated content docs
description: pnpm content:docs flattens discriminated unions (spell delivery, spell effects[], fact) into one field list: rows from different variants share a path (e.g. effects[].impulse is an object for damage and a number for force), and the variant descriptions (.describe on each op/delivery) are dropped. Group rows per variant with its discriminator value and description. Found while shipping mw-e06.1 (PR #88).

title: Offer optional, explicit upload of a playtest bundle
description:
## Why
Manual file sending adds friction for remote testers; an explicit upload button can help, but only with separate consent.
## What
As a playtester, I want to optionally upload my bundle with one click after reviewing it so that I do not have to email files.
Separate consent per upload (preview + "Upload" button), minimal endpoint (e.g. serverless function writing to private storage) with size limit and rate limiting, no cookies, delete-by-receipt-code.
## Scope
- In: Upload UI, endpoint spec, ADR on hosting choice
- Out: Automatic/background upload (never)
## Notes
- Deferred post-MVP: file export covers MVP playtests. Requires secret handling for the endpoint — no secrets in the repo.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the upload dialog, when the player does not press Upload, then zero network requests leave the page.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a bundle > 25 MB, when upload is attempted, then it is refused client-side with a message.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a successful upload, when complete, then a receipt code is shown that can be used to request deletion.

title: Extended trick arrows as pure data: frost, shock, smoke
description:
## Why
Proves the systemic promise: new arrows need data, not code, and immediately interact with existing world properties.

## What
As a designer, I want to add frost, shock and smoke arrows purely in data so that the arrow roster grows without engineering.
Frost applies `frozen` (e.g. water surfaces become walkable ice per e03 rules); shock applies `electrified` (conducts through wet/conductive); smoke spawns a vision-blocking volume. No new sim code beyond what payload types already support.

## Scope
- In: Three arrow data entries, tests exercising each
- Out: New payload primitives (would need a separate engineering bead)

## Notes
If any arrow needs code, split that capability into its own bead first.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [content] Given the three new arrow entries, when validated, then they pass with no schema changes.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a water surface, when a frost arrow impacts it, then it gains `frozen` per e03 rules.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a smoke arrow impact, when resolved, then a vision-blocking volume exists for its declared duration and blocks sight queries through it.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the change set for this bead, when reviewed, then no files under src/sim are modified (asserted by a CI path check on the PR).

title: Redesign HUD and menus for small touch screens
description:
## Why
Desktop menus and dense HUDs are unusable at phone sizes with touch targets.
## What
As a mobile player, I want HUD and menus sized for touch so that I can manage inventory, books and dialogue comfortably. Coarse placeholder.
## Scope
- In: Touch-target sizing (≥ 44 px), portrait/landscape handling, safe areas
- Out: Desktop UI
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a 390×844 viewport, when each menu renders, then all interactive targets are ≥ 44×44 CSS px and nothing overflows.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given a device rotation, when it occurs, then layout adapts without losing game state.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given a notched device safe area, when the HUD renders, then no HUD element is under the notch.

title: Create a mobile performance preset and memory budget
description:
## Why
Mobile GPUs and memory limits (esp. iOS Safari) need their own budgets.
## What
Mobile preset (render scale, shadows off/low, reduced particles, texture downscale), memory budget per spike findings, added to perf suite. Coarse placeholder.
## Scope
- In: Preset, budgets, perf suite entries
- Out: Desktop presets
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the target floor device, when the combat stress scene runs on the mobile preset, then p95 frame time ≤ 33.3 ms.
- AC-2 [perf] Given iOS Safari, when played for 20 minutes, then the tab is not killed for memory (heap within the spike-defined budget).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a desktop capability profile, when presets are chosen, then the mobile preset is never auto-selected.

title: Design touch controls for movement, camera and class verbs
description:
## Why
Keyboard/mouse verbs must map to touch without losing class expressiveness.
## What
As a mobile player, I want virtual stick, camera drag and contextual verb buttons so that I can play every class on touch. Coarse placeholder — split after the feasibility spike.
## Scope
- In: Touch input adapter onto the action map, layout customization
- Out: Anything before e36-mobile-feasibility
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given touch emulation, when the virtual stick is dragged, then the player moves proportionally.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given simultaneous stick + camera drags (multi-touch), when performed, then both apply independently.
- AC-3 [manual] Given each class, when played on a phone for 10 minutes, then its core verbs are usable (rated ≥ 3/5 by testers).

title: Spike: mobile browser feasibility and target devices
description:
## Why
Mobile only after MVP validation; before committing, measure what mobile browsers can actually run.
## What
Time-box 2 days: run the MVP build on representative iOS Safari and Android Chrome devices, measure fps/memory/load on a mobile preset, identify blockers (memory limits, WASM, audio unlock, fullscreen/orientation); ADR recommending target devices and scope.
## Scope
- In: Measurements, ADR
- Out: Implementation
## Notes
- None.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC-1 [manual] Given 2 iOS and 2 Android devices, when the MVP build runs, then fps, memory and load time are recorded in the ADR.
- AC-2 [manual] Given a device that crashes or fails to load, when recorded, then the cause (memory, API) is identified or marked unknown with next steps.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the ADR, when merged, then it states go/no-go for mobile and target device floor.

title: E36 — Mobile Adaptation
description:
## Outcome
Only after MVP validation: touch UX, mobile performance profiles, interface redesign and mobile browser support.
## Scope
- In: Coarse placeholder items to be re-planned after the MVP go decision
- Out: Any mobile work before e35-mvp-go-no-go is decided
## Exit criteria
- A mobile plan is re-scoped into PR-sized beads after the MVP go decision.
acceptance_criteria: - EC-1 A mobile plan is re-scoped into PR-sized beads after the MVP go decision.
